body:
# Tampa Hotels: Where to Stay by Neighborhood

Search for tampa hotels and you get three different trips served up as if they were one. There is downtown Tampa, with the Riverwalk and Water Street. There is the airport and Westshore side, built around flights and business travel. And there is the Gulf beach stay that plenty of people still file under "hotels in Tampa Florida," which is really Clearwater Beach in Pinellas County. I looked at hotels across all three, and the biggest booking mistake I saw was not the brand. It was the neighborhood.

This page is the front door to my Tampa hotel guides. I sort the options by trip type, give you the facts I could confirm, and point you to the dedicated guide for each property. I am not quoting nightly room rates anywhere on this page. Rates move, and I never got one I would treat as a quote. Fees, check-in times, and addresses are a different story, and those I have.

*Last updated: November 2, 2026*

![Rooftop hotel pool with white loungers overlooking a city skyline](/images/articles/tampa-hotels/tampa-hotels-261102.webp)
*Photo by [Pixabay](https://www.pexels.com/@pixabay/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/architecture-buildings-business-city-261102/)*

## Start with the trip, not the brand

Before comparing hotels, decide which of these you are planning:

- **Aquarium, Convention Center, Riverwalk, Water Street dining:** stay downtown and accept that valet is the norm.
- **A 6 a.m. flight, a layover, or a Westshore business trip:** stay on the airport side and learn the shuttle window.
- **White sand and Pier 60 energy:** you are looking at Clearwater Beach, which is Pinellas County, not Tampa proper.

If you want to see how these areas sit against each other, the [Tampa map guide](/getting-around/tampa-map) helps place the neighborhoods. For arrival logistics, the [Tampa International Airport guide](/getting-around/tampa-international-airport) covers getting in and out. Tampa International is the main arrival airport for hotel guests, and the official [Tampa International Airport site](https://www.tampaairport.com/) is the place to check current details.

## Downtown Water Street and the Riverwalk

This is the cluster most visitors mean by downtown Tampa hotels. The Tampa Convention Center at 333 S Franklin St anchors demand here, and the [Tampa Convention Center site](https://www.tampaconventioncenter.com/) lists Marriott Water Street, the JW, and Embassy Suites across the street, with the Westin Waterside about 0.3 miles away and the Hilton Downtown about 0.5 miles. The Riverwalk itself is described in convention-center attendee materials as about 2.4 miles of walkable path.

Not every hotel with "Riverwalk" in its marketing actually touches the path. If that distinction matters to you, start with my sorter: [Tampa Riverwalk Hotels: Which Ones Touch the Path](/guides/tampa-riverwalk-hotels). Friends of the Riverwalk groups its [Riverwalk hotel list](https://thetampariverwalk.com/visit/hotels.html) to include Hotel Tampa Riverwalk, Hilton Downtown, Hyatt Place and Hyatt House, the Marriott, the JW, and the Barrymore.

### The Marriott pair

Marriott treats JW Marriott Tampa Water Street and Tampa Marriott Water Street as a pair joined by a glass skybridge. Combined, Marriott describes 1,246 rooms and suites across the two buildings, three rooftop pools, a spa, and more than 150,000 square feet of event space. The neighborhood is Water Street Tampa, with the Riverwalk, Benchmark International Arena, and Sparkman Wharf close by.

These are two hotels, not one lobby with two names. I kept catching myself treating "Marriott Water Street" as a single door. Tampa Marriott Water Street is at 505 Water Street (813-221-4900), and the JW is at 510 Water Street (813-221-4950). If a map pin and a phone number ever disagree, trust the phone number. Some older listings still use the name "Tampa Marriott Waterside Hotel & Marina," and a few city materials show scrambled addresses, so matching the number is the safest check.

At Tampa Marriott Water Street, the hotel is pet-friendly. Marriott's rooms page lists a [destination fee of $20 per night](https://www.marriott.com/en-us/hotels/tpamc-tampa-marriott-water-street/rooms/) with inclusions like a daily food and beverage credit, a beverage tasting, a choice of water taxi for two or an hour of water sports or bike rentals, and enhanced Wi-Fi. Fee and inclusions are subject to change, so confirm when you book. For fees, dining hours, parking, and how to tell the two buildings apart, read [Marriott Water Street Tampa: Fees, Dining, Parking and Which Hotel You're Booking](/guides/marriott-water-street-tampa).

Visit Tampa Bay lists check-in at 4 p.m., check-out at 11 a.m., and valet parking with a charge. I never got a garage price, so I am not printing one.

### The Tampa EDITION

The Tampa EDITION is in the same Water Street district at 500 Channelside Drive, but it is its own building. It has 172 guest rooms and 30 suites, including a penthouse listed at 2,059 square feet. Check-in is 4 p.m., check-out is 11 a.m., and the minimum check-in age is 18. The hotel's own getting-here information lists overnight valet at $58 plus taxes, daytime valet at $40 plus taxes, and event valet at $60 plus taxes, with a validation note tied to food-and-beverage spend. That is valet pricing, not a room rate. Dining is under Michelin-starred Chef John Fraser. If you are weighing the more design-forward end of the market, [The Tampa EDITION: 5 Things to Know Before You Book](/guides/the-tampa-edition) lays out what I would check first.

## North of the river and Harbour Island

Downtown Tampa hotels are not all within a few steps of Water Street. The distances quoted by different sources for the same hotel often disagree, which is the main thing to plan around.

**Hilton Tampa Downtown** is at 211 N. Tampa Street (813-204-3000). Its own marketing says "steps from the Riverwalk." Friends of the Riverwalk says two blocks. The city says 0.5 miles from the convention center, and one tourism source puts it at two miles. Steps, two blocks, half a mile, two miles: I would not plan a walk around any of those numbers without checking a map. What I confirmed: 17 floors, check-in at 4 p.m., check-out at noon, pets allowed, a rooftop pool, and a $100 nightly security deposit (a deposit, not the room price). Note that "Hyatt Regency" is the historical name for this property. It is the Hilton now.

**Embassy Suites by Hilton Tampa Downtown Convention Center** is at 513 S. Florida Avenue (813-769-8300). It is an all-suite property with 360 suites, a skybridge to the convention center, and free made-to-order breakfast plus an evening reception. Check-in is 4 p.m. and check-out is 11 a.m.

**Hyatt Place and Hyatt House** share an address at 325 N. Florida Avenue (813-616-1234). The tourism bureau treats them as one dual-branded hotel with 345 guestrooms. Friends of the Riverwalk lists them separately. As far as I can tell it is one roof.

**The Westin Tampa Waterside** is on Harbour Island at 725 S. Harbour Island Boulevard (813-229-5000). It is blocks from the convention center and the cruise port, with the streetcar one block away. Check-in is 3 p.m. and check-out is noon. The hotel's own materials put over 85 percent of rooms with water views and offer a shuttle on demand within three miles, if available. The name trips people up: it has appeared as Westin Tampa Waterside, Westin Tampa Downtown Waterside, and Westin Tampa Harbour Island. One building. "Waterside" sounds like the Gulf, and it is not. The hotel itself lists Clearwater Beach at 25 miles. My full write-up is [6 Things to Know About the Westin Tampa Waterside Before You Book](/guides/the-westin-tampa-waterside).

**Aloft Tampa Downtown** is at 100 W. Kennedy Boulevard (813-898-8000), a select-service hotel with a 24-hour waterfront fitness center and a river-front splash pool. Check-in is 4 p.m. and check-out is 11 a.m.

### The Barrymore

The Barrymore Hotel Tampa Riverwalk is the clearest example of a name that oversells the location. It uses "Riverwalk" in the name but sits near the path, not on it. The city gives the address as 111 W. Fortune Street (813-223-1351), 1.4 miles from the convention center. What I can state firmly: self-parking is $20 a night per vehicle, the pet fee is $75 for the whole stay, check-in is 3 p.m., check-out is 11 a.m., and the pool deck sits over the Hillsborough River with no lifeguard. A shuttle runs 8 a.m. to 10 p.m. within two miles, though not to the airport. Full details are in [Staying at the Barrymore Hotel Tampa: My Honest Riverwalk Guide](/guides/barrymore-hotel-tampa).

### A renovation to know about

Hotel Tampa Riverwalk is on Friends of the Riverwalk's list, but its [FAQ](https://www.hoteltampariverwalk.com/faq) says renovations run through November 30, 2026, with the pool and food and beverage closed during that time. The fitness center stays open 24/7. Confirm on the hotel's FAQ before booking, since closures can change.

## Westshore and the airport side

This is a different trip from Water Street, and it works best when the airport or business travel is the point.

**Westshore Marriott** sits on N Westshore Blvd near the malls and the airport corridor. Before booking, read [Westshore Marriott Hotel Tampa: 6 Things to Know Before You Book](/guides/westshore-marriott-hotel-tampa).

A few other airport-side properties I looked at, so you can see how this category differs:

- **Tampa Airport Marriott** has the airport in its address: 4200 George J. Bean Parkway. It has renovated rooms, soundproof windows, and day-use rooms from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. daily. It suits a layover or an early flight, not a Riverwalk stroll.
- **Holiday Inn Express & Suites Tampa Airport** is at 3025 North Rocky Point Drive East. The hotel lists a complimentary airport shuttle from 5:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m., free breakfast from 6:30 to 9:30 a.m., and complimentary parking for guests (or $10 a day if you leave a car for a cruise or flight). Pets are $75 per stay, dogs only, with a two-pet limit. It has no on-site restaurant and lists the Clearwater beaches at about 20 miles. That last detail is the whole point: an airport hotel can put you near the terminal and still leave the Gulf as a separate drive.
- **Holiday Inn Tampa Westshore - Airport Area** is at 700 North Westshore Blvd. Minimum check-in age is 21, check-in is 3 p.m., and a complimentary airport shuttle runs 6:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. On-site parking is $15 a day. Breakfast is included only for preferred key accounts, so do not assume it is free for everyone.

## Seminole Hard Rock

Seminole Hard Rock Tampa is a separate hotel and entertainment campus, not a downtown waterfront stay, and it should not be treated as a Riverwalk hotel. If you are weighing it for its hotel, dining, or concerts, use the dedicated guide: [Seminole Hard Rock Tampa: Hotel, Dining, Concerts Guide](/guides/seminole-hard-rock-tampa).

## The "Tampa hotel" that is really Clearwater Beach

If your plan is a beach week, a lot of hotels labeled as Tampa are actually on Clearwater Beach. Opal Sands Resort, for example, is at 430 S Gulfview Blvd, Clearwater Beach, with 230 gulf-front rooms and suites and direct beach access. It is a Gulf trip. Selling it as a Tampa hotel without saying Clearwater is how people book the wrong water. The downtown and airport hotels above put you 20 to 29 miles from those beaches by the hotels' own numbers, which is a drive, not a walk.

## Reading the address (for visitors from abroad)

The phrase "hotels in Tampa USA" exists because a bare "Tampa" is not enough on a booking site that sells rooms worldwide. A few things the address wording does and does not do:

- **USA only picks the country.** After that, read the state (Florida), the ZIP, and the street. Downtown Harbour Island and a Westshore business park both say Tampa, Florida, USA, with different ZIP codes.
- **Phone numbers start with +1,** the US country code, then 813 for Tampa. The 1 is not optional.
- **Tampa Bay is the marketing region; Tampa is the city.** A hotel with Tampa in the name can still sit in a different town on the bay or in a different county.
- **Minimum check-in age can be 21,** as at the Westshore Holiday Inn, while other hotels use 18. Check before you arrive.
- **Fees are in US dollars and are extra.** The Marriott's $20 destination fee and Hotel Flor's $30 daily destination fee (with a $15 food-and-beverage credit) are examples of costs that sit on top of a nightly rate.

Check-in times vary by hotel: 4 p.m. at the Marriott towers, EDITION, and Hilton, 3 p.m. at the Westin and the Barrymore. I would not assume a room is ready when the flight lands.

## Getting around without a car

If you stay downtown, the TECO Streetcar connects downtown, Channelside, and Ybor, which helps if you skip a rental car. The Westin is one block from a streetcar stop. Parking, when you do have a car, is usually valet or a city garage downtown. The City's [parking rates page](https://www.tampa.gov/parking/info/parking-hourly-and-daily-rates) covers public garage pricing, and my individual hotel guides carry the hotel-specific numbers I could confirm. At the airport hotels the picture flips: some offer free guest parking, some charge a daily rate, and shuttle windows matter more than walkability.

## How to choose

People ask for the best hotels in Tampa and Tampa luxury hotels, and the honest answer depends on which trip you are on. A few rules of thumb from what I looked at:

1. **Pick the neighborhood first.** Parking and shuttle details come second. The brand name is the easy part.
2. **Treat "near" and "steps from" with suspicion.** Downtown distances to the Riverwalk and the convention center vary by source for the same hotel. Check a map.
3. **Budget for fees.** Destination fees, valet, and parking change the real cost of a stay.
4. **Match phone numbers to addresses** at the two Marriott towers, since old names and scrambled listings are still around.
5. **Confirm what is open.** Renovations, like the one at Hotel Tampa Riverwalk, can close pools and restaurants.
6. **Restaurant reservations are worth making** at the downtown hotel dining rooms, including Lilac at the EDITION, Anchor and Brine at the Marriott, and Lona.

For more lodging beyond the hotels covered here, browse the [Visit In Tampa directory](/directory) and the [places section](/places). Visit Tampa Bay also keeps a directory of downtown properties at [visittampabay.com](https://www.visittampabay.com/), which is useful context but not a source for rate quotes.

## Frequently asked questions

**Where should I stay in Tampa for the first time?**
If you want the Riverwalk, the Aquarium, Water Street dining, and the Convention Center, stay downtown. Start with [Tampa Riverwalk Hotels: Which Ones Touch the Path](/guides/tampa-riverwalk-hotels) to sort which properties are actually on the path.

**Is Seminole Hard Rock a downtown Tampa hotel?**
No. It is a separate hotel and entertainment campus. See the [Seminole Hard Rock Tampa guide](/guides/seminole-hard-rock-tampa) for hotel, dining, and concerts.

**Are Tampa hotels near the beach?**
Generally not. Downtown and airport hotels are a drive from the Gulf. The Westin lists Clearwater Beach at 25 miles, and the Rocky Point Holiday Inn Express lists the Clearwater beaches at about 20 miles. For a beach stay, you are looking at Clearwater Beach.

**Do Tampa hotels charge extra fees beyond the room rate?**
Often, yes. Tampa Marriott Water Street lists a $20 nightly destination fee, and Hotel Flor lists a $30 daily destination fee. Valet at the EDITION runs $40 to $60 plus taxes depending on the type. Always confirm current fees on the hotel's official page.

**What is the difference between the JW Marriott and Tampa Marriott Water Street?**
They are two connected hotels at different addresses (510 and 505 Water Street). Read [Marriott Water Street Tampa: Fees, Dining, Parking and Which Hotel You're Booking](/guides/marriott-water-street-tampa) before you book.

## Where to go next

I spent six months in Tampa from November 2025 to May 2026, based downtown with my aunt and cousins, so the Water Street and Riverwalk side is the part of town I know best. For the full picture, work through the guides above: the [Riverwalk sorter](/guides/tampa-riverwalk-hotels), the [Marriott Water Street guide](/guides/marriott-water-street-tampa), the [Westin Waterside](/guides/the-westin-tampa-waterside), the [Tampa EDITION](/guides/the-tampa-edition), the [Barrymore](/guides/barrymore-hotel-tampa), the [Westshore Marriott](/guides/westshore-marriott-hotel-tampa), and [Seminole Hard Rock](/guides/seminole-hard-rock-tampa). Pick the neighborhood first, and the rest of the booking gets a lot easier.

Meeting demand often tracks the [Tampa Convention Center](/guides/tampa-convention-center) on Franklin Street.


Dinner plans pair naturally with the [Tampa restaurants](/food-and-drink/tampa-restaurants) hub.

title: Tampa Stadium Guide: Ray Jay, the Arena and the Trop
dek: Which Tampa stadium do you need? Raymond James Stadium, Benchmark Arena and Tropicana Field compared, with parking, rideshare, bag and ticket rules.
metaTitle: Tampa Stadium Guide: Ray Jay, Arena and the Trop
metaDescription: Which Tampa stadium do you need? Raymond James Stadium, Benchmark Arena and Tropicana Field compared, with parking, rideshare, bag and ticket rules.
coverAlt: Aerial view of an American football game in a stadium
coverCredit: Photo by Terrance Barksdale on Pexels
body:
# Tampa Stadium Guide: Ray Jay, the Arena and the Trop

People type tampa stadium, stadium Tampa FL, Tampa Florida stadium and stadium in Tampa, and those searches do not all point at one building. When I was sorting this out, I only kept venues that genuinely tie to the phrase. There are three buildings that get lumped together, and one of them is not even in Tampa. This guide separates them, then spends most of its time on the one most people mean: Raymond James Stadium.

*Last updated: November 2, 2026*

![Aerial view of an American football game in a stadium](/images/articles/tampa-stadium-guide/stadium-night-39590560.webp)
*Photo by [Terrance Barksdale](https://www.pexels.com/photo/aerial-view-of-american-football-game-in-stadium-39590560/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/aerial-view-of-american-football-game-in-stadium-39590560/)*

## Which stadium do you mean?

Here is the short version, matched by ticket type:

- **Buccaneers, USF Bulls football, a bowl game or a stadium concert:** Raymond James Stadium, 4201 N. Dale Mabry Hwy, Tampa, FL 33607.
- **Tampa Bay Lightning:** Benchmark International Arena, 401 Channelside Drive, Tampa, FL 33602. It is an arena, not a stadium, and plenty of people still call it by its old name.
- **Tampa Bay Rays:** Tropicana Field, 1 Tropicana Dr, St. Petersburg, FL 33705. That is St. Petersburg, not Tampa.

The Tampa Sports Authority is the landlord for the football stadium, the arena and George M. Steinbrenner Field, according to the stadium's own A-to-Z guide. Those are three different pieces of ground, and Steinbrenner Field matters mostly because it doubles as a rideshare staging lot for stadium events. My rule of thumb: match the team first, then the city, then the lot. Dale Mabry, Channelside and Tropicana Drive are three different trips. For a visual on how far apart they sit, our [Tampa map](/getting-around/tampa-map) helps.

## Raymond James Stadium: the Tampa stadium for football

Raymond James Stadium, nicknamed Ray Jay, is the building most people mean when they say the Tampa stadium. USF athletics says it has been the Bulls' home since 1998, describes it as a roughly 65,000-seat stadium, and notes it is also home to the NFL's Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The stadium first welcomed fans on September 20, 1998. If you want the team side of the story, start with our page on the [Tampa Bay Buccaneers](/events).

Beyond the two football tenants, USF names the annual ReliaQuest Bowl and Gasparilla Bowl, concerts and WrestleMania among its events. The stadium's own guide also lists Monster Jam.

### Super Bowls and big games

USF's list of major games hosted here:

- Super Bowl XXXV (2001), Ravens and Giants
- Super Bowl XLIII (2009), Steelers and Cardinals
- Super Bowl LV (2021), Chiefs and Buccaneers
- The 2017 College Football Playoff National Championship, Clemson over Alabama

That is USF's account of the history; I took it as published rather than checking each game myself.

### The pirate ship

The landmark everyone mentions is the replica pirate ship in the north end zone. USF describes it as a roughly 103-foot-long replica of an early 1800s pirate ship, set among end-zone pavilions and palm trees. The stadium's guide adds that it was built in 1998, is owned by the Buccaneers, is closed to the public during events, and fires cannons at Buccaneers games. It can be rented on non-event days through the stadium office at 813-350-6500.

### Why the name is a company, not a person

The namesake is Raymond James Financial, a firm headquartered in St. Petersburg. USF says the company has held the naming rights since the stadium debuted in 1998 and continues as sponsor through the 2027 season, which USF calls the second-longest continuous active stadium naming-rights partnership in the NFL. That is USF's claim. So the dropped first name in "James Stadium Tampa" is really a financial firm across the bay, while the stadium sits on Dale Mabry.

### Clubs and suites

The stadium guide's figures, which I would treat as the stadium's own claims: the Hyundai West Club at roughly 60,000 square feet and the East Club at roughly 64,000 square feet with Bar 76, named for 1976. There are 134 suites seating 8 to 36 people, and a renovation begun in 2016 was expected to exceed $180 million. Club access varies by event.

## Getting there: parking, rideshare and RVs

The stadium's directions are more useful than any nickname.

### Parking

All parking lots use cashless, contactless payment with major credit cards. Price varies by event, advance parking is a separate purchase, and event-day parking is first come, first served. Lot opening times are set event by event, so there is no standing clock. I am not putting a dollar figure here because there isn't one fixed number. The A-to-Z guide puts capacity at approximately 10,000 on-site spots and approximately 15,000 off-site.

### Rideshare: where the cars actually go

Rideshare is where people get frustrated. For Uber and Lyft, the stadium's general directions say drop-off and pickup are both at George M. Steinbrenner Field, not a random curb on Dale Mabry. Taxi, bus and limo staging is there too. The A-to-Z guide is less uniform: it describes the mass-transit turnaround by the pedestrian bridge as the designated drop-off and says pickup may be Steinbrenner Field for major events and the mass-transit turnaround for smaller ones. Concerts and heavier-volume nights can change the pickup spot, so follow the instructions for your specific event.

The event pages I looked at show how much this varies. A USF game listed rideshare at mass transit, a Buccaneers game listed Steinbrenner Field, and a concert listed it as TBD. Go by the event page, not memory.

### RVs and campers

RVs, buses and campers split by event. For Buccaneers games, use Publix Lot 14 with the entrance off MLK Blvd. For most other stadium events, use Lot 8 off Himes Ave. No overnight stays are allowed on stadium property, campers included. RV and camper passes are sold in advance for a majority of events, using the same lot split.

### Bikes, ADA parking and car trouble

Bicycle racks sit in front of the chain-link area by each dock, A through D, and the stadium says it is not responsible if a bike disappears. ADA parking cannot be bought ahead; you arrive early, first come, first served, and show a valid license and identification. If your car dies in a lot, call the stadium office at 813-350-6501, pop the hood, or find an officer at a lot entrance. The assistance named is gas, lockout and a dead battery.

### Decide to ride

At events that serve alcohol, the stadium runs a decide-to-ride program. Pledge as designated driver (21 or older, with a license) at a guest services booth and you get a free soft-drink coupon for permanent concession stands. The stadium says the same program can get you a discounted rideshare home. Details are at guest services.

## Tickets, bags, kids and the rules to know

### Mobile tickets only

Tickets to every event are on a phone only, and the stadium prefers Apple Wallet or Google Wallet with no screenshots. Each guest needs their own mobile ticket, and the A-to-Z guide suggests turning screen brightness all the way up. If a ticket will not load, the guide sends you to the ticket office.

### Where is the ticket office?

Here the stadium's own wording conflicts. The A-to-Z guide says the ticket office is in the South Plaza between the Suzuki Marine gate and the Fifth Third Bank gate, next to the stadium office, open on event days only. Some event pages instead say it is between Gates C and D. I cannot tell you whether those are the same door, so check the event page for your game before you walk the plaza.

### Bag policy

It is a no-bag policy for every event, with one exception: a clutch no larger than 4.5 by 6.5 inches. Lockers are on Tom McEwen Blvd south of the Suzuki Marine gate; the guide does not name the fee. Anything bigger goes back to the car.

### Kids and tickets

Kid rules differ by event, which trips people up:

- **Buccaneers and Gasparilla Bowl:** every age needs a ticket.
- **USF and ReliaQuest Bowl:** age 3 and under free if not taking a seat.
- **Monster Jam, Supercross and some concerts:** age 2 and under free if not taking a seat.

Always use the rule posted for the event you are attending.

### Alcohol

The limit is two alcoholic drinks per person per purchase, none brought in or out, with 21+ ID required. Sales cut-off timing differs by stand and quarter in the stadium's guide, so I would not plan around a precise last-call.

### Contacts and extras

- Stadium office, normal hours: 813-350-6500; event days: 813-350-6501
- Buccaneers tickets: 813-879-2827
- USF ticket operations: 813-974-3002, or 1-800-GO-BULLS
- Guest services text line: 813-680-2827
- Tours: 813-350-6553
- Wi-Fi network name: bucswifi

For anything time-sensitive, use the [official stadium site](https://www.raymondjamesstadium.com/) and the [USF Athletics site](https://gousfbulls.com/).

## Why people say James Stadium Tampa

When people drop the first name, they mean Raymond James Stadium. It is genuinely in Tampa, which already separates it from the Rays' ballpark in St. Petersburg. The stadium's guide says the Buccaneers became an NFL franchise in 1976, are in the NFC South, and were Super Bowl XXXVII champions for the 2002 season. It also says Raymond James is the official investment services and financial planning provider for the Buccaneers.

## Benchmark International Arena: the downtown arena people still call Amalie

The other building that gets called a stadium in Tampa is an arena. Benchmark International Arena, at 401 Channelside Drive, Tampa, FL 33602 (phone 813-301-6500), is home of the Tampa Bay Lightning, who the arena calls three-time Stanley Cup champions. Official features include lightning-throwing Tesla coils, an 11,000-square-foot Mich Ultra Sky Deck and a five-manual, 105-rank digital pipe organ.

The name is the confusing part. The Lightning announced on August 13, 2025, a multiyear naming-rights deal between Vinik Sports Group and Benchmark International, with the building moving on from its AMALIE Motor Oil name. The team calls Benchmark a Tampa-headquartered firm that set up its international headquarters in Tampa in 2010, says the premium club level gets renamed and the all-inclusive club experience becomes "The Mark," and says the agreement includes more than $3 million in nonprofit contributions. If your ticket says one name and a map pin says the other, trust the Channelside address. For the team itself, see our [Tampa Bay Lightning](/events) page, and check the [arena's official site](https://www.benchmarkintlarena.com/) for current event listings.

## Tropicana Field: not in Tampa

Searches for stadium Tampa Florida also pull in the Rays. The club gives its ballpark as Tropicana Field, 1 Tropicana Dr, St. Petersburg, FL 33705. Rays tickets are mobile only through the MLB Ballpark app. The club's site also mentions a new ballpark, which I did not look into, so I cannot tell you anything about a replacement stadium. For the team, see our [Tampa Bay Rays](/events) page and the [Rays site](https://www.mlb.com/rays). If a search for a "Tampa stadium" put you on a Rays page, that is the wrong city for football and Lightning plans.

## Tampa stadium FAQ

**Is there a separate USF stadium?**
No. USF athletics says the Bulls play at Raymond James Stadium, the same building as the Buccaneers. I never found a separate USF stadium address.

**What is the address of the Tampa football stadium?**
Raymond James Stadium is at 4201 N. Dale Mabry Hwy, Tampa, FL 33607.

**Where do Uber and Lyft drop off at Raymond James Stadium?**
The stadium's directions point to George M. Steinbrenner Field as the main rideshare staging area, though some events use the mass-transit turnaround. Check the instructions for your event.

**Can I bring a bag into Ray Jay?**
Only a clutch no larger than 4.5 by 6.5 inches. Lockers are available on Tom McEwen Blvd south of the Suzuki Marine gate.

**Is the Lightning's arena a stadium?**
No. Benchmark International Arena, formerly known as Amalie Arena, is a downtown arena on Channelside Drive.

## My take

When I lived downtown for six months, the phrase "the stadium" never meant just one place, and the same confusion catches visitors constantly. If the plan is Bucs, Bulls or a bowl, think Dale Mabry and check the rideshare pin. If it is the Lightning, think Channelside. If it is the Rays, think St. Petersburg. Match the team, then the city, then the lot, and read your specific event page before you leave.

For Single-A Yankees baseball, see the [Tampa Tarpons](/events/tampa-tarpons) guide.

title: Tampa to Fort Myers: 124 Miles Down I-75

metaDescription: FDOT lists Tampa to Fort Myers at 124 miles (125 reverse). Keep RSW and Fort Myers Beach separate, stay on I-75, and treat drive time as an estimate.
coverAlt: Aerial view of a coastal highway lined with palm trees beside turquoise water
coverCredit: Photo by Quang Viet Nguyen on Pexels
body:
# Tampa to Fort Myers: 124 Miles Down I-75

Tampa to Fort Myers is 124 miles by Florida's official count, and the entire drive runs on toll-free I-75. That is the short version. The longer version matters because people searching "tampa to fort myers" tend to mean one of three different places at the far end: the city, the airport, or the beach. Those are three different trips with three different mileage figures, and mixing them up is how you end up at the wrong exit.

This guide sorts them out, covers the route and the exits worth knowing, and flags the wrong turns (the Skyway fork near Ellenton and Alligator Alley past Naples) that catch drivers who follow the shield without checking the destination.

*Last updated: November 2, 2026*

![Aerial view of a coastal highway lined with palm trees beside turquoise water](/images/articles/tampa-to-fort-myers/gulf-highway-13267133.webp)
*Photo by [Quang Viet Nguyen](https://www.pexels.com/photo/aerial-view-of-highway-near-the-ocean-13267133/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/aerial-view-of-highway-near-the-ocean-13267133/)*

## The short answer

- **City to city:** FDOT lists Tampa to Fort Myers at 124 miles, and Fort Myers to Tampa at 125 miles.
- **Road:** I-75 the whole way. It is toll-free for its entire Florida length once you are north of Alligator Alley.
- **Drive time:** An OSRM routing estimate for downtown Tampa to downtown Fort Myers comes out around 125.6 miles and roughly 2.4 hours. Treat that as an estimate only. Traffic, construction, and your actual start and end points all move it.
- **Airport:** Southwest Florida International (RSW) uses I-75 exit 128.
- **Beach:** Fort Myers Beach uses I-75 exit 131 and then a string of surface roads.

If you want the wider picture of the city you are leaving, the [Tampa Florida overview](/guides/tampa-florida-overview) covers the basics, and the [Tampa map](/getting-around/tampa-map) helps you place downtown, the airport, and the I-75 bypass before you start driving.

## The miles: 124, 125, 126, 138 and 149

I kept running into five different numbers for this trip, so here is what each one actually is.

**FDOT's official intercity mileage** is the cleanest source. The spreadsheet was last updated 9/14/2026, it is in whole miles, and FDOT describes the figures as the shortest distances between city pairs, used for mileage reimbursements. For this pair:

- Tampa to Fort Myers: **124 miles**
- Fort Myers to Tampa: **125 miles**

I do not average those into 124.5. I also do not know why the direction changes the number. FDOT's table does the same thing on other pairs, sometimes by a mile and sometimes by more.

**A separate count** gave me about **126 miles** for Tampa, Florida to Fort Myers, Florida. That one comes from a different directions tool, so I keep it apart from FDOT's figures. A one- or two-mile gap between two counting methods is normal and not worth worrying about on a two-hour drive.

Then there are two numbers that are not the city at all:

- Tampa to RSW airport: about **138 miles**
- Tampa to Fort Myers Beach: about **149 miles**

FDOT does not measure either of those. They are different destinations, so they get different mileage. I am not blending 124, 125, 126, 138 and 149 into a single "the drive."

For FDOT's current table, check the [official intercity mileage page](https://www.fdot.gov/statistics/hwydata/intercity.shtm).

### Why you should not add up the in-between cities

It is tempting to build the total out of pieces. I did it once in my head with Punta Gorda: Punta Gorda to Tampa is 103 miles both ways, and Punta Gorda to Fort Myers is 24 both ways. Added together that gives 127, which is not 124 and not 125. FDOT's direct city-pair figure is the one to quote. The pieces are allowed to disagree with the total.

Other Gulf Coast pairs from the same FDOT table, for reference:

| Pair | FDOT miles |
|---|---|
| Tampa – Bradenton | 41 (reverse 40) |
| Tampa – Sarasota | 52 both ways |
| Tampa – Venice | 71 both ways |
| Tampa – Punta Gorda | 103 |
| Tampa – Naples | 164 (reverse 162) |
| Bradenton – Fort Myers | 86 |
| Sarasota – Fort Myers | 74 |
| Venice – Fort Myers | 53 |
| Punta Gorda – Fort Myers | 24 |
| Fort Myers – Naples | 37 |
| Clearwater – Fort Myers | 128 (reverse 129) |

Treat these as separate pairs, not building blocks for a Tampa total.

## The route: stay on I-75

Between Tampa and Fort Myers the road is I-75, and there is no toll to pay. Florida's I-75 is about 470.741 miles end to end, Miami Lakes to the Georgia line. After Alligator Alley, the interstate turns north near County Road 951 (exit 101, just east of Naples) and stays toll-free for the rest of its Florida length. Heading north from Fort Myers, the corridor passes Punta Gorda, Port Charlotte, Venice, Sarasota, and Bradenton before reaching the Tampa Bay area.

US 41, the Tamiami Trail, runs parallel through the towns along the Gulf side. South of Tampa it is the town-through route and I-75 is the eastern bypass. I do not have a separate FDOT mileage for a US 41-only trip, so I am not publishing a second Tampa-to-Fort Myers distance under that name. In practice you will touch US 41 anyway once you leave the interstate for Fort Myers Beach.

## Starting from Tampa: downtown versus the airport

The 124 miles are not measured from the airport terminal, and not from any particular hotel. Your first job is getting onto I-75.

I-75 is the eastern bypass around Tampa. Through the metro area it stays east of the bay through Brandon, Temple Terrace, and New Tampa. Downtown connections off the bypass are:

- **The Selmon Expressway (SR 618), exit 256**
- **I-4, exit 261**

If you are starting at Tampa International Airport, the airport says it sits just five miles west of downtown, at 4100 George J. Bean Parkway. Plan on that extra stretch before you reach the interstate. Check the [airport's own directions](https://www.tampaairport.com/) for the current approach roads.

## The wrong fork: I-275 and the Skyway

The mistake I would watch for is near Ellenton. I-275 splits off the I-75 corridor there (I-275 begins at I-75 exit 228 near Palmetto and runs about 60.237 miles). It heads toward St. Petersburg over the Sunshine Skyway, or toward Tampa over the Howard Frankland, while I-75 stays east of the bay.

If you are going Tampa to Fort Myers, you want I-75, not I-275. The Skyway is a roughly 4.1-mile bridge and it is tolled. Florida's Turnpike West Central Florida rate card, effective April 12, 2026, lists the Skyway at one plaza per direction (North Plaza southbound, South Plaza northbound): $1.16 with SunPass or $1.62 by toll-by-plate for a two-axle vehicle. That toll belongs to the Pinellas crossing. It is not on I-75 between Tampa and Fort Myers, so if you see it coming, you are on the wrong fork.

If St. Petersburg is actually where you are headed, see [Tampa to St. Petersburg](/guides/tampa-to-clearwater). For current toll amounts, check the [Florida's Turnpike toll rates page](https://floridasturnpike.com/tolls/toll-rates/) rather than relying on a number frozen in an article.

## The toll that is not on this trip: Alligator Alley

Alligator Alley is the tolled Everglades stretch of I-75, and it is east-west. It runs from exit 19 in Sunrise to exit 101 just east of Naples, about 75 miles. It has nothing to do with the north-south Tampa to Fort Myers drive.

I mention it because of how the signs read. If you are driving south and you stay on I-75 past Fort Myers because the shield still says south and you assume south means the city, you are aimed at Naples and then at the Alley toward Miami. A historical two-axle toll figure of $3.75 (as of July 1, 2023) is out there, but confirm the current rate on the Turnpike's card before quoting any live number.

Tampa to Miami is a different, longer trip: FDOT lists 250 miles Tampa to Miami and 248 Miami to Tampa. If that is your real destination, see [Tampa to Miami](/guides/tampa-to-miami). For Fort Myers, do not continue to exit 101.

## Three different endings: city, airport, beach

This is the part most distance pages skip. "Fort Myers" can mean three places, and each has its own exit.

### The city

Quote FDOT's 124 miles southbound and 125 northbound, and stay on I-75. Which exit you take depends on where in town you are going, so pin the actual address before you leave.

### The airport (RSW)

Southwest Florida International Airport is at 11000 Terminal Access Road, Fort Myers, FL 33913. It sits southeast of the city and roughly three miles east of I-75. Use **exit 128**, then Treeline Avenue. The roughly 138-mile Tampa-to-RSW figure is a separate count and is not FDOT's 124 or 125. FDOT has no airport figure. The airport's own site is the place for current terminal and access details: [Lee County Port Authority](https://www.flylcpa.com/).

### Fort Myers Beach

The beach is farther west, on a barrier island. I followed the Fort Myers Beach chamber's directions:

1. Take **I-75 exit 131** onto Daniels Parkway, heading west.
2. Turn left on Tamiami Trail (also called Cleveland Avenue and US 41), about a mile.
3. Turn right on Gladiolus Drive, about a mile.
4. Merge onto Summerlin Road toward the beach, about four miles.
5. Turn left on San Carlos Boulevard, and the beach is at the end.

From the airport, the chamber's sequence starts on Treeline Avenue to Daniels Parkway, then picks up the same US 41 and Summerlin steps.

I am not adding up those "about a mile" and "about four miles" pieces into a precise total. The chamber gave them as loose lengths inside a list of turns. The only full-trip beach figure I have is the roughly 149 miles from Tampa, and it stays labeled as a separate count.

### What about Cape Coral?

People often swap in Cape Coral. It is not among the cities FDOT measures, and neither is Fort Myers Beach. There is no Cape Coral pair on FDOT's city list to quote from that table. If Cape Coral is your destination, map it directly.

## The drive back: Fort Myers to Tampa

Going north, FDOT's figure is 125 miles. The road is the same I-75, and the toll situation is the same: none.

Where you aim at the Tampa end decides your exit:

- **Tampa International Airport:** Coming from the south side of the map, the airport's own directions say I-75 North to I-4 west, then I-275 south to exit 39.
- **Downtown Tampa:** Use the I-4 junction (exit 261) or the Selmon (SR 618, exit 256), not the airport exit.
- **Staying on I-75:** If you simply keep going north on the bypass, you skip both airport and downtown and end up out in Brandon.

## Drive time

I do not have a published drive time from FDOT, because FDOT gives miles. The OSRM routing model puts downtown Tampa to downtown Fort Myers at about 2.4 hours. That is an estimate. Real trips vary with traffic, construction, and whether your destination is the city, RSW, or the beach.

I-75 in Florida has a 70 mph speed limit, but I am not dividing 124 by 70 and calling it your drive time, and I have no construction update to share for the Sarasota or Charlotte County stretches. Check a live traffic map before you leave.

## What I would actually do

My Tampa stay ran six months, November 2025 through May 2026, downtown with my aunt and cousins, and the thing I kept coming back to was how many people ask this exact question with the wrong ending in mind. So here is how I would plan it:

- **City to city:** Quote 124 miles southbound and 125 northbound, and stay on I-75, not the Skyway.
- **Airport pin:** Get off at exit 128, and do not call that the 124.
- **Beach pin:** Get off at exit 131 and follow the chamber's US 41, Gladiolus, Summerlin, and San Carlos sequence. Quote 149 miles only as the separate beach count.
- **Miami is not on this trip:** Do not keep going to exit 101 and pay the Alligator Alley toll unless Miami is the real destination.

I never priced a hotel on this route, so I have no rate to quote for Fort Myers, Brandon, or anywhere along I-75.

## FAQ

**How far is Tampa from Fort Myers?**
FDOT lists 124 miles from Tampa to Fort Myers and 125 miles from Fort Myers to Tampa. A separate directions count showed about 126. These are city-to-city figures, not airport or beach figures.

**How long is the drive from Tampa to Fort Myers?**
An OSRM routing estimate for downtown to downtown is roughly 2.4 hours. Treat it as an estimate, since traffic, construction, and your exact start and end points change it.

**Are there tolls between Tampa and Fort Myers?**
Not on I-75. The interstate is toll-free for the rest of its Florida length once you are past Alligator Alley. The tolls people mention are the Sunshine Skyway, which is on the I-275 Pinellas fork, and Alligator Alley, which is east-west beyond Naples. Neither is on this drive.

**Which exit do I take for Fort Myers airport?**
I-75 exit 128, then Treeline Avenue. RSW is at 11000 Terminal Access Road, roughly three miles east of I-75.

**Which exit do I take for Fort Myers Beach?**
Exit 131 onto Daniels Parkway west, then the chamber's sequence of Tamiami Trail (US 41), Gladiolus Drive, Summerlin Road, and San Carlos Boulevard. The Tampa-to-beach figure of about 149 miles is a separate count from FDOT's city pair.

body:
# Tampa Population: City, County and Metro Numbers Explained

Ask for the Tampa population and you will get a handful of different numbers, and most of them are accurate. They just describe different boundaries. After spending time in the city, I went to the Census Bureau instead of repeating a number I had heard. Here is what the official figures say, which one answers your question, and where people mix them up.

![Aerial view of downtown Tampa skyline along the waterfront](/images/articles/tampa-population/tampa-skyline-38724264.webp)
*Photo by [Vinícius Gianelli Braido](https://www.pexels.com/photo/aerial-view-of-downtown-tampa-skyline-with-waterfront-38724264/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/aerial-view-of-downtown-tampa-skyline-with-waterfront-38724264/)*

## Quick answer: how many people live in Tampa?

The U.S. Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate for **Tampa city, Florida** is **413,554**. That is the municipality only. The wider **Tampa–St. Petersburg–Clearwater metropolitan area** had an estimated **3,418,895** residents on the same date. Both figures are real; they answer different questions.

If you are filling out a form, writing a report, or settling a trivia argument, ask which boundary you mean:

- **The city of Tampa:** 413,554 (July 1, 2025 estimate)
- **The Tampa–St. Petersburg–Clearwater metro:** 3,418,895 (July 1, 2025 estimate)

I would not round either one. Saying "about 400,000" for the city is not a figure the Census Bureau gives, and "3.4 million" hides which boundary you were talking about.

*Last updated: November 2, 2026*

## The city number: Tampa population 2025

The 413,554 figure comes from the Census Bureau's QuickFacts page for Tampa city, Florida, marked V2025. It is labeled as the city, not the county and not the metro. The Census Bureau's city and town population file for Florida lists the same Tampa estimate, so the two sources agree.

A note on the "V2025" label: it means the final year of the 2020–2025 estimates series. The Census Bureau says estimates from different vintage years are not comparable, so I would not set this figure next to an older estimate you remember from a different release.

### Growth since 2020 and 2010

The Census Bureau gives several reference points, and they are not interchangeable:

| Measure | Tampa city |
|---|---|
| Census count, April 1, 2010 | 335,709 |
| Census count, April 1, 2020 | 384,959 |
| Estimates base, April 1, 2020 (V2025 series) | 385,336 |
| Estimate, July 1, 2025 | 413,554 |

The bureau reports a **7.3 percent** change from the April 1, 2020 estimates base to July 1, 2025. The estimates base (385,336) and the 2020 census count (384,959) are two different things, and both appear on QuickFacts, so I have kept them separate here rather than folding one into the other.

### Land area and density

Tampa city covers **114.02 square miles** of land (2020). The Census Bureau's 2020 population density is **3,376.4 people per square mile**. For comparison, the 2010 figures were 113.41 square miles and 2,960.2 people per square mile.

Those density numbers belong to the census years. Dividing the 2025 estimate by the 2020 land area would produce a number, but it would not be a Census Bureau density figure, so I am not offering one.

## Who lives in Tampa

QuickFacts also breaks the city down by age, origin, and household. Some of these come from the American Community Survey's 2020–2024 five-year window rather than the July 1, 2025 headcount, so treat them as survey-based profiles.

**Age and sex**
- Under 18: 19.4%
- 65 and over: 13.7%
- Female: 49.8%

**Race and origin**
- White alone: 49.0%
- Black or African American alone: 20.4%
- Asian alone: 4.9%
- Two or more races: 19.9%
- White alone, not Hispanic or Latino: 44.3%
- Hispanic or Latino (any race): 26.2%
- Foreign-born persons, 2020–2024: 19.4%
- Language other than English spoken at home, age 5+: 28.3%

**Education and health**
- High school graduate or higher, age 25+: 90.2%
- Bachelor's degree or higher, age 25+: 45.7%
- Disability, under 65: 8.1%
- Without health insurance, under 65: 12.1%

**Work**
- Civilian labor force, age 16+: 66.1%
- Female civilian labor force: 62.3%
- Mean travel time to work: 24.8 minutes

**Households, income and housing (2020–2024)**
- Households: 166,278, at 2.31 persons per household
- Median household income (2024 dollars): $75,475
- Per capita income (2024 dollars): $52,528
- Persons in poverty: 15.5%
- Median gross rent: $1,701
- Median value of owner-occupied housing units: $420,400
- Owner-occupied housing unit rate: 50.3%
- Median selected monthly owner costs: $2,179 with a mortgage, $640 without

One thing QuickFacts leaves blank: housing units for July 1, 2025 are flagged "not applicable" (X) for the city, so there is no current housing-unit count to quote.

If you are weighing a move and want to see how these numbers translate into neighborhoods, our [Tampa Florida overview](/guides/tampa-florida-overview) is the place to start, and the [Tampa map guide](/getting-around) shows how the city sits within the surrounding area.

## The metro is a different boundary

The 3,418,895 figure is for the **Tampa–St. Petersburg–Clearwater, FL Metropolitan Statistical Area**. The Census Bureau's Population Division released these metro estimates in March 2026, and the 2020–2025 totals are published on the [Census Bureau's metro and micro area estimates page](https://www.census.gov/data/datasets/time-series/demo/popest/2020s-total-metro-and-micro-statistical-areas.html). The metro covers Hernando, Hillsborough, Pasco, and Pinellas counties, not just the city's 114.02 square miles.

### Metro growth, year by year

The metro's July 1 estimates in the same vintage:

| Year | Metro population |
|---|---|
| April 1, 2020 estimates base | 3,175,282 |
| 2020 | 3,187,831 |
| 2021 | 3,230,962 |
| 2022 | 3,307,164 |
| 2023 | 3,370,351 |
| 2024 | 3,405,357 |
| 2025 | 3,418,895 |

From July 1, 2024 to July 1, 2025 the metro added **13,538** people. That is noticeably slower than the gains in the early part of the series.

For the metro, the bureau's components of change for July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2025 break down this way: 31,956 births, 34,862 deaths (natural change of minus 2,906), net international migration of 18,413, net domestic migration of minus 1,539, and a residual of minus 430. In other words, migration from abroad did the heavy lifting for the metro that year, not a surplus of births. These components are for the metro only. I do not have them for the city, and they should not be applied to the 413,554 figure.

The St. Louis Fed's [FRED series for the metro](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/TMAPOP) reports the same 2025 figure, shown in thousands of persons. Don't read that as a second, competing population: it is the same estimate presented in a different unit.

### The divisions inside the metro

The Census Bureau follows metropolitan division delineations issued in July 2023. Two divisions make up this metro:

**Tampa, FL metropolitan division (July 1, 2025): 2,470,332**
- Hernando County: 221,701
- Hillsborough County: 1,574,115
- Pasco County: 674,516

Hillsborough County alone (1,574,115) is far above the city's 413,554, which is a good reminder that the county and the city are not the same place. The Census Bureau does not publish a figure for "the rest of the county," so I would not subtract one number from the other to invent it.

**St. Petersburg–Clearwater–Largo, FL division (Pinellas County)**
- July 1, 2025: 948,563
- July 1, 2024: 960,397
- April 1, 2020 base: 959,090

Pinellas County's 2025 estimate is lower than its 2024 estimate. The Census data I worked from does not say why, so I am not going to guess at a cause.

## Tampa, St. Petersburg and Clearwater side by side

The metro's name lists three cities, and people sometimes assume the metro population is just those three added up. The Census Bureau's side-by-side QuickFacts for the three cities (July 1, 2025 estimates) shows how far off that would be:

| | Tampa | St. Petersburg | Clearwater |
|---|---|---|---|
| July 1, 2025 estimate | 413,554 | 264,033 | 114,364 |
| April 1, 2020 estimates base | 385,336 | 258,358 | 117,343 |
| Change since 2020 base | +7.3% | +2.2% | −2.5% |
| April 1, 2020 census count | 384,959 | 258,308 | 117,292 |
| April 1, 2010 census count | 335,709 | 244,769 | 107,685 |
| Land area (2020, sq mi) | 114.02 | 61.82 | 26.08 |
| People per sq mi (2020) | 3,376.4 | 4,178.7 | 4,496.9 |
| Age 65 and over | 13.7% | 21.1% | 24.1% |
| Median household income (2024 dollars) | $75,475 | $75,192 | $66,381 |

Adding the three 2025 city estimates gives 791,951. That is my own arithmetic, not a census geography, and it is nowhere near the metro's 3,418,895. Most of the metro lives outside those three city limits.

Clearwater is worth a careful read. Its 2025 estimate is below its 2020 base, even though its 2010 census count was lower than its 2020 count. Those are different comparisons, and I would not blur them into a simple growth story. If you are comparing the two sides of the bay for a visit or a move, our guide to [getting from Tampa to St. Petersburg](/guides/tampa-to-clearwater) covers the practical side.

## Why different sources give different Tampa numbers

A few things explain the confusion:

1. **Boundary.** City, county, metropolitan division, and metro are four different geographies. Tampa the city is 413,554; Hillsborough County is 1,574,115; the metro is 3,418,895.
2. **Estimate versus count.** The April 1, 2020 census count (384,959) and the 2020 estimates base (385,336) are both official, and both differ from a July 1, 2025 estimate.
3. **Vintage.** The Census Bureau warns that different vintage years of estimates are not comparable.
4. **Survey versus headcount.** Income, rent, and demographic shares come from the 2020–2024 American Community Survey window, which is a sample, not a July 1, 2025 headcount.
5. **Units.** QuickFacts reports 2022 total retail sales of 11,377,387 in *thousands* of dollars, which is not eleven million dollars. Retail sales per capita ($28,563) is a separate figure in different units.

Tampa-area questions often travel in packs. If you landed here looking for a code or a place rather than a headcount, our [Tampa ZIP code guide](/guides/tampa-usa-zip-code) covers that side of things.

## FAQ

**What is the population of Tampa, Florida?**
The Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate for Tampa city is 413,554. The Tampa–St. Petersburg–Clearwater metro area is estimated at 3,418,895 for the same date.

**How much has Tampa grown since 2020?**
The Census Bureau reports a 7.3 percent change from the April 1, 2020 estimates base of 385,336 to the July 1, 2025 estimate of 413,554. The 2020 census count itself was 384,959.

**Is Tampa bigger than St. Petersburg?**
Yes. Tampa city's July 1, 2025 estimate is 413,554, compared with 264,033 for St. Petersburg city and 114,364 for Clearwater city.

**Does the Tampa population include St. Petersburg and Clearwater?**
Not the city figure. The metro figure of 3,418,895 does cover the wider area, including Pinellas County, where St. Petersburg and Clearwater sit.

**Where can I check the latest figures myself?**
The [Census Bureau's QuickFacts page for Tampa city](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/tampacityflorida/PST045225) is the source for the city numbers in this guide, and the bureau's [Florida city and town totals file](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/popest/datasets/2020-2025/cities/totals/sub-est2025_12.csv) lists the same estimate.

## The short version

If someone asks for the Tampa population, the answer depends on the boundary: **413,554 for the city, 3,418,895 for the metro**, both as of July 1, 2025. Name the date, name the geography, and call them estimates. That keeps you consistent with the Census Bureau and clear of the most common mix-up.

Mailing and phone layers sit beside the headcount — see [Tampa area code](/guides/tampa-area-code) when the search is dialing, not ZIP.

title: Tampa USA Zip Code: How to Write the Address Right
dek: Tampa has many ZIP codes, not one USA code. How USPS wants Tampa FL ##### on the last line, where the country goes, and why 33602 is only City Hall.

coverCredit: Photo by craveiro_ pics on Pexels
body:
# Tampa USA Zip Code: How to Write the Address Right

If you typed "tampa usa zip code" into a search box, you probably want one thing: a postal code for Tampa that a form will accept as American. I understand the impulse. In a lot of countries, that box holds a single code for a whole town, and the country is obvious because you are already standing in it. Tampa plus USA plus zip code is that habit pointed at Florida.

The honest answer is that it is not one number, and the words in that phrase are in an order the postal service does not use. This guide covers what a Tampa address looks like, where "USA" actually goes, why 33602 is not "the" Tampa code, and how to get the right ZIP for the street you mean. It is also a companion to my broader notes on [Hillsborough Tampa ZIP codes](/guides/zip-code-hillsborough-tampa-fl), which dig into the pile of five-digit codes and the county layer. This page is about a different mistake: the one where "USA" ends up in the middle of the line.

*Last updated: November 2, 2026*

![Scattered airmail envelopes and postcards with postage stamps](/images/articles/tampa-usa-zip-code/postal-mail-15873606.webp)
*Photo by [craveiro_ pics](https://www.pexels.com/photo/close-up-of-scattered-envelopes-with-postage-signs-15873606/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/close-up-of-scattered-envelopes-with-postage-signs-15873606/)*

## The short answer

- There is no single Tampa ZIP code. Tampa is a multi-ZIP 336xx area.
- The domestic last line is the city, the two-letter state abbreviation, then the ZIP or ZIP+4: **TAMPA FL #####**.
- "USA" is not part of that line. It belongs on its own bottom line, and only when the piece crosses a border.
- The ZIP belongs with the city and state, never on the country line.
- Phone codes (+1, 813) are not postal codes and never go in the postal field.

## Why "tampa usa zip code" scrambles the order

The phrase puts USA in the middle and the zip last, as if the country were an adjective attached to the code. On an envelope, the pieces sit differently. USPS's rule for the last line of a domestic address is short and strict: city name, two-letter state abbreviation, then ZIP or ZIP+4. The example form is TAMPA FL 33602, and the rule asks for at least one space between city, state, and ZIP+4, with two spaces preferred between the state abbreviation and the ZIP+4. The details are in [USPS Publication 28](https://pe.usps.com/text/pub28/pub28c2_009.htm).

The country is not in that line at all. For a domestic piece, the address elements run in this order: recipient, street (with any unit), city and state, ZIP. That is it.

## The address line USPS wants

Here is the shape for a Tampa address:

1. Recipient
2. Street address, with the unit if there is one
3. TAMPA FL and the ZIP (or ZIP+4)

A few details that trip people up:

**Punctuation can be dropped.** Except for the hyphen inside a ZIP+4, punctuation may be omitted in the delivery address block. Commas after the city are not required.

**Florida is "FL," and so is floor.** This is the mix-up I did not expect when I started reading the rules. On an American address, FL means Florida on the city line, and FL also appears in USPS's list of secondary unit abbreviations as the abbreviation for floor. Florida is the state abbreviation and goes on the city and state line. Floor is a unit designator and goes with the street line. Someone spelling out "Florida" because that is what Tampa's own letterhead does is not wrong about the place, only about the format USPS prefers. Someone who tucks the state's FL next to an apartment number has put the state in the wrong slot. I did both in my own notes before I slowed down.

**Street address plus PO Box.** If a piece carries both a street address and a PO Box, USPS delivers to the address immediately above the city and state line (or to the PO Box if both sit on the same line). The ZIP has to match whichever one is the delivery element.

## ZIP or ZIP+4

USPS says to use ZIP+4 when you know it and the five-digit ZIP when you do not. The ZIP+4 format is five digits, a hyphen, then four digits. The +4 should never be guessed. The City of Tampa lists City Hall at 306 East Jackson Street, Tampa, Florida 33602, with five digits and no extension, and that is all I saw on the buildings. A finished-looking line is not worth made-up digits. The extra four is for when you actually have it. The rules sit in [USPS DMM 602](https://pe.usps.com/teXt/dmm300/602.htm).

## Why there is no single Tampa ZIP code

This is where the "one code for the whole town" habit breaks. Tampa does not sit still for it, and the city's own materials show it.

City Hall is at 306 East Jackson Street, ZIP 33602. But the same city government publishes other addresses with different codes:

| Location | Address | ZIP |
|---|---|---|
| Courtney Campbell beach | 7740 W Courtney Campbell Causeway | 33607 |
| Cypress Point | 5620 W Cypress St | 33607 |
| Davis Islands seaplane basin | 864 Severn Ave | 33606 |
| Picnic Island | 7409 Picnic Island Blvd | 33616 |
| Parks office | 3402 W Columbus Dr | 33607 |

That is multiple codes from a single city government, and the City of Tampa's [homepage](https://www.tampa.gov/) is the place to confirm its main contact address. If a friend abroad asks for "the Tampa zip code" and you hand them 33602, you have handed them City Hall. It will not sort a letter meant for the beach on Courtney Campbell.

USPS facilities tell the same story. Under the Tampa city name alone, USPS facility listings show different codes:

- Commerce, 401 N Ashley St: 33602
- Carrollwood, 12651 N Dale Mabry Hwy: 33618
- Forest Hills, 11800 N Florida Ave: 33612
- Hilldale, 3201 W Hillsborough Ave: 33614
- Interbay, 4520 W Oakellar Ave: 33611
- CFS, 6013 Benjamin Rd: 33634

Those come from the [USPS Florida facility list](https://about.usps.com/newsroom/local-releases/fl/2022/0929-usps-resumes-operations-in-central-and-southwest-florida.htm). At the sorting level, USPS's labeling list shows the three-digit destination 336 labeled TAMPA FL 336, which confirms that Tampa is a 336xx area rather than a single code. For the broader picture of where those codes fall, my [Tampa map guide](/getting-around) helps.

One more wrinkle: a "Tampa" mailing city on a piece is a USPS last-line name. It is not proof that the parcel sits inside Tampa city limits. The mailing city and the municipal boundary are different questions, and I cover that split in the [Tampa Florida overview](/guides/tampa-florida-overview).

## Where USA goes (international mail)

The word USA is doing real work in your search, because it is what someone says when they are outside the country or filling in a form built for another country's postal code. So here is where it lands.

For international mail, the bottom line of the address shows only the country name, written in full with no abbreviations, preferably in capital letters. Do not place the postal code on that last line. The ZIP stays with the city and state above it. So a piece headed to Tampa from abroad reads:

- Recipient
- Street address
- TAMPA FL 33602 (or the ZIP that belongs to the street)
- UNITED STATES

I used to write the city, state, ZIP and country as one smear on a single line. USPS wants the country on its own line and the code up with the city and the state. Many countries print the postal code before the city, but the American shape is city, state abbreviation, ZIP, and then the country alone underneath. The guidance lives in [USPS international addressing standards](https://pe.usps.com/text/pub28/pub28c2_001.htm).

## A rule worth knowing: foreign return addresses

USPS changed a rule effective December 14, 2023: domestic shipments with a foreign return address are no longer accepted, and undeliverable pieces with foreign returns go to dead mail. A foreign return address belongs on international mail with customs forms. If you send a package to a Tampa street through domestic mail with your home address abroad in the corner, it will not come back to you when the street or ZIP is wrong. And the ZIP will be wrong if the only code used was a one-size "Tampa USA zip code" that did not belong to that street.

## Phone codes are not ZIP codes

Another common mix-up: the +1 and the 813. The +1 is the country calling code. The 813 is a local phone area code (Tampa also has 656). The City of Tampa's main line is (813) 274-8211. None of these is a ZIP, and none belongs in the postal field. For more on the phone side, see my [Tampa area code guide](/guides/tampa-area-code).

## The reliable way to get the right ZIP

Do not guess a citywide code. USPS provides ZIP Code lookup and address tools that return the matching ZIP or ZIP+4 from a street, city, and state. The [USPS Address Information API overview](https://www.usps.com/business/web-tools-apis/address-information-api.htm) describes the product, and the same lookup logic is what you want if you are filling in a form. Start with the street you actually mean, then let the lookup hand back the code that belongs to it.

## What I would write if I were the one writing from outside

I would write the street I actually mean. Then a line with Tampa, then FL, then the five digits that belong to that street, with the two spaces USPS prefers if I am being fussy. If the piece is coming from outside the country, the last line is the country alone, written out and not abbreviated, with no ZIP repeated on it. I would not put the code in front of Tampa. I would not put USA between the city and the code. I would not use 33602 unless the building is the one on Jackson Street. And I would not put +1 or 813 in the postal box.

The question sounds like it should get a number with a flag on it. What it should get is an order of lines. I went looking for a code during my six months in Tampa and got handed a sequence instead.

## FAQ

**What is the ZIP code for Tampa, USA?**
There is no single one. Tampa is a multi-ZIP 336xx area. City Hall at 306 East Jackson Street is 33602, but other Tampa addresses carry 33606, 33607, 33616, and more. Use the ZIP that matches the street.

**Where does "USA" go in a Tampa address?**
Only on international mail, and only on its own bottom line, written as the country name alone. It never sits between the city and the ZIP.

**Should I write Florida or FL?**
USPS prefers the two-letter abbreviation FL on the last line. The City of Tampa spells Florida out on its letterhead, which is fine for a letterhead but not the format USPS asks for on a mailpiece.

**Do I need the ZIP+4?**
Use it if you know it. Otherwise the five-digit ZIP is fine. Do not make up the last four digits.

**Is 813 a ZIP code?**
No. 813 is a phone area code, and +1 is the country calling code. Neither goes in the postal field.

## Related reading

For the pile of five-digit codes and the county layer, see [Hillsborough Tampa ZIP codes](/guides/zip-code-hillsborough-tampa-fl). For a general orientation, start with the [Tampa Florida overview](/guides/tampa-florida-overview) and the [Tampa map](/getting-around/tampa-map).

For dialing, see the companion [Tampa area code](/guides/tampa-area-code) guide (813/656 overlay).
