body:
# Tampa Riverwalk Hotels: Which Ones Touch the Path

Search for tampa riverwalk hotels, hotels riverwalk Tampa, riverwalk Tampa hotels, or the shorter hotel riverwalk Tampa, and it sounds like everyone means one building. They don't. One hotel carries the name. A handful describe themselves as along the path, steps from it, or with direct access. And several places get lumped in that never claim any of that.

This guide sorts them by what each property says about itself, with addresses and phone numbers so you can match a reservation to the right door. One caveat up front: I never got a nightly rate from any of these hotels, so there are no room prices here. Where a fee is published, I give it. Everything else, confirm when you book.

*Last updated: November 2, 2026*

![Downtown Tampa waterfront with modern buildings along the bay](/images/articles/tampa-riverwalk-hotels/riverwalk-hotels-12104693.webp)
*Photo by [Nathan Rostampour](https://www.pexels.com/photo/sign-in-bay-12104693/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/sign-in-bay-12104693/)*

## What people mean by Tampa Riverwalk hotels

Three different things hide inside the phrase:

1. **A hotel with direct access to the path.** The claim is that you walk out a door and you're on the Riverwalk.
2. **A hotel "along" or "steps from" the path.** Close, and described that way by the hotel or by Marriott, Hilton, or Friends of the Riverwalk, but the wording is softer.
3. **A hotel that uses the Riverwalk in its name or marketing** without saying the building is on the path.

I sorted by what each property says in its own words, because the gap between "direct access," "steps away," and "near" is the whole point. For the path itself, see my guide to the [Tampa Riverwalk](/guides/tampa-riverwalk-hotels), and for a wider look at where to stay, see [Tampa hotels](/guides/tampa-hotels).

## Hotel Tampa Riverwalk: direct access

Friends of the Riverwalk groups its hotels under "stays along the Riverwalk," and Hotel Tampa Riverwalk makes the plainest claim of the bunch: along the Hillsborough River with direct access to the path. If you want the one building that matches the name, this is it.

- **Address:** 200 North Ashley Drive, Tampa, FL 33602
- **Phone:** (813) 223-2222; reservations (813) 761-3201
- **Check-in / check-out:** 4:00 p.m. / 11:00 a.m.
- **Rooms:** the site's own schema describes 275 oversized rooms. Confirm that against the property's materials before you rely on it.
- **Distance:** City of Tampa materials put it about 0.8 miles from the convention center.

**Renovation warning.** The hotel's FAQ says renovations run through November 30, 2026, with work happening 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. During that period the pool and all food and beverage outlets are closed, though the fitness center stays open 24/7. If you're booking before the end of November, that matters a lot: the restaurant and lounge that the hotel normally advertises are not available. Check the [hotel's official FAQ](https://www.hoteltampariverwalk.com/faq) for the current status.

Direct access is the claim, and I'd still ask which door meets the path when you call.

## Steps from the path: Marriott, JW and Embassy Suites

These are the big downtown properties near the convention center, and the Riverwalk wording varies by hotel.

### Tampa Marriott Water Street

Per Visit Tampa Bay, this one is waterfront, adjacent to the convention center, and just steps from the Riverwalk, the aquarium, the arena, and Sparkman Wharf. The amenities include a Riverwalk Terrace, and Marriott describes it as having a private Riverwalk terrace. I count it as a Riverwalk hotel.

- **Address:** 505 Water Street, Tampa, FL 33602
- **Phone:** +1 813-221-4900
- **Check-in / check-out:** 4:00 p.m. / 11:00 a.m.
- **Destination fee:** listed at $20 per night on Marriott's rooms page. Confirm when booking.

The published room counts disagree. Visit Tampa Bay's sleeping-room figure is 727 (with 28 suites and 27 floors), the meeting figures say 719, and Friends of the Riverwalk says 717. That affects how big the hotel feels, not whether it's near the path. I cover the details in my full guide to the [Tampa Marriott Water Street](/guides/marriott-water-street-tampa), so I won't repeat every fee and amenity here. See Marriott's [official overview](https://www.marriott.com/en-us/hotels/tpamc-tampa-marriott-water-street/overview/) for current information.

### JW Marriott Tampa Water Street

This is the other half of the pair, joined to the Marriott by a glass skybridge.

- **Address:** 510 Water Street, Tampa, FL 33602
- **Phone:** +1 813-221-4950
- **Check-in / check-out:** 4:00 p.m. / 11:00 a.m.
- **Valet:** $55 daily, as published by the hotel
- **Pets:** not allowed
- **Rooms:** about 519 rooms and suites; Marriott's combined figure for the two hotels is 1,246

Friends of the Riverwalk lists the JW without mentioning the Riverwalk at all. Marriott does mention it, describing both hotels as having the Riverwalk at the doorstep. I count the JW only because Marriott puts the path at both doorsteps. Details are on Marriott's [JW overview page](https://www.marriott.com/en-us/hotels/tpajd-jw-marriott-tampa-water-street/overview/).

### Embassy Suites by Hilton Tampa Downtown Convention Center

Hilton describes this one as located along Tampa's Riverwalk, steps from the arena, Sparkman Wharf, and the aquarium, with a skybridge to the convention center. I'm going with the "along" wording the hotel itself uses. Friends of the Riverwalk doesn't list it, and the city includes it without repeating the Riverwalk line.

- **Address:** 513 South Florida Avenue, Tampa, FL 33602
- **Phone:** +1 813-769-8300
- **Check-in / check-out:** 4 p.m. / 11 a.m.
- **Rooms:** all suites, 360 of them
- **Extras:** free cooked-to-order breakfast and an evening reception, per my notes

See the [Hilton page](https://www.hilton.com/en/hotels/tpaeses-embassy-suites-tampa-downtown-convention-center/) for current details.

## Near the path, but not on it: The Barrymore

The Barrymore Hotel Tampa Riverwalk has the words in the name, which is exactly why it lands in these searches. Friends of the Riverwalk says "near the Riverwalk" with river views, next to the Straz. The hotel itself says its pool deck overlooks the Hillsborough River and names the convention center, the arena, and Curtis Hixon as nearby. It never says the building sits on the path. Near is not beside.

- **Address:** 111 West Fortune Street, Tampa, FL 33602
- **Phone:** (813) 223-1351
- **Check-in / check-out:** 3:00 p.m. / 11:00 a.m.
- **Pool:** sunrise to sunset, no lifeguard
- **Shuttle:** 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. within 2 miles; it does not go to the airport
- **Parking and pets:** self-parking is $20 a night and the pet fee is $75 per stay in my notes. Confirm both at booking.
- **Distance:** the city puts it 1.4 miles from the convention center

I don't count it as a Riverwalk hotel, but it's a practical choice if you want a downtown base with a shuttle. Booking is on the [hotel's site](https://www.barrymorehotel.com/).

## On or near the Riverwalk: Westin, EDITION, Hilton, Hyatt, Aloft

These were held out of the first draft only because open/closed status hadn’t been re-checked against official sites. As of November 2, 2026, each has a live brand page. They’re near the path or the Riverfront / Water Street waterfront — not always “direct access.”

### Westin Tampa Downtown Waterside

Marriott’s [Westin Tampa Downtown Waterside](https://www.marriott.com/en-us/hotels/tpawh-westin-tampa-downtown-waterside/overview/) page is live at **725 South Harbour Island Boulevard, Tampa, FL 33602**, phone +1 813-229-5000. Check-in 4:00 p.m.; check-out 12:00 p.m. Harbour Island waterfront; Marriott copy places it near the Florida Aquarium, Sparkman Wharf, arena, Riverwalk, and convention center. Full stay details are in our [Westin Tampa Waterside guide](/guides/the-westin-tampa-waterside).

### The Tampa EDITION

Marriott’s [Tampa EDITION overview](https://www.marriott.com/en-us/hotels/tpaeb-the-tampa-edition/overview/) is live at **500 Channelside Drive, Tampa, FL 33602**, phone +1 813-221-4600. Water Street district; Marriott notes walking access toward the Riverwalk and arena. Room counts on brand materials: 172 rooms and 30 suites. See our [Tampa EDITION guide](/guides/the-tampa-edition).

### Hilton Tampa Downtown

The former Hyatt Regency Tampa is now **Hilton Tampa Downtown**. Hilton’s page lists the hotel as steps from the Riverwalk; [Friends of the Riverwalk](https://thetampariverwalk.com/visit/hotels.html) says two blocks. Confirm the door with a map before you roll a suitcase. Address commonly listed as 211 North Tampa Street — verify on Hilton’s booking page when you reserve.

### Hyatt Place + Hyatt House Tampa Downtown

Friends of the Riverwalk lists both. They share **325 N. Florida Avenue, Tampa, FL 33602**, phone (813) 616-1234, with a combined Hyatt Place / Hyatt House building (property site [hphhtampa.com](https://hphhtampa.com/)). Friends describes each as steps from the arena and Riverwalk. There is no current Hyatt Regency on this corridor — that name moved to Hilton years ago.

### Aloft Tampa Downtown

Marriott’s [Aloft Tampa Downtown](https://www.marriott.com/en-us/hotels/tpatl-aloft-tampa-downtown/overview/) is live at **100 West Kennedy Boulevard, Tampa, FL 33602**, phone +1 813-898-8000. Brand copy markets easy Riverwalk access; that is access, not a door on the path. Check-in 4:00 p.m.; check-out 11:00 a.m.

### Still not a hotel night

**AVE Tampa Riverwalk** calls itself steps from the path, but it’s furnished apartments for 30 days or more, plus longer leases — not a Saturday-night hotel stay.

## The address problem: match the phone, not the pin

The other mess is the curb. City of Tampa materials have historically listed the Marriott at 700 S. Florida Avenue, while the hotel's own address is 505 Water Street. The JW is sometimes mixed up with 505, though it's 510 Water Street. Visit Tampa Bay's meeting description still calls the Marriott "Tampa Marriott Waterside Hotel & Marina."

I'm not ruling on whether those addresses are one building. What I'd do is match the reservation phone number to the hotel before following a map pin: 813-221-4900 for the Marriott, 813-221-4950 for the JW. A pin on the wrong address is how you miss the Riverwalk door. Use my [Tampa map](/getting-around/tampa-map) to see how these hotels sit relative to each other and the convention center.

## Quick comparison

| Hotel | Riverwalk wording | Address | Phone |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hotel Tampa Riverwalk | Direct access | 200 N. Ashley Dr. | (813) 223-2222 |
| Tampa Marriott Water Street | Steps away; Riverwalk terrace | 505 Water St. | 813-221-4900 |
| JW Marriott Tampa Water Street | Doorstep (Marriott's wording) | 510 Water St. | 813-221-4950 |
| Embassy Suites Downtown Convention Center | Along the Riverwalk | 513 S. Florida Ave. | 813-769-8300 |
| Westin Tampa Downtown Waterside | Near Riverwalk / Riverfront | 725 S. Harbour Island Blvd. | 813-229-5000 |
| The Tampa EDITION | Water Street; walk toward Riverwalk | 500 Channelside Dr. | 813-221-4600 |
| Hilton Tampa Downtown | Steps / two blocks (sources differ) | 211 N. Tampa St. (confirm) | Hilton booking page |
| Hyatt Place / Hyatt House | Steps (Friends of the Riverwalk) | 325 N. Florida Ave. | (813) 616-1234 |
| Aloft Tampa Downtown | Easy access (not on-path) | 100 W. Kennedy Blvd. | 813-898-8000 |
| The Barrymore | Near, not beside | 111 W. Fortune St. | (813) 223-1351 |

## Planning notes

- **Don't budget for valet blindly.** Most of these hotels don't publish a price. The JW is the exception at $55 daily; confirm everything else.
- **Check renovation dates.** Hotel Tampa Riverwalk's pool and food and beverage are closed through November 30, 2026.
- **Ask about the door.** "Direct access" and "steps away" are different promises. Ask which entrance meets the path.
- **Confirm fees at booking.** The Marriott's destination fee, the Barrymore's parking and pet fees, and valet charges can change.

## FAQ

**Is there really a hotel called Hotel Tampa Riverwalk?**
Yes. Hotel Tampa Riverwalk is at 200 North Ashley Drive and claims direct access to the path. It is the one building that carries the name.

**Which Tampa Riverwalk hotel is closest to the convention center?**
The Marriott and JW are adjacent, joined to the convention center area per Visit Tampa Bay, and Embassy Suites has a skybridge to the convention center. Hotel Tampa Riverwalk is about 0.8 miles away, per City of Tampa materials.

**Is The Barrymore on the Riverwalk?**
No. It sits near the Riverwalk with river views, but the hotel doesn't say it's on the path. The city puts it 1.4 miles from the convention center.

**Does Hotel Tampa Riverwalk have a pool and restaurant right now?**
Not through November 30, 2026. The pool and all food and beverage are closed during renovations, while the fitness center stays open 24/7.

**Why do the Marriott's room counts differ?**
Published sources give different figures: 727, 719, and 717. The size differs by source, but the Riverwalk location doesn't change.

For a broader look at lodging, see my guide to [Tampa hotels](/guides/tampa-hotels).

body:
# Trampoline Parks Tampa: Altitude, Sky Zone and Urban Air

When people search for trampoline parks in Tampa, they usually expect a list. Three parks in the Tampa area have live official sites with ticketing as of November 2, 2026: **Altitude Tampa** on West Hillsborough Avenue, **Sky Zone Tampa** on East Adamo Drive, and **Urban Air Adventure Park** in New Tampa. This guide covers those three, then flags near-miss parks in other cities so you don’t pin the wrong door. For the Hillsborough Avenue building in more depth, see also [trampoline park Tampa Hillsborough](/events/trampoline-park-tampa-hillsborough).

*Last updated: November 2, 2026.*

![Athlete flipping on an indoor trampoline in a gym](/images/articles/trampoline-parks-tampa/trampoline-park-6572557.webp)
*Photo by [Tima Miroshnichenko](https://www.pexels.com/photo/people-sport-motion-young-6572557/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/people-sport-motion-young-6572557/)*

## The short answer

| Park | Address | Phone | Official site |
|---|---|---|---|
| Altitude Tampa (Drew Park) | 4340 W Hillsborough Ave, Tampa, FL 33614 | (813) 399-1529 | [Altitude Tampa](https://www.altitudetrampolinepark.com/locations/florida/tampa/4340-west-hillsborough-ave/) |
| Sky Zone Tampa | 10137 E Adamo Dr, Ste 800B, Tampa, FL 33619 | (813) 833-1740 | [Sky Zone Tampa](https://www.skyzone.com/tampa/) |
| Urban Air New Tampa | 6250 Commerce Palms Dr, Tampa, FL 33647 | (813) 522-5401 | [Urban Air New Tampa](https://www.urbanair.com/florida-new-tampa/) |

Before any visit: sign the waiver, confirm hours on that park’s own calendar, and don’t invent a jump price from an old promo.

## Altitude Tampa, Drew Park

Drew Park is the neighborhood label in the park’s name. It is not a second building. Altitude’s official Tampa location page lists **4340 West Hillsborough Avenue, Tampa, Florida 33614**. In another spot the company writes Suite 350. The street and ZIP match; put Suite 350 in the map pin and still look for the door.

Altitude also lists a second phone, (813) 503-4428, without a label, plus email chesley@altitudetampa.com. For questions, start with **(813) 399-1529**.

### Hours: confirm before you drive

Hours Altitude has posted for Tampa (treat as published, not holiday-proof):

| Day | Posted hours |
|---|---|
| Sunday | 11:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. |
| Monday–Thursday | 10:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. |
| Friday | 10:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. |
| Saturday | 9:30 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. |

Third-party listings sometimes show earlier closes. Check the official [hours and calendar page](https://www.altitudetrampolinepark.com/locations/tampa/hours-calendar) the day you go. If the door disagrees with the website, the door wins.

### What’s inside

Altitude’s Tampa attraction list names Basketball Trampoline Dunk, Battle Beam, Extreme Dodgeball, Kid’s Court, Main Court, Performance Trampoline, Trapeze, Tumble Track, and ZipLine. Programs named for this location include Birthday Party On, Glo in the Park, Jump Happy Hour, and Junior Jumpers Jam. Brand galleries sometimes show equipment from other cities — only plan around what Tampa lists.

### Booking, waivers, socks, prices

Open jump books through [CenterEdge](https://altitudetampa.centeredgeonline.com/). Waivers and a short safety video are required. Safety socks are required but not included. Online redemption needs the paying card and matching ID.

I’m not printing a jump price as guaranteed — posted figures mix promos and dated sales. Check the booking page or call before promising a kid a dollar amount. Party deposits and full-park buyouts vary; ask whether Tampa participates in “book the park.”

## Sky Zone Tampa

Sky Zone’s [official Tampa page](https://www.skyzone.com/tampa/) is live with ticket CTAs. Address: **10137 E Adamo Dr, Suite 800B, Tampa, FL 33619**. Phone **(813) 833-1740**. Schema hours on the official page (confirm before you go): Mon–Thu 11:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.; Fri 10:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m.; Sat 9:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m.; Sun 10:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.

Attractions named for this park include Freestyle Jump, SkySlam, Ultimate Dodgeball, Foam Zone, Speed Zone, Boulder Balls, Sky Tower, FreeClimb, Ninja Warrior Course, Parkour Blox, Air Court, and iWall. Book tickets and parties on the Sky Zone site; don’t invent walk-up prices here.

## Urban Air New Tampa

Urban Air’s [New Tampa page](https://www.urbanair.com/florida-new-tampa/) is live with hours and contact. Address: **6250 Commerce Palms Drive, Tampa, FL 33647**. Phone **(813) 522-5401**. Regular open-play hours published there: Mon–Thu 4:00 p.m.–8:00 p.m.; Fri 4:00 p.m.–10:00 p.m.; Sat 10:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m.; Sun 11:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. Holiday and school-break hours change — the page posts those separately (for example, closed Thanksgiving Day on the calendar I saw).

Urban Air is a broader adventure park (trampolines plus other attractions). Confirm height rules and which attractions are open the day you visit. There is also an Urban Air in **Brandon** (179 E Bloomingdale Ave) — useful if you’re on that side of town, but it is not a Tampa city address.

## Parks that are not Tampa

A map app will happily label a park “near Tampa” when it’s another city:

- **Altitude Bradenton:** 201 Cortez Road West, Bradenton, FL 34207 — different attraction list.
- **Altitude Spring Hill:** 11162 Spring Hill Drive, Spring Hill, FL 34609.
- **Get Air New Port Richey:** 7431 SR 54, New Port Richey, FL 34653, (727) 347-7701 — Pasco County, not Tampa.

Altitude’s Florida city list files Tampa once. Don’t drive to Bradenton or Spring Hill expecting a Tampa sign.

## Same searches, different pins

“Trampoline park Tampa Hillsborough,” “Altitude Tampa,” and “Hillsborough Ave trampoline” all mean the Drew Park Altitude building. “Sky Zone Tampa” and “Urban Air New Tampa” are separate pins on the east and north sides of town. For the rest of a Tampa weekend, see [Tampa attractions](/things-to-do/tampa-attractions) and [Tampa events](/events/tampa-events). The [Tampa map](/getting-around/tampa-map) helps place Hillsborough Ave, Adamo, and New Tampa relative to downtown.

## Tips

1. Do the waiver at home.
2. Bring required socks (Altitude) / follow each brand’s gear rules.
3. Confirm hours the same day — holiday calendars move.
4. Call or book online before quoting a price to a kid.
5. Match the brand name to the address so you don’t end up in Bradenton.

## FAQ

**How many trampoline parks are in Tampa?**
Three with confirmed-open official sites in this guide: Altitude Tampa, Sky Zone Tampa, and Urban Air New Tampa. Other brands nearby sit in Bradenton, Spring Hill, New Port Richey, or Brandon.

**Where is Altitude Tampa?**
4340 West Hillsborough Avenue, Tampa, FL 33614 (sometimes listed with Suite 350).

**Where is Sky Zone Tampa?**
10137 E Adamo Drive, Suite 800B, Tampa, FL 33619.

**Where is Urban Air New Tampa?**
6250 Commerce Palms Drive, Tampa, FL 33647.

**Do I need a waiver?**
Yes at these parks. Complete it online before you arrive when the brand offers that.

body:
# Tampa RV Show: Florida RV SuperShow and Fall Show Dates

People search tampa rv show, rv show tampa, and tampa florida rv show as if there were one weekend. There are two. Both use the Florida State Fairgrounds. The big one is the Florida RV SuperShow every January. The smaller one is the Tampa Bay Fall RV Show in November. Prices, hours, and which weekend is still sellable all change with the year — so this page leads with the next SuperShow on the books, then the fall show.

*Last updated: November 2, 2026*

![Aerial view of an RV park with rows of recreational vehicles](/images/articles/tampa-rv-show/rv-show-34287640.webp)
*Photo by [Viktoria B.](https://www.pexels.com/photo/aerial-view-of-rv-park-with-modern-amenities-34287640/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/aerial-view-of-rv-park-with-modern-amenities-34287640/)*

## Next Florida RV SuperShow (January 2027)

The Florida RV Trade Association already lists the **2027 Florida RV SuperShow** on its [official SuperShow page](https://www.frvta.org/show/florida-rv-supershow/):

- **Industry Day:** Tuesday, January 12, 2027 (RV industry credentials and ID required; not a public day)
- **Public days:** January 13–17, 2027
- **Hours:** Wednesday, January 13 – Saturday, January 16, 9:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m.; Sunday, January 17, 9:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m.
- **Location:** Florida State Fairgrounds, 4800 US Highway 301 North, Tampa, FL 33610
- **Admission:** Adults $15.00 per person (2-day pass); children under 16 free. Pre-sale tickets listed as available mid-December
- **Discounts:** Wednesday–Friday Senior Citizen’s Day, $2 off; First Responders & Military $2 off every day (not valid with other discounts)
- **Parking (fairgrounds):** cars $12 onsite / $10 online presale (presale marked coming soon on the page); RVs $20. Contact 813-621-7821 or info@FloridaStateFair.com for parking questions

FRVTA lists **2026 attendance at 70,635** on that same page — a prior-year figure, not a 2027 forecast. Mild-tempered dogs on a leash are welcome; clean up after them. Confirm hours, tickets, and parking on the official page before you travel, because organizer details update.

Enter the SuperShow via **MLK Jr Blvd or US Hwy 301** when those instructions are active on the fairgrounds listing.

## Tampa Bay Fall RV Show

The fall show is the cheaper, shorter weekend at the same fairgrounds. Per FRVTA’s [Tampa Bay Fall RV Show page](https://www.frvta.org/show/tampa-bay-fall-rv-show/) (checked November 2, 2026):

- **Dates:** November 5–8, 2026
- **Hours:** 9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. Thursday–Saturday; 9:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m. Sunday
- **Admission:** Adults $5.00; children 16 and under free. $1 offline before the show; at the gate, seniors $1 off Thursday only; Military / 1st Responders $1 off all days (discounts not valid with other discounts)
- **Parking:** cars $12 onsite / $10 online; RVs $20 onsite / $18 online
- **Published dealers:** Blue Compass RV; General RV Center; Lazydays powered by Campers Inn; North Trail RV
- **Pets:** welcome on a leash or in a carrier; clean up after them
- **Prior-year attendance:** 5,403 in 2025 (not a 2026 forecast)

November 5, 2026 is a Thursday, so the Thursday–Sunday clock matches. Re-check the FRVTA page the week of the show for dealer or parking updates. The fall listing does not spell out a numbered gate the way SuperShow materials sometimes do — use the street address and fairgrounds signs.

## How to Tell the Shows Apart

| | Florida RV SuperShow | Tampa Bay Fall RV Show |
|---|---|---|
| Typical month | January | November |
| Next dates on the books | Jan 13–17, 2027 (public) | Nov 5–8, 2026 |
| Adult admission | $15 (2-day pass) | $5 |
| Children | Under 16 free | 16 and under free |
| Scale | Large manufacturer show; 2026 attendance 70,635 | Smaller; four published dealers for 2026 |

A **$15 / 2-day pass** search result is almost always the SuperShow. A **$5** ticket is the fall show. Both say “Tampa” and both sit at 4800 US Highway 301 North.

## The 2026 SuperShow (already over)

For anyone still holding an old January bookmark: the **2026 Florida RV SuperShow ran January 14–18, 2026** and is finished. Fairgrounds materials for that edition used the same 9:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. Wed–Sat / 9:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m. Sunday pattern, $15 adult 2-day admission, and $10/$12 car parking. Do not treat those January 2026 dates as still open.

## Getting to the Right Gate

The fairgrounds are large enough that “the fairgrounds” is not a door. The same property includes the MidFlorida Amphitheater, Bob Thomas Equestrian Center, TECO Arena gate, Cracker Country, Expo and Entertainment Halls, the Florida Center, and the Special Events Center. You can be at the right address and still be at the wrong entrance.

FRVTA’s office is **not** the show gate: 5407 Boran Place, Tampa, FL 33610, phone (813) 741-0488.

For orientation around town, see the [Tampa map](/getting-around/tampa-map) and the [Tampa Florida overview](/guides/tampa-florida-overview). Nearby lodging options are in [Tampa hotels](/guides/tampa-hotels). Other calendar noise (concerts, casino ads, stadium games) is not the RV aisle — check [Tampa events](/events/tampa-events) for those.

## FAQ

**When is the next Tampa RV SuperShow?**
Public days are January 13–17, 2027, with industry day January 12, 2027, per [FRVTA](https://www.frvta.org/show/florida-rv-supershow/).

**When is the Tampa Bay Fall RV Show?**
November 5–8, 2026, per [FRVTA](https://www.frvta.org/show/tampa-bay-fall-rv-show/).

**Where are the shows held?**
Florida State Fairgrounds, 4800 US Highway 301 North, Tampa, FL 33610.

**How much is admission?**
SuperShow adults $15 (2-day pass), children under 16 free. Fall show adults $5, children 16 and under free. Confirm on the official pages before you go.

**Can I bring a dog?**
Yes at both, if leashed (or in a carrier at the fall show) and you clean up after them.

body:
# Tampa to Miami: Distance, Drive, Flight and Train

People search this trip a dozen ways: tampa to miami, miami to tampa, tampa fl to miami fl, how far is Tampa from Miami. It's the same trip with the words shuffled. The practical answer for a car is about **280 miles** and roughly **4.5 to 5.5 hours** behind the wheel, labeled as an estimate. This guide leads with that drive, explains how the I-75 route is built, and then covers flying, Amtrak, and bus.

*Last updated: November 2, 2026*

![Aerial view of a highway winding through palm trees on a sunny day](/images/articles/tampa-to-miami/florida-highway-6872326.webp)
*Photo by [Quang Nguyen Vinh](https://www.pexels.com/photo/aerial-view-of-highway-among-palm-trees-6872326/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/aerial-view-of-highway-among-palm-trees-6872326/)*

## How Far Is Tampa From Miami?

**Driving distance:** about **280 miles** city center to city center on the usual I-75 / Alligator Alley routing (a routed estimate on November 2, 2026 came out at about 279.7 miles). Common map directions land in the same ~280–283 mile band.

**Drive time:** treat **about 4.5 to 5.5 hours** as a planning estimate. The same routing model put duration near 5.2 hours. Real trips swing with traffic, fuel stops, Everglades conditions, and Miami congestion. It is not a guarantee.

**Straight line:** about **205 miles (331 km)** southeast as the crow flies — useful for orientation, not for packing a cooler.

If you want to see where the two cities sit relative to each other, the [Tampa map](/getting-around/tampa-map) helps.

## Driving From Tampa to Miami

There are two realistic drives. The one most people picture is the Gulf-coast route on I-75. The other cuts inland on Florida's Turnpike.

### Route A: I-75 and Alligator Alley

The road is not a straight line, and that's the part people don't picture. From the Tampa bypass, I-75 runs south along the Gulf, past Bradenton, Sarasota, Venice, Fort Myers and Naples, and only then turns east across the Everglades.

FDOT's [2026 interchange report](https://fdotwww.blob.core.windows.net/sitefinity/docs/default-source/statistics/mileage-rpts/interchange_2026.pdf?sfvrsn=9cc3e80b_8) helps explain why the interstate segment alone is long: the I-4 interchange east of Tampa is exit 261 at about mile 260.729, and the south end of I-75 in Florida is mile 0.000 at the SR 826 (Palmetto) / SR 924 (Gratigny) interchange on the Hialeah–Miami Lakes line. That mainline stretch is about **261 miles** — useful for understanding the route, but it is not the full city-to-city drive. It leaves out the miles from your hotel or the airport to that I-4 junction, and whatever you still drive after the Palmetto to Brickell, the beach, or the port.

I-75 doesn't land you downtown or on the sand. It ends on the Hialeah–Miami Lakes line, and you can be "in Miami" on the map and still not be at the beach. The ~280-mile / 4.5–5.5-hour planning figures above are the ones that try to cover the fuller city drive.

### Alligator Alley and the toll

The tolled stretch across the Everglades is Alligator Alley. It's a 75-mile run with few services, and the toll is the one you can't skip if this is your route. The wildlife fencing and crossings are there mainly for the Florida panther, and the road passes through Big Cypress. The exit list shows rest areas around mile 35 and mile 63. I haven't checked what the plaza at the Miccosukee exit carries, so I won't name fuel brands. I wouldn't start the Alley low on gas.

[Florida's Turnpike toll card for South Florida](https://floridasturnpike.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/South-Florida-8-3-2026.pdf), effective **August 3, 2026**, lists the East Toll Plaza (milepost 25) and the West Toll Plaza (milepost 100):

| Vehicle | SunPass | Toll-By-Plate |
|---|---|---|
| 2 axles | $3.18 | $3.51 |
| 3 axles | $6.36 | — |
| 4 axles | $9.54 | — |
| 5 axles | $12.72 | — |

The card shows the same rates eastbound and westbound.

An older figure I'd seen listed $3.75 for a two-axle vehicle as of July 1, 2023, with cash accepted. That doesn't agree with the August 2026 card, which shows $3.18 by SunPass and $3.51 by plate. I'd trust the card with the 2026 effective date and still check the day I left, because older numbers linger online.

One open question: the card lists both plazas at $3.18, but it doesn't say whether a single crossing bills both. I read the setup as one plaza per crossing, not a doubled charge, but I haven't seen a $6.36 trip total and I'm not going to write one. Confirm on the signs and with your SunPass account. If you're in a rental without a transponder, expect the plate rate and then whatever the rental company adds. I never saw a rental contract, so I won't guess at their fee.

Outside the Alley, the rest of I-75 in Florida is toll-free.

### Route B: Florida's Turnpike via Orlando

The inland alternative follows Florida's Turnpike (SR 91) through the Orlando area instead of crossing Alligator Alley. Where you hop on and off varies. Some drivers pick it up around I-4 and the Orlando area, others join near Wildwood where I-75 connects.

Tolls on this route are a sum of plazas and ramps, not one flat fee. Some sample two-axle SunPass rates from the Turnpike's cards: $4.13 at the Leesburg and Three Lakes plaza areas on the Central Florida sheets, and $0.60 at Lantana Plaza on the South Florida sheet. I'm not adding those into a total, because the exits you choose change everything. Use the [Turnpike toll calculator](https://floridasturnpike.com/TollCalc/) for your exact entry and exit points, and see the [toll rates hub](https://floridasturnpike.com/tolls/toll-rates/) for the current cards.

Miami is not a longer version of the Orlando hop. It's a different road, with a toll crossing in the Everglades on the Gulf-coast route and a patchwork of plazas on the Turnpike route.

### Nearby drives for comparison

If you're mapping a longer Florida trip, Fort Myers sits well before Miami on the Gulf-coast corridor. Our guide to [Tampa to Fort Myers](/guides/tampa-to-fort-myers) covers that shorter leg if you want to break the drive up.

## Flying From Tampa to Miami

Tampa International Airport (TPA, 4100 George J. Bean Pkwy, Tampa, FL 33607) lists [nonstop service to Miami (MIA)](https://www.tampaairport.com/destinations/south/miami) on its destinations pages. American Airlines [publishes and operates](https://www.aa.com/en-us/flights-from-tampa-to-miami) nonstop TPA–MIA flights, and a FlightAware board spot check on November 2, 2026 showed American flights such as AAL3156 on the pair.

From the schedule I looked at, as of October 4, 2026:

- **Distance:** 204 miles (328 km) airport to airport
- **Flight time:** about 1 hour 10 minutes
- **Airline:** American only on the nonstop, roughly 46 flights a week, about seven a day
- **Earliest departure:** 5:00 a.m., arriving 6:04 a.m.
- **Latest departure:** 8:38 p.m., arriving 9:44 p.m.
- **Aircraft:** A319, A320, 737-800, 737 MAX 8, Embraer 170 and 175

The sample flights run a little over an hour gate to gate, while the summary figure says 1 hour 10 minutes, so I've left both. Cabin information was inconsistent. One source said the nonstop sells economy and business only, while the schedule I saw also marked a first-class code. I couldn't resolve that, so ask American. I never priced a current fare, so I have none to quote.

A separate flight-time model gave 55 minutes by assuming 500 mph plus 30 minutes for takeoff and landing. It's a calculation, not a schedule, and it tells you to add taxi time and delays. Go with the schedule.

Two airports get called "Miami" for this route: MIA and Opa-locka. The nonstop flights discussed here are TPA to MIA.

Tampa also lists nonstop service to Fort Lauderdale (FLL) on its [Fort Lauderdale destination page](https://www.tampaairport.com/destinations/south/fort-lauderdale). A November 2 board spot check showed Breeze Airways activity involving FLL. Carrier mix changes, so check TPA flight status or the airlines before assuming who flies it.

## Tampa to Miami by Train

### Amtrak

The current Tampa–Miami train is the Floridian. Per the [Amtrak timetable](https://content.amtrak.com/content/timetable/Floridian.pdf) dated November 1, 2026, it runs daily:

- **Southbound (Train 41):** departs Tampa Union Station at 12:43 p.m., arrives Miami at 6:09 p.m. (about 5 hours 26 minutes)
- **Northbound (Train 40):** departs Miami at 11:05 a.m., arrives Tampa at 4:49 p.m. (about 5 hours 44 minutes)

Tampa Union Station is commonly listed at 601 N Nebraska Avenue, Tampa, FL 33602. Confirm on Amtrak's station page before you go. A separate Silver Star timetable still exists, but it's dated September 26, 2025, so for travel now use the Floridian. I don't have coach fares, so check Amtrak directly. One note from my own research: this is a long-distance train with a routing that doesn't run as a shuttle down Alligator Alley, so don't expect the road's logic.

### Why Brightline Isn't an Option From Tampa

Brightline runs between Orlando and South Florida, not from Tampa. Its Orlando station page lists Orlando to Miami at about 3 hours 30 minutes, with 16 daily round trips between Central and South Florida. That's a useful option if you're already in Orlando, but it doesn't help a Tampa departure.

The Tampa extension is still in planning. Brightline's [August 2026 ridership report](https://www.gobrightline.com/content/dam/brightline/pdfs/investor-relations/2026/brightline-florida-august-2026-ridership-report.pdf) describes an Orlando–Tampa extension in development, with a phased approach that puts Tampa in a later phase. There are no Tampa Brightline tickets to buy, so I'm leaving it off any Tampa-to-Miami itinerary.

## Tampa to Miami by Bus

Three bus brands serve the route, and the details differ a lot.

- **FlixBus** ([route page](https://www.flixbus.com/bus-routes/bus-tampa-fl-miami-fl)): about 7 hours, roughly 309–311 miles by bus, fares from $39.98, nine rides daily, first departure 6:20 a.m., last 10:35 p.m. Boarding is at Tampa Bus Station, 1315 N Marion St, with a USF stop as well. Miami stops include the Miami Intermodal Center, Golden Glades and Miami Beach.
- **Greyhound** ([route page](https://www.greyhound.com/bus-routes/tampa-fl-miami-fl)): the same network presentation, about 7 hours, fares from about $39.98 (one banner showed $40.98), nine daily departures, 6:20 a.m. first and 10:35 p.m. last. Boarding is at the Hart Transfer Center, with loading gates moved from the West Platform to the North Platform.
- **RedCoach** ([route page](https://www.redcoachusa.com/route/tampa-to-miami/)): fares from about $31.36 (the buy-ticket page also shows $24.99), up to two buses, a sample window of 9:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. Trip time is listed around 5 hours 7 minutes, with the FAQ saying roughly 5 hours fastest and 5 hours 15 minutes average. The listed route distance is 277 miles, though the FAQ also mentions 236 miles for the fastest trip, and I won't try to reconcile those. Tampa boarding is at 3801 USF Holly Drive, 33620, and the Miami stop is near MIA.

Note how different these bus numbers are from each other and from the driving figures. The 7-hour Flix/Greyhound trips and the roughly 5-hour RedCoach trip are listed on their own pages, and they use different stops.

## Which Way Should You Go?

The ~280-mile drive, the ~204 air miles, and the ~261-mile I-75 mainline segment aren't interchangeable. The flight time skips the ride to TPA, security, and the ride out of MIA. The interstate segment skips city access at both ends. For packing a day, use about 280 miles and 4.5–5.5 hours as the drive estimate.

My own preference, for what it's worth: I'd fly nonstop if I'm traveling alone and don't need a car in Miami. I'd drive with several people, if I need a car at the other end, or if I want the Gulf coast on the way down. The train is the slow, steady option, and the bus is the budget one.

If you're planning a longer Florida itinerary, our [Tampa Florida overview](/guides/tampa-florida-overview) covers the area, and [Tampa to St. Petersburg](/guides/tampa-to-clearwater) is the short hop across the bay.

## FAQ

**How far is Tampa from Miami?**
Plan on about **280 miles** for the usual drive. Straight-line distance is about **205 miles**. The I-75 mainline from the I-4 interchange to the Palmetto end is about **261 miles** by itself — part of the route, not the full city-to-city total.

**How long is the drive from Tampa to Miami?**
About **4.5 to 5.5 hours**, labeled as an estimate. Traffic, stops, and Miami congestion change the clock.

**Is there a toll on the drive?**
On the Gulf-coast route, yes: Alligator Alley. Effective August 3, 2026, the two-axle rate is $3.18 with SunPass and $3.51 Toll-By-Plate. Confirm on the signs whether one or both plazas apply to your crossing. Florida's Turnpike route has multiple plazas, so use the official toll calculator.

**Is there a nonstop flight from Tampa to Miami?**
Yes. American Airlines flies TPA to MIA nonstop, about seven times a day, with a scheduled flight time around 1 hour 10 minutes.

**Can I take Brightline from Tampa to Miami?**
No. Brightline doesn't serve Tampa. The extension is still in planning, so there are no Tampa tickets to buy.

body:
# Marriott Water Street Tampa: Fees, Dining, Parking and Which Hotel You're Booking

*Last updated: November 2, 2026*

The Marriott Water Street Tampa is the hotel at 505 Water Street, on the downtown waterfront next to the Tampa Convention Center. The trouble is that a lot of people search for it using three or four different names, and a second Marriott sits across the street with a very similar one. Before you book, it helps to know exactly which front desk you're dealing with, what the destination fee covers, which restaurants are open when, and what parking costs.

This guide pulls from Marriott's own pages, the City of Tampa's parking pages, and Visit Tampa Bay's listing, and I've kept the sources separate where they don't agree. For a wider look at where to stay downtown, see my [Tampa hotels overview](/guides/tampa-hotels) and the [Tampa Riverwalk hotels guide](/guides/tampa-riverwalk-hotels).

![Rooftop pool at a downtown waterfront hotel with city and water views](/images/articles/marriott-water-street-tampa/waterfront-hotel-rooftop-3225525.webp)
*Photo by [Pixabay](https://www.pexels.com/@pixabay) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/architecture-buildings-city-cityscape-3225525/)*

## Address and which hotel you're booking

**Tampa Marriott Water Street**
- Address: 505 Water Street, Tampa, FL 33602
- Local phone: 813-221-4900
- Toll-free booking line: 1-800-228-9290

People say "Tampa Marriott Water Street," "Marriott Tampa Water Street," "Marriott Water Street Tampa," and "Water Street Tampa FL" for this same property. They all land on 505 Water Street.

The mix-up that matters is the neighbor. **JW Marriott Tampa Water Street** is at 510 Water Street (phone 813-221-4950). It's a different hotel under the Marriott Bonvoy umbrella, connected to the Tampa Marriott Water Street by a glass skybridge on the third floor. Marriott markets the two together as one destination with 1,246 rooms and suites combined, three rooftop pools across the pair, spa access, and more than 150,000 square feet of event space.

Same district, same skybridge, different front desks and different restaurant lineups. Anchor and Brine and Lona are on the Tampa Marriott Water Street side. Beacon and Driftlight are on the JW side. When you book, check that the confirmation says 505, not 510.

## Old names and other mix-ups

**Waterside vs. Water Street.** Visit Tampa Bay's description of this property still carries older wording in places that calls it the "Tampa Marriott Waterside Hotel & Marina." Marriott itself uses Water Street now. Plenty of people still say Waterside because that's the name on their old conference badge. I'd book through Marriott under the Water Street name.

**The marina.** Visit Tampa Bay mentions a 28-slip full-service marina among the property's amenities. That doesn't mean a boat slip comes with your room, and nothing in the sources says it does. What Marriott does describe on the water side is a water taxi, water sports, and bike rentals as part of the destination fee.

**The ballroom.** If you're booking for an event, the hotel matters more than the neighborhood name. Marriott splits the event space like this: the JW has about 100,000 square feet, including what Marriott calls the largest hotel ballroom in Tampa Bay, while the Tampa Marriott Water Street has about 50,000 square feet of redesigned meeting space.

## Rooms, fees and check-in

Marriott's basics for this hotel:
- **Check-in:** 4:00 p.m.
- **Check-out:** 11:00 a.m.
- **Minimum age to check in:** 18
- **Smoke-free property**, with electric car charging stations listed (subject to availability)

Visit Tampa Bay lists the property at 727 sleeping rooms including 28 suites, across 27 floors. Marriott's meetings page references roughly 699 guest rooms plus 28 suites for this hotel. The counts differ by source, so don't treat either as exact. Visit Tampa Bay also lists AAA Four Diamond status.

### The destination fee

A destination fee applies (listed at $20/night on Marriott's rooms page); confirm the amount when booking. According to that same rooms page, the fee currently includes:
- A daily $20 food and beverage credit
- Daily fitness or wellness classes
- A daily beverage tasting
- Your choice of admission for two on a round-trip water taxi, one hour of water sports, or one hour of bike rentals
- Enhanced daily Wi-Fi

Marriott notes that the rate and inclusions are subject to change.

### Early check-in and late check-out

Guaranteed early arrival or late departure starts at $100 plus tax. Guaranteed connecting rooms are also a bookable option.

### Cancellation

Visit Tampa Bay's listing gives a cancellation window of 24 hours before arrival to avoid a one-night-plus-tax charge. Check your own reservation terms, since rate types vary.

### Room types and packages

Marriott describes the Presidential Suite as about 1,800 square feet, with multiple oversized balconies, a formal dining room, a living room, and a personal office. There's also a Family Fun Package that includes connecting waterfront rooms, toys and crafts, complimentary breakfast for children, and special seating at the pool. I didn't find a price for the package, so ask when you book.

The Concierge Lounge is closed Saturdays and is complimentary for Platinum, Titanium, and Ambassador Elite members plus one guest.

### Nightly rates

I'm not quoting a nightly rate. Rates move with events, conventions, and season, so the destination fee and early check-in fee are the only dollar figures here that come from Marriott directly. Price your dates on [Marriott's official page](https://www.marriott.com/en-us/hotels/tpamc-tampa-marriott-water-street/overview/).

## Pool, fitness and Wi-Fi

**Rooftop pool.** The outdoor rooftop pool is a complimentary amenity, and cabanas/palapas are available for $100. The **Pool Bar & Grill** on the roof keeps limited hours: **Friday through Sunday, 11:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., closed Monday through Thursday.** Assuming the pool bar is open every afternoon like a resort is how people end up disappointed on a Tuesday.

**Fitness center.** The on-site fitness center is complimentary and newly redesigned, with cardio and free-weight equipment.

**Wi-Fi.** In-room Wi-Fi is available. Marriott Bonvoy members get complimentary in-room internet when booking direct, and the destination fee includes enhanced daily Wi-Fi.

## Where to eat

Marriott lists seven outlets at this hotel. Hours below are from Marriott's dining page.

**Riverwalk Terrace** (breakfast and brunch, smart casual)
- Mon–Fri: 6:30 a.m.–11:00 a.m.
- Sat–Sun: 6:30 a.m.–1:00 p.m.
- Phone: 813-204-6391
- Note that weekend service runs later than weekday service, which is the reverse of what people assume if they only remember "brunch until one."

**PERK** (coffee, teas, pastries, grab-and-go; cashless)
- Every day, 6:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m.

**Anchor and Brine** (seafood-forward; cashless)
- Mon–Thu and Sun: 11:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m.
- Fri–Sat: 11:00 a.m.–11:00 p.m.
- Phone: 813-431-6951
- Visit Tampa Bay also mentions weekend brunch here, Saturday and Sunday from 11:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. That comes from Visit Tampa Bay, not a separate Marriott schedule, so confirm before planning around it.

**Lona by Chef Richard Sandoval** (modern Mexican; cashless; smart casual)
- Every day, 4:00 p.m.–11:00 p.m.
- Phone: 813-204-6390

**Pool Bar & Grill**
- Fri–Sun: 11:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; closed Mon–Thu

**Bright Ice**
- Fri–Sat: 1:00 p.m.–10:00 p.m.
- Sun: 1:00 p.m.–9:30 p.m.

**A La Carte** (room service and grab-and-go)
- Mon–Thu and Sun: 6:30 a.m.–10:00 p.m.
- Fri–Sat: 6:30 a.m.–11:00 p.m.

Anchor and Brine and Lona take reservations. Groups of 13 or more go through the hotel's events email. Picnic baskets for two to four guests are offered, but I didn't find a price.

## Parking

This is where downtown trips get expensive, so it's worth sorting out before you arrive.

**Hotel valet (published by the hotel):**
- Daily valet: $55
- Short-term daytime valet: $35
- The hotel asks guests to contact the property about self-parking options

**Pam Iorio Parking Garage (City of Tampa):** The hotel lists this city garage, 0.2 miles away at 301 Channelside Drive, for public off-site parking.
- Non-event rate: $3 per hour, with a $18 daily maximum
- Event rates: $5 to $50, depending on the event
- 790 total spaces, 41 ADA spaces, 2 EV charging stations
- Visitor hourly parking runs overnight up to 6:00 a.m.

On a Lightning home night or a convention week, that event pricing is what to plan for. The [Tampa Bay Lightning page](/events) covers game nights, and the [Tampa map](/getting-around/tampa-map) helps you see how far the garage sits from where you're headed. Rates change, so confirm on the [City of Tampa parking page](https://www.tampa.gov/parking/info/parking-hourly-and-daily-rates) before you go.

## Getting here from the airport

Tampa International Airport is about 9 miles from the hotel, and St. Pete–Clearwater International is about 22 miles. Marriott lists no hotel shuttle from either airport. Visit Tampa Bay's listing mentions a courtesy area shuttle and gives a slightly different airport distance, so if a shuttle matters to your trip, call the hotel at 813-221-4900 and ask directly.

If you're also planning to cross the bay, my [Tampa to St. Petersburg guide](/guides/tampa-to-clearwater) covers that trip.

## What you can walk to

The hotel sits on the Tampa Riverwalk waterfront, and Marriott describes Riverwalk access as steps from the property. Marriott also names the Florida Aquarium, Benchmark International Arena, and Sparkman Wharf as nearby landmarks.

Walking distances below are routing estimates from OpenStreetMap pedestrian routing from 505 Water Street. Confirm on a map the day you go:

- **Benchmark International Arena** (formerly Amalie Arena, 401 Channelside Drive): about 0.32 miles
- **Sparkman Wharf** (615 Channelside Drive): about 0.43 miles
- **Florida Aquarium** (701 Channelside Drive): about 0.77 miles

## Meetings and the Convention Center

The hotel is adjacent to the Tampa Convention Center and offers about 50,000 square feet of renovated meeting space. Visit Tampa Bay lists large ballroom capacities and wheelchair accessibility. There's also a UPS Business Center on the second level: Monday–Friday 8 a.m.–6 p.m., Saturday 10 a.m.–2 p.m., closed Sunday.

During a trade show week, confirm which skybridge and entrance your badge line uses before you leave the room.

## Pets

Pets are welcome. Marriott's policy allows up to 2 pets per room, 50 lbs maximum per pet, with a non-refundable pet fee of $150 per stay.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is the Marriott Water Street the same as the JW Marriott Tampa Water Street?**
No. The Tampa Marriott Water Street is at 505 Water Street and the JW Marriott Tampa Water Street is at 510 Water Street. They're separate hotels connected by a third-floor glass skybridge and marketed together as one destination.

**What does the destination fee cover?**
A destination fee applies (listed at $20/night on Marriott's rooms page); confirm the amount when booking. That page currently lists a $20 daily food and beverage credit, fitness or wellness classes, a beverage tasting, a water taxi, water sports, or bike rental option, and enhanced Wi-Fi. Rate and inclusions are subject to change.

**How much is parking at the Tampa Marriott Water Street?**
The hotel publishes daily valet at $55 and short-term daytime valet at $35. The nearby city-run Pam Iorio Garage charges $3 an hour with a $18 daily maximum outside events, and $5 to $50 on event days.

**Is the hotel pet-friendly?**
Yes. Up to two pets per room, 50 lbs each, with a $150 non-refundable fee per stay.

**What time is check-in and check-out?**
Check-in is 4:00 p.m. and check-out is 11:00 a.m. Guaranteed early check-in or late check-out starts at $100 plus tax.

## The short version

If you want one thing to remember: confirm you're booked at 505 Water Street, confirm the destination fee amount when you book, and don't count on the pool bar midweek. For the full picture of nearby options, start with the [Tampa hotels overview](/guides/tampa-hotels), and go to [Marriott's hotel page](https://www.marriott.com/en-us/hotels/tpamc-tampa-marriott-water-street/overview/) to check current rates and policies.

Event weeks often center on the [Tampa Convention Center](/guides/tampa-convention-center) a short walk away.

body:
# Tampa to St Petersburg: Distance, Bridges and the Road

People type this a dozen ways: tampa to st petersburg, st petersburg to tampa, tampa fl to st petersburg fl, tampa st petersburg florida with no "to" in the middle. I treat all of them as one question. How far is it by road, and which road actually crosses the water?

The short version: FDOT's official mileage between the two cities is 20 miles, and the bay in the middle means your choice of bridge matters more than the number. This guide covers that number, the three bridges across Old Tampa Bay (only two of which are for this trip), what's happening on I-275 right now, and the routing mix-ups that send drivers to the wrong side of the water.

*Last updated: November 2, 2026*

![Long bridge spanning a wide bay under a bright sky](/images/articles/tampa-to-st-petersburg/st-pete-bridge-2081166.webp)
*Photo by [Pok Rie](https://www.pexels.com/@pok-rie-33563/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/bridge-near-body-of-water-2081166/)*

## How far is Tampa to St. Petersburg?

FDOT publishes the official highway mileage between Florida cities in its [intercity mileage matrix](https://www.fdot.gov/statistics/hwydata/intercity.shtm), dated 9/14/2026. The department describes it in one line I kept: shortest distance between city pairs, used for mileage reimbursements.

By FDOT, Tampa to St. Petersburg is **20 miles**. St. Petersburg to Tampa is also **20 miles**. I'm using 20 because both directions say 20, not because I averaged anything. The same figure covers every variation of the search, whether you wrote tampa fl to st petersburg fl, st petersburg florida to tampa, or st petersburg florida to tampa florida.

Two things that number is not:

- **It is not a drive time.** I'm not publishing a door-to-door estimate. Nobody official gives one, and traffic on the bay crossings varies.
- **It is not a neighborhood, airport, beach, or hotel distance.** FDOT's matrix lists cities only. Brandon is not one of FDOT's cities. Wesley Chapel is not one of FDOT's cities. If you're asking how far St. Petersburg is from a Brandon inn or from Tampa International, there's no official mile for that, and I won't tack a guess onto the 20.

A few nearby pairs from the same matrix, kept as their own numbers:

| City pair | FDOT miles (each direction) |
|---|---|
| Tampa ↔ St. Petersburg | 20 |
| St. Petersburg ↔ Clearwater | 20 |
| St. Petersburg ↔ Sarasota | 37 |
| St. Petersburg ↔ Lakeland | 53 |
| St. Petersburg ↔ Orlando | 105 |
| Tampa ↔ Orlando | 85 |

The St. Petersburg–Clearwater 20 is a different 20, along the Pinellas side, not a second copy of the bay crossing. And Orlando being "on the way" in someone's head doesn't make St. Petersburg a stop on the Tampa–Orlando number. Don't subtract one figure from another.

If you're still sorting out where everything sits, the [Tampa map](/getting-around/tampa-map) helps, and the [Tampa Florida overview](/guides/tampa-florida-overview) covers the bigger picture. St. Petersburg is a separate city on the peninsula across the bay, not a Tampa neighborhood.

## The bay and the bridges

Old Tampa Bay is the water between these cities. Three bridges cross it, but only two of them connect Tampa and St. Petersburg.

- **W. Howard Frankland Bridge (I-275):** the central bridge from St. Petersburg to Tampa and by far the most traveled of the bay's bridges.
- **Gandy Bridge (US 92):** the southernmost crossing, also running between St. Petersburg and Tampa.
- **Courtney Campbell Causeway (SR 60):** the northernmost crossing, and the wrong bridge for this trip. It carries SR 60 between Clearwater and Tampa.

If a map app offers the Courtney Campbell, it's sending you toward Clearwater's side of the bay. That's fine if Clearwater is your destination (see the [Tampa to Clearwater guide](/guides/tampa-to-clearwater)), but it has no place in the St. Petersburg mileage.

## I-275 express lanes and the new bridge

For the current Howard Frankland, I trust FDOT's own construction project, because it names both cities. The details I kept from it:

- **Project:** 422904-2-52-01, a new bridge
- **Limits:** 4th Street in Pinellas to SR 60 in Hillsborough
- **Length:** 5.8 miles
- **Cost:** $973.4 million
- **Started:** spring 2020
- **Estimated completion:** late 2026
- **Contractor:** Archer Western/Traylor Bros.

**Express lanes.** FDOT says the new express lanes are open on I-275 across the new bridge. They run from 4th Street North in St. Petersburg to just north of the bridge in Tampa, in the median, separated by barrier walls and flexible plastic poles. As of August 22, 2026, tolls are collected electronically 24 hours a day through SunPass. Only passenger vehicles, registered vanpools, and buses are allowed.

FDOT's materials I checked don't give a dollar amount, so I won't quote one. Confirm current toll information with FDOT before you drive. General-use lanes remain available beside the express lanes, so you aren't forced into the toll. A rental car shouldn't wander into the express lanes just because there's a gap in the plastic poles. Unless you mean to pay a SunPass toll, stay in the general-use lanes.

**Speed limits.** FDOT says the posted speed on the bridge is 65 mph, effective August 22, 2026, and 55 mph on either side because the approaches are still work zones.

**Which way is "southbound"?** In 2025 FDOT put the new southbound I-275 bridge into service. The 1990s bridge, which FDOT says originally connected Tampa to St. Petersburg, was converted to northbound, and the 1960s bridge was removed. The interstate is signed north and south, while the cities sit east and west of each other across the bay. "Southbound" on this bridge is not a drive toward Naples. Follow the signs for St. Petersburg or Tampa, not the compass in your head.

**Walking and biking.** A shared-use path of nearly seven miles, 12 feet wide, debuted on the north side of the bridge. It's open sunrise to sunset, from the north end of 4th Street in St. Petersburg and the south end of Reo Street in Tampa. More connections, including Ulmerton Road and another tie at 4th Street North, plus more at Reo Street, are separate projects still being built.

**Three different measurements.** The 5.8-mile bridge project, the nearly seven-mile path, and the 20-mile city pair are all separate figures. Don't merge them into one "about six miles across."

**Closures.** When I checked, FDOT had scheduled overnight closures on the bridge between Hillsborough and Pinellas, Sunday, October 5 through Saturday, October 10, 9 p.m. to 6 a.m. That was a scheduled window, not something I watched happen. Check FDOT for anything current before you go.

## Gandy Bridge (US 92)

Gandy is the southernmost of the three, spans Old Tampa Bay from St. Petersburg to Tampa, carries US 92, and is maintained by FDOT. It's almost three miles long: 14,859 feet eastbound and 13,886 feet westbound. Those lengths describe the bridge, not the trip, so don't add them to FDOT's 20.

A bit of history, kept as history: the 1924 bridge cut the Tampa–St. Petersburg distance from 43 miles to 19. Today's official pair is 20, so don't treat 19 or 43 as a current figure. The eastbound span in use is the 1975 bridge, and the westbound span is the 1997 bridge. The old Friendship Trail span is gone, with demolition finished as of July 2016. There has been talk of a possible fifth span, with a design phase to begin sometime in 2025, but nobody has told me a new Gandy span is under construction, so I won't say one is.

**Current work.** FDOT District Seven has a bridge repair project on the eastbound US 92 bridge over Old Tampa Bay in Hillsborough County. It started November 3, 2025, costs $2.9 million, and is estimated to finish in early 2027. Repairs are underneath and aren't expected to affect traffic on Gandy Boulevard. If a lane closure is needed, FDOT says it would run 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. When I checked, no closures were scheduled.

FDOT files that project under Tampa, not St. Petersburg, even though the bridge's other end is St. Petersburg. Seeing only "Tampa" on the project listing, you might decide Gandy is a Tampa-side street job. It's the other St. Petersburg bridge.

Gandy is a real Tampa–St. Petersburg crossing, but I can't tell you it's faster or slower than the Howard Frankland, because I have no current travel time for it.

## The wrong-turn problem: three "St. Petersburg" signs

Most of the confusion comes from three different roads that all seem to point at St. Petersburg.

1. **Howard Frankland, I-275.** The central, busiest bridge, with new express lanes that toll and that don't allow trucks or big RVs. The project isn't finished until late 2026, and the approaches are still at 55.
2. **Gandy, US 92.** The southern bridge, with an eastbound repair that's supposed to stay under the deck.
3. **I-275 from farther south.** This one isn't a Tampa crossing at all. North of Ellenton, I-275 splits from I-75 to serve St. Petersburg and Pinellas via the Sunshine Skyway, and Tampa via the Howard Frankland. The exit list puts I-275 north toward St. Petersburg at exit 228.

Farther north, after I-75 has bypassed the bay through Brandon, exit 274 at Wesley Chapel is I-275 south toward Tampa, St. Petersburg, and the airport. It's the same interstate number with two different ends and two different bridges. I-75 itself stays east, past Brandon, the Selmon at exit 256, and I-4 at exit 261.

If you follow I-75 "toward St. Petersburg" without reading the exit, you can miss the bay entirely or come in over the Skyway from the south. Read the exit, pick the bridge on purpose, and don't treat a Brandon hotel or a Wesley Chapel exit as if it were inside that 20 miles.

## Heading to a Rays game

St. Petersburg is where Tropicana Field is, not Tampa. If you're staying in Tampa and driving over for a Rays game, you're making exactly this trip. The [Tropicana Field guide](/events/tropicana-field) covers the ballpark itself. If you're arriving by air first, the [Tampa International Airport guide](/getting-around/tampa-international-airport) covers that end of things. The ballpark's own site, [MLB.com's Rays ballpark page](https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark), is the place to check for game-day details.

Budget for the crossing on game day without leaning on any number from me. I don't have a verified drive time, and bridge traffic varies.

## Tips before you drive

- **Use 20 miles as a city-to-city reference only.** It's FDOT's reimbursement distance, not a measurement to your hotel or the ballpark.
- **Choose your bridge on purpose.** Howard Frankland (I-275) is the main crossing, and Gandy (US 92) is the southern option.
- **Skip the Courtney Campbell** unless you're actually going to Clearwater.
- **Stay in the general-use lanes** on I-275 unless you intend to pay the SunPass express-lane toll.
- **Expect 55 mph on the approaches** and 65 mph on the bridge itself.
- **Check FDOT for closures** before you leave, especially overnight.

## FAQ

**How far is Tampa from St. Petersburg?**
FDOT's official intercity mileage is 20 miles between Tampa and St. Petersburg, and the same 20 in the other direction. It's a city-to-city figure used for mileage reimbursement, not a distance to a specific address.

**How long does it take to drive from Tampa to St. Petersburg?**
I don't have an official drive time, and I won't invent one. Traffic across Old Tampa Bay varies, so check a live traffic source before you leave.

**Which bridges connect Tampa and St. Petersburg?**
The W. Howard Frankland Bridge (I-275) and the Gandy Bridge (US 92). The Courtney Campbell Causeway (SR 60) connects Tampa and Clearwater, not St. Petersburg.

**Do the I-275 express lanes cost money?**
Yes. As of August 22, 2026, FDOT says tolls on the express lanes are collected electronically 24 hours a day through SunPass. FDOT's materials I checked don't list a dollar amount, so confirm current tolling with FDOT. General-use lanes are still available.

**Is Tropicana Field in Tampa?**
No. Tropicana Field is in St. Petersburg, a separate city on the peninsula across the bay from Tampa.

body:
# Seminole Hard Rock Tampa: The Name, the Address and the Hollywood Mix-Up

*Last updated: November 2, 2026*

I type "seminole hard rock tampa" on purpose, because I did not trust the shorter name. Hard Rock is a brand. Seminole is who owns the building. Before I told anyone that the two names describe the same trip, I wanted the resort itself to use both names at the Tampa address. It does.

This guide covers the hotel stay, the dining and entertainment side, and, mostly, how to make sure you are looking at the Tampa property and not one of its Florida siblings. It does not cover gambling. If you want to know how any casino game works, this is not that page.

![Modern resort hotel exterior with lit windows at dusk](/images/articles/seminole-hard-rock-tampa/hard-rock-258154.webp)
*Photo by [Pixabay](https://www.pexels.com/@pixabay/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/architecture-building-buildings-business-258154/)*

## What Seminole Hard Rock Tampa Actually Is

The Tampa resort calls itself Seminole Hard Rock Hotel & Casino Tampa. Its welcome reads "Welcome to Hard Rock Tampa" and then "Discover your rhythm at Seminole Hard Rock Hotel & Casino Tampa." The address that goes with it is **5223 Orient Road, Tampa, Florida 33610**.

That means seminole hard rock tampa, hard rock seminole tampa, seminole tampa hard rock, and seminole hard rock tampa fl all point to one place. There is no second resort hiding behind the casino name. They are the Orient Road property with the tribal name put back on the front.

The property is a separate campus from the Water Street and Riverwalk hotel cluster downtown. If you are planning a trip around the waterfront, this is a different part of the map. Our [Tampa map guide](/getting-around/tampa-map) helps you see how far apart the pieces are.

## Why the Name Has Both Words

Seminole Gaming is where the name actually gets explained. It names its destinations, and the three I noted were:

- Seminole Hard Rock Hotel & Casino Hollywood
- Seminole Hard Rock Hotel & Casino Tampa
- Seminole Casino Coconut Creek

Tampa is one door among several, not the whole company. Seminole Gaming also says the Seminole Tribe of Florida started the first high-stakes bingo hall and casino in the United States in 1979, and that in March 2007 the Tribe acquired Hard Rock International.

That is why the signs say both words. The casino is tribal. The music brand was a purchase. People who argue about whether "Seminole Hard Rock" is "the real Hard Rock" are arguing with a 2007 date the company states itself. The Seminole part of the name is the tribe that bought Hard Rock in 2007 and still runs both hotels. It is not a direction.

## Tampa vs. Hollywood: Which Resort Is Which

That history is also why the mix-up with Hollywood, Florida is so easy. Hollywood is the other Hard Rock among those destinations, and it is the one with the skyline.

**Hollywood** (1 Seminole Way, Hollywood, Florida 33314):
- The Guitar Hotel is described as back-to-back guitars, 450 feet, with 638 luxury rooms and suites.
- The Oasis Tower is seven stories with 168 rooms, including swim-up suites on a lagoon.
- A third block, just called Hard Rock Hotel, has 465 music-themed rooms.
- The resort describes itself as AAA Four Diamond and Green Lodging Certified, 15 minutes from Fort Lauderdale's beaches and 30 minutes from Miami, and says it tends to sell out.

**Tampa** (5223 Orient Road) is also AAA Four Diamond. Tampa does not describe a guitar-shaped tower, a lagoon, or a drive to Miami. It leads with an event center, bars, lounges, a spa, three pools, and shops.

The quick test: if a photo has a giant guitar, it is not Orient Road. If the show is at Hard Rock Live with a South Florida area code in the description, you are not going to Orient Road either.

## The Phone Number Trap

The phone number is the one I almost fell into. I had both numbers in front of me:

- **Tampa general property line:** 1-866-388-4263
- **1-866-502-7529:** Hollywood gives this as its call line, and Tampa uses that exact number for Rock Spa and Salon customer care.

If you call the spa line and ask for a Tampa casino host, you may be talking to a shared care number that Hollywood also uses as its main line. I would use 388-4263 for the Tampa resort and treat 502-7529 as spa care unless the person on the phone confirms the city. Whichever number you dial, confirm the city before you give anyone a card number.

## Hotel Stays and Discounts

Searchers often type "hard rock hotel tampa" when they want the lodging side of the property. The hotel tower is part of the same Orient Road resort, so a booking should show the Tampa address, not Hollywood's.

I do not have a published rack rate for either hotel, so I will not guess at nightly prices. For current rates, resort fees, and availability, use the [official Hard Rock Tampa site](https://www.seminolehardrocktampa.com/).

What I can say is that discounts differ by city, and people pass along the wrong offer:

| Offer | Tampa | Hollywood |
|---|---|---|
| Florida and Georgia residents | Up to 20 percent off hotel rooms | Up to 10 percent |
| Military | Up to 10 percent | Up to 10 percent |
| AAA | Not noted | Up to 10 percent off the daily rate |

Same tribe, same brand, not the same percentage. A percent off an unpublished number is not a price, so treat these as the starting point for a conversation with the reservations desk. If you are comparing the resort against downtown options, our [Tampa hotels guide](/guides/tampa-hotels) lays out the other neighborhoods.

## Concerts and Entertainment

The concerts make the same mistake in public. On the day I compared the two, Tampa's upcoming act was Flo Raw at the Hard Rock Cafe. Hollywood's Hard Rock Live lineup that month was Billy Currington, Aziz Ansari, Ricky Martin, Freya Skye, Def Leppard, Dalvin La Melodia, a Fists of Fury card, the Doobie Brothers, and Blake Shelton, all in October.

Same weeks, different rooms, different coast. A friend who says "we have Def Leppard at the Seminole Hard Rock" is not talking about Tampa unless Tampa itself announces it. Tampa had not.

Shows change constantly, so use the entertainment calendar on the [official site](https://www.seminolehardrocktampa.com/) for current dates, and check ticket details there rather than trusting a screenshot a friend sent. For a wider look at what is happening across the city, see our [Tampa events guide](/events/tampa-events).

### Nightlife Is Not Interchangeable

Hollywood sells a dayclub. It promotes DAER Nightclub and Dayclub to South Florida and calls it the only dayclub in South Florida. Tampa leads with an event center, bars, lounges, a spa, three pools, and shops.

I am not going to pretend I compared every nightlife room. The point is that the marketing each resort leads with is not interchangeable. One is a South Florida party resort with a guitar in the sky. The other is a Tampa casino hotel on Orient Road.

## Dining

The Tampa resort has on-site restaurants and bars, and the Hard Rock Cafe is one of the places tied to the entertainment calendar. I did not compile a restaurant-by-restaurant list with hours, and hours change, so the official site is the place to confirm what is open the night you visit.

For contrast, the resort is a self-contained option away from the downtown dining scene. If you want to eat your way through the city instead, our [Tampa restaurants guide](/food-and-drink/tampa-restaurants) covers the neighborhoods.

## Unity, Gift Cards and Other Name Traps

Unity is the card that makes people think the buildings are one building. Seminole Gaming calls Unity by Hard Rock a program you earn and redeem at Seminole Gaming casinos and participating Hard Rock cafes, casinos, and hotels. The app shows balances and offers.

That means a card from Hollywood can be a card at Tampa. It does not mean the rooms, the pools, or the show you bought are in Tampa. Check the city on the reservation.

A few more things worth knowing:

- **U-Wallet:** Seminole Gaming describes it as a cash alternative at slot machines "across all 6 Seminole Casinos in South Florida." Tampa is not South Florida by their own description, so that sentence is not about Orient Road. The six were not named alongside that line, and I will not guess at the list.
- **Gift cards:** Seminole Gaming says its gift cards are good for dining, hotel, entertainment, and spa, and cannot be used for slot play or to buy casino chips. A "Seminole Hard Rock" card for your birthday is not necessarily gambling money.
- **Internet play:** Seminole Gaming says its internet casino is only available in New Jersey. Hard Rock Games are social apps, not a Florida casino in your pocket.
- **Sports betting:** Florida does get Hard Rock Bet, with kiosks and windows at the Tampa sportsbook near the box office and an app they say works anywhere in Florida. That is a different product from an internet casino. I had to go over that twice.

## Other Seminole Names Are Not Nicknames for Tampa

Two more names I refuse to fold into Tampa. Seminole Casino Coconut Creek is its own destination. And the Tampa sportsbook, in its list of properties, shows Seminole Hotel Casino Immokalee as a separate label. I did not look into Immokalee. I only needed the label to stop myself from saying "the Seminole casino" as if Florida had one.

## What I Tell People Who Say Seminole Hard Rock Tampa

If you take one thing from this page, make it this checklist:

1. Confirm the address: 5223 Orient Road, Tampa, Florida 33610.
2. Use the Tampa phone, 1-866-388-4263, for the resort.
3. Know that it is the same property as Hard Rock Tampa.
4. It is not the Guitar Hotel. Hollywood is 1 Seminole Way, Hollywood, Florida 33314, a different drive, a different skyline, and a different concert calendar.
5. Check the city on any booking, ticket, or gift card before you pay.

## FAQ

**Is Seminole Hard Rock Tampa the same as Hard Rock Tampa?**
Yes. The resort calls itself Seminole Hard Rock Hotel & Casino Tampa and welcomes you to "Hard Rock Tampa." Both names point to the Orient Road property.

**Where is Seminole Hard Rock Tampa located?**
5223 Orient Road, Tampa, Florida 33610. It is a separate campus from the downtown Water Street and Riverwalk hotel cluster.

**Does the Tampa resort have the guitar-shaped hotel?**
No. The Guitar Hotel is in Hollywood, Florida. Tampa does not describe a guitar-shaped tower or a lagoon.

**What phone number should I call for the Tampa resort?**
Use 1-866-388-4263 for the Tampa property. The 1-866-502-7529 number is Hollywood's call line and is also used for Rock Spa and Salon customer care at Tampa.

**Why is it called Seminole Hard Rock?**
The Seminole Tribe of Florida owns the casino, and in March 2007 the Tribe acquired Hard Rock International. The signs carry both names for that reason.

For current shows, rooms, and dining hours, go to the [official Hard Rock Tampa site](https://www.seminolehardrocktampa.com/).
