body:
# Tampa Tarpons: Yankees Single-A Team and Ballpark Guide

*Last updated: November 2, 2026*

Ask around about Tampa sports and the answers pile up fast: Rays tickets, Bucs kickoffs, Lightning games, Hard Rock casino shows. So when I kept hearing "Tampa Tarpons," I had to figure out what it actually was. A team? A nickname people stuck on the Rays? A high school? A place?

It settled quickly. The Tampa Tarpons are a Minor League Baseball club, the Single-A affiliate of the New York Yankees, playing in the Florida State League. They are not the Rays, not a casino show, and not a Seminole Hard Rock event. They are a real baseball team that sells its own tickets, runs its own schedule, and calls a real ballpark home.

This guide covers who the Tarpons are, where they play, how the name came about, what happened with the confusing 2025 stadium arrangement, and how to sort the Tarpons from everything else on Tampa's sports and entertainment calendar.

![Baseball player swinging during a daytime game](/images/articles/tampa-tarpons/tarpons-2570139.webp)
*Photo by [Laura Tancredi](https://www.pexels.com/@lauratancredi/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/man-in-white-jersey-shirt-and-blue-pants-playing-baseball-2570139/)*

## What the Tampa Tarpons are

The Tampa Tarpons are the Single-A affiliate of the New York Yankees. MLB's own profile of the team's ballpark describes them as the Yankees' Single-A club since 1994, formerly the Tampa Yankees, in the Florida State League. As part of the 2021 Minor League reorganization, the Tarpons and the rest of the Florida State League moved from Class A Advanced to Single-A. The GMS Field venue and the Tarpons ticket office both still describe the club as the low-A or Single-A Yankees affiliate, so there is no higher level to claim here.

In practical terms, that means you are watching young players working their way up the Yankees system. The club's alumni list includes Aaron Judge, Derek Jeter, Mariano Rivera, Luis Severino, David Robertson, Mike Lowell, Tim Raines, and Luis Sojo. That is a Yankees pipeline, not a Rays one. If you landed on "Tampa Tarpons" because you thought it was a Rays nickname, the affiliate paperwork is the correction.

The club has won Florida State League championships in 1994, 2001, 2004, 2009, and 2010, according to MLB's profile. On September 9, 2026, the venue said the Tarpons were back in the playoffs, chasing their first FSL championship since 2010.

## Tampa Tarpons history and the name

The current club started in 1994 as the Tampa Yankees. Minor League Baseball announced on December 11, 2017 that the Tampa Yankees were becoming the Tampa Tarpons for the 2018 season, bringing Tarpons baseball back to the Florida State League after a long gap.

That same announcement said an earlier Tampa Tarpons franchise played in the league from 1957 through 1987 and won titles in 1957 and 1961. So the name covers two layers: the old Florida State League Tarpons, and the modern Yankees affiliate that revived the brand. When people say "Tampa Tarpons" today and are buying tickets, they mean the live club.

### Why a fish?

The name is not a joke. When the club rebranded in 2017, it said tarpons are prized Gulf Coast game fish known for fighting when hooked. The team colors are Legends Navy, Tarpon Silver, and Gulf Blue. MLB adds that tarpons can run upward of eight feet long and are usually released, and that the logo draws on a 1970s-era Tarpons look: a fish holding a bat, set against Yankees-style pinstripes. The mascot name attached to the kids club is King Ripple.

## Where the Tampa Tarpons play

Home is George M. Steinbrenner Field in Tampa. MLB gives the address as 1 Steinbrenner Drive, Tampa, Florida 33614, with the phone number 813-875-7753 (confirm on the [official Tarpons site](https://www.milb.com/tampa) before you call). The venue itself lists the same address and number.

The complex is also the spring training home of the New York Yankees, so the same ballpark serves both the Yankees in spring and the Tarpons during the Florida State League season. You can read more on the [Yankees spring training page](https://www.mlb.com/yankees/spring-training).

### Capacity and field details

Two official sources give slightly different capacity descriptions, and both come from official mouths:

- The Tarpons say the complex seats over 10,000 fans.
- MLB lists capacity at 11,026, with dimensions of 318 feet to left, 408 to center, and 314 to right.

I'm not picking a favorite number. Either way, it is a big ballpark for Single-A baseball.

### What's inside the ballpark

The Tarpons name luxury suites, an all-inclusive dugout club, Bullpen or 3B club space, a Yankees pavilion, Monument Park, and what they describe as the largest Yankees gift shop in the southeast. MLB mentions a 2017 renovation that brought a walk-around concourse feel and photo spots.

### Directions from the team

The team's own directions are simple enough that I wrote them down:

- **From I-275:** take North Dale Mabry (US Highway 92), exit 41A, go north about 3 miles, and the field is on the left.
- **From the airport:** head out to Spruce Street for about 2 miles, turn left on North Dale Mabry for about a mile, and the field is on the left.

Those are the team's figures, not my odometer. For a wider look at routes across the city, the [Tampa map](/getting-around/tampa-map) helps put northwest Tampa in context.

## The 2025 stadium shuffle

This is the part that made the Tarpons confusing for a lot of people. The Tarpons announced on February 4, 2025 that for the 2025 season the team would play on Community Field at GMS Field, the side field next to the tennis courts, because they offered the main stadium to the Tampa Bay Rays for that season.

Details from the announcements:

- Seating capacity for the side field was given as 1,000, with lights added so night games could continue.
- A follow-up on April 4, 2025 nicknamed that temporary home "The Tank" and said BayCare presented the 2025 season.
- Most home games were played at The Tank while the Rays used the main stadium.
- Ticket prices for The Tank that season were $2 on Tuesdays and $5 Wednesday through Sunday, bought ahead.
- The Tarpons still took the main stadium for three dates: May 17, July 4, and August 30, including Independence Day and Fan Appreciation Night, with a 3-Game Stadium Plan on offer.

That is 2025 history, not a promise for every future season. The overlap with the Rays that year is exactly how many people mixed up the two names.

### What about 2026 and 2027?

The Tarpons were still handing out a 2026 printable schedule, and the GMS Field venue was already promoting a 2027 Tarpons schedule. No source I found states which diamond they used for each individual 2026 home date, so I'm leaving that open. What I can say is that the team's current marketing still treats George M. Steinbrenner Field as the home of the Tarpons. Anyone buying tickets should check the details for that specific game to see which field and which gate to use.

## Tampa Tarpons tickets and fan clubs

The Tarpons sell individual game tickets, season tickets, mini and flex plans, group tickets, and birthday parties. They use a GMS Field account for buying, transferring, and accessing mobile tickets. Their advice for individual games is to buy ahead in advance. Prices change, so use the official [MiLB Tampa Tarpons site](https://www.milb.com/tampa) rather than relying on any number quoted in an old article.

### Kids and senior clubs

The Tarpons promote two fan clubs:

- **King Ripple's Kids Club** for fans 12 and younger
- **Silver Kings Club** for fans 55 and older

Both are now described with discounted full-season or mini-plan language. Back in 2025, around The Tank, those clubs were described as free to join that year with Friday or Wednesday ticket perks. The current description is different, so don't paste 2025 club rules onto a later season. Check the club pages before you plan.

### Which phone number?

I came across two phone numbers: 813-673-3055 from older Tarpons announcements, and 813-875-7753 for GMS Field. I would call whichever number is on your ticket confirmation.

### What I'd actually buy

For a first visit, an individual game ticket bought ahead is the low-commitment way to see what a Single-A game feels like. If you are a family with younger kids, the Kids Club is worth a look. If you are a regular, the mini and flex plans exist for exactly that. I did not find a single-game price for the current season in my materials, so I'm not quoting one.

## Tampa Tarpons vs. everything else in town

The same sports and entertainment names follow every Tampa question around, so here is how the Tarpons sort out against them:

- **Tampa Bay Rays:** a different team, at a different level. The Rays play at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg. See the [MLB Rays ballpark page](https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark). The only real overlap was the 2025 stadium share described above.
- **Tampa Bay Buccaneers:** football, at Raymond James Stadium. If you want the NFL side, see our [Tampa Buccaneers guide](/events/tampa-buccaneers). It is a different sport and a different venue.
- **Tampa Bay Lightning:** hockey, at Amalie Arena.
- **Seminole Hard Rock Hotel and Casino Tampa:** on Orient Road, a hotel, dining, and concert destination, not a baseball venue.
- **AMC:** a movie theater chain, nothing to do with the Tarpons.

Steinbrenner Field sits on Dale Mabry in northwest Tampa. If your map app tries to send you toward Orient Road or a Hard Rock show, you have the wrong Tampa night out. For help telling the city's venues apart, our [Tampa stadium guide](/events/tampa-stadium-guide) lays out which stadium belongs to which team, and the broader [Tampa events](/events/tampa-events) page covers what else is happening around town.

### Where to stay near the field

Finding a hotel near the ballpark is its own question. The venue points people toward places to stay, but I did not go through them, so I'm not naming hotels I never looked at. Start with the venue's own lodging suggestions.

## Quick facts

| Detail | Info |
|---|---|
| Team | Tampa Tarpons |
| Level | Single-A, Florida State League |
| MLB affiliate | New York Yankees |
| Home field | George M. Steinbrenner Field |
| Address | 1 Steinbrenner Drive, Tampa, FL 33614 |
| Venue phone | 813-875-7753 (confirm on the official site) |
| Also hosts | New York Yankees spring training |
| Original club | Tampa Yankees, established 1994 |
| Rebrand announced | December 11, 2017, effective 2018 season |
| Earlier Tarpons franchise | 1957–1987, titles in 1957 and 1961 |

## FAQ

### Are the Tampa Tarpons the same as the Tampa Bay Rays?
No. The Tampa Tarpons are a Single-A Minor League Baseball team affiliated with the New York Yankees. The Rays are a separate Major League club that plays at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg.

### Where do the Tampa Tarpons play?
Home is George M. Steinbrenner Field at 1 Steinbrenner Drive, Tampa, FL 33614. In 2025 most home games were played on Community Field, the side field nicknamed "The Tank," while the Rays used the main stadium. For any specific game, check your ticket details for the correct field and gate.

### What league are the Tampa Tarpons in?
The Florida State League, at the Single-A level. They are the Single-A affiliate of the New York Yankees.

### Were the Tampa Tarpons ever called something else?
Yes. The current club began in 1994 as the Tampa Yankees and became the Tampa Tarpons for the 2018 season. An earlier Tampa Tarpons franchise played in the Florida State League from 1957 through 1987.

### How do I buy Tampa Tarpons tickets?
Through the official Tarpons and MiLB channels and the GMS Field account system, which handles buying, transferring, and mobile ticket access. Visit the [official MiLB Tampa page](https://www.milb.com/tampa) for current options rather than trusting an old price.

## The short version

If you are confused after a weekend of mixed-up answers, here it is: the Tampa Tarpons are a Yankees Single-A Florida State League team, not a casino and not the Rays. The brand revived an older Tampa Tarpons name from 1957 to 1987. Home is George M. Steinbrenner Field at 1 Steinbrenner Drive, which also hosts Yankees spring training. In 2025 most home games were on the side field called Community Field, or The Tank, while the Rays used the main stadium. For any date after that, check the specific ticket and schedule details instead of assuming the big bowl. Tickets go through the Tarpons and the GMS Field account manager.

title: Tampa Map: What the City and County Maps Really Show
dek: Tampa map guide explaining city limits versus mailing Tampa, bay shorelines, City Hall at Jackson Street, and why tourist map pins often mislead.
metaTitle: Tampa Map: City Limits and Bay Lines
metaDescription: Tampa map guide explaining city limits versus mailing Tampa, bay shorelines, City Hall at Jackson Street, and why tourist map pins often mislead.
coverAlt: Hands holding a paper map while navigating outdoors
coverCredit: Photo by Pixabay on Pexels
body:
# Tampa Map: What the City and County Maps Really Show

People search for a Tampa map in a dozen ways: map of Tampa Florida, maps Tampa, Tampa Florida map, Tampa FL map, Tampa on a map. Most of them want the same picture, a pin with a blue edge. I wanted that too. What I ended up studying instead were the City of Tampa's own maps and Hillsborough County's boundary maps. They are less pretty. They are also the reason the pretty picture can mislead.

This guide walks through what those official maps say, where a typical tourist map goes wrong, and which pieces of the Tampa picture are worth checking before you rely on a pin.

*Last updated: November 2, 2026*

![Hands holding a paper map while navigating outdoors](/images/articles/tampa-map/tampa-map-346885.webp)
*Photo by [Pixabay](https://www.pexels.com/@pixabay/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/adventure-direction-finger-hand-346885/)*

## Quick answers

- **Is every address labeled "Tampa" inside the city limits?** No. The City of Tampa says many Hillsborough County addresses use the name Tampa without being inside the official city limits. Temple Terrace and unincorporated parts of the county are the examples it names.
- **Where do the city limits stop at the water?** They don't. The city says its legal limits extend into Tampa Bay and Hillsborough Bay.
- **Is Tampa on the Gulf?** The official maps describe the city on Tampa Bay and Hillsborough Bay. I never found them describing it as a Gulf-front beach town.
- **Where is City Hall?** 306 E Jackson Street, Tampa, FL 33602. The city's main number is (813) 274-8211.
- **Where do I verify a boundary?** The City of Tampa's GIS maps at [tampa.gov](https://www.tampa.gov/), which include an address lookup.

## The pin says Tampa, but that is only a word

The first problem with most Tampa maps is the word on the pin. The City of Tampa says many addresses in Hillsborough County include "Tampa" in the mailing address, and not all of those addresses are inside the official city limits. It specifically mentions Temple Terrace and unincorporated parts of the county as places that can carry the same label. If you need to know where the boundary actually falls rather than what the mailing word says, the city points you to an address lookup on its GIS map.

That means any map that drops a pin on "Tampa" and shades a blob has skipped a question the city thinks deserves its own explanation. I felt that during my stay downtown. A shop's sign said Tampa, and I had no way of telling from the sign whether I was in the city or in the county borrowing the city's name.

If you are sorting out how a mailing address relates to a place, the [Tampa USA ZIP code guide](/guides/tampa-usa-zip-code) covers the postal side. And if you are curious how big the city proper is, the [Tampa population guide](/guides/tampa-population) deals with that separately from mailing labels.

## The shoreline is the second place a map misleads

The city is open about this one in writing. Its Tampa Boundary map is described as a modified version of the Tampa city limits, changed so it follows the shoreline and updated as needed. That sounds tidy until you reach the related city map that states the caveat directly: the shoreline version carries a name like a city limit, but the city says it is not the incorporated limits of the City of Tampa. The actual city limits extend into Tampa Bay and Hillsborough Bay. The shoreline version was drawn to follow the southern shoreline instead.

In practice, a map that cuts Tampa off at the beach grass is a drawing. The legal city keeps going out over the water. I had been reading the blue part of every Tampa map as "not Tampa." According to the city, the blue part can still be inside the limit, and the land-only outline is the modified one.

## Hillsborough County draws it the other way, on purpose

If you search for a map of Tampa Florida and land on a county product, expect a similar edit. Hillsborough keeps a municipal limits map showing the city boundaries of Tampa, Temple Terrace, and Plant City. The county says those shapes are clipped along the water's edge for drawing purposes. The real boundary is set by ordinance. The county updates the map when an annexation of unincorporated county land is finished, using the ordinance, the legal description, and a general area map from the city.

So there are two official maps here, both honest about being edited at the water, and neither a substitute for the ordinance line. Whenever a map shows a clean edge along the bay, I now assume I am looking at the drawing cut unless someone says otherwise. If you need a boundary for something that matters, such as a permit, a legal question, or a service area, go to the city's GIS tools rather than a tourist map. They are the better source than any pin on a travel page.

## The bay is part of the picture

Here is the plain version of what Tampa on a map really shows. Tampa is a city in Hillsborough County sitting on Tampa Bay and Hillsborough Bay, with a legal line the city says runs out into those bays, and with a land outline that both the city and the county draw as a modified or clipped version.

It is not a barrier island. It is not the Gulf beach towns a regional map places to the west. I did not measure the bay and I won't put a width on it. The point is which water the official maps are talking about: they name Tampa Bay and Hillsborough Bay. If you want to understand the crossings between Tampa and the other side of the bay, the [Tampa to St. Petersburg guide](/guides/tampa-to-st-petersburg) covers that. For the Courtney Campbell side, see the [Tampa to Clearwater guide](/guides/tampa-to-clearwater).

For a broader picture of the city beyond the lines on a map, the [Tampa Florida overview](/guides/tampa-florida-overview) is the place to start.

## If you were looking for beaches, these are the city's four

Plenty of people searching for a Tampa Florida map are really hunting for sand. The city's parks department is plain about what it runs: four beaches along the shores of Tampa Bay, open sunrise to sunset.

| Beach | Address | Parking, per city info |
|---|---|---|
| Ben T. Davis Beach | 7740 W Courtney Campbell Causeway, 33607 | Metered, $2.50 an hour |
| Cypress Point Park | 5620 W Cypress St, 33607 | Free Monday through Friday until noon; otherwise metered, $1 for the first hour and $2 each hour after |
| Davis Islands (seaplane basin beach) | 864 Severn Ave, 33606 | Not listed in my notes |
| Picnic Island Park | 7409 Picnic Island Blvd, 33616 | Not listed in my notes |

Beach water is monitored by the Florida Department of Health under the Florida Healthy Beaches program, and the city says to check the latest test rather than assume the water is fine. I am not declaring any of these open or clean on a given morning, so check before you go. What I can say is that the city-run sand is bay sand at those four spots, which is a different thing from the Gulf strand a regional map might suggest. Note too that all four carry Tampa addresses and ZIP codes, which, as covered above, is not quite the same as the legal city line.

## Davis Islands: the piece of the map people misread

Davis Islands is the part of the map I would have mistaken for a separate town. The City of Tampa places it in South Tampa, right outside downtown, at the mouth of the Hillsborough River. It was built in the 1920s by D.P. Davis, a Tampa native, from two small natural islands, Little Grassy Key and Big Grassy Key. The land was filled with mud dredged from the bottom of Tampa Bay.

A canal still cuts one portion off from the rest, so the city says it is technically an archipelago, which is why the name is plural. It started as three islands. Airport construction filled the end of a canal and joined the two largest islands at their southern ends, so the count dropped to two.

The city names several things on the islands:

- Peter O. Knight Airport
- The Davis Islands Yacht Club
- Tampa General Hospital
- The Sandra Freedman Tennis Complex
- The Roy Jenkins aquatic center
- Marjorie Park and the Marjorie Park Municipal Yacht Basin, donated to the city and named for Marjorie Merritt Davis

On a map it reads as a knob of land in the bay just off downtown. It also makes the shoreline-versus-limits issue concrete. The place was made out of the bay, and the legal line, by the city's own admission about its shoreline map, still reaches into the bay. A map that stops at the seawall cuts that story in half.

## Neighborhood maps: explore them, don't expect a printed ring of names

I wanted a friendly neighborhood map that labeled the rest of the city the way a map thumbnail does. The city has neighborhood maps and a find-a-neighborhood tool. The find-a-neighborhood tool also mentions demographics, land use, places of interest, association contacts, and meetings. Both are maps you explore yourself, not a printed ring of neighborhood names handed to you.

I am leaving the labels around a pin to the official tools rather than reciting them from memory. Davis Islands is the neighborhood I actually dug into. For the rest of the map of Tampa vocabulary, use the city's find-a-neighborhood tool and read what it shows. City Hall's address, the same 306 East Jackson Street, Tampa, Florida 33602, appears on those city resources.

## Hillsborough County maps pull in other cities too

One more detail from the county side belongs in a note about what a Tampa map shows. The county's ZIP map is a mail map, not a city-limits map. It includes areas whose default city is Saint Petersburg or Clearwater, and others whose default city is Lakeland or Wesley Chapel. Those cities do not become part of Tampa. The point is that a county map with Hillsborough's name on it already contains delivery areas whose preferred name sits on another shore or in another county.

A zoomed-out Tampa on a map does the same visual trick. You see the bay, you see the far shore, and the name Tampa gets credit for all of it. The city's warning about its limits is the correction. So is the shoreline disclaimer, and so are the four bay beaches with their bay addresses.

## Getting your bearings when you arrive

If you are flying in, the [Tampa International Airport guide](/getting-around/tampa-international-airport) is the place to orient yourself before you start looking at maps of the surrounding area. From there, a good habit is to treat any map as a starting sketch. Use a mapping app for directions, and use the city's GIS tools when the boundary itself matters.

## What I would tell someone handing them a Tampa map

- **The pin is a word.** It can cover the legal city, Temple Terrace, and unincorporated county.
- **The outline is probably edited.** It is likely the clipped or shoreline version, and the city says the real limit continues into Tampa Bay and Hillsborough Bay.
- **The city's beaches are bay beaches.** They are open sunrise to sunset and are not the Gulf strand the regional picture suggests.
- **Davis Islands is in the city.** It sits just outside downtown, built into the mouth of the river.
- **33602 is City Hall's ZIP, not a map of the city.**

I came looking for one picture. The official pictures disagree with each other on purpose, and they say so.

## FAQ

**Does a Tampa FL map show the real city limits?**
Usually not exactly. The City of Tampa says its shoreline boundary map is a modified version of the limits and is not the incorporated limits. The county clips its municipal map at the water's edge for drawing purposes. The legal boundary is set by ordinance, and the city's GIS address lookup is the tool to use.

**If my address says Tampa, am I inside the city?**
Not necessarily. The city says many Hillsborough County addresses include Tampa without being inside the city limits, and it names Temple Terrace and unincorporated parts of the county. Use the city's GIS address lookup to check.

**Is Tampa a Gulf beach town?**
The official city and county maps place it on Tampa Bay and Hillsborough Bay. The four beaches the city manages are all on Tampa Bay, not on the open Gulf.

**What are the city's beaches and when are they open?**
Ben T. Davis, Picnic Island, Cypress Point, and Davis Islands, open sunrise to sunset per city information. Check the Florida Department of Health's latest water test before swimming, and check [tampa.gov](https://www.tampa.gov/) for current details.

**Where can I find neighborhood boundaries?**
The city offers neighborhood maps and a find-a-neighborhood tool. Both are interactive, and the tool also covers demographics, land use, places of interest, association contacts, and meetings.

body:
# Tampa Lightning Tickets: Where to Buy Safely

I went after Tampa Lightning tickets on purpose, and not to write a team biography. I wanted three things: the actual window, the official seller, and the ways a resale outfit pretends to be the window. Most of the trouble with Tampa Lightning tickets comes from the last one.

This guide covers who sells Lightning tickets, how the box office works, what the phone numbers are, how student rush works, and why I would double-check any game time before leaving the hotel. For the team itself, see our [Tampa Bay Lightning page](/events/tampa-bay-lightning).

*Last updated: November 2, 2026*

![Illuminated yellow tickets sign against a dark background](/images/articles/tampa-lightning-tickets/lightning-tickets-17527817.webp)
*Photo by [Patrick](https://www.pexels.com/@patrick-88938360/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/tickets-text-on-yellow-wall-17527817/)*

## Quick answers: how to buy Tampa Lightning tickets

- **Who sells them:** Ticketmaster, or the ReliaQuest Ticket Office at the arena. The ticket office says the arena and the Lightning themselves are the only official sellers. Everything else is an outsider.
- **Format:** All tickets are mobile only. The Lightning say delivery includes mobile entry in the Ticketmaster app.
- **Where:** Benchmark International Arena, 401 Channelside Drive, Tampa, FL 33602.
- **Refunds:** None, and no exchanges, on tickets for a game, concert, or event at the arena. If a show is canceled or rescheduled, you go back to the original point of purchase.
- **Prices:** I am not quoting any. Neither the team nor the arena gave a seat price in what I read, so check [the official Lightning tickets page](https://www.nhl.com/lightning/tickets).

## The name: Tampa Lightning, Tampa Bay Lightning, and Amalie

People search for "Tampa Lightning" or "Lightning Tampa," but the club calls itself the Tampa Bay Lightning. Same team, and it is the NHL club you are after.

The building is Benchmark International Arena. Vinik Sports Group and Benchmark International announced a multi-year naming deal on August 13, 2025, and beginning that day AMALIE Arena officially became Benchmark International Arena. It is the same downtown building. The announcement describes it as debuting in 1996, with 19,092 seats, publicly owned, with Vinik Sports Group holding the lease. It sits in the Water Street neighborhood, on the Channelside side of downtown, not the fairgrounds and not a suburban rink.

The old name still causes problems. The ReliaQuest ticket office still lists an Amalie Arena contact address for questions, even while it calls the building Benchmark International Arena. That is one reason old emails and old links still say Amalie. Seeing the old name on an official contact is fine. A website that still calls itself Amalie and asks for a card is another story, and I would not trust it. For the full building rundown, our [stadium guide](/events/tampa-stadium-guide) covers Tampa's venues side by side.

## Official sellers vs. everything else

This is where I think people get hurt. Tickets for games, concerts, and events are sold through Ticketmaster or at the ReliaQuest Ticket Office. The ticket office says it knows about imposter sellers built to look affiliated with the arena or the Lightning, and that anyone other than the arena and the Lightning themselves is not them.

I never found a named official resale marketplace for the Lightning. The Rays point fans to a resale partner. I found nothing like that for the Lightning, and I am not going to nominate one. My rule is simple: if the seat is not in the team account or in Ticketmaster through the team, I would assume I am the product.

Why this matters more than usual: the no-refund, no-exchange policy. If you bought from a lookalike and the game is rescheduled, "go back to the original point of purchase" is not much comfort when the original point of purchase is a stranger. I am also not going to print a resale fee table, because I never saw one from an official source.

## Mobile tickets only

All tickets are mobile. Put yours in the Ticketmaster app and do not rely on a screenshot. I would not plan on a paper ticket at the window, and I would not call the main arena line expecting a will-call miracle when the team says the ticket lives on your phone. Confirm current entry policy on [the Lightning tickets page](https://www.nhl.com/lightning/tickets).

## Who to call

The team and arena publish a full phone list, and I am writing it down because otherwise I would call the wrong desk:

| Need | Number |
|---|---|
| Ticketmaster, individual game tickets | 1-800-745-3000 |
| ReliaQuest Ticket Office | 813-301-2500 |
| Benchmark International Arena | 813-301-6500 |
| Season-ticket member services | 813-301-6800 |
| Group sales and party areas | 813-301-6900 |
| Premium suites | 813-301-2505 |
| Accessible seating | 813-301-6700 |

Lost and found is handled by the arena itself. I never saw a list of what they were holding, so call the arena line if you left something behind.

## The box office window: hours and location

Both the arena and the Lightning put the ReliaQuest Ticket Office on the west side of the venue. It is open on event days only.

- **Lightning games:** both sources say it opens three hours before puck drop and runs until the end of the second period.
- **Concerts and other shows:** it opens three hours before the ticketed show time. As far as I was told, there is no stated closing point.
- **Holidays:** the Lightning say it is closed on major holidays unless an event is happening, and that holiday hours can change, so call 813-301-2500.

I found no regular weekday window for a random Tuesday with no event. If I showed up midweek to buy at the door, by their own description I would find it shut. Plan around event days. For what else is happening around town on those nights, see our [Tampa events guide](/events/tampa-events).

### Payment at the window

This is the one direct disagreement between sources. The arena says the office accepts VISA, MasterCard, and American Express. The ReliaQuest ticket office says VISA, MasterCard, American Express, and Discover. Same office, two lists. I would bring a card that appears on both lists and not be the person who finds out which version is current. I also saw no service fee and no ticket price from either source, so I am not putting numbers here.

## The 2026-27 season in plain terms

The team announced the 2026-27 regular-season schedule, presented by AdventHealth, on July 16, 2026. The headline is the length: the Bolts play 84 games, not the old 82, split 42 home and 42 road. The breakdown:

- Each Atlantic Division opponent four times (two home, two road): 28 divisional games
- Each Metropolitan Division team three times: 24 games
- Western Conference teams twice: 32 games

That adds up to 84. The schedule opened on the road with one game in New York against the Rangers on October 1. The home opener was Saturday, October 3, against the Washington Capitals at Benchmark International Arena, the first game of a three-game homestand.

Other notes straight from the announcement:

- Two six-game homestands: November 14 to 27, and February 12 to 23.
- November has eight home games, the most of any month. December and February have seven each.
- Florida, the cross-state rival, does not come to Tampa until 2027 on this schedule, with home dates of February 16 and March 23.
- Carolina, called the Stanley Cup champion in the announcement, makes its only visit on November 25.
- Montreal comes December 31 and April 8, which the team calls a rematch of the 2026 first-round series.

I am not reproducing the whole calendar here. For the full list of dates and times, use the [official Lightning schedule](https://www.nhl.com/lightning/schedule).

### Check the time on the ticket itself

Here is a catch I would not skip. The team's single-game ticket schedule runs month by month, with each home game listed with a time and a way to buy. The ticket packs for 2026-27 were also on sale when I checked, and some times disagree:

- Single-game schedule: Capitals, Tuesday, November 17, 7 p.m. ET. Packs: Washington, Tuesday, November 17, 7:30 p.m. ET.
- Single-game schedule: Flyers, Thursday, March 25, 7 p.m. ET. Packs: Philadelphia, Thursday, March 25, 6:30 p.m. ET.

Same opponents, different clocks, both straight from the Lightning. Some dates match: October 5 versus Philadelphia at 7 p.m. and October 8 versus Minnesota at 7 p.m. line up between the two. I am not picking a winner on the mismatched ones. Look at the ticket itself before you decide when to leave the hotel.

One more date caution: October 4 is not a Lightning home game on the single-game schedule. The first October home date listed there is Monday, October 5, against the Flyers at 7 p.m. ET, then the Wild on Thursday, October 8, at 7 p.m. ET. Anyone hunting "tickets today" on a non-game date will not find a game.

Single-game tickets went on sale to the public on Friday, August 14, at 10 a.m., with presales earlier that week. That on-sale is behind us now, so what you are buying this season is whatever the team and Ticketmaster still have.

## Discounts: student rush and other offers

Student rush is the one discount path the team actually describes, and it comes with no stated price.

- **College students:** you need a valid .edu address. Tickets are standing room only unless the offer says otherwise, drop at 10:00 a.m. on game days, and are non-transferable.
- **High school students without a .edu address:** go to the ReliaQuest Ticket Office on game day, starting three hours before puck drop, with a student ID, while supplies last. That is the same three-hour mark as the regular window, but it ends when the tickets are gone, not necessarily when the second period ends.

The team also offers GovX deals, theme nights, season-ticket interest forms, and group tickets. The group offer came with no minimum and no price, and I am leaving those blanks blank. Theme nights for 2026-27 are posted as a set, from opening night through fan appreciation, and giveaways are limited items at select home games. Those lists change, so the team is the place to check.

## Inside the building: payments and bags

The arena says its own retail and concession stands are cashless, with mobile ordering at select stands. It also says concert merchandise sales may not be cashless, so a hockey night and a concert are not the same wallet.

I never got a bag policy for this arena. I am leaving out any clear-bag size, since I have no policy in hand, and the football stadium and the baseball dome are different buildings with their own rules. Check the arena's site before you pack: [Benchmark International Arena](https://www.benchmarkintlarena.com/).

The arena's rebrand also renamed a premium level the Benchmark International Club Level, with The Mark described as its signature all-inclusive experience. I never saw a price for The Mark. Premium suites and group areas go through the phone numbers above.

## Don't mix up Tampa's other ticket offices

Asking about Tampa tickets kept turning up other buildings, so here is the separation:

- **Rays:** the 2026 team plays at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, not at this arena.
- **Bucs and USF:** Raymond James Stadium on Dale Mabry has its own ticket office in the south plaza, and the sports authority that runs it says it is the landlord there.
- **Seminole Hard Rock:** a name that comes up in the wider Tampa mix as a hotel and casino. It is not the Lightning box office.
- **Concerts:** the arena sells concert tickets at the same west-side office, on the concert clock described above. A concert, a Lightning game, and a movie are three different buys.

Do not drive to Channelside just because a search for Tampa tickets also surfaced the Bucs, the Rays, a casino, and a movie.

## Planning the trip

If you are coming in from out of town for a game, the arena is downtown on Channelside Drive, so a downtown stay keeps the night simple. Our [Tampa hotels guide](/guides/tampa-hotels) covers where to stay. I spent six months in Tampa (November 2025 to May 2026), staying downtown with my aunt and cousins, and that stretch is why I chased the ticketing details instead of the box scores. I did not find parking prices in anything I read, so I am leaving parking costs out.

## My short checklist

1. Buy from the team or from the ReliaQuest office on the west side, on a night there is an event.
2. Use a card that both payment lists agree on: VISA, MasterCard, or American Express.
3. Put the ticket in the Ticketmaster app, not a screenshot.
4. Ignore any seller that looks official and is not the arena or the team.
5. Trust the time printed on your ticket over a pack listing when they differ.
6. Do not pay a price you never saw written down by the team or Ticketmaster.

## FAQ

**Where is the best place to buy Tampa Lightning tickets?**
Ticketmaster or the ReliaQuest Ticket Office, because the ticket office says the arena and the Lightning themselves are the only official sellers. Start from [the Lightning tickets page](https://www.nhl.com/lightning/tickets).

**Are Lightning tickets mobile only?**
Yes. All tickets are mobile only, and the Lightning say delivery includes mobile entry in the Ticketmaster app.

**Can I get a refund on Lightning tickets?**
There are no refunds and no exchanges on a ticket for a concert, a game, or an event at the arena. If an event is canceled or rescheduled, you go back to the original point of purchase.

**When is the box office open?**
On event days only. For Lightning games it opens three hours before puck drop and runs until the end of the second period. For concerts and shows it opens three hours before show time. It is closed on major holidays unless an event is happening, so call 813-301-2500 to confirm.

**Is Amalie Arena the same as Benchmark International Arena?**
Yes. AMALIE Arena officially became Benchmark International Arena on August 13, 2025. It is the same building at 401 Channelside Drive, and the old name still shows up in some emails and contact addresses.

# Tampa Bay Lightning: Arena, Tickets and the 2026-27 Season

Last updated: November 2, 2026

If you are trying to figure out how to catch the Tampa Bay Lightning in person, there are three things worth sorting out before anything else: what the team and its building are actually called, how tickets work, and what the 2026-27 season looks like now that it is under way. This guide covers all three, using what the team and the arena have published, and points you to the official sites for anything that changes from week to week.

![Ice hockey players competing during a game](/images/articles/tampa-bay-lightning/lightning-88470.webp)
*Photo by [Pixabay](https://www.pexels.com/@pixabay/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/ice-hockey-88470/)*

## What people call the team: Tampa Lightning, Lightning Tampa, and the real name

The name people use in conversation is usually the short one. "Tampa Lightning" and "Lightning Tampa" both get typed into search boxes constantly, and both mean the same NHL club. The team calls itself the Tampa Bay Lightning. There is no separate club called the Tampa Lightning, and the order of the words does not change who you are looking for.

This guide is about that NHL team, the building it plays in, and the season the team has described. The official club site is [nhl.com/lightning](https://www.nhl.com/lightning), and that is where the live schedule and roster details belong. I have kept anything that changes out of this page rather than building a calendar from dates the team did not give.

## The arena: Benchmark International Arena, not Amalie anymore

The first thing that trips people up is the building. The team gives its home as **Benchmark International Arena, 401 Channelside Drive, Tampa, FL 33602**. That is downtown, on the Channelside and Water Street side of the city. It is not out by the fairgrounds and it is not a suburban rink.

### The name change

I kept hearing the old name in my own head, so I went back to the naming announcement. Vinik Sports Group and Benchmark International announced a multi-year naming deal on August 13, 2025. Beginning that day, AMALIE Arena officially became Benchmark International Arena. AMALIE Motor Oil stayed on as a corporate partner, but the name came off the building.

So when someone tells you the Lightning still play at Amalie, you will know what they mean. People will keep saying it for a while. The official name, though, changed in August 2025, and the signs, the ticket window, and the arena's own materials use Benchmark International Arena. If you are navigating, follow the sign that says Benchmark International Arena at 401 Channelside. The arena's official site is [benchmarkintlarena.com](https://www.benchmarkintlarena.com/).

### What the announcement says about the building

The company describes the venue this way:

- It debuted in 1996.
- It is the 19,092-seat downtown home of the Lightning.
- It is publicly owned, with Vinik Sports Group holding the lease.
- It sits in the Water Street neighborhood.
- The Lightning are three-time Stanley Cup champions: 2004, 2020, and 2021.
- The building has hosted three Stanley Cup championships since 1996.

The rebrand includes new exterior and interior signage and a premium level renamed the Benchmark International Club Level, with The Mark described as its signature all-inclusive experience. I never saw a price for The Mark, so I will not put a number on it. The deal also mentions more than $3 million in nonprofit contributions. That is a partnership figure, not a ticket price, and it is worth keeping separate in your head when you are budgeting for a night out.

## Tickets: mobile only, and the phone list is the useful part

The team says tickets for games, concerts, and most events are bought at the ReliaQuest Ticket Office or through Ticketmaster, and that **all tickets are mobile only**. Do not plan on picking up a paper ticket at a window. Your ticket lives on your phone, so charge it before you leave the hotel.

For a fuller walkthrough of buying paths, see the companion guide to [Lightning tickets](/events/tampa-lightning-tickets).

### Who to call

The most practical part of the team's ticketing information is the list of numbers. Different desks handle different things, and calling the wrong one wastes time. These are the numbers the team publishes, and it is worth confirming them on the official sites before you dial:

| Need | Number |
|---|---|
| Benchmark International Arena (main) | 813-301-6500 |
| ReliaQuest Ticket Office | 813-301-2500 |
| Season ticket member services | 813-301-6800 |
| Group sales and party areas | 813-301-6900 |
| Premium suites | 813-301-2505 |
| Accessible seating | 813-301-6700 |
| Ticketmaster (individual game tickets) | 1-800-745-3000 |

The ReliaQuest Ticket Office listing also includes a Vinik Sports Group box office email, which you will find on the arena site.

A few practical notes on using that list:

- **Individual game tickets** go through Ticketmaster or the ReliaQuest window.
- **Season seats, groups, suites, and accessible seating** each have their own number. Do not call the main arena line and expect a will-call fix when the team says your ticket is on your phone.
- **Lost and found** is handled by the arena itself. I never saw a list of what they were holding, so I cannot describe a process beyond the number and the desk. Start with the main arena line.

I do not have a ticket price, and the team's announcement did not give one, so I am not quoting a number here. Check Ticketmaster or the club site for current pricing.

## The 2026-27 season: what the team announced

The team announced the 2026-27 regular season schedule, presented by AdventHealth, on **July 16, 2026**. For anyone who grew up on an 82-game season, the headline is the length: the Bolts play **84 games**.

### How the 84 games break down

The announcement spells out the structure so you can add it up yourself:

- **Atlantic Division opponents:** four games each, two at home and two on the road, for 28 divisional games.
- **Metropolitan Division opponents:** three games each, 24 games.
- **Western Conference opponents:** two games each, 32 games.

That adds to 84. Home and road split evenly, 42 and 42.

### How the season started

The team opened on the road, with one game in New York at Madison Square Garden against the Rangers on October 1. The team recorded that opening night as a 5-1 loss to the Rangers. The home opener came the next Saturday, **October 3**, against the Washington Capitals at Benchmark International Arena, the first game of a three-game homestand. The team promoted a 2026 home-opener pregame guide for that night. I am not writing a Capitals score, because the team was still framing that game as the home opener rather than as a final I could repeat.

### Homestands, road trips, and busy months

The schedule has a few shapes worth knowing if you are planning a trip around a game:

- **Two six-game homestands:** November 14 through November 27, and February 12 through February 23.
- **Longest road trip:** four games, and the team makes a trip that long four times.
- **November** has eight home games, more than any other month.
- **December and February** have seven home games each.
- **December and March** have the most road games, eight each.
- **December** is the busiest month overall, with 15 games.

### Back-to-backs

There are 13 sets of back-to-back games. Eight of those sets are both games on the road. Four are split, one home and one away. One set is both games at Benchmark International Arena.

### Rivals and rematches

A few dates the team called out specifically:

- **Florida**, the cross-state rival, does not come to Tampa until 2027 on this schedule. The home dates named are February 16 and March 23.
- **Carolina**, called the Stanley Cup champion in the announcement, makes its only visit on November 25.
- **Montreal** comes December 31 and April 8. The team calls those games a rematch of the 2026 first-round series.

I am not filling in the other 80-odd dates from memory. Several later dates in the announcement came with start times, such as 7 p.m. ET, 3:30, 4 p.m., 5 p.m., or 2 p.m., but I could not pin an opponent to each one, and a partial list is how a fake schedule starts. For the full calendar, use the official page at [nhl.com/lightning/schedule](https://www.nhl.com/lightning/schedule).

### When single-game tickets went on sale

Single-game tickets were set to go on sale to the public on Friday, August 14, at 10 a.m., with presales through the week of August 10 and each group given its own time. That on-sale is well behind us now, so for current games you will be looking at what is available on Ticketmaster or the box office.

## Theme nights and giveaways

Theme nights for 2026-27 are posted as a set, from opening night through fan appreciation. Arena giveaways are limited items at select home games, and Hockey is for Everyone nights are a design series. I did not copy the item list or the artist list, because those change. The point is to go to the team for them rather than secondhand chatter. If a particular giveaway matters to you, check the club site close to game day.

## Getting to the game: Channelside and the downtown waterfront

The arena sits in downtown Tampa's Channelside waterfront district, in the Water Street neighborhood. That matters for planning, because it puts you close to the rest of downtown rather than in an isolated lot.

During the six months I spent in Tampa, from November 2025 to May 2026, I stayed downtown with my aunt and cousins, so the Channelside side of the city was part of my regular geography. I did not take notes on parking prices or lot rules, so I will not quote any. For parking and the rest of the in-and-out logistics, the [Tampa stadium guide](/events/tampa-stadium-guide) is the better starting point, and the arena site at [benchmarkintlarena.com](https://www.benchmarkintlarena.com/) is where current arena information lives.

If you are coming from out of town and want to stay close, the [Tampa hotels guide](/guides/tampa-hotels) covers neighborhoods, including waterfront options that make an evening game easy. Staying downtown is especially useful for games that run late or for back-to-back travel weekends.

## Planning a Lightning trip around other Tampa events

A game night fits easily into a longer visit. Hockey season overlaps with a lot of what else is happening in the city, so it is worth checking the [Tampa events calendar](/events/tampa-events) when you pick your dates. The long homestands are the easiest windows if you want to see more than one game: November 14 through 27 and February 12 through 23 are both six-game stretches at home.

If you only have one night, the tightest plan is to pick a date from the official schedule, buy through Ticketmaster or the ReliaQuest Ticket Office, and keep your phone charged for entry.

## What I thought people were struggling with

Putting the research together, three points of confusion kept coming up.

**The name.** "Tampa Lightning" and "Lightning Tampa" are how people say it, but the club is the Tampa Bay Lightning. The building is no longer Amalie in anything official. It is Benchmark International Arena, 401 Channelside Drive, Tampa, FL 33602, with 19,092 seats, downtown, since the August 13, 2025 change.

**The phone tree.** Individual tickets go through Ticketmaster or the ReliaQuest window and are mobile only. Season seats, groups, suites, and accessible seating each have their own number.

**The season length.** The 2026-27 schedule is 84 games, not 82, with the division-by-division breakdown laid out so you can check the math. The home opener was October 3, 2026, against Washington, after an October 1 road game at the Rangers.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is "Tampa Lightning" the same team as the Tampa Bay Lightning?

Yes. "Tampa Lightning" and "Lightning Tampa" are shorthand for the Tampa Bay Lightning, the NHL club. There is no separate team by those names.

### Where do the Lightning play?

At Benchmark International Arena, 401 Channelside Drive, Tampa, FL 33602, in downtown Tampa's Channelside and Water Street area.

### Is it still called Amalie Arena?

No. AMALIE Arena officially became Benchmark International Arena on August 13, 2025. AMALIE Motor Oil remained a corporate partner, but the building uses the new name. You will still hear the old name in conversation.

### How do I get Lightning tickets?

The team says tickets are sold through the ReliaQuest Ticket Office or Ticketmaster, and that all tickets are mobile only. See the [Lightning tickets guide](/events/tampa-lightning-tickets) for buying paths, and confirm numbers and availability on the official sites.

### How many games are in the 2026-27 season?

The Lightning play 84 games in 2026-27, 42 at home and 42 on the road, according to the schedule announced on July 16, 2026. Check [nhl.com/lightning/schedule](https://www.nhl.com/lightning/schedule) for the full calendar.

## What I would tell a friend

The Tampa Bay Lightning play at Benchmark International Arena on Channelside, the building that was AMALIE Arena until August 13, 2025. The 2026-27 season, presented by AdventHealth, is an 84-game schedule announced July 16, 2026, with 42 games at home. I do not have a ticket price, a parking price, or a full calendar to hand you, and I would rather point you to the club and arena sites than put a stand-in number on the page.

# Tampa Rays Schedule: Home Dates, Venue and Tickets

Last updated: November 2, 2026

The Tampa Rays schedule is easy to misread, and the mistakes are predictable. People see "Tampa" and head downtown. They see a game on the grid and assume the Rays sell the ticket. They grab the wrong year or the wrong spring or regular-season list. I sat down with the schedule on Sunday, October 4, 2026, which turned out to be a good day to learn it, because the schedule has a gap on exactly that date. This guide is about how the schedule is put together and how to read it, not about a night at the park.

![Baseball and bat on a green field ready for a game](/images/articles/tampa-rays-schedule/rays-schedule-1092671.webp)
*Photo by [Pixabay](https://www.pexels.com/@pixabay/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/ball-ballpark-baseball-baseball-bat-1092671/)*

## The venue column is the trick

The team on the schedule is the **Tampa Bay Rays**, not a club named Tampa. The team calls its ballpark Tropicana Field, home of the Rays, at 1 Tropicana Drive, St. Petersburg, FL 33705. MLB's ballpark page for the club lists the same home venue: Tropicana Field, St. Petersburg.

So home games are in St. Petersburg. If the word Tampa sends you toward downtown Tampa, you are reading the nickname and skipping the venue column, and that column is the whole trick. If you are coming from the Tampa side, the [Tampa to St. Petersburg guide](/guides/tampa-to-st-petersburg) covers the trip, and the [Tropicana Field page](/events/tropicana-field) covers the building. For team background, see the [Tampa Bay Rays overview](/events/tampa-bay-rays).

## How to read a single game

The rule I use is simple. The venue is the park, and the home team is whoever is listed after the at-sign.

- If the Rays are the home team, the game is at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, and the time the club gives is Eastern.
- If the Rays are the away team, the venue is the other club's park, and the ticket warning below applies.

The team's public schedule separates home and away from the full-season view and notes that all times are Eastern unless otherwise noted, subject to change.

## Away games: buy from the home club

This is the warning I wish more people read. If you have picked an away game, tickets are bought from the home club for that date. A game on the Rays schedule is not always a Rays ticket. Road games belong to whoever is hosting. Tickets follow the venue: home means St. Petersburg and the Trop, and away means you are buying from the other club. The Rays' own [ticket page](https://www.mlb.com/rays/tickets) is the place for home dates.

## Where to get the full schedule

I used MLB's full-season schedule for this club, because the team's own version does not show the whole year at once. The team also offers a downloadable schedule for CSV, home and away files, at the [Rays downloadable schedule](https://www.mlb.com/rays/schedule/downloadable-schedule), with the same caveat on the schedule itself: dates, times and opponents can change. The main grid lives at the [MLB Rays schedule page](https://www.mlb.com/rays/schedule).

## Reading the 2026 regular season without double-counting

The 2026 regular season on MLB's full-season view has 164 rows and 162 dates. That is not 164 games played, and the status column explains why.

- 162 rows are final.
- Two rows are still marked postponed, both for rain: May 9, 2026, Rays at Boston, and May 23, 2026, Rays at the Yankees.
- Both were made up as split doubleheaders, which is why a single date can hold two games. July 17 at Fenway is the Boston makeup. September 22 at Yankee Stadium is the Yankees makeup, and MLB labels that first game "Makeup of 5/23 PPD."

If you count every line, you double-count two rainouts that are still sitting there after they were played. The postponed rows did not vanish from the schedule, which is exactly how a schedule snapshot misleads.

The final tally was 81 home games and 81 road games, and every one of the 81 home games was at Tropicana Field. The road games were at other parks.

MLB had the 2026 regular season opening March 26, Rays at the St. Louis Cardinals, at Busch Stadium. The last regular-season date was September 27, Rays at the Philadelphia Phillies, at Citizens Bank Park. There was no regular-season home game after that, so October baseball on this schedule is postseason only.

## Spring training is a separate schedule

Spring training is its own schedule, and the team keeps it separate from the regular season. Anyone searching for the Tampa Rays baseball schedule in February or March needs this section.

- The 2026 spring schedule ran from February 21 through March 24 and had 30 games.
- The 13 home spring games I counted were at Charlotte Sports Park in Port Charlotte, not at Tropicana Field.
- The team thanked fans for joining them in Port Charlotte that spring and said they would be back the next spring.

So a "home" game in February is not a drive to St. Petersburg, and it is not a drive to Tampa either. Same team name, different park, different city. The spring box office at Charlotte Sports Park sells tickets only for the spring games played there, which is another way to end up with the wrong ticket if you mix up the two schedules.

## 2027 is already posted

The 2027 regular-season schedule was released July 16, 2026, per the team's [MLB press release](https://www.mlb.com/press-release/rays-announce-2027-regular-season-schedule). It opens March 25–27, 2027, against the Orioles at Tropicana Field. Game times were to be announced later, and the schedule is subject to change.

The 2027 spring training schedule is also out. In October it is easy to grab the schedule a year forward and think you are still looking at the current month. Check the year in the header before you plan anything.

## The October 2026 stretch: ALDS against the Yankees

On the day I looked, the current stretch was the American League Division Series against the New York Yankees. MLB listed five games, and none of them was October 4. That Sunday was an off day.

| Game | Date | Matchup | Venue | Status when checked | First pitch (Eastern) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Sat, Oct 3 | Yankees at Rays | Tropicana Field | Final | 6:30 p.m. |
| 2 | Mon, Oct 5 | Yankees at Rays | Tropicana Field | Scheduled | 8:00 p.m. |
| 3 | Wed, Oct 7 | Rays at Yankees | Yankee Stadium | Scheduled | 8:00 p.m. |
| 4 | Thu, Oct 8 | Rays at Yankees | Yankee Stadium | Scheduled | 8:00 p.m. |
| 5 | Sat, Oct 10 | Yankees at Rays | Tropicana Field | Scheduled | 8:00 p.m. |

Home games in this series are at the Trop. Road games are in the Bronx. There is no Tampa venue in the series.

### Why a five-game list does not mean five games

A five-game list can look like all five will be played. MLB says the Division Series is a best-of-five in a 2-2-1 format, with home-field advantage to the higher seed. The Rays schedule matches the home side of that shape: Games 1, 2 and 5 at their park, Games 3 and 4 at the other park.

Because it is a best-of-five, a series can end before the last date. The schedule does not mark Games 4 and 5 as optional. It marks them scheduled. If I were buying for October 8 or October 10, I would treat those games as listed, not promised.

MLB's postseason format explains why the series exists. There are twelve teams, six per league. The top two seeds get a bye into the Division Series. The Wild Card round is a best-of-three, all at the higher seed's park, and teams are not reseeded after that. I did not look at standings for this note, so I am not assigning the Rays a seed.

## Is there a Rays game today?

On October 4, 2026, no. The question "is there a Tampa Rays game today" is the one that gets you in the car, so check the dates before you go. The club's postseason ticket offer listed three home dates for the ALDS, October 3, October 5 and October 10, and October 4 was not one of them. MLB's schedule from late September through mid-October showed the same dates and nothing on the 4th. It was an off day in the middle of a series.

On that off day, here is what the schedule showed:

- **Game 1** had been played the night before at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg and was final, Rays 1, Yankees 0.
- **The next home game** was Monday, October 5, at 8:00 p.m., Game 2, Yankees at Tropicana Field. Tickets were still on sale when I looked. Parking for that game was already sold out.
- **Postseason parking** at Tropicana Field is prepaid only, not drive-up. Once the Rays lots are gone, you are in downtown St. Petersburg overflow lots the club does not control.

### Naming differences on the later dates

The team labels October 10 at 8:00 p.m. as ALDS Home Game 3, while MLB calls it Game 5, the if-necessary game. Both can be true: it is the third game in St. Petersburg and the fifth game of the series. Read the date before you buy anything that only says "game 3."

The team also offered American League Championship Series home dates of October 12, October 13, October 19 and October 20, with tickets and parking on offer but no first-pitch time and no opponent listed. World Series tickets were on offer with no dates at all. I am not filling those in.

### Watch parties on road nights

The team advertised official Rays watch parties at Tropicana Field's Hall of Fame Bar & Grill for the road games. Game 3 was Wednesday, October 7, at 8 p.m., with doors at 7 p.m. Game 4, if necessary, was Thursday, October 8, at 8 p.m., with doors at 7 p.m. These are events at the ballpark on nights the team is in New York. They are not the game.

## Tickets and gate basics for a home date

Because most people reading a schedule are really planning to attend, here is what the team's fan guide says for home games at Tropicana Field.

- **Mobile only.** All tickets and parking passes are mobile only, through the MLB Ballpark app.
- **Help at the gates.** Box office staff are at Gates 1 and 4 on game days for mobile-ticket help, starting 90 minutes before first pitch.
- **Gate times.** Gates open 90 minutes before first pitch for Monday through Friday home games, and two hours before on Opening Day and on Saturday and Sunday home games. The postseason offer did not repeat a gate time, so confirm that with the team.
- **Kids.** Once a child reaches their second birthday, they need a game ticket.
- **Bags.** One clear single-compartment bag, no larger than 12 by 12 by 6 inches, and/or one non-clear fanny pack or clutch no larger than 5 by 7. Backpacks stay out.
- **Food and drink.** Outside food and drink are out, except one sealed water bottle of 20 ounces or less per ticketed fan. No metal, ceramic or glass bottles.
- **Strollers.** Allowed if they fit under the seat. Otherwise they are checked at the First or Third Base Food Hall under the escalator.
- **Payments.** The building is cash-free. There is a Republic Bank ATM in the Republic Bank Draft Room, plus reverse ATMs across from the Gate 3 guest services desk and in the 3rd Base Food Hall.
- **Alcohol.** None brought in or taken out, 21 with ID, two per person per purchase, and sales stop in the middle of the 8th.
- **Smoking.** Banned on the property, inside and outside.

### Parking and getting there

Prepaid parking, while it lasts, is in Lots 1, 2, 5, 6 and 7. ADA spots are in Lots 1 and 7, and charging is in Lots 1, 5 and 7, first come. Tailgating is allowed once the lots are open, with no big tents, open flames, charcoal or large commercial grills.

The guide is not consistent on a few points, so confirm these with the team on the day you go:

- **Rideshare.** The fan guide says Gate 1 guests go to Lot 8, and ADA guests plus Gates 4 and 5 use Trop Drive on 16th Street. The parking instructions say drop off at Gate 4.
- **The baseball shuttle.** One line says it operates during the 2026 season, and another line says 2024.
- **Street name.** The team gives the address as both 1 Tropicana Dr and 1 Tropicana Field Drive. Both are St. Petersburg, FL 33705, and the venue is Tropicana Field either way.

The SunRunner is described as every 15 minutes from 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. and every 30 minutes from 8 p.m. to midnight. The [Tampa to St. Petersburg guide](/guides/tampa-to-st-petersburg) helps with the drive from the Tampa side.

## What is not on the Rays schedule

These questions sit right next to this one, but none of them belongs to the Rays schedule:

- **Buccaneers dates** are at Raymond James Stadium, 4201 N. Dale Mabry Highway in Tampa. On Sunday, October 4 the Packers were at the Buccaneers at 1:00 p.m. Eastern. That is football, in Tampa, in a different building from the Trop.
- **Lightning nights, concerts and shows** each have their own venue and their own ticket source.
- **Seminole Hard Rock Hotel and Casino Tampa** is at 5223 Orient Road. It is a hotel, dining and concert destination, not a Rays ticket.

For the broader calendar, the [Tampa events hub](/events/tampa-events) collects what is happening around the city.

## A note on the old Tampa stadium information

Some older team information still refers to seeing a Rays game at George M. Steinbrenner Field in Tampa. The team's story about its return says Hurricane Milton tore the roof off Tropicana Field in October 2024, after Hurricane Helene, and that the club spent a season at Steinbrenner Field in Tampa before coming back. For 2026, home games were at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg. The team also mentions a proposed plan in Tampa, but I did not find a new building to send anyone to. If an old page puts a game in Tampa, check the date on it.

## FAQ

### Do the Rays play in Tampa?

The team is the Tampa Bay Rays, but home games are at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg. The 2026 schedule had 81 home games, all at that venue.

### Where do I buy tickets for a Rays away game?

From the home club for that date. The Rays do not sell tickets for road games.

### Is spring training at Tropicana Field?

No. The 2026 home spring games I counted, 13 of them, were at Charlotte Sports Park in Port Charlotte. Spring training is a separate schedule from the regular season.

### When does the 2027 Rays season start?

The 2027 regular season opens March 25–27, 2027, against the Orioles at Tropicana Field. Game times were still to be announced, and the schedule is subject to change.

### What time zone are the game times in?

Eastern, unless otherwise noted on MLB's schedule.
