# Tropicana Field: Rays Ballpark Guide to Gates, Bags and Parking

If you are searching for the "Tampa Rays stadium," the building you want is Tropicana Field, and it is not in Tampa. The address is 1 Tropicana Drive, St. Petersburg, FL 33705, across the bay from Tampa city limits. The Tampa Bay Rays call it home, and as of this writing nothing I found says a replacement stadium is open or that the club has left the Trop.

I sorted through all of this on Sunday, October 4, 2026, an off day while the Rays were already in postseason mode. This guide is about the building itself: how the gates work, what you can carry in, how parking behaves, how to get there, why so many people say "Tampa," and where the new-stadium plan stands. For game dates, head to the [Rays schedule](/events/tampa-rays-schedule) page, and for the team itself, see [Tampa Bay Rays](/events/tampa-bay-rays).

*Last updated: November 2, 2026. Gate times, bag rules and parking are set by the club and can change by game or by round, so confirm everything on the [official Rays ballpark page](https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark) before you leave.*

![Empty baseball diamond with dirt infield and green grass](/images/articles/tropicana-field/tropicana-374700.webp)
*Photo by [Pixabay](https://www.pexels.com/@pixabay/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/baseball-field-374700/)*

## Tropicana Field address and basics

- **Name:** Tropicana Field, home of the Rays
- **Address:** 1 Tropicana Drive, St. Petersburg, FL 33705
- **City:** St. Petersburg
- **Tickets:** mobile only, in the MLB Ballpark app
- **Payments inside:** cash-free (more on that below)

The club still uses the slogan "Back In the Burg," and it also talks about a "New Ballpark." The club gave me nothing usable about that new building, so I am not going to describe a rendering I never received from them. The later sections lay out what two separate accounts say about it.

## Is Tropicana Field in Tampa?

No. It is in St. Petersburg, on the other side of Tampa Bay. The team name says Tampa Bay, which covers the region, not the city. If you are staying downtown Tampa and planning a game, read [Tampa to St. Petersburg](/guides/tampa-to-st-petersburg) so the cross-bay trip does not catch you off guard.

Searching for the Rays stadium also pulls in a pile of unrelated results: the Seminole Hard Rock, the Bucs, the Lightning, AMC theaters, hotels and concerts. Two clarifications keep you from heading to the wrong place:

- **Raymond James Stadium** is where the Buccaneers play. It is not the Rays' ballpark. See the [stadium guide](/events/tampa-stadium-guide) for the Tampa venues.
- **Benchmark International Arena** is the Lightning's building. Also not the Trop.

## Tickets, gates and the box office

Tickets are mobile only. If you need help on game day, the box office at Gates 1 and 4 handles mobile tickets starting 90 minutes before first pitch. You can scan a QR code at the windows to buy. It is not a paper-ticket window. Spring training is a separate story: that happens at Charlotte Sports Park in Port Charlotte, and that box office only sells those games.

A few ticketing details from the fan guide:

- A child needs a ticket once they reach their second birthday.
- Gates open 90 minutes before first pitch Monday through Friday.
- Gates open two hours before first pitch on Opening Day and on Saturday and Sunday home games.
- All gates are wheelchair accessible.
- VIP Gate 4 is for suite holders and the named premium rooms: DEX Home Plate Club, The Baldwin Group Club, Two Rivers Home Plate Box, Chalk Box and Baseline Premier.
- Screening is the Evolv walk-through system.

Group sales are reachable at 727-825-3406, the number printed in the fan guide.

## Cash-free is not a suggestion

Tropicana Field is cash-free. You pay with credit cards, debit cards or Rays Wallet. If you only have cash, there are workarounds. A Republic Bank ATM sits in the Republic Bank Draft Room. Reverse ATMs, which convert your cash so you can spend it, are across from the Gate 3 guest services desk and in the 3rd Base Food Hall. Cash does not work at the counter until you convert it.

## Clear-bag rules and what stays outside

The bag policy is strict, so pack for it before you get to the gate.

**Allowed:**
- One single-compartment clear bag made of plastic, vinyl or PVC, no larger than 12 x 12 x 6 inches
- One non-clear fanny pack or clutch no larger than 5 x 7 inches

**Not allowed:** backpacks.

**Exceptions:** diaper bags when you are with a young child, and medical device bags.

I never saw a bag-check counter mentioned in the guide, so do not count on being able to drop a bag off. If you are unsure about a particular bag, check the [official ballpark page](https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark).

**Alcohol:** it cannot come in or go out. You have to be 21, the limit is two drinks per person per purchase, and sales stop in the middle of the 8th inning.

**Water and outside food:** the guide words this two different ways, so I am passing along both without trying to merge them. The food policy says one sealed, personal-sized bottle of water, with exceptions for medical reasons or childcare. The guest code says one sealed bottle of water, 20 ounces or less, or one empty plastic bottle or cup, per ticketed fan. When two official pages disagree, plan for the stricter reading and ask at the gate.

## Inside the building

Once you are in, a few landmarks are worth knowing:

- **First aid:** presented by Orlando Health St. Petersburg, located between Gates 3 and 4 on the 100 level behind home plate, staffed by St. Petersburg Fire and Rescue.
- **Elevators:** at Gates 1, 2, 4 and 6.
- **MaintenX SkyDeck:** reached by the Gate 6 elevator. It is described as all-inclusive, above left field, with ballpark fare, beer, wine and soft drinks. The guide gives no ticket price, so check the club for pricing.
- **Cownose Clubhouse:** a 35-foot, 10,000-gallon exhibit beyond the right-center field fence.
- **Netting:** runs from home plate to the foul poles at sections 137 and 138, which matters if you are picking seats near the field.
- **3rd Base Food Hall:** one of the two reverse ATM locations.

## Parking at Tropicana Field

Parking is part of the stadium experience here, and the October rules were the postseason version, so treat them as that and not as the everyday setup.

**2026 postseason parking:**
- Parking for all postseason games is prepaid only. The Rays say it will not be sold drive-up.
- If it sells out, overflow is downtown St. Petersburg. The Rays say they do not set the rates or rules there.
- Lot 1 is premium, for seats behind home plate.
- Lots 6 and 7 are general parking.

**Accessible parking:**
- Wheelchair spaces are in Lots 1 and 7, mostly Lot 7, and are van-accessible, entered from 3rd Avenue South or 4th Avenue South.
- St. Petersburg police watch the accessible spaces. If the placard holder is not in the car when it parks, the club says tickets can be written.

**Drop-off and rideshare:**
- Drop-off is in front of Gate 4, across from Lot 1 on 16th Street South.
- Rideshare is at Gate 4. ADA rideshare can use Gate 1 or Gate 4.
- Oversized vehicles may be sent elsewhere.

My own takeaway for a postseason game: do not count on buying parking at the lot. Prepay or pick another way in.

## Getting there without a car

The SunRunner stops on the north side of the field. It runs every 15 minutes from 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. and every 30 minutes from 8 p.m. to midnight. The fan guide also says a Looper baseball shuttle runs during the 2026 season. I never got trolley details, so I have no stops or times to share. If you are coming from the Tampa side, the cross-bay planning is in [Tampa to St. Petersburg](/guides/tampa-to-st-petersburg).

## The roof, the hurricanes and the 2025 detour

This is the reason so many people connect the Rays to Tampa, and the story is worth getting straight.

Hurricane Helene flooded the area a few days after the last 2024 home game. Thirteen days later, in October 2024, Hurricane Milton tore the roof apart. The ballpark belongs to the City of St. Petersburg, which the club says was obligated to make it playable again. By the club's telling, the repair came in at nearly $60 million, on schedule and on budget. A separate account later put St. Petersburg's repair at $59.7 million. Those are close but not identical, so I am leaving both.

Here is how the timeline reads:

- **2025 home games** were played at the Yankees' spring training ballpark across the bay, which the club names as Steinbrenner Field. There was no home rainout there. One line from the club puts the Trop at 72 degrees, which is why they wanted the dome back.
- **The last roof panel** went in on November 21, 2025.
- **AECOM Hunt**, which the club says helped build the place in 1990 when it was the Florida Suncoast Dome, ran the repair.
- **The reopening** the club built toward was against the Cubs, on a Monday at 4:10 p.m. ET, the first game in the building in 561 days. Ken Babby names April 6.
- **Seven cownose stingrays** that stayed inside during Milton are back in the clubhouse.
- **The new owners** paid for extra work on top of the city repair, including premium seating and a bigger video board.
- **The club dates** the inaugural Devil Rays game to March 31, 1998.

So the Tampa ballpark people remember from 2025 is the borrowed one. It was a temporary home, and it is not where the Rays play now.

## What is happening with the new stadium

When the club's return story was written, the long-term home was still "a proposed plan in Tampa," and the Trop was still theirs for the next three seasons. Ken Babby calls the Trop the home while they work on a forever home. That story does not describe a finished new building.

Two later accounts give different numbers, and I am not averaging them.

**August 28, 2026 account:**
- Hillsborough County commissioners voted 5-2, the day after Tampa City Council voted 4-3, on a new stadium and development in Tampa, ideally open for 2029.
- Total: $2.3 billion. The city contributes roughly $80 million, the county almost $800 million, and about $1.4 billion plus overruns is private.
- Location: near Hillsborough College's Dale Mabry campus.
- The county will own the stadium, the Rays pay $4 million a year in rent, and the lease is expected to run 35 years.
- The Trop lease runs through the end of the 2028 season, which matches "the next three seasons" if you count 2026 through 2028.

**October 2, 2026 figures:**
- $2.36 billion, 31,000 seats, a fixed roof, on the Hillsborough College campus, with the Rays committing $1.37 billion plus overruns.
- The mixed-use development around it is $8 billion to $10 billion, private, on 130 acres along Dale Mabry Highway, across from Raymond James Stadium and next to Steinbrenner Field.
- Bond validation is the next step, including $796 million from the county and $80 million from Tampa. Groundbreaking comes after validation.
- AECOM Hunt/Turner is named as already in pre-construction.
- Opening Day 2029 is a target, not something to plan a trip around.

That is why Raymond James Stadium keeps coming up when people search for the Rays' future home: the newer account puts the planned complex across the street from it. The Bucs are still not playing at this gate.

In short, the Tampa park in the August and October accounts is a financed plan beside a college, still waiting on bonds. Nothing I found says a replacement stadium is open in 2026 or that the Rays have left the Trop.

## What is next at the Trop

The Rays' 2027 season opens at Tropicana Field March 25 to 27 against the Orioles, according to the club's [2027 schedule press release](https://www.mlb.com/press-release/rays-announce-2027-regular-season-schedule). The release notes it is the first Tropicana Field opener since 2024. For the full slate, use the [Rays schedule](/events/tampa-rays-schedule) page.

## Quick tips for a game at the Trop

- Use a mobile ticket in the MLB Ballpark app.
- Bring a clear bag, or just a small clutch or fanny pack.
- Leave the backpack and the cash plan behind. Convert cash at a reverse ATM if you must.
- In the postseason, prepay parking or choose the SunRunner or rideshare.
- Arrive with the gate window in mind: 90 minutes before first pitch on weekdays, two hours before on weekends and Opening Day.

## FAQ

**Is Tropicana Field in Tampa?**
No. It is at 1 Tropicana Drive in St. Petersburg, across Tampa Bay from Tampa.

**What can I bring into Tropicana Field?**
One clear single-compartment bag (plastic, vinyl or PVC, up to 12 x 12 x 6 inches) plus one non-clear fanny pack or clutch up to 5 x 7. Backpacks are out, with exceptions for diaper bags with a young child and medical device bags. The water rules are worded two ways in the fan guide, so check the [official ballpark page](https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark) before you go.

**Can I pay with cash at Tropicana Field?**
Not directly. The park is cash-free, so use cards or Rays Wallet. Reverse ATMs across from the Gate 3 guest services desk and in the 3rd Base Food Hall convert cash.

**Can I buy parking at the lot on game day?**
For 2026 postseason games, no. Parking was prepaid only and not sold drive-up. If it sells out, overflow is downtown St. Petersburg, where the Rays say they do not set the rates or rules.

**Are the Rays moving to a new stadium in Tampa?**
A Tampa stadium near Hillsborough College's Dale Mabry campus is planned, with 2029 as a target, but it is waiting on bond validation. The Trop lease runs through the end of the 2028 season, and the Rays still play at Tropicana Field.

# Tampa Bay Rays: Where They Play and How to Go

*Last updated: November 2, 2026*

The Tampa Bay Rays play at Tropicana Field, 1 Tropicana Drive, St. Petersburg, Florida 33705. Not Tampa. If you drive toward downtown Tampa because the nickname dropped the word "Bay," you end up on the wrong side of the bridge. The team's own slogan makes the point: Back In the Burg.

I came at this the way a visitor does, with a city and a sport in my head and the hope that the obvious answer was the building. It is not. The team corrected the city before it corrected anything else. This guide covers where the Rays play, why people still say "Tampa stadium," how the 2027 schedule starts, what a game day at the Trop requires, and where the long-term stadium story stands.

![Crowd watching a baseball game from the stands on a sunny day](/images/articles/tampa-bay-rays/rays-25547645.webp)
*Photo by [NIKOLAI FOMIN](https://www.pexels.com/@nikolai-fomin-2148174933/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/view-of-the-baseball-game-at-the-wrigley-field-in-chicago-illinois-25547645/)*

## Where the Tampa Bay Rays play

Home is Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg. The team's ballpark page confirms the address, and you can check the details at the [official MLB Rays ballpark page](https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark). For more on the building itself, see our [Tropicana Field guide](/events/tropicana-field).

The ballpark belongs to the City of St. Petersburg, not to the club. That matters for the next section, because it explains a year when the team played somewhere else.

## Why people still say "Tampa" (and where Steinbrenner Field fits)

The confusion is not a dumb one. For a year, the home games really were in Tampa.

According to the club's own story about the return, Hurricane Helene flooded the Tampa Bay area a few days after the last 2024 home game. Thirteen days later, in October 2024, Hurricane Milton tore the Tropicana Field roof apart. The Rays spent the 2025 season outdoors at Tampa's George M. Steinbrenner Field, the Yankees' spring training ballpark across the bay.

The city was contractually obligated, the club says, to put the ballpark back in playable condition. The team's account puts the repair at nearly $60 million, on schedule and on budget. Another account I read later puts St. Petersburg's repair at $59.7 million. Those two figures are close but not identical, so I am leaving both.

The team says they returned for a home game against the Cubs on Monday, April 6, 2026, first pitch 4:10 p.m. ET, the first game in the building in 561 days. By the time I was paying attention it was October, the team was celebrating October baseball returning to the Trop, and a completed game against the Yankees was already on the board. The return is not a plan anymore. It happened.

One wrinkle: the team's "Updates From Under the Roof" page still reads as if the April 6 reopening is ahead of them. I trust the schedule and the ticket sales for where a game is, and I would not treat that page as proof about whether the doors are open.

So the short version: 2025's home was Steinbrenner Field in Tampa, on purpose, because the roof was gone. The home now is the Trop. Don't confuse either one with the Tampa Tarpons, who play at Steinbrenner as a minor-league club. The Rays and the Tarpons are different teams, and the [MiLB Tampa page](https://www.milb.com/tampa) covers the Tarpons.

## Three parks, one team name

People fold three addresses into "the Tampa stadium":

- **Tropicana Field**, St. Petersburg: the Rays' regular-season home.
- **George M. Steinbrenner Field**, Tampa: the 2025 temporary home, and the Yankees' spring training park.
- **Charlotte Sports Park**, Port Charlotte: the Rays' spring training home, per the team's A-to-Z guide.

Spring training parking at Charlotte Sports Park, according to that guide, is $15 plus tax, cash-free and mobile only, through the MLB Ballpark app. You can use the main lot or the Charlotte County Fairgrounds lot across El Jobean Road, and lots open two and a half hours before first pitch. That is not Tropicana Field and it is not Steinbrenner Field. Three parks, three cities, one nickname. Writing that down was the point of the whole exercise.

## The 2027 schedule

The Rays announced their 2027 regular-season schedule on July 16, 2026. The press release describes 2027 as the start of the club's 30th season. Here is how it opens:

- **March 25–27:** home vs. the Baltimore Orioles at Tropicana Field
- **March 29–31:** home vs. the Los Angeles Angels
- **April 2–5:** first road trip, at the Minnesota Twins
- **April 6–8:** at the Texas Rangers

The schedule is subject to change, and game times are announced later. The [official Rays press release](https://www.mlb.com/press-release/rays-announce-2027-regular-season-schedule) has the full slate. If you want a CSV or calendar file, the [downloadable schedule page](https://www.mlb.com/rays/schedule/downloadable-schedule) has it. We keep a running summary on our [Rays schedule page](/events/tampa-rays-schedule) too.

## Tickets, bags, and cash at the Trop

This is where a Tampa visitor gets turned around even after accepting St. Petersburg. Going by the team's fan guide and parking information:

**Tickets.** Mobile only, in the MLB Ballpark app. The box office at Gates 1 and 4 is open on game days, starting 90 minutes before first pitch, to help with mobile tickets. It is not a window that hands you a paper ticket. You can also scan a QR code at the windows to buy. The team points to SeatGeek as its resale path. For current prices, use the [official Rays ticket page](https://www.mlb.com/rays/tickets). I won't quote a price I can't back up, with one exception noted below.

**Kids.** A child needs a ticket starting at their second birthday. Under 2 can sit on an adult's lap.

**Cash.** The ballpark is cash-free. Credit cards, debit cards, and Rays Wallet are what concessions, the team store, and parking take. A Republic Bank ATM sits in the Republic Bank Draft Room. Reverse ATMs, which convert your cash to a card, are across from the Gate 3 guest services desk and in the 3rd Base Food Hall.

**Bags.** The rule is clear-bag. You can bring one single-compartment clear bag (plastic, vinyl, or PVC) no larger than 12 by 12 by 6 inches, plus one small non-clear clutch or fanny pack no larger than 5 by 7. Backpacks and other non-transparent bags stay out. Diaper bags with a small child and medical bags are the exceptions the guide names. I never saw a bag-check counter mentioned, so if you bring the wrong bag, plan on walking it back to the car.

**Alcohol.** You must be 21. It is two drinks per person per purchase, sales stop in the middle of the 8th inning, and you cannot bring alcohol in or take it out.

**Outside drinks.** The guide words this two ways. The food policy says one sealed, personal-sized water bottle, with exceptions for medical reasons or childcare. The code of conduct says one sealed bottle of water, 20 ounces or less, or one empty plastic bottle or cup, per ticketed fan. I am not flattening those into one rule.

**Gates.** Per the fan guide, gates open 90 minutes before first pitch Monday through Friday, and two hours before on Opening Day and on Saturday and Sunday home games. Security is an Evolv walk-through. All gates are wheelchair accessible.

A few small things I would have guessed wrong: small cowbells are allowed, brooms have to be under 3 feet, and kids run the bases after Sunday home games. The Rays dugout is on the first-base side, even-numbered sections are on that side too, and seat 1 is on the left when you face the field. Protective netting runs to the foul poles at sections 137 and 138, and the guide notes that netting is not the same as no risk.

## Parking and getting there

Parking is the part that changes with the calendar. The team's parking information was already in postseason mode when I looked: parking for all postseason games at Tropicana Field is prepaid only, with no drive-up sales. If it sells out, overflow is downtown St. Petersburg, and the Rays say they do not set the rates or rules at those lots. I saw tickets still on sale for an October 5 game at 8:00 p.m. while parking was already sold out. A ticket and a place for the car are not the same purchase.

- **Lot 1** is the premium lot, recommended for premium seats behind home plate.
- **Lots 6 and 7** are general parking.
- **Wheelchair spaces** are in Lots 1 and 7, mostly Lot 7, entered from 3rd Avenue South or 4th Avenue South. They are van-accessible. St. Petersburg police watch the accessible spaces, and the team says tickets can be written if the placard holder is not in the car when it parks.
- **Drop-off** is in front of Gate 4, across from Lot 1 on 16th Street South.
- **Rideshare** is at Gate 4, per the parking information. ADA rideshare can use Gate 1 or Gate 4. The fan guide gives a different instruction for 2026: guests heading to Gate 1 get dropped in Lot 8, and ADA guests plus Gates 4 and 5 get dropped on Trop Drive on 16th Street. Same club, two instructions. Confirm which is current the morning of the game.
- **Oversized vehicles** may be sent to another lot.

If you would rather not drive, the team describes the SunRunner, a bus rapid transit route with a stop on the north side of the field. It runs every 15 minutes from 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. and every 30 minutes from 8 p.m. to midnight.

The fan guide also mentions a baseball shuttle, the Looper trolley. One heading says it operates during the 2026 season, while the parking section says the 2024 season. I never got stop details, so I can't tell you it is running or where it stops.

Coming from the Tampa side, our [Tampa to St. Petersburg guide](/guides/tampa-to-st-petersburg) covers the trip across the bay. For a broader look at the area's venues, see our [Tampa stadium guide](/events/tampa-stadium-guide).

## Inside the rebuilt Trop

I only kept what the team's update stated plainly. The last roof panel went in on November 21, 2025. AECOM Hunt, the firm the club says helped build the place in 1990 when it was the Florida Suncoast Dome, ran the repair. The fabric was designed by the Serge Ferrari Group in France, produced in Germany as PTFE-coated fiberglass, cut and sewn in China into 24 panels, then shipped to St. Petersburg. Each panel weighed about 5,000 pounds, and crews worked on ropes more than 200 feet up.

The field is new. The update describes a three-quarter-inch pad on the concrete, more than 137,000 square feet of Shaw Sports Turf, 450 tons of DuraEdge infield clay, and a warning-track mix of walnut shell and sand. The club says the new ownership group paid for extra work on top of the city's repair, including premium seating and an expanded video board.

Players quoted by the club missed the air-conditioning. One line puts the building at 72 degrees and notes there was not a single home rainout at Steinbrenner, which is a compliment to the temporary park and still a reason they wanted the dome back.

Premium areas named in the update include a Home Plate Box, a Baseline Premier section behind the Rays bullpen, and a Chalk Box on the first baseline. The MaintenX SkyDeck above left field is all-inclusive, with food, beer, wine, and soft drinks, and the team says tickets start at $49. That is the only ticket price I am repeating. The seven cownose stingrays that rode out Milton inside the building are back in a Cownose Clubhouse beyond the right-center field fence, and the Longoria and Iwamura statues are back at Gate 4.

## The long-term stadium question

The Trop is the home today, and the long-term argument is not fully settled. The club's return story says it has spent decades trying to lock in a long-term home, with high hopes for a proposed plan in Tampa, and that Tropicana Field was still theirs for the next three seasons. Ken Babby is quoted calling the Trop the home of the Tampa Bay Rays while they work on a forever home. The Devil Rays history in the same story starts with an inaugural game on March 31, 1998.

Later accounts I read add detail, though the numbers don't match. As of August 28, 2026, the report was that Hillsborough County commissioners voted 5-2, the day after Tampa City Council voted 4-3, on a new stadium and development in Tampa, ideally open for 2029. That account used a figure of $2.3 billion, with the city contributing roughly $80 million, the county almost $800 million, and about $1.4 billion plus overruns private. By October 2, 2026, the figures I was given were $2.36 billion, 31,000 seats, a fixed roof, on the Hillsborough College campus. In that version the Rays commit $1.37 billion plus overruns, public money is $796 million from the county and $80 million from Tampa, and the mixed-use development around the stadium is $8 billion to $10 billion, private, on 130 acres along Dale Mabry Highway. Bond validation is the next step, with groundbreaking after. Opening Day 2029 is a target, not something to plan a trip around.

I am not averaging those figures. Nothing I found says a replacement stadium is open in 2026 or that the Rays have left the Trop. The August account says the Trop lease runs through the end of the 2028 season. The Tampa site in those accounts is a financed plan, still waiting on bonds.

## Mixing up the Rays with other Tampa Bay events

Searches for a Tampa game or night out pull in Seminole Hard Rock, the Bucs, the Lightning, concerts, and shows. None of those is this gate. Raymond James Stadium comes up in the newer plan because it sits across Dale Mabry Highway from the proposed site, which is why the Bucs keep showing up in the same conversation. For a Rays game, the building is the Trop in St. Petersburg.

## What I would tell a visitor

The team is the Tampa Bay Rays, American League East, and the official home ballpark is Tropicana Field at 1 Tropicana Drive in St. Petersburg. The Tampa stadium people remember is Steinbrenner Field, and that was the 2025 hurricane detour, not the current home. Spring training is Charlotte Sports Park in Port Charlotte. For a game at the Trop, use a mobile ticket, bring a clear bag, expect no cash at the counter, and in the postseason do not count on buying parking at the lot. The point, for me, is the building and getting to the right side of the bridge.

## FAQ

**Do the Tampa Bay Rays play in Tampa?**
No. Home games are at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg. The 2025 season was played at Steinbrenner Field in Tampa because Hurricane Milton damaged the Trop roof in October 2024.

**When do the Rays open the 2027 season at home?**
The Rays open 2027 at Tropicana Field March 25–27 against the Baltimore Orioles, then host the Los Angeles Angels March 29–31. The schedule is subject to change and game times are announced later.

**Where is Rays spring training?**
Charlotte Sports Park in Port Charlotte, Florida. The team lists parking there at $15 plus tax, mobile only, through the MLB Ballpark app.

**Can I pay cash at a Rays game?**
No. The ballpark is cash-free. There are ATMs and reverse ATMs inside if you need to convert cash.

**Is a new Rays stadium being built?**
A plan for a new stadium in Tampa near Hillsborough College's Dale Mabry campus has been reported, targeting a 2029 opening. As of the latest reports I found, it was waiting on bond validation, and the Rays still play at Tropicana Field.

# Tampa Buccaneers: Schedule, Radio and Raymond James Guide

People type "tampa bucs" and "bucs tampa" into a search bar, and what they usually want is the team: the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, football, not a concert and not baseball. I put this page together around Sunday, October 4, 2026, when the Packers were in town and the Buccaneers were 0-3. It covers where the team plays, how to watch and listen, how the 2026 schedule shapes up, and how to get to the stadium without ending up at the wrong building. The schedule is the team's own, and I flag the places where the team's own pages disagree with each other.

*Last updated: November 2, 2026. Schedules, kickoff times, and broadcast details change, so check the official [Buccaneers schedule](https://www.buccaneers.com/schedule/) before you plan anything around a game.*

![Night American football game under bright stadium lights](/images/articles/tampa-buccaneers/bucs-37578663.webp)
*Photo by [Stephen Leonardi](https://www.pexels.com/@stephenleonardi/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/night-football-game-at-illuminated-stadium-37578663/)*

## Where the Tampa Buccaneers play

The Bucs play at Raymond James Stadium, 4201 N. Dale Mabry Hwy, Tampa, Florida 33607. Fans call it Ray Jay, and some drop the first name and say "James Stadium." The building belongs to Tampa, not St. Petersburg, and that matters because Tampa Bay has two very different football-and-baseball addresses. The Rays play across the bay at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg. The Lightning play downtown at Benchmark International Arena. The Bucs are on Dale Mabry.

The stadium says the Buccaneers became an NFL franchise in 1976, play in the NFC South, and were Super Bowl XXXVII champions for the 2002 season. The stadium also hosts the University of South Florida Bulls, bowl games, and concerts, so not every event at Ray Jay is a Bucs event. USF athletics says the Bulls have played there since 1998 and calls it a 65,000-seat stadium. I'm repeating USF's number because the stadium's own pages never gave me a seat count.

Raymond James Financial, a firm headquartered in St. Petersburg, holds the naming rights. The name is a company, not a person, which explains why it gets shortened so often.

For the full building breakdown, including the other Tampa venues people confuse with it, see my [Tampa stadium guide](/events/tampa-stadium-guide).

## Where the season stood on October 4, 2026

The Buccaneers were 0-3 when I wrote this, heading into Week 4: Sunday, October 4, 1:00 p.m. Eastern, Green Bay Packers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Raymond James Stadium. The team had the Packers at 1-2. The schedule row, the team's event calendar, and the stadium's own events list all agreed on that game, so I'm confident about the date and time. The row wasn't marked final when I checked, and I'm not writing a score for it.

The three losses, in order, from the team schedule:

- **Week 1, Sunday, September 13:** loss, 27-33, at the Cincinnati Bengals, Paycor Stadium.
- **Week 2, Sunday, September 20:** loss, 19-23, versus the Cleveland Browns, Raymond James Stadium.
- **Week 3, Sunday, September 27:** loss, 16-23, versus the Minnesota Vikings, Raymond James Stadium.

One small trap: the team's preview calls the Vikings game a "23-16 loss." That's the same game as 16-23, just written with the winner's score first. If someone quotes 23-16 without saying who had 23, that's how recaps mislead.

The preseason is a separate set of games and not part of the 0-3. The team went 2-1 in August: a 24-16 win at the Jets, a 16-15 win over the Chiefs at Ray Jay, and a 0-19 loss at the Jaguars. Those don't change the regular-season record.

### Injury and quarterback news

The team's how-to-watch preview said Baker Mayfield suffered a dislocated thumb in the Week 3 game. It also said undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels was trying to become the fifth quarterback in franchise history to win his first NFL start. "Trying" is not an outcome, and I'm not treating it as one.

Two team headlines went further than the preview. One said the October 2 injury report ruled out Morrison, Mayfield, Bain, and Kieft. Another said the Bucs elevated quarterback Easton Stick and linebacker Caden Fordham for the Packers game. I didn't read the injury report itself, so treat those as headlines. For anything depth-chart related, go to the club's site on game week.

## The rest of the 2026 regular-season schedule

This is the part worth saving. These are the times and opponents the team listed as of my check:

| Week | Date | Time | Matchup | Venue |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | Thu, Oct 8 | 8:15 p.m. EDT | at Dallas Cowboys | AT&T Stadium |
| 6 | Oct 18 | 1:00 p.m. EDT | Steelers at Buccaneers | Raymond James Stadium |
| 7 | Oct 25 | 1:00 p.m. EDT | at Carolina Panthers | Bank of America Stadium |
| 8 | Nov 1 | 1:00 p.m. EST | Falcons at Buccaneers | Raymond James Stadium |
| 9 | Nov 8 | 8:20 p.m. EST | at Chicago Bears | Soldier Field |
| 10 | — | — | Bye | — |
| 11 | Nov 22 | 1:00 p.m. EST | at Detroit Lions | Ford Field |
| 12 | Mon, Nov 30 | 8:15 p.m. EST | Panthers at Buccaneers | Raymond James Stadium |
| 13 | Dec 6 | 1:00 p.m. EST | Chargers at Buccaneers | Raymond James Stadium |
| 14 | Dec 13 | 1:00 p.m. EST | at Baltimore Ravens | M&T Bank Stadium |
| 15 | Dec 20 | 1:00 p.m. EST | Saints at Buccaneers | Raymond James Stadium |
| 16 | TBD | TBD | at Atlanta Falcons | — |
| 17 | TBD | TBD | Rams at Buccaneers | Raymond James Stadium |
| 18 | TBD | TBD | at New Orleans Saints | — |

A few notes on reading that table:

- **The Week 5 Thursday game** was listed on AMZ and 98ROCK rather than FOX.
- **The label flips from EDT to EST at Week 8.** I'm not converting anything; I'm repeating the team's labels. If you're planning travel, confirm the time on the official schedule.
- **Weeks 16, 17, and 18** said the time was still to be determined. I'm not filling those in. Flights and hotels booked around those dates are a gamble until the times are set.
- **Week 12 is a Monday night on ESPN** at Ray Jay, so plan for a late finish if you're staying in town.

That's six scheduled home games remaining after the Packers: Steelers, Falcons, Panthers, Chargers, Saints, and Rams. If you're building a visit around one, my [Tampa events calendar](/events/tampa-events) has what else is happening that week, and my [Tampa hotels guide](/guides/tampa-hotels) covers where to stay.

## How to watch the Buccaneers

Per the team's how-to-watch preview for the Packers game:

- **Local TV:** FOX, with Chris Myers on play-by-play, Jonathan Vilma as analyst, and Jen Hale on the sideline.
- **In-market mobile stream:** NFL+.
- **Out-of-market stream:** NFL Sunday Ticket on YouTube TV.
- **International:** Game Pass International on DAZN.

Broadcast partners change by week, as the Thursday Dallas game shows. Check the team's schedule page for each game's network before kickoff.

## How to listen: Buccaneers radio

Radio is where the team's own instructions started to fight each other, so here's what I found and where the conflicts are.

**English:** The flagship is WXTB 97.9 FM, also called 98ROCK, serving Tampa Bay and Sarasota. The crew is Tony Castricone on play-by-play, Dave Moore as analyst, and Jay Recher on the sideline. SiriusXM channel 380 carries the national stream. The affiliate list runs well past Tampa, including an Oklahoma City station, KRXO 107.7 FM. That's the same broadcast, not a second Bucs team.

**The streaming contradiction:** One line says you can listen in English and Spanish on the team's app or the team's desktop stream, in-market. The English stream line says both are in-market. The team's FAQ says the app stream is in-market and the desktop stream is all markets. I couldn't tell which sentence is the rule. If you're out of town, I'd try the desktop stream before assuming you're blacked out, and I wouldn't promise a friend that the app will work.

**Spanish:** The team lists WTMP, La Invasora, on 1150 AM, 1590 AM, and 96.1, 92.9, 94.9, 102.1, and 103.9 FM. Martin Gramatica is the analyst and Santiago Gramatica is on play-by-play. The team's FAQ calls the station WTPM instead. That's one letter off, and I can't say whether it's a typo or a second station, so I'm listing both and not correcting the team.

## Getting to Ray Jay: parking, rideshare, and RVs

The stadium's own directions are more useful than any nickname.

**Parking.** All lots are cashless and contactless, major credit cards only. The price varies by event, and advance parking is a separate purchase. The stadium doesn't give a flat number, so I won't either. Lot opening times also change by event. For a Bucs home game, the stadium's event page listed parking and the team store opening at 9:30 a.m., ticket office at 10:00, suite and club gates at 10:30, general gates at 11:30, and kickoff at 1:00 p.m. That was for the Packers game; check the specific event for the others. For lot maps and current pricing, go to the [Raymond James Stadium site](https://www.raymondjamesstadium.com/).

**Rideshare.** For Uber and Lyft, the stadium's general directions say drop-off and pickup are both at George M. Steinbrenner Field. The stadium's A-to-Z guide says something slightly different: designated drop-off at the mass transit turnaround by the pedestrian bridge, with pickup at Steinbrenner for major events and mass transit for smaller ones. The stadium's October 4 Bucs game details said Steinbrenner Field. For a USF game the day before, they said mass transit. A Karol G concert said TBD. So go by the specific event, not the general directions.

**RVs and campers.** Buccaneers games: Publix Lot 14, entrance off MLK Blvd. Most other events: Lot 8 off Himes Ave. Nothing stays overnight on stadium property, campers included. RV and camper passes are sold in advance for most events.

**Other lot details.** Bike racks are in front of the chain-link area by each dock, A through D, and the stadium says it isn't responsible for lost bikes. ADA parking can't be bought ahead; arrive early, first come first served, with a valid license and identification. If your car dies in a lot, the stadium says to call 813-350-6501 on event days, pop the hood, or find an officer at a lot entrance. They mention help with gas, lockouts, and dead batteries.

**Decide to Ride.** At events that serve alcohol, you can pledge as designated driver (21 or older with a license) at a guest services booth and get a free soft-drink coupon for permanent concession stands. The stadium says the program can also point you to a discounted rideshare home.

Use my [Tampa map](/getting-around/tampa-map) to see how Dale Mabry, downtown, and the airport relate before you pick a hotel or a route.

## Tickets, mobile entry, and the bag rule

**Tickets.** Go through the club: [buccaneers.com/tickets](https://www.buccaneers.com/tickets/). The stadium says tickets for all events are mobile only, no screenshots, and they want the ticket loaded in Apple Wallet or Google Play before you reach the gate. Each guest needs their own mobile ticket. There are no printed tickets. If a ticket won't load, the stadium's guide sends you to the ticket office in the South Plaza.

I'm not quoting face values; they vary by game and opponent. Ticket questions for Buccaneers games go to the team, at 813-879-2827 per the stadium's guide.

**The ticket-office confusion.** The stadium's A-to-Z guide places the ticket office between the Suzuki Marine gate and the Fifth Third Bank gate. The Steelers game details put it between Gates C and D. The lost-or-stolen instructions say between Suzuki Marine and D. I can't tell whether D and Fifth Third are the same door. If you need the office, ask a staff member near the South Plaza rather than trusting one sign.

**The bag rule.** The stadium has a no-bag policy for every event, with one exception: a single clutch no larger than 4.5 by 6.5 inches. Anything else goes back to the car or to lockers on Tom McEwen Boulevard, south of Suzuki Marine, for a small fee the guide doesn't name. Fans who decline to be wanded aren't admitted. Re-entry is only for a medical emergency, through a Tampa Sports Authority supervisor. Strollers and umbrellas stay out. The stadium is open air, rain or shine. The guide advises against heels and sandals and requires a shirt. Footwear is advice; the shirt is a rule. Policies get updated, so check the stadium's current policy page before you go.

**Kids.** The age rule changes by event. Buccaneers games and the Gasparilla Bowl: every age needs a ticket. USF and the ReliaQuest Bowl: three and under are free if they don't take a seat. Monster Jam and Supercross: two and under, same condition. With a toddler, the rule for your specific event is the one that counts.

**Alcohol.** The stadium says two drinks per person per purchase, none brought in or taken out, 21 with ID. Its own guide gives two different cutoffs: sales on the main and upper concourses stop at the start of the fourth quarter, then in the next breath that sales stop at the end of the third quarter depending on the stand. Don't plan around the last call.

## Inside the stadium

A few details from the stadium's guide for first-timers:

- **The pirate ship.** A 103-foot replica in the north end zone, built in 1998, closed to the public during events, with cannons fired at Buccaneers games. It can be rented on non-event days at 813-350-6500.
- **Clubs.** The guide describes the Hyundai West Club at 60,000 square feet with 178 4K monitors, and the East Club at 64,000 square feet with Bar 76, named for 1976, and 76 beers. Club access varies by event.
- **Suites.** 134 suites, seating 8 to 36.
- **Tours.** Most Mondays through Thursdays and select Fridays at 2:00 p.m., reservations required. Private groups need at least 10 people and two weeks' notice for a 10:00 a.m. tour. Pricing is a phone call to 813-350-6553.
- **Wi-Fi.** The network is bucswifi.
- **Money.** Concessions are cashless, with reverse ATMs at select spots.
- **Resale.** Ticket resale is prohibited on the property, lots included.
- **Help.** Guest services takes texts at 813-680-2827. The stadium office number is 813-350-6500 normally and 813-350-6501 on event days.
- **Team store.** The guide lists weekday and Saturday hours and Sunday closed, but the stadium's October 4 event details, a Sunday, had the team store opening at 9:30 a.m. Hours change with events.

## Tampa has more than one stadium: don't buy the wrong ticket

The phrases "stadium tampa fl" and "tampa florida stadium" point at more than one building:

- **Raymond James Stadium (Tampa):** Bucs, USF football, bowl games, and some concerts. 4201 N. Dale Mabry Hwy.
- **Benchmark International Arena (Tampa):** The Lightning's home, at 401 Channelside Drive, Tampa, FL 33602. Hockey, not football. The Lightning announced a naming-rights deal on August 13, 2025, replacing the old AMALIE name, though some downtown businesses still used the old name when I checked.
- **Tropicana Field (St. Petersburg):** The Rays' home, listed by the club as 1 Tropicana Dr, St. Petersburg, FL 33705. Not in Tampa. The club also mentions a "New Ballpark," which I didn't research.
- **George M. Steinbrenner Field:** Not a Bucs venue. It's the rideshare and staging lot for Ray Jay events. A baseball fan following that name could end up in a football rideshare lot.
- **Seminole Hard Rock Hotel and Casino Tampa:** 5223 Orient Road. A hotel and entertainment venue, not a kickoff.

A Lightning ticket is hockey, a Rays ticket is baseball, and an AMC showtime is a movie. Even the big October concert at Ray Jay, Karol G on October 9, is its own event with its own gates.

## Other Bucs-related dates

The team's calendar also listed a non-game event: the Jr. Bucs Trick or Treasure, Saturday, October 10, 4:00 to 7:00 p.m., at the AdventHealth Training Center, with trick-or-treating and football activities for Jr. Bucs members. That's a members event at the training center, not a stadium kickoff.

## A little history, kept in its place

The team's Packers preview noted that the two clubs shared the NFC Central from 1977 through 2001, before the Buccaneers moved to the NFC South in 2002. Since the move it counts 12 meetings, postseason included, with the Buccaneers winning seven, three of the last four, and six earlier meetings that went to overtime. Old photos in that preview carried captions naming Tampa Stadium, Houlihan's Stadium, Milwaukee County Stadium, Lambeau, and Raymond James, with old final scores. A caption from the 1970s is not the 2026 record.

## FAQ

**Where do the Tampa Buccaneers play?**
Raymond James Stadium, 4201 N. Dale Mabry Hwy, Tampa, FL 33607. It's in Tampa, not St. Petersburg.

**Where can I watch or listen to Bucs games?**
Local TV is on FOX for most Sunday games, though some, like the Week 5 Thursday game, air elsewhere. English radio is WXTB 97.9 FM (98ROCK), with SiriusXM channel 380 nationally. Check the team's schedule for each game's network.

**Can I bring a bag to Raymond James Stadium?**
Only a single clutch no larger than 4.5 by 6.5 inches. Everything else stays in your car or goes to lockers on Tom McEwen Boulevard. Confirm on the stadium's official site before game day.

**How much is parking for a Bucs game?**
The stadium doesn't publish one flat price. It varies by event, and all lots are cashless. Check the official parking maps on the stadium's site.

**Do the Tampa Bay Rays play at Raymond James Stadium?**
No. The Rays' club lists Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg as its ballpark. Raymond James Stadium hosts the Bucs, USF football, bowl games, and concerts.

A different Dale Mabry sports night: the [Tampa Tarpons](/events/tampa-tarpons) at Steinbrenner Field.

body:
# Armature Works Tampa: Food Hall Guide (Not the Motor Shop)

“Armature Works Tampa” is the short name I actually say from a car—and the name that once led me to the wrong company. Tampa Armature Works is still a business name, and it is not the food hall. The hall borrowed the company’s name because the company once owned the building. Visitors mean 1910 N Ola Ave, Tampa, FL 33602, in Tampa Heights on the river—not a Riverview motor-repair headquarters.

From downtown, Armature Works is the easy upriver walk or short ride when everyone wants options without committing to one restaurant. **Last updated:** November 2, 2026.

![Shared plates of food on a wooden restaurant table](/images/articles/armature-works-tampa/armature-941861.webp)
*Photo by [Life Of Pix](https://www.pexels.com/@life-of-pix/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/food-on-table-941861/)*

## Visit Snapshot

- **Address:** 1910 N Ola Ave, Tampa, FL 33602 (Tampa Heights / Heights District)
- **Building hours:** Mon–Thu 7:30 a.m.–10 p.m.; Fri 7:30 a.m.–midnight; Sat 8 a.m.–midnight; Sun 9 a.m.–9 p.m.
- **Parking:** Four guest lots—most free Mon–Fri until 4 p.m. (excludes 220 lot); after 4 p.m. typically $10+ on non-event days
- **Venue fee:** 3% on checks (not a tip)
- **Not the same:** Tampa Armature Works / TAW motor company in Riverview

Confirm hours and parking on [Armature Works location](https://www.armatureworks.com/location/armature-works/).

## Why the Short Name Misleads

On April 12, 2022, Integrated Power Services announced it would acquire Tampa Armature Works, Inc. (TAW)—a Riverview-based, fourth-generation company founded in 1921 by James Arthur Turner, Sr., working electric motors, generators, transformers, and related equipment. Riverview is not 1910 North Ola. If a search for armature works tampa dumps you on tawinc.com or a motor shop, the words did exactly what they say and missed the hall.

A History Center curator’s version: Tampa Electric used the Oak and Ola barn for storage after streetcars stopped in 1946; Tampa Armature Works bought the building in May 1956. Oak and Ola’s own history (credited to Armature Works) dates the structure to 1910, says the streetcar system was abandoned in 1946, and says the company bought from TECO in 1960—not 1956. I keep both years. Either way, the machinery company left its name on the brick. The building visitors go to is the restored warehouse. Crane rails and the pit under the tracks are why the space feels industrial—not an invitation to a motor-repair tour.

## It Is Not One Restaurant

It sounds like one restaurant. It is a market plus several dining rooms. Heights Public Market is the counter side: beer and cocktails at Bar AW, smoked meat at Butcher n’ Barbeque, coffee at Buddy Brew, custard-style ice cream at Chill Bros, Venetian pasta to go at DalMoros, empanadas at Empamamas, pizza at The Fold, dumplings at Ling’s, and more stalls than one menu can hold. Sit-down rooms include Oak and Ola (Euro-American, wood-fired), Steelbach (Southern chophouse), Stones Throw (river pavilion), M.Bird (rooftop lounge), and Champagne Porch. Steelbach and Oak and Ola were both 2022 Michelin Recommended. Walking in and asking for “a reservation at Armature Works” is the mistake. Some counters get marked coming soon, so a name you remember may now be an empty slot.

Every check carries a 3% venue fee. The restaurant keeps it for facilities, equipment, and overhead—it is not a tip and is not distributed to staff. Tip separately. I thought people were struggling with the fee—and with the company-versus-hall mix-up—more than with finding the front door.

## Tampa Heights, Not Downtown or Ybor

The operator calls the hall the heart of the Heights District—about 50 acres anchored by the river and downtown—and puts the warehouse at about 73,000 square feet. The city places it in the Tampa Heights Riverfront CRA, charts about 73,440 square feet on a 2.8-acre parcel, year built 2019 on the chart, two-story market hall with co-working and events. Close to downtown is not downtown. The Pearl apartments—314 units on the block bounded by North Ola, West Palm, North Massachusetts, and West Ross—sit next door. Heading for the hall and ending up at a leasing office is the apartment version of the name mix-up. Ybor is a different historic district. A wooden Ybor streetcar barn burned in 1908; this brick barn is the one on Ola.

North Ola itself is a historic brick-paved street. Sidewalks on both sides; no marked bike lane on Ola (nearby lanes are on West Palm and North Highland). The Riverwalk stretch along the southern edge of this CRA, from Water Works Park to the Northern Avenue Bridge, finished in 2020 and sits directly across from the hall, with more than thirty-four slips for small boats. If your pin is a block off and you cannot see the water, you are not at the door yet. ZIP for the hall is 33602—one of the Tampa Heights ZIPs—not a forced swap to 33605 just because Ybor uses that code.

City project WTR-20-0011 will replace water mains along Ola in Tampa Heights, with construction planned for calendar year 2028—not a 2026 curb closure. Check again if you visit after that window starts.

## Parking: Free Until 4 p.m., Then Plan Ahead

There are four guest lots. All Armature Works lots except the 220 lot are free Monday through Friday until 4 p.m. Events and holidays vary. After 4 p.m. on non-event days, pricing typically starts around $10+. A garage about a block away sits in the same complex as Sprouts, F45, and Escapology. Meters on West 7th, West Palm, Oak, and North Highland run 8 a.m. to midnight, seven days a week, from $1.50 an hour, city-enforced.

Four o’clock on a weekday is when the free window ends—exactly when I would be arriving for dinner. If you care about free parking, get there early. The city has noted visitor spillover into residential streets north of West Ross; a permit idea for those streets had not been adopted when I checked. Do not treat a quiet residential curb as overflow just because the short name never mentioned parking.

Building hours (not every stall’s hours): Monday–Thursday 7:30 a.m.–10 p.m.; Friday 7:30 a.m.–midnight; Saturday 8 a.m.–midnight; Sunday 9 a.m.–9 p.m. Confirm each restaurant if you need a kitchen open late.

## Events Change the Day

When I checked in early October, there was a pumpkin patch for all of October. Fall Fest ran October 10–11 on the West Lawn and Market Street—free, with vendors and camel rides. Rides by the River happens every third Saturday—free, no ticket, cars lined up along the river. Private events use The Gathering, the Theatre, and Rooftop 220 (roughly 25 to 550 guests), plus private dining at Steelbach, Stones Throw, M.Bird, and Champagne Porch. A third Saturday means a car show, not a quiet hour at the market. The Heights District Fourth of July celebration for July 4, 2026, was listed as free admission 5–10 p.m. with fireworks—event parking prices vary.

For a quieter Riverwalk museum morning first, see [Tampa Museum of Art](/things-to-do/tampa-museum-of-art). For shopping west of downtown, [International Plaza](/shopping/international-plaza-tampa) is a different errand entirely.

## Tips From Our Visits

Keep “Armature Works Tampa” as the nickname, then pin the street: 1910 North Ola, 33602, Tampa Heights, hall on the river. Throw out Riverview and anything about rewinding a motor. Throw out the idea of a single host stand. Check the clock before trusting a free lot. Know the 3% line before you decide the server slipped in a tip. The name is popular because it is short—being short is why it points to two companies and one building with a dozen kitchens.

## FAQ

### Where is Armature Works?

1910 N Ola Ave, Tampa, FL 33602, in the Heights District / Tampa Heights on the Hillsborough River—not Ybor and not Riverview.

### Is parking free?

Most surface lots (excluding the 220 lot) are free Monday–Friday until 4 p.m. After 4 p.m. and on events/holidays, expect paid parking; the Heights garage near Sprouts is another option.

### Do I need a reservation?

For sit-down rooms (Oak and Ola, Steelbach, and others), book the specific restaurant. Market counters are walk-up. There is no single “Armature Works” reservation for the whole building.

### What is the 3% venue fee?

It is an operational fee retained by the restaurant for facilities and overhead. It is not a gratuity—tip staff separately.

### Is Tampa Armature Works the same place?

No. Tampa Armature Works (TAW) is the historic motor/power company whose name stayed on the brick. The visitor destination is the restored food hall and restaurants at 1910 N Ola.

## Final Thoughts

From downtown, this is the easy “everyone wants something different” dinner building—as long as you plan parking after 4 p.m. and tip on top of the venue fee. I would go back for a weekday lunch when the lots are free, and I would skip a third-Saturday car-show afternoon if I wanted a quiet market stroll.

Combine with [things to do in Tampa](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa) or a morning at the [Tampa Museum of Art](/things-to-do/tampa-museum-of-art). For a classic steakhouse night instead of a food hall, see [Rusty Pelican](/food-and-drink/rusty-pelican-tampa) on Rocky Point.

For a wider plate list, start at [Tampa restaurants](/food-and-drink/tampa-restaurants).

body:
# Tampa Museum of Art: My Downtown Visit Guide

People shorten it every way: Tampa art museum, art museum Tampa, art museum in Tampa, art museum Tampa FL. They all mean the same building—the Tampa Museum of Art in the Cornelia Corbett Center at 120 W. Gasparilla Plaza. There is not a second, smaller “Tampa art museum” under another name.

I went on a weekday from downtown. The Riverwalk walk to Curtis Hixon was the easy part. The hard parts were parking, Thursday pricing, and telling this museum apart from Glazer Children’s Museum next door. **Last updated:** November 2, 2026.

![Visitor viewing a painting in a bright art museum gallery](/images/articles/tampa-museum-of-art/museum-1572386.webp)
*Photo by [Pixabay](https://www.pexels.com/@pixabay/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/person-looking-at-painting-1572386/)*

## Visit Snapshot

- **Address:** 120 W. Gasparilla Plaza, Tampa, FL 33602 (Cornelia Corbett Center)
- **Hours:** Mon–Wed, Fri–Sun 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; Thursday 10 a.m.–8 p.m.
- **Adult admission:** $25 (advance purchase available)
- **Thursday 4–8 p.m.:** Art on the House, pay-as-you-will
- **Parking:** No museum-owned lot—City of Tampa / private lots nearby
- **Closed:** Gasparilla, Thanksgiving, Christmas Day; early close 3 p.m. on July 4, Dec. 24, Dec. 31

Confirm live hours and tickets on the museum’s [Plan Your Visit](https://tampamuseum.org/visit/) page.

## Parking Reality (No Museum Lot)

The museum does not own a parking lot. Everything nearby is City of Tampa or private. I used the William F. Poe Parking Garage and paid through ParkMobile zone 9913—or at the pay-by-plate station with the license plate entered before walking away. I watched people argue at the kiosk about how many hours to buy. Undershoot and you walk back. The museum also names the Royal Street Regional Lot (ParkMobile zone 9709) plus metered street spots. Gold-level Art+ patrons and above can get a Poe garage validation code at the front desk. I was not in that tier, so I paid.

ADA parking is fussier. Closest accessible spaces are on the 4th and 5th floors of the Poe garage at 802 N. Ashley Drive—take the southeast elevators so you do not cross the railroad tracks at W. Gasparilla Plaza. The museum counts 17 ADA spaces across five floors and a 7-foot garage clearance for most vans. The accessible museum entrance is the Vinik Family Education Center door on the east side, facing Glazer Children’s Museum. There is a drop-off curb on Gasparilla Plaza between the two buildings—it is not a parking space. I watched a rideshare sit there while the car behind got annoyed.

## Getting There Without a Car

The museum says it is the only museum in the country you can reach by boat, with two Riverwalk slips—first come, free. Pirate Water Taxi stop 12 drops at Curtis Hixon Park in front of the building. I did not come by boat. I did walk the river side, and the glass ground floor does what the renovation promised: you can see art from the path without buying a ticket.

HART routes 7 and 10 stop on W. Cass between the Poe garage and the library. Routes 1, 5, 19, and 30 stop on Tampa Street between Zack and Twiggs. TECO streetcar stop 11 at the Ft. Brooke garage is about a 15-minute walk—I would not sell that as “nearby” to anyone with tired kids. For a wider downtown day, pair this with the [Riverwalk](/guides/tampa-riverwalk-hotels) or dinner near [Armature Works](/food-and-drink/armature-works-tampa) upriver in Tampa Heights.

## Hours, Tickets, and the Thursday Trap

Straight from the museum: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday, Saturday, and Sunday 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. Thursday 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. Closed Gasparilla, Thanksgiving, and Christmas Day. Early close at 3 p.m. on July 4, Christmas Eve, and New Year’s Eve.

Thursday from 4 to 8 p.m. is Art on the House—pay-as-you-will. That is the thing people miss. I heard someone at the desk ask why their phone still showed a $25 ticket on a Thursday evening. Posted adult price is $25. Adults 65+, Florida educators, professional artists, and military (when that discount is listed) are $15; K–12 students $5; children 6 and under free; college students with ID free; SNAP EBT free. Art+ members enter free. No refunds on purchased tickets. Do not prepay full price five minutes before a Thursday 4 p.m. arrival without knowing Art on the House exists.

Art on the Spectrum: last Sunday of the month the museum opens at 9 a.m. It is in the CARD autism-friendly directory, with staff trained with CARD USF, and they will hand you headphones, sunglasses, and sensory toys. Quieter stretches they name: Tuesday–Sunday 10–11 a.m., and Monday–Wednesday 10 a.m.–noon. Temperatures change room to room. There is a projection room marked for light sensitivity. Service dogs yes; emotional support animals no. Two public dog parks sit across Curtis Hixon if the dog needs a break. Complimentary wheelchairs at the welcome desk, first come. Galleries, classrooms, and restrooms are elevator-served, with portable chairs in the galleries.

Buy advance tickets through the museum shop when you want a locked date; discounted tickets need valid ID at the Welcome Desk.

## What Was on the Walls (Fall 2026)

When I went in early October 2026, the lead show was David Hockney: Perspective Should Be Reversed, from the Jordan D. Schnitzer collections—September 24, 2026 through February 28, 2027. Over 140 prints, collages, photographs, and iPad drawings across sixty years. People clustered at the iPad drawings and argued about whether a screen drawing belongs in a museum. In this show, it does.

Around it, permanent-collection rooms do more work than the Hockney banner suggests. Mysteries of the Nile: Ancient Egypt runs June 25, 2026 to June 25, 2028—the museum calls it the first Egypt show in Tampa. Eye of the Beholder (William Knight Zewadski Greek and Roman gift) through January 3, 2027. The Etruscans—about 70 objects, called the largest public Etruscan collection in the Southeast—through May 23, 2027. The Five Suns (Haiti’s Saint Soleil) from a collection the museum describes as one of the largest public holdings of Haitian modern art in the country. Avant Garde (women in the permanent collection, many with Tampa Bay roots) through April 4, 2027. Suchitra Mattai’s *to leave a trace* into May 2027. Sam Modder’s wall drawings *Her Hair Like the Sun and Clouds* July 23, 2026 to July 4, 2027—she teaches at the University of Tampa. Esterio Segura’s *Hybrid of a Chrysler* (winged 1953 Windsor) is back. If someone tells you this museum is only a small contemporary box, they walked the lobby and left. The antiquities and Caribbean holdings surprised me most.

The museum is in a centennial renovation and expansion for more exhibition and education space. I could see the finished clearer ground floor and art visible from Curtis Hixon. I did not see a finished new wing. People talk as if the museum is closed for construction. It was open—the construction story is the next phase, not a shutdown.

## Gallery Rules I Wish I Knew on the Sidewalk

Backpacks (including purse-style backpacks), bags over 11×15 inches, luggage, food, drinks, tripods, and umbrellas go in free lockers at the welcome desk. Personal photography is allowed in most permanent and temporary galleries unless a sign or visitor rep says otherwise—no flash, no selfie sticks, no tripods, monopods, stands, drones, or extra lights. Handheld cameras or phones under 3 pounds. Stop at the welcome desk and ask for the free digital companion guide (audio, exhibition stories, translation in 52 languages). Bring headphones. I did not, and the guide is useless if you are sharing one phone speaker in a quiet gallery.

Out-of-town perk I only found deep in the visitor info: Le Méridien downtown hands out Unlock Art passes that cover general admission for hotel guests. I was not staying there.

## Tips From My Visit

The mix-ups I watched at the desk and garage: people ask for “art museum Tampa FL,” then cannot tell this building from Glazer next door; they expect a museum lot; they prepay the wrong ParkMobile zone; they buy full price on a Thursday evening; they think military free is year-round when the museum only promises a seasonal window when it lists one; they think expansion means closed; they bring a backpack and get sent to a locker. None of that is hard once you know the visitor rules. Almost nobody learns them before they are already on Gasparilla Plaza.

## FAQ

### How much does Tampa Museum of Art cost?

Adult general admission is $25. Discounts include $15 for adults 65+, Florida educators, and professional artists; $5 for K–12 students; free for children 6 and under, college students with ID, SNAP EBT participants, and Art+ members. Thursday 4–8 p.m. is pay-as-you-will (Art on the House).

### Does the museum have its own parking?

No. Use nearby City of Tampa or private lots—commonly the Poe garage (ParkMobile 9913) or Royal Street Regional Lot (9709).

### What are the museum hours?

Most days 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; Thursday 10 a.m.–8 p.m. Last Sunday of the month opens at 9 a.m. for Art on the Spectrum.

### Is the museum closed for renovation?

No. It remains open during its centennial renovation and expansion. Confirm the day’s hours on the museum visit page before you go.

### Can I take photos?

Personal handheld photography is generally allowed in most galleries unless posted otherwise—no flash, sticks, tripods, or drones.

## Final Thoughts

From downtown, this is the art stop that actually sits on the Riverwalk—once you solve parking and Thursday pricing. I would go back for the antiquities and Caribbean rooms even if the banner show has rotated, and I would bring headphones next time for the companion guide.

Pair a museum morning with lunch upriver at [Armature Works](/food-and-drink/armature-works-tampa) or a broader [things to do in Tampa](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa) plan. For kids next door, Glazer is a separate ticket and a separate day job.

title: Tampa to Clearwater: My Beach-Day Drive Guide
dek: FDOT’s 23-mile city figure, Courtney Campbell vs Memorial Causeway, and why the beach is a longer hop.

metaDescription: Tampa to Clearwater guide covering FDOT 23 city miles, Clearwater Beach versus city, Courtney Campbell Causeway tips, and TPA SR 60 tie-ins.
keywords: how far is clearwater from tampa
body:
# Tampa to Clearwater: My Beach-Day Drive Guide

People ask it every way: Tampa to Clearwater, Clearwater to Tampa, Tampa Clearwater, and every FL/Florida combo. FDOT’s city figure is short. The arguments are about which Clearwater and which Tampa, and which of three roads across the bay you are actually on.

Weekend beach plans from downtown always started with the same question: city Clearwater or Clearwater Beach? Those are not the same mile.

![Clear turquoise coastal water under a sunny sky](/images/articles/tampa-to-clearwater/clearwater-1174732.webp)
*Photo by [Asad Photo Maldives](https://www.pexels.com/@asadphoto/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/body-of-water-1174732/)*

## Quick Answers

- **City to city (FDOT):** 23 miles either way  
- **Toward Clearwater Beach:** about 25 miles in the separate beach count I used—then the Memorial Causeway after downtown Clearwater  
- **Main water crossing:** Courtney Campbell Causeway (SR 60)  
- **Not the same road:** I-275 / Howard Frankland (St. Pete side) or Veterans Expressway tolls north–south  

## The Official City Miles

FDOT’s official intercity mileage was last updated 9/14/2026. Those figures are the shortest distance between city pairs for mileage reimbursements. Tampa to Clearwater is **23 miles**. Clearwater to Tampa is **23 miles**. Both directions match. Confirm the matrix on [FDOT intercity highway mileage](https://www.fdot.gov/statistics/hwydata/intercity.shtm).

Another city-to-city count also came to 23. That agreement does not make it the beach. Tampa to Clearwater Beach came out at **25 miles** in that same count. Clearwater Beach is not one of the cities FDOT measures in that matrix.

Nearby traps: Clearwater to Largo is 4 miles; Tampa to Largo is 25 (Largo to Tampa 24). St. Petersburg to Clearwater is 20; St. Petersburg to Tampa is 20. Three official pairs, two the same length, none of them the beach sand.

## Three Roads, Three Mistakes

### Courtney Campbell Causeway (SR 60)

The direct crossing is the Courtney Campbell Causeway—northernmost bridge across Old Tampa Bay, four lanes of SR 60, maintained by FDOT, from Clearwater in Pinellas to Tampa in Hillsborough. It runs about 9.9 miles from eastern Clearwater to Tampa’s Rocky Point island and then to western Tampa mainland. It first carried traffic as the Davis Causeway in 1934 with a toll then; the state took it over in 1944. That toll is history. Current Turnpike West Central Florida schedules name the Courtney Campbell next to the Veterans and give no plaza rate for it.

FDOT District Seven has a PD&E study (started June 2025) for capacity and storm hardening—limits about CR 611 / N. McMullen Booth Road in Pinellas to west of SR 589 (Veterans) in Hillsborough, roughly 9.5 miles. Study expected to finish third quarter 2027. That is a study, not a new bridge you drive today. The 9.9 and 9.5 describe the causeway corridor, not the whole 23-mile city pair.

The causeway has beaches of its own: Ben T. Davis Municipal Beach (City of Tampa) at the east end, and an FDOT-owned beach on the west end. Those are on the drive between the cities. They are not Clearwater Beach.

### Clearwater Memorial Causeway

Clearwater Beach is a second bridge. The Clearwater Memorial Causeway carries SR 60 between downtown Clearwater and Clearwater Beach across the Intracoastal—six lanes, opened August 2005, hurricane evacuation route. Want the sand? Finish the Courtney Campbell, get through the city, then cross this span. The 25-mile idea is that longer trip. FDOT’s 23 stops at the city.

### I-275 and the Veterans

Tampa International sits on the SR 60 version of this trip. The airport says Highway 60 passes the entrance just east of the start of the Courtney Campbell. From St. Petersburg, Clearwater, the gulf beaches, and the west, the airport says I-275 North to exit 39—that is the Howard Frankland side, not the Courtney Campbell. See [TPA](/getting-around/tampa-international-airport).

If you are in Clearwater and get on I-275, you chose the St. Petersburg interstate, not SR 60. The Sunshine Skyway toll (if your route dips that far south) appears on Turnpike West Central Florida schedules—separate plazas, SunPass vs toll-by-plate rates. Do not put that toll on a Courtney Campbell trip.

The Veterans Expressway (SR 589) runs north as a toll road—segment plazas, not a Tampa–Clearwater total. It is how someone in Carrollwood reaches the airport and SR 60. It is not the road over to the beach.

## Where “Tampa” Starts Matters

I-75 is the east-side bypass past Brandon, Temple Terrace, and New Tampa. Plant City to Tampa is 22 miles by FDOT; Lakeland to Tampa is 33. A hotel by I-75 is a different start than downtown. Downtown to the beach and airport to the beach are not the same trip even though both get called Tampa to Clearwater. The airport’s “about five miles west of downtown” figure is terminal position—not a substitute for the 23.

I am not writing a drive time. The causeway has lower capacity and lower posted speeds than a freeway. The PD&E study is not a live detour map.

For theme-park miles instead, use [Tampa to Orlando](/guides/tampa-to-orlando). For a day back in town after the beach, [things to do in Tampa](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa) and [Ybor](/guides/ybor-city-tampa-fl-33605) cover the return.

## Rocky Point on the Way

The causeway hits Rocky Point on the Tampa side—handy for waterfront dinner at [Rusty Pelican](/food-and-drink/rusty-pelican-tampa) before or after the beach run. Westshore shopping at [International Plaza](/shopping/international-plaza-tampa) sits near the airport end of SR 60. From downtown, that Rocky Point stop is how a beach return becomes dinner without another long hop across the bay the same night.

## What I Actually Did From Downtown

Beach Saturdays started with the same checklist: city Clearwater or Clearwater Beach, gas before the causeway, and no reliance on a single drive-time promise. FDOT’s 23 settled arguments about “how far.” The Memorial Causeway settled arguments about “why are we still not at the sand.” I noticed how often apps offered I-275 when SR 60 was the plan—useful if you are coming from St. Pete, wrong if you already decided on Courtney Campbell from Westshore or the airport corridor.

I also learned not to treat Ben T. Davis or the FDOT beach on the causeway as the destination photo people mean by Clearwater Beach. Those stops are on the drive. The island is after downtown Clearwater. For a short water view without committing to the full beach day, the causeway beaches were enough. For Pier 60, budget the extra city-plus-Memorial miles and a later return.

**Last updated:** November 2, 2026 (FDOT mileage matrix dated 9/14/2026).

## FAQ

### How far is Tampa to Clearwater?

FDOT’s official city-to-city figure is 23 miles each way (matrix updated 9/14/2026).

### How far is Tampa to Clearwater Beach?

Treat the beach as a separate, longer idea—about 25 miles in the count I used—plus the Memorial Causeway from downtown Clearwater to the island. It is not FDOT’s city pair.

### Which bridge should I take?

For city Clearwater from western Tampa / the airport corridor, SR 60 / Courtney Campbell is the direct bay crossing. I-275 is the St. Pete interstate. The Veterans is a north–south toll expressway, not the beach road.

### Is the Courtney Campbell a toll bridge?

The historic toll is gone. Current schedules do not post a Courtney Campbell plaza rate the way they do for Skyway or Veterans plazas.

### Can I combine this with TPA?

Yes—Highway 60 passes the airport entrance near the start of the Courtney Campbell. Build time for airport traffic separately from beach traffic.

## Final Thoughts

Quote 23 for city Clearwater on SR 60, quote the beach as its own hop after the Memorial Causeway, and do not mix Howard Frankland instructions into a Courtney Campbell day. From downtown, that is the beach plan I actually used as a mental map.

When you come back sandy, downtown dinner and a Riverwalk walk beat another causeway crossing the same night—start with [things to do in Tampa](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa).
