title: Tampa to Orlando: My Drive Guide (I-4 Miles, Tolls, Bus, Train)
dek: I-4 mileposts, Disney vs Universal exits, Express toll peaks, stops, and car vs bus vs train.
metaTitle: Tampa to Orlando: I-4 Miles, Tolls & Bus
metaDescription: Tampa to Orlando drive guide covering I-4 miles to Disney and downtown, Express toll rules, FlixBus times, Amtrak notes, and Brightline status.
body:
# Tampa to Orlando: My Drive Guide (I-4 Miles, Tolls, Bus, Train)

People ask it as Tampa to Orlando and Orlando to Tampa. The road is Interstate 4. The train people expect from Tampa is not running yet. The bus is real. I am not writing a door-to-door drive time, because nobody I trust publishes one that matches every driveway.

From downtown Tampa, I-4 was the ruler for Disney days and Orlando airport runs. The mileposts start at Malfunction Junction—not at TPA, not at a Brandon hotel, and not at Disney’s gate. That single fact cleaned up more bad GPS math for me than any app tip. **Last updated:** November 2, 2026.

![Open highway stretching toward the horizon](/images/articles/tampa-to-orlando/orlando-drive-210182.webp)
*Photo by [Pixabay](https://www.pexels.com/@pixabay/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/asphalt-empty-road-210182/)*

## Trip Snapshot

- **Road:** I-4 east from the I-275 interchange (Malfunction Junction)  
- **Disney:** World Drive ~exit 62 (eastbound Disney traffic uses 62B toward the resort; 62A toward Celebration / World Drive south)  
- **Universal / north I-Drive:** exits 74–75 (Sand Lake, Universal Blvd, Kirkman)  
- **Downtown Orlando:** Colonial Drive ~exit 84A  
- **Tolls:** general-use I-4 is free; I-4 Express is optional, transponder-only, Orlando end only  
- **Bus:** FlixBus advertises about 1 hour 40 minutes, fares from the mid-teens  
- **Brightline Tampa:** still planning as of May 2026 city materials—not a ticket you can buy yet  

## I-4 as the Ruler

Per FDOT, I-4 is 132.30 miles, maintained by FDOT, signed east-west even though it runs diagonal, at least six lanes the whole way. It starts at the interchange with I-275 near downtown Tampa. That junction is Malfunction Junction, mile 0 for exit numbers. Mileposts measure distance from that interchange.

Going down the exit list using FDOT mileposts and the [I-4 exit number table](https://www.fdot.gov/traffic/trafficservices/exitnumb/i-4.shtm): World Drive, signed Disney World, is exit 62. Sand Lake Road, exit 74A, is mile 73.732, signed toward International Drive and Orlando International Airport. Orange Blossom Trail, exit 80, is mile 80.474. Colonial Drive, exit 84A, is mile 83.792, toward downtown Orlando. About 62 miles of interstate to the Disney World exit. About 74 to Sand Lake and International Drive. About 84 to Colonial Drive. If you start at Tampa International or in Clearwater, those miles are not the whole trip—add your own first leg.

East of the junction the road passes north of Ybor, then Brandon, Plant City, north of Lakeland, and the Polk Parkway. Weigh stations sit at mile 12. The Polk City rest area sits on the Tampa–Orlando stretch. The Longwood rest area is east of Orlando—useful only if you are continuing past the metro, not for a Disney/Universal/downtown Orlando arrival.

For a shorter Gulf-side hop instead, see [Tampa to Clearwater](/guides/tampa-to-clearwater). For Naples south, use my [Tampa to Naples](/guides/tampa-to-naples) guide. Flying into Tampa first? [TPA](/getting-around/tampa-international-airport).

## Disney vs Universal vs Downtown Orlando Routes

These are different exits. Mixing them up is how you add a theme-park day of I-4 between gates.

### Walt Disney World (exit 62)

From Tampa, stay on I-4 east to **exit 62 / World Drive**. FDOT lists World Drive at exit 62. Recent eastbound work split the World Drive ramps: **62B** for northbound World Drive toward Walt Disney World Resort, **62A** for World Drive south toward Celebration. If your GPS still shows a single “World Drive” split after one ramp, confirm the live ramp letters before you commit—Disney-bound traffic wants the resort / northbound World Drive side.

You reach exit 62 **before** I-4 Express begins near mile 75. You can finish a Disney day without ever entering the toll lanes.

Nearby Disney-area exits on the same FDOT table: **64** (US 192), **65** (Osceola Parkway), **67** (SR 536 / Epcot Center Drive corridor), **68** (SR 535). Those matter if your hotel is on US 192 or near Disney Springs rather than on World Drive itself.

### Universal Orlando and north International Drive (exits 74–75)

Universal Orlando’s published directions: from **eastbound I-4**, take **exit 75A**, then left onto Universal Boulevard; from **westbound I-4**, use **exit 74B** and turn right on Hollywood Way. There are also approaches from Kirkman Road (**exit 75B**), Turkey Lake Road, and Vineland Road. Universal Boulevard connects the International Drive area to Universal via an overpass over I-4.

There is **no single I-4 exit signed only “International Drive.”** Practical approaches from FDOT’s table and local wayfinding:

- **74A** — SR 482 / Sand Lake Road (common for mid/south I-Drive)  
- **75A / 75B** — Universal Boulevard / Kirkman Road (north I-Drive and Universal)  
- **72** — SR 528 / Beachline (airport and east–west connector)  
- **71** — Central Florida Parkway (SeaWorld / south-of-Universal corridor)

I-4 Express starts around Kirkman (about mile 75)—right where Universal and north I-Drive traffic is densest. Disney traffic that stayed off at 62 never meets that merge. Universal and downtown traffic does.

### Downtown Orlando (exit 84A and neighbors)

For downtown, FDOT’s useful markers are **84A** Colonial Drive (SR 50) toward downtown, with nearby **80** Orange Blossom Trail, **82** SR 408 (East–West Expressway), and **83** South / Anderson Street depending on direction. That is roughly the mid-80s in exit numbers—past Disney, past Universal, into the city grid.

If your real destination is Orlando International Airport rather than downtown, Sand Lake / Beachline logic (74A / 72) is usually closer to the airport conversation than Colonial Drive. Confirm your hotel or terminal pin; “Orlando” is not one exit.

## Traffic and When Peak Pricing Shows Up

I am still not publishing a single drive-time promise. What I will publish is what I-4 Express and FDOT say about the Orlando end.

I-4 Express calls this the busiest interstate corridor in Central Florida. After the Express lanes debuted (February 26, 2022, following I-4 Ultimate on those 21 miles), reported stats for that Orlando section showed fewer crashes and higher speeds—those minutes are the **21 Orlando miles**, not the haul from Tampa. International Drive stays within about 1.5 miles of I-4 between Kissimmee and the Turnpike. The stretch that fights you is Disney through downtown, which is also where the toll lanes appear.

**Weekday peaks that matter for Express tolls:** I-4 Express and FDOT dynamic-tolling materials say drivers are most likely to see higher Express prices on the busiest segments near downtown Orlando during **6–9 a.m. and 3–7 p.m. weekdays**. Tolls adjust by segment (about every 15 minutes under dynamic tolling). General-use lanes stay free either way.

**Practical leave windows from Tampa (judgment, not a clock guarantee):**

- **Disney park open:** leave early enough that exit 62 is behind you before the Orlando commute peak eats the last third of the trip. Mid-morning after the 6–9 a.m. Express peak can be calmer at the Orlando end than aiming to arrive in that window—but park entry lines are a separate problem.  
- **Universal / I-Drive hotel check-in:** you will hit exits 74–75, which is Express territory. If you can avoid 3–7 p.m. weekdays for that last segment, do.  
- **Downtown Orlando evening:** Colonial Drive in the 3–7 p.m. weekday band is exactly when Express signs near downtown are most likely to spike.  
- **Weekends:** Express peak guidance is framed around weekday commute hours; weekend traffic still exists around parks—use live navigation.

Use live traffic and build buffer into park open, park close, and flight times. I will not invent a “always 90 minutes” number.

## I-4 Express Tolls (Orlando End Only)

The general-use lanes are not a toll road. I-4 Express is 21 miles in the median, roughly mile marker 75 just west of Kirkman Road to mile marker 95 east of State Road 436, in Orange and Seminole counties. Barrier-separated, speed limit 60, two axles and buses only. No large RVs or trailers.

Tolls move with traffic. I-4 Express says a segment can be as low as 50 cents. Overhead signs show the price before you enter; you never pay more than the sign you passed. If average travel speed in Express falls under 40 mph, statute drops you to the minimum Express toll. Transponder only: SunPass, E-PASS, E-ZPass, LeeWay, Peach Pass, NC Quick Pass, PIKEPASS, KTAG, TollTag, and other listed interoperable tags. No cash. No normal Toll-By-Plate. Enter without a tag and you risk a mailed bill plus fees / violation charges—confirm current amounts on [I-4 Express FAQs](https://i4express.com/faqs/).

**Rental cars are the trap.** An optional transponder means the rental company charges the tolls; enter without one—including by accident—and the company bills tolls and fees. Set GPS to avoid tolls unless you already took that product. Miss an express exit and you keep going. Road Rangers via *347 can help on the express section.

FDOT has studied more express lanes toward Tampa; those are proposals, not open pavement. Do not plan as if they exist yet. Check [FDOT](https://www.fdot.gov/) and live I-4 Express signage for rules.

## Stops Along the Way

Useful fixed points from the highway description—not a restaurant review:

- **Mile 12:** weigh stations  
- **Polk City area:** rest area (restrooms, water, vending) on the Tampa–Orlando haul  
- **Polk Parkway (SR 570):** exits in the high 20s / low 40s depending on east vs west connectors—Lakeland / Polk County access, not Orlando  
- **Plant City / Lakeland corridor:** the long middle of the drive between Brandon and the Disney exits  
- **Longwood-area rest area:** farther northeast on I-4 **past** downtown Orlando—only relevant if you continue beyond Orlando, not for a Disney / Universal / downtown drop

I did not inventory every gas brand. Plan fuel before you need it in park traffic. For a beach day instead of this corridor, switch to [Tampa to Clearwater](/guides/tampa-to-clearwater).

## Car vs Bus vs Train

| Mode | What is real today | What it costs in practice | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Car on general-use I-4** | Full door-to-door control; Disney at 62 without Express | Fuel + parking at destination; no I-4 toll if you stay out of Express | Families, park luggage, multiple Orlando stops |
| **Car + I-4 Express** | Optional last 21 miles near Orlando; transponder required | Dynamic tolls (signs before entry); rental-toll products can surprise you | Time-sensitive downtown / Universal approaches on weekdays |
| **FlixBus** | Advertised ~1 hr 40 min; ~7 trips/day; fares from ~$14.98 (moves) | Ticket + getting to Marion Street / USF or Orlando board points | Solo / light bags, no rental car |
| **Amtrak Floridian + thruway** | Long-distance train stops in both cities; some thruway coach segments on the timetable | Amtrak fare for that itinerary | Already on a longer rail trip—not a hop |
| **Brightline Tampa** | Planning only (May 2026 city materials)—no Tampa tickets | N/A | Do not plan your weekend on it yet |

### Bus detail (FlixBus)

FlixBus puts the Orlando–Tampa bus at 1 hour 40 minutes. They gave 82 miles one time and 83 another—both sit near the I-4 mileposts. Fares from $14.98, price moves. Seven trips a day. First Orlando departure 2:45 a.m., last 8:45 p.m. Orlando boards at 555 N. John Young Parkway and Florida Mall (1634 Florida Mall Avenue), no overnight parking. Tampa: 1315 N. Marion Street at the HART center, or USF on Holly Drive (campus parking rules). One carry-on to 7 kg and one checked bag to 20 kg. Wheelchair access if you note it when booking. Wi-Fi is offered subject to availability. Confirm current times and fares on FlixBus before you rely on them. Neither Tampa stop is a theme-park gate—budget a rideshare or local transit after you land.

### Train detail

Amtrak’s Floridian timetable includes a Fort Myers–Orlando thruway by chartered motorcoach. A clean run I could follow left Tampa Union Station at 9:25 a.m., Lakeland 10:10 a.m., Orlando 11:50 a.m., with a return Orlando 1:30 p.m. and Tampa 3:30 p.m. The long-distance Floridian train stops in both cities on a Chicago–Miami schedule—not an all-day shuttle. Confirm Amtrak for your date; times move.

Brightline is what people mean by skipping I-4. The City of Tampa’s transportation department, as of May 27, 2026, still marked the Orlando–Tampa extension as planning—about 85 miles from Orlando International along I-4, proposed stops at Disney or International Drive and Lakeland, Tampa station not chosen. Bond talk is not a train. Construction has not started. Do not buy a Tampa Brightline ticket. Miami–Orlando trains do not pick you up here.

## FAQ

### How many miles is Tampa to Orlando on I-4?

From Malfunction Junction (I-4/I-275), about 62 miles to the Disney World exit, about 74 to Sand Lake/International Drive, about 84 to Colonial Drive toward downtown Orlando—using FDOT mileposts along I-4.

### Which exit for Disney vs Universal?

Disney / World Drive is exit 62 (use the resort / northbound World Drive ramp—62B in the newer eastbound split). Universal from eastbound I-4 is typically exit 75A to Universal Boulevard; westbound often uses 74B to Hollywood Way. Confirm Universal’s current directions the day you drive.

### Are there tolls the whole way?

No. General-use I-4 lanes are not a toll road. I-4 Express is an optional toll facility near Orlando for eligible vehicles with a transponder.

### When are I-4 Express tolls highest?

I-4 Express says higher prices are most likely on busy downtown Orlando segments weekdays **6–9 a.m. and 3–7 p.m.** Read the overhead sign before you enter.

### How long does the drive take?

I do not publish a single drive time. Traffic varies. Use live navigation and build buffer into Disney, Universal, and airport days.

### Is there a train from Tampa to Orlando?

Not a frequent Brightline hop yet. Amtrak serves both cities on longer routes, and a thruway coach appears on some schedules. Confirm Amtrak for your date.

### Where does the bus drop in Tampa?

FlixBus lists the HART center on N. Marion Street and a USF stop. Neither is a theme-park gate.

## Final Thoughts

Treat Malfunction Junction as mile zero, get off at 62 for Disney before Express matters, use 74–75 only when Universal or I-Drive is the real destination, and do not let a rental-car toll product surprise you at the Orlando end. The bus is the simple no-drive option; Brightline to Tampa is still a plan.

For beach instead of theme parks, switch to [Tampa to Clearwater](/guides/tampa-to-clearwater). For a first day back in town, use [things to do in Tampa](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa).

body:
# Staying at the Barrymore Hotel Tampa: My Honest Riverwalk Guide

The name is The Barrymore Hotel Tampa Riverwalk. That long phrase is the hotel’s own name, not a booking-site nickname. Address: 111 West Fortune Street, Tampa, Florida 33602. Phone (813) 223-1351. It calls itself a downtown waterfront hotel.

I wanted the hotel’s own word on rooms, amenities, dining, parking, and the shuttle—not a booking-site summary. Fortune Street puts you on the river side of downtown, close enough that Riverwalk walks and arena nights feel walkable, and far enough from TPA that the free shuttle will not save an airport fare. **Last updated:** November 2, 2026.

![Hotel lobby seating area with soft lighting](/images/articles/barrymore-hotel-tampa/barrymore-271624.webp)
*Photo by [Pixabay](https://www.pexels.com/@pixabay/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/architecture-building-business-chairs-271624/)*

## Book With These Facts First

- **Check-in 3:00 p.m., check-out 11:00 a.m.** Early/late options depend on occupancy.
- **Shuttle is 2 miles, 8:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m.** Not an airport van.
- **Self-parking $20 per night** in the gated lot.
- **Pets: $75 flat** for the stay, not per night.

## Location Along the Riverwalk

The hotel says it is near the Tampa Convention Center, Amalie Arena, Armature Works, Curtis Hixon Waterfront Park, and the Tampa River Center, and “moments” from Busch Gardens and Adventure Island. It also says Raymond James Stadium is 4.9 miles away. Moments and a two-mile shuttle radius are not the same measurement—I noticed that when I lined the claims up against a real downtown stay.

The outdoor pool deck overlooks the Hillsborough River. The pool is open sunrise to sunset daily with no lifeguard on duty. Do not send a kid there assuming a guard is watching. Sunrise to sunset is a moving clock, not a fixed open/close time.

ZIP 33602 is the code this hotel uses—and the City of Tampa uses for city hall at 306 East Jackson Street. It is not “the” Tampa ZIP. See my [Tampa ZIP guide](/guides/tampa-zip-code) if you are filling a form.

For neighborhood food and walks, pair a Barrymore stay with [Armature Works](/food-and-drink/armature-works-tampa) upriver and my [things to do in Tampa](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa) list. Convention weeks overlap with the [Tampa Convention Center](/guides/tampa-convention-center) calendar when that guide is live; the hotel itself names the center as a nearby landmark.

## Shuttle, Airport, and Getting Around

Complimentary shuttle: inside a 2-mile radius, first come first served, 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. daily. It does not go to Tampa International Airport. The hotel says airport and other trips can be arranged with Blue One Transportation at (813) 282-7351, and that the hotel is not affiliated with Blue One. Uber and Lyft are the other option.

If you land at TPA expecting a free hotel airport ride, this property will disappoint you on purpose. Two miles covers a chunk of downtown. It does not cover the airport, and it does not cover Busch Gardens. Use my [TPA arrival guide](/getting-around/tampa-international-airport) for the curb, then rideshare or Blue One.

On-site Zipcar station, lobby ATM (fees apply), guest laundry plus dry-cleaning pickup, and free high-speed Wi-Fi throughout.

## Parking and Pets

Self-parking is on site in a gated lot at **$20 per night per vehicle**—stated more than once on the hotel site. Buses and RVs have space; call the front desk before arrival. Confirm current parking on [Barrymore amenities](https://www.barrymorehotel.com/amenities).

Pet-friendly: **$75 pet fee** no matter the length of stay. “Doggie Business Center” at the back of the property. Pet gifts at check-in, one per guest room. They partner with the Humane Society of Tampa Bay. Dog walks: across the Fortune Taylor Bridge to Julian B. Lane Riverfront Park (the hotel sometimes spells it Julien) and Curtis Hixon, which they call about a 15-minute walk. Water Works Park is also nearby for a splash-pad afternoon with kids.

## Rooms and Cancellation

Three room types: one king; two queens; accessible room with one queen and an ADA roll-in shower. Overlapping amenities: complimentary Wi-Fi, linens, European bath amenities, mini-fridge, microwave, 42-inch flat-screen, single-cup coffee maker, alarm clock. King and two-queen rooms also mention an activity table.

When I checked, each of the three types was quoted at $132.00. Treat that as a moment-in-time quote, not a locked rate—hotel prices move. Recheck when you book. Cancellation: cancel at no charge until 4:00 p.m. the day before arrival; after that the fee is the first night’s room and tax. Non-refundable promotional rooms are excepted.

24-hour fitness center: treadmills, ellipticals, free weights, stationary bikes, leg machines, Precor FTS Glide. Barry’s Market is the lobby grab-and-go.

Ship & Shore cruise package (when offered): exclusive room rate, parking up to 10 days during the cruise, shuttle to/from Port Tampa Bay—present boarding passes at check-in. Details on the hotel’s offers pages.

## Gaudin Kitchen & Bar Hours

Gaudin Kitchen & Bar is the on-site restaurant, connected to the lobby—cocktail-forward, New American. Hours from the hotel’s FAQ answers (the marketing blurb alone does not list them):

- **Breakfast:** 7:00 a.m.–11:00 a.m. daily  
- **Lunch:** Thursday–Sunday 11:30 a.m.–4:00 p.m.  
- **Dinner:** 4:00 p.m.–10:00 p.m. daily  
- **Late-night menu:** Wednesday–Saturday 10:00 p.m.–midnight  
- **Bar:** 4:00 p.m.–1:00 a.m.

Monday at noon looking for lunch is the trap—I thought that split was the real difficulty, not the menu adjectives. Confirm on [Barrymore FAQs](https://www.barrymorehotel.com/faqs) before you plan around Gaudin.

Compared with [The Westin Tampa Waterside](/guides/the-westin-tampa-waterside) or [The Tampa EDITION](/guides/the-tampa-edition), the Barrymore’s pitch is Riverwalk practical: gated lot price you can plan around, pet fee that does not shrink on a one-night stay, and a shuttle that is downtown-sized.

## Meetings and Events

Over 4,000 square feet of flexible meeting space, ballroom, outdoor pool deck space, linens, lighting, A/V, podium, projector, screen, flip charts, plated or buffet catering. Setups named: theater, classroom, U-shaped, and more. Guest room blocks available. Weddings, receptions, and engagement parties are marketed. Ask planning staff for counts and rental prices—those were not posted as a simple public chart when I looked.

## What I Would Plan Around

The shuttle radius is the trap I noticed first: two miles covers a chunk of downtown; it does not cover TPA, and it does not match the hotel’s “moments” wording for Busch Gardens. Self-parking at $20 a night and the flat $75 pet fee are the numbers the hotel actually states. Gaudin’s split hours are the other lesson—breakfast daily is real; lunch only Thursday–Sunday is easy to miss. If I showed up Monday at noon looking for lunch, the restaurant blurb would not have warned me; the hotel FAQ would. Recheck the room rate the day you book, and confirm Gaudin hours before you build a meal plan around it.

**Last updated:** November 2, 2026.

## FAQ

### Does the Barrymore shuttle go to Tampa International Airport?

No. The complimentary shuttle stays inside a 2-mile radius, 8:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m. For TPA, use rideshare or arrange Blue One Transportation (hotel not affiliated).

### How much is parking?

Self-parking in the gated lot is $20 per night per vehicle on the hotel’s amenities page. Call ahead for bus or RV parking.

### Is the Barrymore pet-friendly?

Yes. Flat $75 pet fee per stay, pet amenities on property, and nearby riverfront parks for walks. Ask the front desk about restrictions.

### What are Gaudin’s hours?

Breakfast daily 7–11 a.m.; lunch Thursday–Sunday only; dinner daily from 4 p.m. Late-night menu Wednesday–Saturday. Confirm before you go.

### When is check-in?

3:00 p.m. check-in and 11:00 a.m. check-out. Early check-in and late check-out depend on occupancy and room type.

## Final Thoughts

The Barrymore is a downtown Riverwalk hotel with a clear parking number, a real pet fee, and a shuttle that stops being free the moment you aim it at the airport. Recheck the room rate the day you book, and do not plan Monday lunch at Gaudin without reading the FAQ hours.

For Water Street / Convention Center instead, see [Marriott Water Street Tampa](/guides/marriott-water-street-tampa). For a Westshore base instead, see the [Westshore Marriott](/guides/westshore-marriott-hotel-tampa). For waterfront dining a short ride west, [Rusty Pelican](/food-and-drink/rusty-pelican-tampa) on Rocky Point is the airport-adjacent seafood room—not a hotel restaurant inside TPA.

body:
# Rusty Pelican Tampa: My Honest Rocky Point Guide

Rusty Pelican Tampa is the waterfront seafood restaurant on Rocky Point—fresh Gulf seafood, surf and turf, tropical ambiance, and bay views. People go for brunch by the water, a romantic dinner, a late-night meal after landing near [Tampa International Airport](/getting-around/tampa-international-airport), or a private event with a Tampa Bay backdrop. Visit Tampa Bay files the cuisine as Seafood and the style as Upscale Casual, and highlights plates like Key West Black Grouper and Crispy Whole Local Snapper plus Midwestern beef cuts with Caribbean flair on local seafood.

Address: **2425 N Rocky Point Drive, Tampa, FL 33607**. Phone **(813) 281-1943**. Book through the restaurant’s [reservations page](https://www.therustypelicantampa.com/reservations). **Last updated:** November 2, 2026.

![Plated dinner on a restaurant table](/images/articles/rusty-pelican-tampa/rusty-pelican-262047.webp)
*Photo by [Pixabay](https://www.pexels.com/@pixabay/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/food-dinner-lunch-table-262047/)*

## First Things First

- **Bay views and seafood first**—then confirm you booked Tampa, not Miami.
- **Brunch Sat–Sun; happy hour in the bar/lounge on weekdays** (see hours below).
- **Self-park and valet** are both listed; put the full street number in the rideshare.
- **Reservations accepted**—use the restaurant’s own hours when directories disagree.

## Location Mix-Up (Tampa vs Miami, TPA vs Terminal)

The same brand name points at a different restaurant in Miami / Key Biscayne: 3201 Rickenbacker Causeway, Key Biscayne, FL 33149, phone (305) 361-3818, different hours. Booking the Key Biscayne sunset and then driving to TPA because the name matched ruins the night.

Visit Tampa Bay places the Tampa room minutes from Tampa International, minutes from downtown, and between Pinellas, Hillsborough, and Pasco. That is **airport-adjacent**, not inside a terminal. You still need a car, rideshare, or hotel shuttle. Rocky Point is west of downtown—not Ybor, not Water Street.

Bahama Breeze at 3045 N Rocky Point Drive East is a different driveway. Put **2425** in the reservation note.

For Westshore shopping before dinner, [International Plaza](/shopping/international-plaza-tampa) is the nearby mall people mean.

## Menu Highlights

Official / visitor-bureau highlights (menus change—confirm on [all menus](https://www.therustypelicantampa.com/all-menus)):

- Fresh local seafood with Caribbean flair  
- **Key West Black Grouper** and **Crispy Whole Local Snapper** (named on Visit Tampa Bay)  
- Classic Midwestern cuts of beef alongside the seafood  
- Separate menu tracks for food, lunch, brunch, drinks, and happy hour on the restaurant site  

I am not freezing plate prices here beyond the visitor bureau’s average-entree figure below—ask for the current menu.

## View and Atmosphere

Visit Tampa Bay describes breathtaking views of Tampa Bay and a waterfront banquet, dining, and event facility. The restaurant pitches tropical ambiance for romantic dinners, brunch by the water, and late-night meals. Style: **Upscale Casual**. Wheelchair accessible per Visit Tampa Bay. Event spaces include outdoor patios and a ceremony gazebo; the Bay Room is described with fireplace, stained-glass, bay views, private entry, and up to **50** guests.

## Brunch

On the restaurant’s reservations hours: **Saturday and Sunday brunch 10:30 a.m.–4:00 p.m.**, with dinner from 4:30 p.m. Confirm the brunch menu on the restaurant site before you go.

## Happy Hour

- Reservations hours card: **Monday–Thursday happy hour 4:00–6:00 p.m.**  
- Happy Hour menu page: **Monday–Friday 4:00–6:30 p.m.**, **Bar and Lounge only** ([happy hour menu](https://www.therustypelicantampa.com/menus/happy-hour))  

Those two restaurant pages do not match exactly on Friday or the end time. Use the happy-hour menu page for bar/lounge rules, and call **(813) 281-1943** if your night is a holiday.

## Reservations

Reservations are accepted (Visit Tampa Bay lists “Accept Reservations”). Book at [therustypelicantampa.com/reservations](https://www.therustypelicantampa.com/reservations). For large parties and weddings, contact the events team rather than guessing from directory capacity fields.

## Dress Code

Visit Tampa Bay lists style as **Upscale Casual**. The restaurant site does not publish a separate banned-items dress code that I could confirm—dress to that upscale-casual bar.

## Price Range

Visit Tampa Bay lists **average price of entree: $28**. That is a directory average, not a frozen menu. For live entrée prices, use the restaurant menus. Major credit cards accepted per Visit Tampa Bay.

## Parking

Visit Tampa Bay lists **self park** and **valet parking**. No dollar amount for valet appears on the restaurant’s public reservations page when I checked—ask the host or valet stand the night you go. Do not confuse this lot with Bahama Breeze’s driveway.

## Hours (Restaurant Reservations Page)

- **Monday–Thursday:** 11:00 a.m.–10:30 p.m. (lunch 11 a.m.–4:00 p.m.; dinner 4:30–10:30 p.m.)  
- **Friday:** 11:00 a.m.–12:00 a.m. (lunch 11 a.m.–4 p.m.; dinner 4:30 p.m.–12 a.m.)  
- **Saturday:** 10:30 a.m.–12:00 a.m. (brunch 10:30 a.m.–4:00 p.m.; dinner 4:30 p.m.–12 a.m.)  
- **Sunday:** 10:30 a.m.–10:30 p.m. (brunch 10:30 a.m.–4:00 p.m.; dinner 4:30–10:30 p.m.)  

Source: [reservations](https://www.therustypelicantampa.com/reservations). Visit Tampa Bay’s hours card has disagreed with these clocks—trust the restaurant.

## Events

Waterfront banquet and event facility for corporate and social groups (Visit Tampa Bay). The restaurant markets event spaces, outdoor patios, and a ceremony gazebo. Meeting rooms named in visitor materials include Grand Ballroom, Pelican Ballroom, Coral Room, Tampa Room, and Bay Room. Directory capacity fields bounce (indoor seats, total restaurant capacity, and private/group capacity do not all describe the same Tuesday four-top). For a wedding or company dinner, talk to the venue—**50 in the Bay Room** is the number the restaurant itself stands behind for that room. In-house catering and a liquor license are listed on the visitor-bureau amenities.

## Hours vs Directories

Visit Tampa Bay’s hours card has disagreed with the restaurant’s reservations clocks—weekday lunch ending earlier, different Sunday brunch cutoffs, Saturday labeled lunch instead of brunch. People repeat the visitor-bureau hours and then argue with the host. I go by the restaurant’s own [reservations](https://www.therustypelicantampa.com/reservations) page and still call (813) 281-1943 on holidays.

## Where People Struggle

First, the Miami restaurant. Second, treating “minutes from TPA” like a terminal walk. Third, hours wars between directories and the restaurant. Fourth, picking the wrong Rocky Point driveway. Fifth, planning a seated dinner off contradictory capacity fields instead of calling events.

It is not Bern’s on South Howard, and it is not a hotel restaurant inside TPA. If what you really wanted was “nice restaurants near my airport hotel,” say the Rocky Point address out loud before you confirm. For a churrascaria night instead of Rocky Point seafood, see [Terra Gaucha](/food-and-drink/terra-gaucha-tampa) or [Texas de Brazil](/food-and-drink/texas-de-brazil-tampa). Downtown Water Street after a Channelside day is a different errand—[Yard House](/food-and-drink/yard-house-tampa) sits in that cluster.

## FAQ

### Is Rusty Pelican Tampa the same as the Miami Rusty Pelican?

No. Tampa is at 2425 N Rocky Point Drive, phone (813) 281-1943. Miami/Key Biscayne is a separate restaurant on Rickenbacker Causeway.

### Do they have brunch and happy hour?

Brunch Saturday–Sunday 10:30 a.m.–4:00 p.m. on the reservations hours. Happy hour is weekday bar/lounge service—see the happy-hour menu page for Mon–Fri 4:00–6:30 p.m. Bar and Lounge only.

### How much does it cost?

Visit Tampa Bay’s average entree figure is $28. Confirm live menu prices at the restaurant.

### Is there parking?

Yes—self-park and valet per Visit Tampa Bay. Confirm valet pricing on site.

### What should I wear?

Upscale casual (Visit Tampa Bay style listing).

## Final Thoughts

Go for the bay view and the seafood house on Rocky Point; then double-check the city and the street number so you do not end up in Key Biscayne or at Bahama Breeze. For a churrascaria night instead, see [Terra Gaucha](/food-and-drink/terra-gaucha-tampa) or [Texas de Brazil](/food-and-drink/texas-de-brazil-tampa). For a broader eat list, start with [things to do in Tampa](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa).

### Fact sources

- [Rusty Pelican reservations / hours](https://www.therustypelicantampa.com/reservations)  
- [Happy hour menu](https://www.therustypelicantampa.com/menus/happy-hour)  
- [All menus](https://www.therustypelicantampa.com/all-menus)  
- [Visit Tampa Bay — The Rusty Pelican](https://www.visittampabay.com/listings/the-rusty-pelican/8334/)

# Terra Gaucha Tampa: My Honest Guide (Dale Mabry Churrascaria)

Terra Gaucha Tampa is the South Tampa Brazilian steakhouse at **1108 South Dale Mabry Highway, Tampa, FL 33629**—fire-roasted cuts carved tableside, a Gourmet Hot and Cold Table, desserts, and handcrafted cocktails under what the restaurant calls the Ultimate Churrasco Experience. People go for a full rodizio night, a hot-and-cold-table-only meal, a weekend lunch that prices closer to dinner, Tuesday live music, or a private/semi-private group event.

Phone **(813) 999-4332**. Email office@terragaucha.net. Confirm city and pricing on [Terra Gaucha Tampa](https://terragaucha.com/location-tampa/). **Last updated:** November 2, 2026.

I started with the longer search phrase because the short name mixes this room up with every other Brazilian steakhouse nearby—especially [Texas de Brazil](/food-and-drink/texas-de-brazil-tampa) on Boy Scout in Westshore and Terra Gaucha Jacksonville on Southside Boulevard. I would put the street number in the rideshare note so the pin lands on Dale Mabry.

![Grilled meat dinner plate ready to serve](/images/articles/terra-gaucha-tampa/terra-gaucha-323682.webp)
*Photo by [Pixabay](https://www.pexels.com/@pixabay/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/food-plate-healthy-dinner-323682/)*

## Before You Book

- **Confirm the city** on the reservation (Jacksonville, Stamford, and other cities exist).  
- **Pick a price tier**—full churrasco, table only, or chicken/pork/seafood.  
- **Weekday lunch ≠ weekend lunch.**  
- **Parties over 15** use group dining.  

## Menu Highlights

From the Tampa location page and FAQs:

- **Full Churrasco Experience** — premium fire-roasted cuts carved tableside plus the Gourmet Hot and Cold Table  
- **Gourmet Hot and Cold Table only** — a real purchase tier, not a free graze  
- **Chicken, pork, and seafood** option — includes the hot and cold table  
- Desserts named on materials include Brazilian flan and papaya cream  
- Large portion of the menu described as gluten-free; tell the server about allergies  
- Vegetarian path: hot and cold table with fresh dishes and vegetables ([FAQs](https://terragaucha.com/faqs/))  
- No separate kids menu; ages 0–5 complimentary, 6–12 half price  

Live music in Tampa: **Tuesdays 7:00–9:00 p.m.** (schedule may change without notice).

## Atmosphere

The Tampa page describes a refined nightlife feel in South Tampa near US 92, with private and semi-private spaces for events. Group dining materials emphasize a refined atmosphere, premium cuts, Brazilian-inspired dishes, and a dedicated server for larger parties. This is a sit-down churrascaria experience, not a food-hall counter and not a quick Westshore mall dinner. If your group wants a quieter corner, ask about semi-private space when you book through group dining—those rooms are part of how the Tampa location markets itself for celebrations and business nights.

Terra Gaucha also operates in Jacksonville, Stamford, Indianapolis, Omaha, Rockville, and Phoenix. Tampa is its own restaurant on Dale Mabry. If a confirmation says Southside Boulevard or a Connecticut mall, you booked the wrong city.

## Brunch / Lunch

There is no separate “brunch” label on the Tampa page—**lunch** is the midday service:

- **Mon–Thu:** 11:30 a.m.–2:00 p.m.  
- **Fri:** 11:30 a.m.–2:30 p.m.  
- **Sat–Sun:** 11:30 a.m.–3:00 p.m.  

Weekend lunch prices sit much closer to dinner than weekday lunch (see Price Range).

## Happy Hour

**Terra Bites** (happy hour) is **Monday–Friday 4:30–6:30 p.m.** at patio or bar—and FAQs state it is **exclusive to Terra Gaucha Stamford**. There is no Tampa Terra Bites window. Expect a weekday gap between lunch end and dinner start (dinner begins 5:00 p.m. Mon–Thu).

## Reservations

Reservations are **not required**, but the restaurant encourages booking—especially weekends and holidays—at [terragaucha.com/reservations](https://terragaucha.com/reservations) (FAQs). Parties **over 15** go through [group dining](https://terragaucha.com/groupdining) for private/semi-private rooms, buyouts, and packages (birthdays, engagements, rehearsal dinners, end-of-year events, business meetings).

## Dress Code

FAQs: no specific dress code; they **recommend smart casual**.

## Price Range

Posted on the Tampa location page (subject to change; holiday pricing can apply):

| | Full Churrasco | Hot & Cold Table | Chicken/Pork/Seafood |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Dinner (every night)** | $65.95 | $29.95 | $41.95 |
| **Weekday lunch (Mon–Fri)** | $42.95 | $19.95 | $31.95 |
| **Weekend lunch (Sat–Sun)** | $59.95 | $29.95 | $38.95 |

Children 6–12 half price; 0–5 complimentary. Confirm live numbers before you go.

## Parking

Tampa location page: **ample parking lot on site**. No valet fee posted. Dale Mabry is a busy commercial road—still use 1108 South Dale Mabry so you do not land at Westshore.

Nearby on the same corridor (different meals): [Wright’s Gourmet House](/food-and-drink/wrights-gourmet-house-tampa) and [Yummy House](/food-and-drink/yummy-house-tampa).

## Hours (Dinner)

- **Mon–Thu:** 5:00–9:30 p.m.  
- **Fri:** 5:00–10:30 p.m.  
- **Sat:** 4:00–10:30 p.m.  
- **Sun:** 4:00–9:30 p.m.  

Thanksgiving and other holidays can post special windows—the Tampa page has listed an extended single-day window around Thanksgiving in the past. Call (813) 999-4332 rather than assuming the regular dinner clock.

## Special Offers (Terra Club)

Birthday and anniversary deals run through Terra Club email signup ([FAQs](https://terragaucha.com/faqs/)):

- **Birthday:** $25 off the visit tied to the birthday email, plus a $25 birthday dining card for a later visit—must show the Terra Gaucha birthday email. Restrictions apply.  
- **Anniversary:** free dessert for the table plus a $25 anniversary dining card for a later visit if you are on the list. Restrictions apply.  

Do not walk in announcing a birthday and expecting the discount without that email.

## Where People Get Stuck

The first stuck point is the name and city—booking without reading the city on the confirmation is how Jacksonville and Stamford reservations happen. The second is the price tier: full churrasco, table only, and chicken-pork-seafood are three different checks, and weekend lunch is not weekday lunch. The third is the afternoon gap with no Tampa Terra Bites. The fourth is a party of 16 trying a regular reservation instead of group dining. The fifth is building a birthday around Tuesday music that might not run that week.

If booking gives you trouble, call (813) 999-4332 or email office@terragaucha.net. For a same-night party-size change, call rather than assuming the inbox is watched during dinner service.

South Tampa is the neighborhood context the restaurant gives; US 92 is the road context. Westshore / Boy Scout is a different Brazilian steakhouse night entirely—use [Texas de Brazil Tampa](/food-and-drink/texas-de-brazil-tampa) if that is the pin you meant.

## FAQ

### Is Terra Gaucha Tampa the same as Texas de Brazil?

No. Terra Gaucha is on South Dale Mabry in South Tampa. Texas de Brazil is on Boy Scout Boulevard in Westshore.

### How much does it cost?

Dinner full churrasco posts at $65.95; weekday lunch full experience $42.95; weekend lunch full experience $59.95—confirm on the Tampa location page.

### Do I need a reservation?

Not required; book for weekends and holidays. Over 15 guests: group dining.

### Is there happy hour in Tampa?

Terra Bites is Stamford-only per FAQs. No Tampa happy hour window.

### What should I wear?

Smart casual recommended; no formal dress code.

## Final Thoughts

Terra Gaucha Tampa is the Dale Mabry churrascaria, not the Westshore Texas de Brazil and not Jacksonville. Get the pin right, pick the price tier on purpose, and do not treat weekend lunch like the weekday deal. Tuesday music is a bonus when it runs—not a promise to build a whole night around. Recheck the Tampa location page the day you go; pricing is posted as subject to change without notice.

For Rocky Point seafood instead of churrasco, see [Rusty Pelican Tampa](/food-and-drink/rusty-pelican-tampa). For airport logistics, use [TPA](/getting-around/tampa-international-airport). Broader plans: [things to do in Tampa](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa).

### Fact sources

- [Terra Gaucha Tampa location (hours, prices, parking, music)](https://terragaucha.com/location-tampa/)  
- [Terra Gaucha FAQs (reservations, dress, kids, Terra Bites, vegetarian/GF)](https://terragaucha.com/faqs/)

metaDescription: Tampa flea market guide: Big Top closed in 2020; Oldsmar weekend booth hours and free parking; Ybor Saturday Market seasonal times explained.
body:
# Tampa Flea Market: Big Top Closed, Where to Go Instead

I went looking for a flea market in Tampa under every name people use: tampa flea market tampa fl, tampa flea market, flea market tampa, florida flea market tampa, flea markets in tampa. I expected one obvious place with that name on the gate. I did not find a market, open now, whose real name is Tampa Flea Market—and I am not inventing one.

What I found hunting the name from Tampa: a famous market that closed, a large weekend market that is real but not inside the city, and a Saturday market that is inside Tampa ZIP 33605 but is not a classic junk flea. **Last updated:** November 2, 2026.

![Outdoor market stall filled with fresh produce](/images/articles/tampa-flea-market/flea-market-264636.webp)
*Photo by [Pixabay](https://www.pexels.com/@pixabay/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/fruits-and-vegetables-on-market-stall-264636/)*

## Quick Answers

- **Big Top Flea Market:** permanently closed April 26, 2020—do not drive to Fowler for booths
- **Oldsmar Flea Market:** the acres-of-booths weekend market—180 Racetrack Rd, Oldsmar, FL 34677; Sat–Sun 8 a.m.–3 p.m.; free parking
- **Ybor City Saturday Market:** inside Tampa 33605—produce and makers, not a classic flea; seasonal end times
- **No live “Tampa Flea Market” brand** matching the search phrase as a gate name

## Big Top Is What People Still Mean—and It Is Gone

The name that kept coming up as “Tampa’s flea market” is Big Top. In January 2020, management told vendors the last day open would be April 26, 2020, at 5 p.m., after 26 years. Vendors could return April 27–May 3 to clear stalls. After May 3, Big Top was permanently closed.

Local photo history: Big Top started in the early 1960s on Dale Mabry Highway in Tampa, later moved to a larger Fowler Avenue site in Thonotosassa, and was called one of the largest flea markets in the Southeast. The “26 years” line matches the Fowler era more than the entire Dale Mabry history. After the 2020 sale and rezoning, the site became the Livano Uptown apartment community. As of 2026, remaining commercial parcels on the old footprint are redeveloping—including a Wawa planned for a Fowler Avenue parcel with construction underway toward a mid-2027 opening. There is no live Big Top operation with current hours. If a directory still shows a phone and a Fowler address, treat it as a leftover. The mini-donut memories are history. The market is not there.

## Oldsmar: The Big Weekend Flea That Is Actually Open

The market that matches what people mean when they say flea market tampa and picture acres of booths is Oldsmar Flea Market. It is not in Tampa. Address: 180 Racetrack Road, Oldsmar, Florida 34677. Office phone 813-855-2587.

**Hours:** Saturday and Sunday 8 a.m. to 3 p.m. Monday–Friday the office lists closed. A limited number of vendors may be open on weekdays—Wacky Wizard Hardware, Everything Birds, and T&D Golf—check those vendors directly; that is not “the whole market is open Wednesday.”

**Parking:** free for visitors.

**Dogs:** welcome only if carried or in a stroller.

**ATMs:** one in building D, one in building H. Several vendors take cards—which implies not all do. Bring cash backup.

Goods people find without needing a treasure map: snacks, fresh produce, fashion, vintage clothing, golf equipment, sunglasses, rugs, furniture, classic video games. Featured booths when I looked included a family cigar seller in the J West breezeway, a hemp and glass shop, and a luggage booth in building I East.

**Fact update from older “28 acres” talk:** in July 2026 the market announced it would keep operating after selling the southern portion of the property for apartments, continuing from the remaining **16-acre** portion, still every weekend 8 a.m.–3 p.m. Confirm on [Oldsmar Flea Market](https://www.oldsmarfleamarket.com/).

That is the struggle with “florida flea market tampa.” People want this scale, and the open answer is a weekend drive to Oldsmar with a hard stop at 3 p.m. I would go Saturday morning, not Tuesday, and I would not bring a dog that has to walk.

From downtown, build time for the drive—this is not a Riverwalk hop. Pair with a beach day using [Tampa to Clearwater](/guides/tampa-to-clearwater) only if you want a long Saturday; otherwise keep Oldsmar as its own errand.

## Ybor City Saturday Market: In Tampa, Not a Classic Flea

If tampa flea market tampa fl means “inside the city, in the ZIP,” the recurring market I could confirm is the Ybor City Saturday Market. It is not a flea in the Big Top sense. It has operated since 2000 and calls itself the largest continually operating outdoor market in the Tampa Bay area—local produce, gourmet foods, bread, herbs, plants, pet treats, honey, cigars, gifts, art, jewelry, woodwork, and candles.

**Location:** 1901 North 19th Street, Tampa, FL 33605 (state agriculture department and Ybor chamber agree). Phone 813-241-2442.

**Hours:** every Saturday, year-round, rain or shine—October through April 9 a.m.–3 p.m.; May through September 9 a.m.–1 p.m. They post updates for lightning or tropical storms. No Sunday version.

A cool-season Saturday runs until 3. A summer Saturday is a four-hour market done at 1 p.m. If someone calls the Ybor market “the flea market,” they are mixing a producer and artisan market with a booth flea. Both can be worth a morning. They are not the same errand. For more on the district, see [Ybor City](/guides/ybor-city-tampa-fl-33605).

## Three Mix-Ups I Kept Seeing

**Dead map pin.** Searching tampa flea market still drags up Big Top. Last public day was April 26, 2020. Showing up on Fowler for antiques is how you find apartments (and future Wawa construction), not booths.

**City line.** Oldsmar is the acres-of-booths answer, open Saturday and Sunday 8–3, free parking, dogs carried, weekdays mostly dark. Calling it a Tampa flea market is a habit, not an address.

**Expecting one market to be both.** Ybor’s Saturday market is in 33605 on 19th Street and shuts earlier in hot months. It will not scratch the itch for a football field of used tools. Oldsmar will not scratch the itch for a walk from Centro Ybor.

## Tips From My Search

Go to Oldsmar when you want the flea—weekend, early, cash as backup because they bothered to tell you where the ATMs are. Go to the Ybor Saturday market when you want produce, bread, and small-maker stalls and you are already in the historic district; leave by 1 p.m. May–September. Do not go back to Big Top. There is nothing there to go back to.

For indoor shopping instead, [International Plaza](/shopping/international-plaza-tampa) is the Westshore mall day. For a food-hall morning in Tampa Heights, [Armature Works](/food-and-drink/armature-works-tampa) is a different kind of browse.

## FAQ

### Is there a Tampa Flea Market open right now?

There is no major market currently operating under the exact name “Tampa Flea Market.” Big Top closed in 2020. Use Oldsmar for a classic flea or Ybor Saturday Market for a city producer market.

### What happened to Big Top Flea Market?

It closed permanently on April 26, 2020. The Fowler / Thonotosassa site was redeveloped; apartments and new commercial projects occupy the footprint.

### Where is the closest big flea market to Tampa?

Oldsmar Flea Market at 180 Racetrack Road, Oldsmar—Saturday and Sunday 8 a.m.–3 p.m., free parking.

### Is the Ybor market a flea market?

It is an outdoor Saturday market focused on produce, food, and artisans—not a classic multi-acre junk-and-tools flea like Oldsmar or historic Big Top.

### Can I bring my dog to Oldsmar?

Only if the dog is carried or in a stroller.

## Final Thoughts

The search phrase wants one gate. Tampa gives you a closed legend, a weekend drive to Oldsmar, and a Saturday produce market in Ybor. Once I stopped hunting for a living “Tampa Flea Market” sign, the plan got simple: Oldsmar for the flea, Ybor for the makers, Fowler only if you like looking at apartments.

For a full weekend list beyond markets, start with [things to do in Tampa](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa).

body:
# Skatepark of Tampa (SPoT): Hours, Rates, and How to Get There

People ask for skatepark of tampa and the shorter tampa skatepark. What I wanted was one address and a straight answer about what is actually on the lot. The address was the easy part. Hours and prices used to fight each other on the park’s own pages—now the live card is clearer, and you should still confirm at the shop before you pay.

From east of Ybor, SPoT is a short I-4 hop when someone wants to ride—not a downtown Riverwalk stop. **Last updated:** November 2, 2026.

![Skateboarder performing a trick in a skate park](/images/articles/skatepark-of-tampa/spot-32435746.webp)
*Photo by [Andres Idda Bianchi](https://www.pexels.com/@andres-idda-bianchi-2148503290/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/skateboarder-performing-trick-in-skate-park-32435746/)*

## Visit Snapshot

- **Address:** 4215 East Columbus Drive, Tampa, FL 33605-3202
- **Phone:** (813) 247-1785
- **Regular hours (Aug. 10–Dec. 20, 2026):** Mon–Fri 2–9 p.m.; Sat 11 a.m.–9 p.m.; Sun 11 a.m.–6 p.m.
- **Non-member skate:** $20 all day; last hour half price
- **BMX:** Wednesdays and Sundays (full session); other days bowl/concrete course only at lower rate
- **Must:** waiver for everyone; helmet required for everyone except skateboarders

Confirm live hours and rates on [SPoT hours](https://skateparkoftampa.com/pages/hours-page) and [rates](https://skateparkoftampa.com/pages/rates).

## Exact Address and the Exit That Matters

The park’s exact address is 4215 East Columbus Drive, Tampa, FL 33605-3202—a Tampa ZIP, not St. Petersburg. The park’s own directions say it is one exit east of Ybor City off Interstate 4. That is the useful part. From north or south: I-4 to exit 3 (50th Street / Columbus Drive). Coming off I-4 East: left at the first light onto Columbus, then less than half a mile—park on the left at 4215. From I-4 West: follow the Columbus Drive sign; again on the left, less than half a mile. From Highway 60 on the east side: U.S. 41 / 50th Street north to Columbus, left, then about a mile on the left.

One west-side approach disagrees with itself: Courtney Campbell → I-275 → I-4 East → exit 3 → left on Columbus → park on the left, versus a Tampa Road / Hillsborough / 40th Street version that puts the park a quarter mile down on the right. Left in one set, right in another, same street number. Trust the number and exit 3. Do not trust a single “it’s on your left” once you are on Columbus.

This is not a casino, Bucs stadium, Lightning arena, AMC, hotel, or concert hall. Those addresses are not 4215 East Columbus Drive.

## What Is on the Property

Going by how the park describes itself: a skate shop, a snack bar, an indoor bowl, and outdoor concrete. SPoT Skateshop at Skatepark of Tampa was established in 1993 and has shipped online since 1997—inventory live, usually ships within one business day. Free shipping on orders of $93 or more (cannot combine with other discounts). In kids’ morning-session rules (when that window is running), ages 13 and up may ride the cement courtyard and indoor bowl only during the early window. The rate card talks about a bowl and a concrete course—same idea in different words. Birthday parties get a designated snack-bar area. Nobody publishes square footage or an obstacle count, so I am not inventing one.

Riding rules are clearer than the floor plan. Skateboards, roller skates, inlines, and scooters are permitted every day. BMX is not every-day—Wednesdays and Sundays for full sessions; other days the bowl and concrete course only at the BMX day rate. Full pads encouraged for everyone. Everyone except skateboarders must wear a helmet, even over 18. Waiver required for everyone. Under 18: a parent or legal guardian over 18 must be with you, or bring a printed waiver that has been notarized.

## Hours and Rates: What Changed From Older Cards

When I first researched SPoT, the park posted conflicting cards—one with noon–8 p.m. weekday sessions and $8/$10 non-member prices, another with $20 days and $100/$500 memberships, plus a dated “August 10–December 20” block with no year. That conflict is why my notes refused to pick a door price.

**Current published regular hours (August 10–December 20, 2026):** Monday–Friday one session 2 p.m.–9 p.m.; Saturday 11 a.m.–9 p.m.; Sunday 11 a.m.–6 p.m. BMX permitted all day Wednesday and Sunday. Hours can still change for holidays and special events—ask at the shop.

**Non-member skate:** $20 all day every day; last hour of every session half price; military, police, paramedics, and firefighters half price with valid ID ($10).

**$100 membership (skate):** $10 admission; free shirt (up to $30 value); sticker pack; free the day you sign up; free on your birthday with a friend; free Mondays (“Membership Mondays”); free first Friday of the month; one free private lesson ($50 value); 10% off programs.

**$500 membership (skate):** framed as free skating all year with passes and lesson perks—confirm current math at the shop.

**BMX non-member:** $20 all day Wednesday and Sunday; $10 other days for bowl and concrete course only; last hour half price; first-responder half price with ID.

**Old Man Tuesday:** ages 30+ skate for $5 every third Tuesday of the month.

**Private lessons:** $50/hour on the rate card. **Private park rental:** 8 p.m.–11 p.m. excluding event days; $300 for three hours; $100 each extra hour; limited to 20 people; $15 each additional person—email info@skateparkoftampa.com.

**Birthday parties:** check current member/non-member package prices at the shop; book ahead; pad/helmet/board rental often included for the birthday kid.

Group lessons and after-school sessions still appear on older cards with different dollar amounts—confirm the live program board rather than an archived screenshot.

## Contests and Stale Dates

SPoT still promotes contests (Tampa Am, Tampa Pro, Damn Am, girls’ meetups) and sells Am tickets through Will Call. When I researched, some pages still showed 2024 contest dates. Treat year-old dates as history, not your weekend plan. Buy tickets for the date printed on the Will Call product, not a memory of last year’s flyer. A Rays-game retail promo the park ran is a shop discount—not a reason to think the skatepark is at the ballpark.

For a downtown art day instead of concrete, see [Tampa Museum of Art](/things-to-do/tampa-museum-of-art). Flying in first? [TPA](/getting-around/tampa-international-airport). Broader weekend plans: [things to do in Tampa](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa).

## Tips From Checking the Park

Trust 4215 East Columbus and I-4 exit 3. Confirm which hours card is on the door the week you go—especially around August and December when the “regular hours” window flips. Budget $20 for a non-member skate day unless you are in the last hour or have first-responder ID. Fill the digital waiver before you arrive; if the rider is under 18, bring the parent or a notarized printout. Helmets for everyone who is not on a skateboard. Do not mix this address with stadium or casino day plans.

## FAQ

### Where is Skatepark of Tampa?

4215 East Columbus Drive, Tampa, FL 33605—east of Ybor, I-4 exit 3 (50th / Columbus).

### How much does it cost to skate?

Non-member skate admission is $20 all day; last hour is half price. Members pay less under $100 or $500 plans. First responders skate half price with ID.

### Can I bring a BMX bike any day?

Full BMX sessions are Wednesdays and Sundays. Other days, BMX is limited to the bowl and concrete course at the posted BMX day rate.

### Do I need a helmet?

Yes if you are not on a skateboard—even over 18. Full pads are encouraged for everyone. Skateboarders are the helmet exception in the park’s posted rules.

### Do kids need a parent?

Under 18 requires a parent/guardian over 18 present, or a notarized printed waiver. Everyone needs a signed waiver.

## Final Thoughts

SPoT is a real Tampa skatepark with a shop and a bowl—not a downtown tourist stop. I would go back with the waiver already done and cash/card ready for the $20 day rate, and I would double-check BMX day before packing a bike.

If you want food after, [Ybor](/guides/ybor-city-tampa-fl-33605) is the nearby historic-district option. For a water-park day instead of concrete, see [Adventure Island](/things-to-do/adventure-island-tampa)—and confirm that seasonal calendar separately.

body:
# Visiting Adventure Island Tampa: My Honest Water Park Guide

When people ask me about a Tampa water park, they almost never mean a place with that exact name on the gate. There is no attraction branded Tampa Water Park. What they usually mean is Adventure Island, the seasonal United Parks water park at 10001 N McKinley Drive, Tampa, FL 33612, immediately north of Busch Gardens. Phone 813-884-4386.

From downtown / the Riverwalk, Adventure Island is a real drive, not a streetcar hop, and the calendar matters as much as the ticket. Adventure Island is a **seasonal** water park. On its Park Info page the park says thanks for the season, that it is **now closed for the 2026 season**, and that it looks forward to welcoming guests back in **2027**—meaning the 2026 operating season has ended, not that the park sat dark every day of the calendar year. The site does not publish a specific 2027 opening day on Park Info; plan on **spring 2027 and check the site** for the live calendar. 2027 Fun Card materials already list Adventure Island validity through **October 24, 2027**, which is an end-of-season marker, not an opening date. **Last updated:** November 2, 2026.

![Bright water slides at a sunny water park](/images/articles/adventure-island-tampa/adventure-island-261327.webp)
*Photo by [Pixabay](https://www.pexels.com/@pixabay/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/blue-and-yellow-water-slide-261327/)*

## What to Know Before You Go

- **Name check.** “Tampa water park” almost always means Adventure Island next to Busch Gardens.
- **Season first.** Confirm the 2027 calendar on the park site before you book a hotel day around it.
- **Separate tickets.** A Busch Gardens ticket does not automatically include the water park.
- **Pack light.** Outside food and personal chairs stay out; water bottles are the usual exception through security.

## Where Adventure Island Is, and Why the Name Confuses People

Adventure Island’s own directions put it about eight miles northeast of downtown, two miles east of I-275 at Busch Boulevard, and two miles west of I-75 at Fowler Avenue exit 265. It is not downtown and it is not the beach. It shares a neighborhood and a parent company with Busch Gardens Tampa Bay, which is the trap that burns day-trippers.

You can buy Busch Gardens alone, Adventure Island alone, or multi-park tickets that mix Florida parks including both. A dry-park ticket does not get you into the wet park on its own. Adventure Island is seasonal. The park tells you to check its calendar for hours and the same for tickets. In fall seasons I watched, the calendar often ran a Friday-through-Sunday pattern with a late-October end. I would not drive from a downtown hotel on a random weekday without checking that calendar first—and right now, with the 2026 season ended, the check is the 2027 calendar (spring 2027, confirm on the site).

Confirm status and hours on [Adventure Island park info](https://adventureisland.com/park-info/).

## What Is Inside When the Park Is Open

By the park’s own description: Endless Surf, a 17,000-square-foot wave pool; Rambling Bayou, a half-mile lazy river; Paradise Lagoon; Castaway Falls, the multi-level splash complex with tipping buckets and kid slides; Shaka-Laka Shores, a zero-depth splash zone with 25 play elements. Slides include family raft rides like Colossal Curl with a 48-inch minimum. Height rules are enforced per attraction.

Outside food and coolers stay out except water bottles, with dietary exceptions through security. Personal chairs stay out. Parking starts at $35 plus tax unless you have the right annual pass tier. Tickets are date-specific and non-refundable. Capacity can pause entry on crowded days.

Heat is half the story. Weather-or-Not Assurance on eligible tickets can cover early weather closures, long weather-related ride stops, or a heat index of 110 or above, but it does not refund parking or cabanas. That is the Tampa water park most people are hunting, even when they never say Adventure Island.

## Other Water Places People Mean (and What They Are Not)

While I was sorting the phrase, I also confirmed the near-misses so I would not send someone to the wrong gate.

**Buccaneer Bay** sits inside Weeki Wachee Springs State Park at 6131 Commercial Way, Weeki Wachee / Spring Hill, north of Tampa, not in Tampa city limits. Beach and swimming run daily; park hours were listed 9:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. year-round when I checked, with a separate seasonal schedule for slides and the lazy river. Cannonball needs 48 inches; Pirate’s Revenge and the lazy river need 42 inches. The kiddie pool was closed for renovations when I looked. Coolers larger than 45 quarts, tents, and grilling are restricted. Spring-fed water and a different vibe—not a clone of Adventure Island.

**ZooTampa at Lowry Park**, 1101 W. Sligh Avenue, is a zoo, not a water park. It has the Billabong Splash Pad in the Australia realm and Roaring Springs as cool-off spots if you already bought zoo admission. That is a splash pad inside a zoo day. See my [ZooTampa guide](/things-to-do/tampa-zoo) if that is the animal day you want.

Downtown, public splash pads at Water Works Park and Julian B. Lane Riverfront Park work for little kids after a Riverwalk walk. They are not ticketed water parks. Water Works is an easy add after lunch near [Ulele](/food-and-drink/ulele-tampa).

Further out, people also lump in Splash Harbour in Indian Rocks Beach, Epperson Lagoon in Wesley Chapel, SouthShore Bay Lagoon in Wimauma, Mirada Metro Lagoons in San Antonio, Florida, and LEGOLAND Florida Water Park in Winter Haven (water-park add-on required). Those are real. None is named Tampa Water Park. None sits next to Busch Gardens the way Adventure Island does.

## Tickets, Parking, and Getting There From Downtown

From downtown or the Riverwalk, plan a drive or rideshare to McKinley Drive. If your hotel is already near Busch Gardens, you still need an Adventure Island ticket and an open calendar day.

Online single-day tickets have been advertised from the low $30s when the park is selling dates; parking is separate and starts around $35 plus tax for general parking on the park FAQ. Preferred parking costs more. Annual pass tiers can change the parking math. Buy parking ahead when you can. Confirm live ticket and parking prices on [Adventure Island tickets](https://adventureisland.com/tickets/water-park-tickets/) and [parking](https://adventureisland.com/upgrades/parking/) before you go.

Multi-park Fun Cards and length-of-stay tickets still require Adventure Island to be operating that day. I noticed people buy a combo in Orlando, take a morning shuttle to Tampa, and arrive on a weekday when the water half is closed for the season. The park reminds you in the fine print that Adventure Island is seasonal. After the 2026 season ends, combo tickets and Fun Cards still need an open operating day in 2027 before the water-park half is useful.

If you are flying in first, use my [TPA arrival guide](/getting-around/tampa-international-airport), then decide whether a water-park day belongs in this trip or a 2027 return.

## Packing and Heat Mistakes I Would Avoid

Leave coolers and personal chairs in the car. Bring a refillable water bottle. Check swimwear for metal bits before you queue for a body slide. Measure kids at home against the posted height rules. Cabana shade sells out. Prepaid parking is smarter than circling on a hot morning.

At Weeki Wachee, watch the slide and lazy-river calendar separately from beach hours. At downtown splash pads, bring towels and expect no theme-park lockers.

For a wider Tampa plan that is open year-round, my [things to do in Tampa](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa) list and the [Florida Aquarium](/things-to-do/florida-aquarium-tampa) cover indoor and downtown options when the water park is dark.

## FAQ

### Is there a place called Tampa Water Park?

No. People saying “Tampa water park” or “water parks in Tampa” usually mean Adventure Island at 10001 N McKinley Drive, next to Busch Gardens.

### Is Adventure Island open in 2026?

As of the park’s own park-info page in late 2026, Adventure Island is closed for the 2026 season and looks forward to welcoming guests back in 2027. Check [adventureisland.com](https://adventureisland.com/park-info/) for the current calendar before you book.

### Does a Busch Gardens ticket include Adventure Island?

No. They share a company and a neighborhood, but tickets are separate unless you buy a product that specifically includes both and the water park is operating that day.

### How much is parking at Adventure Island?

General parking starts at $35 plus tax on the park FAQ, with preferred parking priced higher. Pass members may park free or discounted with the right tier and ID. Confirm current rates when you book.

### What else can I do if I wanted a water day in Tampa?

For toddlers, try downtown splash pads at Water Works or Julian B. Lane. For a spring-fed swim and slides on a day trip, look at Buccaneer Bay at Weeki Wachee. For a cool indoor day, the Florida Aquarium downtown is the easier play from a Riverwalk hotel.

## Final Thoughts

Adventure Island is the real answer behind “Tampa water park,” and seasonality is the rule that trips people up. From downtown, it is a McKinley Drive day, not a sidewalk hop. Right now the honest planning tip is simpler than a slide list: confirm 2027 dates before you build a Tampa itinerary around Endless Surf.

If you need something open while you wait, start with my [things to do in Tampa](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa) guide, keep [ZooTampa](/things-to-do/tampa-zoo) for animals, and save Westshore shopping at [International Plaza](/shopping/international-plaza-tampa) for a cooler afternoon.

metaTitle: Tampa International Airport: My TPA Arrival Guide
metaDescription: Tampa International Airport (TPA) guide from Ben: SkyConnect vs airside trains, parking rates, Uber pickup, PIE mix-ups, and arrival timing.
body:
# Tampa International Airport: My Honest TPA Arrival Guide

Tampa International Airport is where most of my Tampa trips actually started. The address is 4100 George J. Bean Parkway, Tampa, FL 33607. TPA sits on the Tampa side of the bay, not in St. Petersburg, and a cheap fare into the wrong airport can undo a good arrival before you leave the curb.

Here is the map I wish I had earlier: airsides, SkyConnect, parking, rideshare, and the traps that send you to PIE or the wrong New York airport. **Last updated:** November 2, 2026.

![White commercial airplane airborne against a blue sky](/images/articles/tampa-international-airport/tpa-358319.webp)
*Photo by [Pixabay](https://www.pexels.com/@pixabay/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/white-airplane-358319/)*

## Landing Checklist

- **Confirm the code is TPA.** PIE is St. Pete-Clearwater, across the bay.
- **Know your train.** Airside shuttles go to the gates. SkyConnect goes to economy parking and the rental car center.
- **Use the Express curbs for Uber and Lyft.** Not a random arrivals door.
- **Book parking ahead when you can.** Online is cheaper than drive-up, and the first hour is free in the garages.

## The Building: Airsides, SkyConnect, and Baggage Claim

The main terminal is not where the planes are. Airside shuttles run from Level 3 of the main terminal to airsides A, C, E, and F. SkyConnect is a different train. It debuted in 2018 and goes to economy parking and the rental car center. The monorail that used to reach long-term parking closed in 2020 and is no longer in service.

SkyConnect runs 24 hours, slower overnight, under five minutes to the rental center, about every two minutes. If you have no checked bag, the entrance they describe is between P.F. Chang's and Hard Rock Cafe. With a bag, claim it on Level 1 first.

Baggage claim is on Level 1: Red on the north side, Blue on the south. The sign over the escalator names your airline's color. Red ground transportation is nearest belt 9. Blue is nearest belt 7. The color is not the airside letter.

From the airport's airline directory:

- **Airside A:** Breeze, JetBlue, Sun Country, United
- **Airside C:** Alaska, Avelo, Southwest
- **Airside E:** Aeromexico, Air Canada, Delta, Frontier
- **Airside F:** American, Avianca, British Airways, Cayman Airways, Copa, Discover, Edelweiss, Porter, Virgin Atlantic, WestJet

Red ticketing and baggage: Air Canada, Alaska, Avelo, Breeze, British Airways, Discover, Edelweiss, Frontier, Southwest, Sun Country, WestJet. Blue: Aeromexico, American, Avianca, Cayman Airways, Copa, Delta, JetBlue, Porter, United, Virgin Atlantic.

Curbside check-in, where offered, runs through BAGS from 4:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. American, Delta, Frontier, JetBlue, Southwest, and United were marked for it when I looked. Airline airsides can change, so confirm on the [TPA airlines page](https://www.tampaairport.com/airlines) before you leave home.

## Security Times and How Early to Arrive

From the airport's own answers: airsides C and E open at 3:30 a.m., A at 3:45, F at 4:00, with the eGates a few minutes before each. The airport says arrive two hours early for domestic and three for international. Some international guidance also says at least two hours. I use three for international.

There is no airport luggage storage. The Marriott on airport property sells day passes that include it; check the hotel for current rates.

Tampa sits in Eastern Time. If you are still sorting clocks after a red-eye, my [Tampa time zone guide](/guides/what-time-zone-is-tampa-florida) is the short version.

## Distances, Driving In, and Ground Transport

Airport distances from TPA: downtown about 9 miles, cruise port about 9.5, St. Petersburg about 20, Clearwater about 20, Clearwater Beach about 20 to 25, St. Pete Beach about 27, Disney about 76, Orlando about 85. A Tampa ticket and a beach hotel are not the same trip.

Driving in, the exit off I-275 is 39, or 39B if you are coming from St. Pete on I-275 north. East and south fold in through I-4. Highway 60 hits the entrance just east of the Courtney Campbell, west of Westshore.

HART and PSTA do not stop at the terminal door. Their stop is the rental car center, so SkyConnect first. Hotel buses use the four Level 1 lots because the departure-level west crossover is closed to buses.

Yellow Cab is at Red 1 and Blue 2. For current cab rates to downtown, call the company or check the [ground transportation page](https://www.tampaairport.com/ground-transportation).

Uber, Lyft, and Wridz pick up at Red Express, Blue Express, or the SkyCenter One remote curb. A $5 service fee is added to the fare—I noticed that line on the receipt before I understood why downtown rides felt a bit high. Drop-off can be ticketing, baggage claim, or SkyCenter. Follow the app to the marked Express curb, not whichever arrivals door looks closest. That curb mistake is the tip I kept repeating to anyone flying in for a weekend.

## Parking and Rental Cars

Rentals are at the Rental Car Center on SkyConnect. Companies on the airport list include Alamo, Avis, Budget, Dollar, Enterprise, Hertz, National, Thrifty, Ace, American, Fox, Payless, Sixt, and Zipcar. Off-airport vans use the remote curb by that center. Waiting there is not allowed. The free cell phone lot is the waiting spot.

Remote bag check runs 5:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. for most domestic flights, and you have to be there 90 minutes before departure. American, Delta, Frontier, JetBlue, Southwest, and United participate. No extra airport fee, but airline bag fees still apply. A firearm in a checked bag has to go to the ticket counter.

Current parking rates on the airport site: short term, levels 4 through 9, free the first hour, then $8 an hour, $32 max per 24 hours, clearance 6 feet 8 inches. Long term is free the first hour, then $8 an hour, $26 max, with a Level 4 walkway. Economy on SkyConnect is free the first hour, then $5 an hour, $22 max. Booking ahead is cheaper if you do it at least 24 hours out. Cancel inside that window and they keep half, unless the airport closes. Weather cancellations can support a refund request. Airline delays do not. After 45 days they may impound the car. Confirm live rates on [TPA parking](https://www.tampaairport.com/parking) before you leave the car.

Westshore hotels sit close enough that many visitors skip a long economy stay. I have a separate note on the [Westshore Marriott](/guides/westshore-marriott-hotel-tampa), and [International Plaza](/shopping/international-plaza-tampa) is the mall people mean when they say they will kill time near TPA.

## International Arrivals and the New York Trap

I did not fly in from overseas during my stay, but the wait is what strands the person at the curb. The airport says you may not reach the main terminal for an hour or more after landing, and the driver cannot sit at baggage claim until you are out. The first hour of short-term is free if they come inside. Otherwise it is the cell phone lot until customs is finished.

They say about 80 percent of arriving passengers can use the passport kiosks. Duty free opens two hours before departure, in airside E across from gate 74 and in airside F in front of screening.

Boston is on the airport's nonstop list. New York is the sloppy search. The route list showed JFK on Delta, Frontier, and JetBlue; LaGuardia on Delta, American, and JetBlue, plus Southwest with a seasonal tag; Newark on JetBlue and United. Islip and White Plains appear too. Flights from Tampa to "New York" will dump you in Newark or a suburban field if you let the cheapest fare decide. Pick the airport first.

One cheap fare billed as New York to Tampa was actually New York to PIE, St. Pete-Clearwater. That is the other side of the bay. Check [Tampa International Airport](https://www.tampaairport.com/) for the live route list before you lock a "Tampa" ticket that is not TPA.

Hurricane season runs June 1 through November 30. The airport's plan ties watches and warnings to the National Weather Service office in Ruskin. Parking may refund a weather cancellation. It will not refund an airline delay. Check with the airline before you head to the curb.

If I do this again, I fly TPA for a Tampa hotel and only take PIE when I mean the beaches and have priced the drive. For a first full day after you land, my [things to do in Tampa](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa) guide is a cleaner start than winging it from the rental car center.

## FAQ

### Is Tampa International Airport the same as PIE?

No. TPA is Tampa International at 4100 George J. Bean Parkway in Tampa. PIE is St. Pete-Clearwater International across the bay. A cheap fare into the wrong airport adds a real drive.

### How far is TPA from downtown Tampa?

About 9 miles, per the airport's own distance list.

### Which airside is my airline at TPA?

It depends on the carrier. As of the airport directory: JetBlue, United, Breeze, and Sun Country use Airside A; Southwest, Alaska, and Avelo use Airside C; Delta, Frontier, Air Canada, and Aeromexico use Airside E; American and most of the long-haul international carriers on the list use Airside F. Confirm on the [airlines page](https://www.tampaairport.com/airlines) before you go, because assignments can move.

### How early should I arrive at TPA?

The airport says two hours for domestic and three for international, with some international guidance also saying at least two. I use three for international. Security open times vary by airside, with some doors opening around 3:30 a.m.

### Where do Uber and Lyft pick up at Tampa International Airport?

At Red Express, Blue Express, or the SkyCenter One remote curb. A $5 service fee is added to the fare. Drop-off can be ticketing, baggage claim, or SkyCenter.

### How much is parking at Tampa International Airport?

On the current airport rate card, short-term maxes at $32 per 24 hours after a free first hour, long-term at $26, and economy at $22. Book ahead when you can, and confirm live rates on the parking page before you leave the car.

## Tips From Arrivals

Confirm the ticket says TPA, not PIE. I liked SkyConnect once I stopped confusing it with the airside shuttle; I disliked watching people wait at the wrong curb for rideshare. Book garage parking ahead when you can, and use the free first hour if someone is only circling to pick you up. For international arrivals, send the driver to the cell phone lot until you clear customs—the baggage-claim wait can run long.

For Rocky Point waterfront seafood near the airport corridor, see [Rusty Pelican Tampa](/food-and-drink/rusty-pelican-tampa).

Heading to Disney or downtown Orlando instead? Use my [Tampa to Orlando](/guides/tampa-to-orlando) I-4 guide.

For the beach hop across the bay, see [Tampa to Clearwater](/guides/tampa-to-clearwater).

## Final Thoughts

TPA is a clear airport once you separate the airside shuttle from SkyConnect and stop treating every "Tampa" fare as this campus. Get the code right, get the curb right, and give yourself time on an early bank of flights.

From here I usually point people to a Westshore base like the [Westshore Marriott](/guides/westshore-marriott-hotel-tampa), a shopping break at [International Plaza](/shopping/international-plaza-tampa), or a first downtown day from my [Tampa things to do](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa) list. If Naples is the next drive, use my [Tampa to Naples](/guides/tampa-to-naples) road notes once you have the car.
