body:
# International Plaza Tampa: The Mall Behind "Tampa Mall"

I went looking for a place called Tampa Mall and I did not find one. That name is not on any sign. What people usually mean is International Plaza and Bay Street at 2223 N. Westshore Boulevard, Tampa, Florida 33607. Simon runs it and calls it Tampa's big luxury shopping destination. If a hotel clerk says "the mall," this is the one I ask them to name out loud.

It sits in Westshore, minutes from [Tampa International Airport](/getting-around/tampa-international-airport) by the mall's own description, and less than five miles from the Port of Tampa cruise terminal. When I needed a real shopping afternoon from downtown—air-conditioning and options in one stop—Westshore was the go-to. Here is how I tell International Plaza apart from the other centers, what is actually inside, and the parking and hours mistakes that waste half a trip. **Last updated:** November 2, 2026.

![Retail clothing displays inside a shopping mall](/images/articles/international-plaza-tampa/intl-plaza-264507.webp)
*Photo by [Pixabay](https://www.pexels.com/@pixabay/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/assorted-clothing-lot-264507/)*

## Quick Mall Notes

- **Say the real name.** Ask for International Plaza, not "Tampa Mall."
- **Check Dillard's separately.** Its hours are shorter than the center clock.
- **Park first.** Three garages, or valet if you do not want to circle.
- **Bay Street is the open-air side.** That is where a lot of the sit-down dining sits, and where Simon says redevelopment is headed.

## What "Tampa Mall" Actually Means

There is no property branded Tampa Mall. International Plaza is the center those words belong to. WestShore Plaza is a different enclosed mall at 250 WestShore Plaza, Tampa, Florida 33609, phone 813-286-0790. Citrus Park Town Center is north at 8021 Citrus Park Town Center, Tampa, Florida 33625, phone 813-926-4644. Tampa Premium Outlets is also Simon, but at 2300 Grand Cypress Drive, Lutz, Florida 33559, about 20 miles north of the airport. People say "Tampa outlets" and land in Lutz.

International Plaza claims more than 170 stores and a restaurant lineup of about 30 options, with Bay Street as the open-air piece for restaurants, cafes, and nightlife.

For a wider Tampa plan after shopping, I usually send people back to my [things to do in Tampa](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa) guide rather than trying to force every errand into one Westshore afternoon.

## Hours, Phones, and Department Store Traps

Mall regular hours: Monday through Saturday 10 a.m. to 9 p.m., Sunday 11 a.m. to 6 p.m., closed Thanksgiving and Christmas. Confirm on [Simon's International Plaza page](https://www.simon.com/mall/international-plaza) before you go, especially around holidays.

Dillard's is on the east side, phone 813-342-1220, and its hours are shorter: Sunday noon to 6 p.m., Monday through Saturday 11 a.m. to 8 p.m. That gap is the mistake I would have made. You can stand at a locked Dillard's door while the rest of the mall is already open, or find Dillard's closed after 8 on a weeknight while other doors are still going.

Neiman Marcus and Nordstrom are the other department-store landmarks the mall uses for elevators, restrooms, and ATMs. Elevators are at Grand Court next to Dillard's, at Nordstrom, and at Bay Street. Restrooms are on the lower level in the corridor between Tesla and Vineyard Vines, on the upper level in the food court, and inside the three department stores. The food court is upper level near the Bay Street entrance. Lost and found sits with security on the lower level in that same Tesla-to-Vineyard-Vines corridor.

Mall phones: management 813-342-3780, shopping line 813-342-3790, security 813-342-3789.

## Stores, Dining, and Bay Street

The luxury names the mall leans on include BOSS, Breitling, Burberry, Chanel fragrance and beauty, David Yurman, Golden Goose, Gucci, IWC, Mayors, MCM, Montblanc, Omega, Saint Laurent, TAG Heuer, Tiffany & Co., and Versace, plus Neiman Marcus and Nordstrom.

Dining names I could pin to their own roster: Bar Louie, Bazille inside Nordstrom, Brio Italian Grille, California Pizza Kitchen, Ceviche Tapas Bar and Restaurant, Doc B's, Ocean Prime, Rocco's Tacos and Tequila Bar, Shake Shack, Street Crust, Suki Hana, The Capital Grille, The Cheesecake Factory, and Whiskey Cake. Bazille is upper level inside Nordstrom. California Pizza Kitchen is lower level near Nordstrom. Street Crust and Suki Hana are in the food court. Ocean Prime sits toward West Shore Boulevard and Spruce Street. Confirm which restaurants are open before you plan dinner around a "coming soon" name.

If you want a churrascaria dinner after Westshore shopping, [Texas de Brazil Tampa](/food-and-drink/texas-de-brazil-tampa) is on Boy Scout Boulevard nearby, not inside the mall. For a hotel base in the same district, I have a separate guide to the [Westshore Marriott](/guides/westshore-marriott-hotel-tampa).

## Parking, Shuttles, and Getting There

There are three garages: Dillard's and Neiman Marcus, Nordstrom, and under Bay Street. They also mention paid parking near the entrances. Valet was $10 a car Monday through Thursday and $12 Friday through Sunday, all day, when I checked, with complimentary valet in a Lexus when that offer applies. For self-park garage rates, check at the entrance or ask the mall.

Bus 15 stops on the outer ring road near Dillard's. Bus 3 runs along the West Shore / Kennedy corridor and includes the airport.

Simon counts the Renaissance Tampa International Plaza Hotel as part of the center. The mall also lists courtesy shuttle arrangements from a long set of Westshore hotels, each with its own rule. Call the hotel desk for the current shuttle, rather than trusting a printed list.

Wheelchairs are complimentary at security, lower level near the bathrooms. Nursing rooms are by the food-court restroom and by the lower-level restroom at Grand Court. The Muma Children's Hospital play area is open during mall hours.

## Other Malls People Mix In

Citrus Park's weekday hours are shorter than International Plaza's: Monday through Thursday 11 a.m. to 8 p.m., Friday and Saturday 10 a.m. to 9 p.m., Sunday 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. Lutz outlets are a northern drive, not a Westshore hop.

## Construction to Expect on Bay Street

On February 4, 2026, Simon announced an investment of more than $250 million across three properties, including International Plaza, after taking full control from Taubman. For Tampa they described a 50,000-square-foot open-air expansion, a reimagined Bay Street, new finishes, and upgraded amenities, with construction expected to begin in 2026. No completion date. The center has kept regular hours through the announcement. Bay Street is the piece they say they are redoing, so build dinner plans with that in mind and confirm current store and restaurant status on Simon's page.

## FAQ

### Is there a mall called Tampa Mall?

No. People saying "Tampa Mall," "mall of Tampa," or "best mall in Tampa" are usually pointing at International Plaza and Bay Street at 2223 N. Westshore Boulevard.

### What are the best stores at International Plaza?

If you came for the luxury pitch, the mall leans on names like Gucci, Saint Laurent, Tiffany & Co., Burberry, Neiman Marcus, Nordstrom, and Dillard's. For a quicker stop, Tesla and Vineyard Vines sit near a lower-level restroom corridor that is easy to use as a landmark. Match the store list to what you actually need that day.

### How far is International Plaza from Tampa International Airport?

The mall describes itself as minutes from Tampa International Airport in Westshore, and less than five miles from the Port of Tampa cruise terminal. It is a short Westshore hop, not a Lutz or Clearwater drive.

### What are International Plaza's hours?

Monday through Saturday 10 a.m. to 9 p.m. and Sunday 11 a.m. to 6 p.m., closed Thanksgiving and Christmas, when I last confirmed the regular schedule. Department stores can open later or close earlier. Check Dillard's before you aim for that door first.

### How much is parking at International Plaza?

Valet was $10 Monday through Thursday and $12 Friday through Sunday, all day, when I checked. For self-park rates in the garages, check at the entrance. There are garages at Dillard's/Neiman Marcus, Nordstrom, and under Bay Street.

### Is International Plaza the same as WestShore Plaza or the outlets?

No. WestShore Plaza is a different enclosed mall nearby. Tampa Premium Outlets is in Lutz. Citrus Park Town Center is farther north. Same metro, different addresses.

## Tips From Westshore Afternoons

Say International Plaza out loud to hotel desks—never “Tampa Mall.” I liked Bay Street for sit-down dinners after a store run; I disliked aiming for Dillard’s on the mall clock and finding that door still closed. Park first (garage or valet) before you commit to circling. Treat WestShore Plaza, Citrus Park, and Lutz outlets as different trips. The food court upstairs near Bay Street was the reset button when someone was done shopping and someone else was not.

Hunting a flea market? Big Top is closed—see [Tampa flea market options](/shopping/tampa-flea-market) (Oldsmar and Ybor Saturday Market).

For Rocky Point waterfront seafood near the airport corridor, see [Rusty Pelican Tampa](/food-and-drink/rusty-pelican-tampa).

## Final Thoughts

International Plaza is the shopping center behind the "Tampa Mall" search. From downtown, it was our reliable Westshore afternoon: luxury-store pitch, Bay Street for dinner, and a parking plan before we went. Say the real name when you ask a desk clerk for directions.

If you are flying in, land the plan with my [TPA arrival guide](/getting-around/tampa-international-airport). If you want dinner on Boy Scout after the stores, use my [Texas de Brazil Tampa](/food-and-drink/texas-de-brazil-tampa) notes. For a Westshore hotel base, start with the [Westshore Marriott](/guides/westshore-marriott-hotel-tampa).

body:
# Visiting the Florida Aquarium: My Honest Tampa Guide

When people say "Tampa aquarium," they almost never mean a building with that name on the door. They mean The Florida Aquarium at 701 Channelside Drive in the Channel District. Phone (813) 273-4000. From a downtown base, this was the Channelside stop I reached for when I wanted a real attraction without turning the day into a theme-park slog.

It is a science and conservation aquarium, not a theme park and not [ZooTampa](/things-to-do/tampa-zoo). Most of the walk is air-conditioned, which matters on hot Channel District afternoons—something I noticed the first time we walked over from the Riverwalk side. Here is how I plan a visit: tickets, hours, parking, what general admission covers, and the name traps that send people to the wrong waterfront. **Last updated:** November 2, 2026.

![School of fish swimming in blue aquarium water](/images/articles/florida-aquarium-tampa/aquarium-2156311.webp)
*Photo by [Tom Fisk](https://www.pexels.com/@tomfisk/) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/school-of-fish-in-body-of-water-2156311/)*

## Before You Buy Tickets

- **Buy ahead.** Plan-ahead pricing by date means the earlier purchase for that day is usually the better price. Aim for at least 24 hours ahead when you can.
- **Start under the dome.** Wetlands of Florida, then the big reef windows, then The Tide Pool upstairs.
- **Park with a plan.** Use prepaid parking from your ticket email when it is offered, or one of the Channelside garages below. Valet at the door is not a sure thing on cruise-ship days.
- **Leave the 2024 rumor behind.** Advance tickets help, but walk-up window tickets are allowed again. Members do not have to reserve.

## Tickets, Hours, and Getting There

The aquarium prices admission by the date you pick. Buy ahead before you arrive for the cheapest price on that date. They say the price can go up, never down, the longer you wait. The window costs more.

Tickets are for the date you selected, non-refundable, and non-transferable. Resale is prohibited. If you cannot go, call (813) 273-4000. They may move an unused ticket up to a year, and you pay any price difference. SeaTREK has to be moved at least 24 hours ahead or it is gone. The Wild Dolphin Cruise moves with the admission ticket inside that same year.

Posted hours: January through May 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., June and July 9 a.m. to 6 p.m., August through December 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., closed Thanksgiving and Christmas. Hours can change on public holidays, holiday weekends, and school breaks. Confirm the morning you go on [The Florida Aquarium site](https://www.flaquarium.org/visit/visitor-information/plan-your-visit/).

**Address:** 701 Channelside Drive, Tampa, FL 33602

**Phone:** (813) 273-4000

For a wider downtown plan, I pair this stop with my [favorite things to do in Tampa](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa) list and keep Water Street dinner for after, often at [Yard House](/food-and-drink/yard-house-tampa).

## 1. Walk the Wetlands Under the Glass Dome

The Wetlands of Florida under the 80-foot glass dome is the stretch I care about most. Mangroves that have been growing inside for decades, river otters, an alligator, roseate spoonbills, white ibis. It feels like a Florida habitat folded into a downtown building.

Above that, Lemur Lookout surprised me. I did not come to an aquarium for ring-tailed lemurs, and then there they were. The dome is glass, so I would not call this zone cool in July just because the rest of the building is air-conditioned.

## 2. Stand at the Coral Reefs and Heart of the Sea Windows

Their map describes a 500,000-gallon Coral Reefs habitat with a panoramic window. Heart of the Sea is the second-largest tank, about 15 feet deep, redone in June 2024 as an Indo-Pacific scene with a loggerhead, Napoleon or Māori wrasse, blue speckled grouper, spotted unicornfish, and clownfish.

SeaTREK is the paid walk on the bottom of that tank for non-divers ages 10 and up. It is an add-on, not part of general admission. Book it as its own thing if you want it.

## 3. Touch The Tide Pool, Then Decide on Add-Ons

The Tide Pool opened August 1, 2025, on the second-floor mezzanine: a cold-water touch habitat with more than 200 marine invertebrates. General admission covers habitats and exhibits including that tide pool. It does not cover the add-ons.

The extras people mix into the main ticket: Penguin Encounter, sloth encounter, stingray feeding, AquaEd, Undersea Explorer VR, SeaTREK, and the Wild Dolphin Cruise. The cruise runs on their 72-foot catamaran, Bay Spirit II, from near the outdoor plaza. When I checked, the cruise was $17 per adult and $15 per child ages 3 to 11, free under 2, and you still need same-day general admission. Weekday departures were 1:00 and 2:30, weather permitting. Get wristbands from Guest Services and arrive early for boarding. Stroller parking at the boat. Limited access for mobility devices; do not assume a wheelchair user can board. Confirm current cruise pricing and times before you go.

## 4. Know What Is Not in This Building

The sea turtle hospital is not downtown. Their Sea Turtle Rehabilitation Center is in Apollo Beach. Downtown you get the conservation story, the coral exhibit work, and the Coral Conservation and Research Center. If you came expecting rehab turtles in a hospital ward, you are on the wrong block.

They also stopped printing maps. QR codes on the walls, or ask a staffer. Bring a charged phone.

This is not [ZooTampa at Lowry Park](/things-to-do/tampa-zoo), not Busch Gardens, not Clearwater Marine Aquarium, and not MOSI. CityPASS can put several of those on one pass. Clearwater Marine Aquarium is across the bay. People who want the Tampa aquarium and then burn a day in Clearwater by accident are working off the wrong pin.

## Parking Near the Florida Aquarium

Channel District parking fills—I learned that the hard way on a weekend when a cruise ship was in and the door valet was not running. The aquarium points people to prepaid parking in the ticket confirmation email. Walking options they name:

- Channelside Parking Garage, 369 S 12th Street, about 0.2 mile
- City of Tampa lot, 864 Channelside Drive, about 0.2 mile
- Cumberland Garage, 1045 E Cumberland Avenue, about 0.3 mile

Valet sits at the main entrance on Channelside, run by The Car Park, most days during regular hours, subject to availability. Regular valet rates are $20 for up to three hours and $40 after three hours, with $5 off for members who show a membership card. They cannot run valet when a cruise ship is in at Terminal 2, and pricing can change in peak periods. Check [current parking details](https://www.flaquarium.org/visit/visitor-information/parking/) before you rely on the door. Bike, bus, scooter, the TECO Line Streetcar, or water taxi are the other ways in.

If you are flying in the same trip, my [Tampa International Airport arrival guide](/getting-around/tampa-international-airport) covers the TPA side before you head downtown.

## Useful Things to Know Before You Go

**Advance tickets are about price and a smoother entry.** Window tickets are allowed. Advance is recommended. Members do not have to reserve; members without a reservation check in at the window. Member help line: (813) 273-4030.

**Military discount is a window deal.** Military and retired military get 10 percent off the whole order at the window with ID, and that one does not need an advance reservation. AZA reciprocal membership is a separate program.

**CityPASS is a bundle, not a parking pass.** It can cover this aquarium plus other Tampa Bay stops. It does not include parking. Treat pass comparison numbers as pass math, not the aquarium's live calendar price.

**Confirm hours the morning you go.** Holiday weeks and school breaks move the clock. Thanksgiving and Christmas are closed on the regular calendar.

## FAQ

### Is the Tampa aquarium the same as The Florida Aquarium?

Yes. "Tampa aquarium," "aquarium in Tampa," and "Florida Aquarium Tampa" all point to The Florida Aquarium at 701 Channelside Drive. There is no separate attraction branded only as the Tampa aquarium.

### How long does a visit to the Florida Aquarium take?

The aquarium says the average visitor spends about two hours. Add more time if you booked SeaTREK, an encounter, or the Wild Dolphin Cruise.

### Is the Florida Aquarium worth it?

For me, yes, especially on a hot day when I still want something downtown. The wetlands dome and the reef windows are the heart of a regular ticket. If you want rides and a full outdoor park day, that is a different stop.

### When is the best time to go with kids?

Go earlier in the day, when the building is quieter and you still have energy for The Tide Pool upstairs. Weekday mornings outside school-break weeks are usually calmer than weekend afternoons. Summer hours stretch to 6 p.m. in June and July, which helps if you need a longer buffer.

### How much does the Florida Aquarium cost?

Admission is priced by date. Advance purchase for your date is the cheapest path they describe. Add-ons cost extra. Check [live tickets on flaquarium.org](https://www.flaquarium.org/) for your day.

### Where should I park for the Florida Aquarium?

Start with prepaid parking in your ticket email. Nearby options include the Channelside Parking Garage, the city lot on Channelside Drive, and Cumberland Garage. Valet at the entrance is not available on some cruise-ship days.

## Tips From Our Visits

Buy the date ahead when you can—the price ladder is real. Start under the wetlands dome while everyone still has patience, then the reef windows, then The Tide Pool upstairs. I liked the indoor heat relief and the otters; I disliked discovering add-ons were separate after someone assumed the cruise was “included.” Leave Clearwater Marine Aquarium for a different day across the bay. Bring a charged phone because they stopped printing maps.

## Final Thoughts

I like the Florida Aquarium because it answers the downtown heat problem without turning the day into a theme-park slog. From downtown it is the easy Channelside win. The wetlands dome and the big reef windows are the heart of it. The name confusion is the tax you pay for living in a bay area with more than one water attraction.

Plan by the Channelside address, buy ahead when you can, and confirm hours before you leave. If you are building a bigger Tampa day, start with my [things to do in Tampa](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa) guide, keep [ZooTampa](/things-to-do/tampa-zoo) for a separate animal day, and save Westshore shopping at [International Plaza](/shopping/international-plaza-tampa) for another afternoon.

body:
# My 13 Favorite Things to Do in Tampa (From Riverwalk to Ybor)

I went in expecting one tidy list of things to do in Tampa. What I found was a city that works more like a handful of neighborhoods, each with its own personality and its own logistics. 🌴

There's a walkable downtown clump of waterfront attractions, a pair of big theme parks to the north, a zoo and an old Cuban-and-Italian cigar district. The main challenge is that these places are spread out, and a couple of them have confusing addresses. Busch Gardens and Adventure Island are the classic example.

Based on everything I explored, here are my favorite things to do in Tampa FL, plus the practical tips I wish I'd had before I arrived. Along the way I've included free activities, options for adults and a few places worth a trip just outside the city.

![Walkers on the Tampa Riverwalk beside the Hillsborough River near Curtis Hixon Park](/images/wm/articles/20739680.webp)
*Photo by [Nate Biddle](https://www.pexels.com/@nxbid0) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/cyclist-20739680/)*

## Short on Time? Here Are My Quick Travel Tips ⏱️

This is a detailed guide, so if you just want the essentials, start here.

- **My top Tampa recommendations:** These are my picks for the best things to do in Tampa.
  - Walk the Riverwalk, because it ties the best downtown stuff together.
  - Visit ZooTampa for the manatees.
  - Spend an evening on Seventh Avenue in Ybor City for a completely different feel from the rest of town.
- **If you want to save money:** The TECO Line streetcar is free seven days a week, and walking the Riverwalk costs nothing. If you plan to see several attractions, look into the Riverwalk Attraction Pass, and check exactly which attractions are included and what it costs when you buy.
- **Where to start:** Heights Market at Armature Works, 1910 N Ola Avenue, is the easiest launch point for the Riverwalk.
- **Getting around:** Stay on foot and on the streetcar downtown, and drive to the zoo and the theme parks.
- **One thing I learned the hard way:** Don't treat Busch Gardens and Adventure Island as one address. They have separate street addresses and share one phone number.

## Getting Around Tampa

Tampa is easier once you plan by area. Most Tampa Florida things to do fall into three groups: downtown on foot, the north-side parks by car, and [Ybor City](/guides/ybor-city-tampa-fl-33605), which you can reach by streetcar. Sorting the things to do Tampa Florida offers into those groups saved me a lot of backtracking.

### Downtown on Foot and by Streetcar

The Riverwalk, the aquarium, the museums, the parks and the arena sit close together. I'd leave the car parked and walk. Parking rates can change, so check them at the entrance before you commit.

The [TECO Line streetcar](https://tecolinestreetcar.org/) covers the rest. It runs 2.7 miles from downtown through the Channel District to Ybor City, with 11 stations, and it's free. Trains come about every 15 to 20 minutes, so check the schedule before you count on it.

### Driving to the North-Side Parks

[ZooTampa](/things-to-do/tampa-zoo), Busch Gardens and Adventure Island are all north of downtown, so you'll want a car or a ride. Each has its own address in the sections below. Put the exact street address into your GPS rather than just the park name.

### On the Water

Tampa looks different from the water. I've covered the boat options in item 7.

## 1. Walk the Tampa Riverwalk

![Riverwalk path along the Hillsborough River in downtown Tampa](/images/wm/articles/36029477.webp)
*Photo by [Mark Stebnicki](https://www.pexels.com/@nc-farm-bureau-mark) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/aerial-view-of-wilmington-riverfront-skyline-36029477/)*

If I could only recommend one thing, this would be it. The Riverwalk is 2.6 miles from the Hillsborough River to the Garrison Channel, and it links many of the downtown places in this guide. You can walk it, bike it or take a scooter.

I'd start at the north end at Heights Market in Armature Works, then follow the path through Curtis Hixon Park and on to Sparkman Wharf. You pass parks, museums and waterfront views, and you can stop whenever your feet need a break. It's the best way I found to understand how downtown fits together.

**Tip:** Do the whole route in sections if it's hot. The food stops at each end make good breaks.

**Address:** Heights Market, Armature Works, 1910 N Ola Avenue, Tampa (north end of the walk).

## 2. Meet the Sea Creatures at The Florida Aquarium

![Otters at The Florida Aquarium in the Channel District, Tampa](/images/wm/articles/13866083.webp)
*Photo by [Tibor Szabo](https://www.pexels.com/@tibszabo) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/close-up-photograph-of-otters-13866083/)*

This is one of the great things to do in Tampa when the weather isn't cooperating, and it's also an easy pick if you're traveling with kids. The aquarium has thousands of animals, including otters and lemurs. You can also add a Bay Spirit II dolphin trip.

I liked how central it is. It sits between two cruise terminals, right on the streetcar line, so you can reach it without a car. It also works as a pre-cruise stop.

**Tip:** Check the opening hours the morning you go, because they can change. The aquarium also runs a Guppyween event later in October, so check the dates if you're visiting then.

**Address:** 701 Channelside Drive, Tampa, FL 33602. Phone: (813) 273-4000.

**How to Get There:** Take the TECO Line streetcar to the Channel District. The aquarium is between two cruise terminals.

## 3. Ride the Free TECO Line Streetcar

![TECO Line streetcar stopped in downtown Tampa](/images/wm/articles/12350835.webp)
*Photo by [Eyes2Soul Eyes2Soul](https://www.pexels.com/@eyes2soul) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/modern-city-tram-on-stop-12350835/)*

Free things to do in Tampa are not easy to come by, so I'm giving the streetcar its own spot. It's transport and sightseeing in one. The line runs 2.7 miles through downtown and the Channel District to Ybor City, free seven days a week, with 11 stations. 🚋

I used it to link the waterfront with Ybor without worrying about parking at both ends. You'll wait about 15 to 20 minutes between trains, so it's not a "dash for it" kind of system. Just build in a little slack.

**Tip:** Ride it one way toward Ybor in the afternoon, and plan to stay for dinner on Seventh Avenue.

**How to Get There:** Look for the stations in downtown, the Channel District and Ybor City. Check the schedule before you go.

## 4. Explore the Museums on Water Street and Gasparilla Plaza

![Tampa Bay History Center and the museums near Gasparilla Plaza in downtown Tampa](/images/wm/articles/35120562.webp)
*Photo by [Stephen Leonardi](https://www.pexels.com/@stephen-leonardi-587681991) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/uss-midway-museum-at-night-in-san-diego-35120562/)*

Three museums sit close together downtown, so you can mix and match depending on your group.

- **Tampa Bay History Center:** 12,000 years of local history, including the Treasure Seekers exhibit. It's at 801 Water Street.
- **Tampa Museum of Art:** 120 W Gasparilla Plaza.
- **Glazer Children's Museum:** 110 West Gasparilla Plaza. It's best for kids under 12, so I'd skip it if you're traveling without them.

**Tip:** Don't expect museum admission to be free. Check ticket prices before you go. If you're planning to see several attractions, the Riverwalk Attraction Pass may be worth a look. Confirm which places it includes.

## 5. Relax in Curtis Hixon and the Riverfront Parks

![Curtis Hixon Park on the Tampa riverfront](/images/wm/articles/38197218.webp)
*Photo by [Roy Serafin](https://www.pexels.com/@roythephotographer) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/scenic-view-of-historic-st-augustine-waterfront-38197218/)*

Among all the Tampa FL things to do, a lazy afternoon in a park is easy to overlook. It shouldn't be. Curtis Hixon Park is about 8 acres, sits right on the Riverwalk and has yoga on Sundays.

A few more parks are worth knowing about:

- **Julian B. Lane Riverfront Park:** about 25 acres, north of the University of Tampa and across from the Straz.
- **Water Works Park:** 1701 N Highland Avenue.
- **Cotanchobee Park:** another riverfront park along the water.

**Tip:** If you want yoga, check the schedule before you go, since classes can change.

**Address:** Curtis Hixon Park, 600 N Ashley Drive, Tampa. Julian B. Lane Riverfront Park, 1001 North Boulevard, Tampa.

## 6. Eat and Wander at Armature Works, Sparkman Wharf and Ulele

![Armature Works food hall in the former trolley barn in Tampa](/images/wm/articles/37100502.webp)
*Photo by [James Mirakian](https://www.pexels.com/@james-mirakian-774977502) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/bustling-interior-of-west-side-market-cleveland-37100502/)*

The two ends of the Riverwalk are also good places to eat and hang out. Armature Works, the old trolley barn, is now a food hall and the start of the walk. Sparkman Wharf sits at the other end, close to the arena, so it works well before or after a Lightning game.

[Ulele](/food-and-drink/ulele-tampa), at 1810 N Highland Avenue, is another well-known Riverwalk stop. It debuted in 2014. I'd pick based on your appetite and your timing. [Yard House](/food-and-drink/yard-house-tampa), across from the arena on Water Street, is the other sit-down stop.

**Tip:** Check opening hours, since they vary by spot.

**Address:** Armature Works, 1910 N Ola Avenue. Sparkman Wharf, 615 Channelside Drive. Ulele, 1810 N Highland Avenue. All in Tampa.

## 7. Get Out on the Water

![Water taxi on the Hillsborough River in downtown Tampa](/images/wm/articles/30554305.webp)
*Photo by [AJ  Ahamad](https://www.pexels.com/@aj-ahamad-767001191) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/aerial-view-of-water-taxi-on-dubai-s-scenic-waters-30554305/)*

You have plenty of ways to see Tampa from the water, including eBoats, Pirate Water Taxi, Riverwalk Boating, Tampa Bay Fun Boat, Tampa Bay Waterbike and Yacht Starship. Sail Plaza and the water taxi both use 333 South Franklin as their address.

If you like ships, the American Victory is at 705 Channelside. It was delivered May 24, 1945, and is billed as one of three fully functioning ships of its kind.

**Tip:** Boat schedules and prices vary by operator, so check before you head out.

**Address:** Sail Plaza and the water taxi, 333 South Franklin, Tampa. American Victory, 705 Channelside, Tampa.

## 8. Catch a Show at the Straz Center

![Exterior of the Straz Center for the Performing Arts in downtown Tampa](/images/wm/articles/13257233.webp)
*Photo by [Laura Paredis](https://www.pexels.com/@laura-paredis-1047081) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/the-roofing-of-the-kilden-performing-arts-centre-13257233/)*

One of the coolest things to do in Tampa after dark is catch a performance at the Straz. It's a big theater complex with Broadway shows, the Florida Orchestra and Opera Tampa. [Tampa Theatre](/things-to-do/tampa-theatre), on Franklin Street, is the movie palace if you want a film instead.

It's right across from Julian B. Lane Riverfront Park, so you can walk the riverfront before curtain.

**Tip:** Check what's on and book ahead for the show you want.

**Address:** 1010 North Macinnes Place, Tampa.

## 9. Go to a Lightning Game or Event at Benchmark International Arena

![Benchmark International Arena on Channelside Drive in Tampa](/images/wm/articles/13237897.webp)
*Photo by [Scott Foltz](https://www.pexels.com/@scottyfoltz95) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/fast-moving-car-on-a-race-track-13237897/)*

This is the home of the Lightning, and it hosts well over 150 events a year. It sits between The Florida Aquarium and the convention center, so it's an easy add to a downtown day.

**Tip:** Some places still call it Amalie Arena. Match the address, 401 Channelside Drive, rather than the old name.

**Address:** 401 Channelside Drive, Tampa.

## 10. Meet the Manatees at ZooTampa at Lowry Park

![Manatee at ZooTampa at Lowry Park](/images/wm/articles/12237825.webp)
*Photo by [Jorge Luis Morales](https://www.pexels.com/@jorge-luis-morales-238540862) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/close-up-photo-of-sea-lion-underwater-12237825/)*

For fun things to do in Tampa, this is my top family pick, and it's one of the things I'd tell any first-timer to see. The zoo has around 2,000 animals, including Florida panthers, an Africa area and a Florida Waters section with manatees, jellies and otters. The manatee hospital has been running since 1991.

**Tip:** Check hours the morning you go. The zoo sometimes adds evening events in the fall; I check [the zoo's calendar](https://zootampa.org/), and whether that needs a separate ticket.

**Address:** 1101 W. Sligh Avenue, Tampa, FL 33604. Phone: (813) 935-8552.

**How to Get There:** Drive or take a ride to the address above.

## 11. Ride the Coasters at Busch Gardens

![Roller coaster at Busch Gardens Tampa Bay](/images/wm/articles/38331893.webp)
*Photo by [marclyc li](https://www.pexels.com/@marclyc-li-2160558161) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/colorful-amusement-park-ride-with-sculpture-38331893/)*

Busch Gardens calls itself the coaster capital of Florida, and it has 200-plus species of animals too. Iron Gwazi and Cheetah Hunt are the names I'd look for, and Falcon's Fury stands 335 feet tall. Tigris is one of the newer rides. 🎢

Getting there is simple once you know the layout. The park is about eight miles northeast of downtown, two miles east of I-275 at Busch Boulevard, and two miles west of I-75 exit 265. It's about an hour from Orlando on I-4 and roughly 30 minutes east of the beaches and the airport.

**Tip:** Busch Gardens often runs Halloween events in the fall; I check the park's site for this year's dates. A separate after-dark event needs its own ticket, so I check before I buy.

**Address:** 10165 N McKinley Drive, Tampa, FL 33612. That address does not take mail.

## 12. Splash Around at Adventure Island

![Water slides at Adventure Island in Tampa](/images/wm/articles/31166924.webp)
*Photo by [Vika Glitter](https://www.pexels.com/@vika-glitter-392079) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/thrilling-water-slide-adventure-with-inner-tube-31166924/)*

Adventure Island is the water park next door, and it's one of the best fun things to do Tampa has for a hot day. It covers about 30 acres and has a slide called Colossal Curl.

Here's where I'd be careful. The park's own directions put it north of Busch Gardens, so follow those rather than looking for it right across the street.

**Tip:** Busch Gardens and Adventure Island share one phone number, (813) 884-4386, which is how people end up calling the wrong gate. Double-check which park you need.

**Address:** 10001 N McKinley Drive, Tampa, FL 33612.

## 13. Step Back in Time in Ybor City

![Seventh Avenue in the Ybor City Historic District, Tampa](/images/wm/articles/4250339.webp)
*Photo by [Brett Sayles](https://www.pexels.com/@brett-sayles) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/urban-street-with-illuminating-lights-at-night-4250339/)*

Among all the things to do in Tampa Florida, Ybor City is the one that feels least like a theme park or a riverwalk. It's a National Historic Landmark northeast of downtown, with more than 950 buildings. Visit Seventh Avenue, nicknamed La Sétima, which runs from Nick Nuccio Parkway for 11 blocks to 26th Street.

Look for the Columbia, the Italian Club, El Centro Español and the Ritz. The district dates to 1885.

**Tip:** Ride the free streetcar to get here. Since Seventh Avenue is a lively nightlife street after dark, plan your ride home.

**How to Get There:** Take the TECO Line streetcar to Ybor City.

## Free Things to Do in Tampa

The free things to do Tampa offers are few, but they're good. If you're after free things to do in Tampa Florida, here are the ones I can vouch for:

- **Ride the TECO Line streetcar.** It's free seven days a week.
- **Walk the Riverwalk.** There's no ticket for the walk itself.

Museums, the aquarium, the zoo and the theme parks all charge admission, so check prices before you go. For things to do in Tampa for free, the streetcar plus the Riverwalk makes a solid day.

## Things to Do Near Tampa FL

If you have extra time, some good places sit just outside the city. Lettuce Lake Park in north Tampa and Hillsborough River State Park in Thonotosassa are the nearby nature options.

For beaches, head to Clearwater, St. Pete Beach and Caladesi. These are all things to do near Tampa that make a good day trip from the city.

## Cool Things to Do in Tampa Florida for Adults

For adults, I'd lean toward the Straz, Lightning games and the after-dark park nights, which are separately ticketed. [Topgolf](/events/topgolf-tampa), the bay building east of downtown, is the other evening that is not a show. The Glazer Children's Museum is aimed at kids, so I'd skip it without them.

## Visiting Tampa in October: Weekend and Saturday Options

October is a good time for seasonal events. Busch Gardens runs Spooktacular on Saturdays and Sundays from September 12 through November 1, plus a separately ticketed after-dark event. ZooTampa has Creatures of the Night on select October nights. The aquarium has Guppyween later in the month.

Dates and tickets can change, so check each park before you plan your weekend. 🌅

## Useful Things to Know Before You Go

- **Check today's hours before you go.** Opening hours can change, so look them up the morning of your visit. I wouldn't plan a whole week around a single notice.
- **Match the address, not the old name.** The arena is Benchmark International Arena at 401 Channelside Drive, though some guides still say Amalie Arena.
- **Busch Gardens and Adventure Island have two addresses.** Busch Gardens is at 10165 N McKinley Drive and Adventure Island is at 10001 N McKinley Drive. They share one phone number, so if you're going to both, save both addresses.
- **Confirm the pass before you buy.** Check exactly which attractions the Riverwalk Attraction Pass includes, and what it costs.
- **Night events are separate.** Seasonal after-dark events may need a separate ticket.
- **Plan by area.** Group downtown stops, north-side parks and Ybor City into separate days or half-days.

## FAQ

### What are the best things to do in Tampa Florida?

I'd start with the Riverwalk, The Florida Aquarium, ZooTampa, Busch Gardens and Ybor City. They cover downtown, the north-side parks and the historic district.

### What are fun things to do in Tampa Florida?

The zoo, the aquarium and the theme parks are the most fun for families. Adventure Island is the pick on a hot day.

### Are there free things to do in Tampa Florida?

Yes. The TECO Line streetcar is free seven days a week, and walking the Riverwalk costs nothing.

### What are the things to do near Tampa FL?

Lettuce Lake Park and Hillsborough River State Park are close, and the beaches at Clearwater, St. Pete Beach and Caladesi are a short trip away.

### What is there to do in Tampa this weekend or on a Saturday?

Busch Gardens often runs Halloween events in the fall; check the park's site for this year's dates. ZooTampa sometimes adds evening events in the fall; check the zoo's calendar.

### Are Busch Gardens and Adventure Island at the same address?

No. Busch Gardens is at 10165 N McKinley Drive and Adventure Island is at 10001 N McKinley Drive. They share one phone number.

### How do I get between downtown and Ybor City?

Take the free TECO Line streetcar. It runs 2.7 miles with 11 stations.

### How long is the Tampa Riverwalk?

The Riverwalk is 2.6 miles, from the Hillsborough River to the Garrison Channel.

For a downtown Channelside stop when you want an indoor attraction, see my [Florida Aquarium](/things-to-do/florida-aquarium-tampa) guide.

Flying in first? Start with my [Tampa International Airport](/getting-around/tampa-international-airport) arrival guide.

Looking for the seasonal water park next to Busch Gardens? See [Adventure Island Tampa](/things-to-do/adventure-island-tampa).

For the skatepark east of Ybor off I-4 exit 3, read [Skatepark of Tampa](/things-to-do/skatepark-of-tampa).

For the Riverwalk art museum on Gasparilla Plaza, see [Tampa Museum of Art](/things-to-do/tampa-museum-of-art).

For the Heights food hall on North Ola (not the motor shop), see [Armature Works Tampa](/food-and-drink/armature-works-tampa).

## Final Thoughts

Tampa won me over because it isn't one thing. You can spend a morning on the Riverwalk, an afternoon with manatees and an evening on Seventh Avenue, and it feels like three different trips. That's what makes the things to do in Tampa so rewarding.

My big planning tip is to organize your days by area. Keep downtown on foot, give the north-side parks their own day, and save Ybor City for the evening. That's the best way I found to enjoy the Tampa things to do on this list without wasting time in the car.

body:
# Ulele, Tampa: My Honest Guide (What to Know Before You Go)

I walked up to [Ulele](https://ulele.com/) Tampa expecting a pretty riverside dinner spot and not much more. I also said the name wrong the whole way there. It's pronounced You-lay-lee, and the restaurant set me straight. 😄

Ulele is a native-inspired lunch and dinner restaurant on [Tampa's Riverwalk](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa), inside a reimagined 1903 water works building in Tampa Heights. The food comes off a huge barbacoa grill, and the beer is brewed on site. The challenges are small but real: getting a table, getting the dress code right and not mixing it up with another Ulele.

Here is everything I'd want a friend to tell me before going, from reservations and parking to what to drink and what to skip.

![Exterior of Ulele restaurant in the historic Water Works building on the Hillsborough River in Tampa Heights](/images/wm/articles/10895022.webp)
*Photo by [Vitaly Kushnir](https://www.pexels.com/@kartatos) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/grayscale-photography-of-a-building-near-pond-10895022/)*

## Short on Time? Here Are My Quick Travel Tips ⚡

This is a detailed guide, so if you just want the essentials, start here.

**My top recommendations:**

- **Call ahead for a table.** The patio and waterfront seats are the ones everyone wants at sunset.
- **Try the house-brewed beer.** It's made on site, and you can only get it at Ulele.
- **Walk Water Works Park next door.** It's the easiest way to burn off a heavy plate or kill time before your table is ready.

**Where to start:** The Riverwalk. Plenty of downtown hotel guests walk to Ulele along the river. On Water Street, [Yard House](/food-and-drink/yard-house-tampa) and [The Pearl](/food-and-drink/the-pearl-tampa) are the other downtown rooms.

**Where to park:** Plan on valet at the front drive when it's running. Street parking fills up fast on busy nights.

**One thing I'd double-check before leaving the hotel:** Men need sleeves for the main dining rooms. Otherwise you may get steered to the patio.

## What It's Like

Ulele sits at 1810 North Highland Avenue in Tampa Heights, right on the Hillsborough River. It's about 400 yards from the [Straz Center for the Performing Arts](/things-to-do/tbpac-tampa). It opened in August 2014 and is part of the Columbia Restaurant Group. It shares a family tree with other Columbia restaurants, including the one in [Ybor City](/guides/ybor-city-tampa-fl-33605), but it's a completely different concept.

![Dining room and riverside patio at Ulele with the Hillsborough River in the background](/images/wm/articles/8753757.webp)
*Photo by [Team Picsfast](https://www.pexels.com/@picsfast) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/fresh-pizza-and-beer-on-railing-of-balcony-8753757/)*

The restaurant calls its food native-inspired. The story it tells is about Florida's waters and land, with ingredients that would have been familiar to the Native peoples of the area, including the princess the restaurant is named for. There are multicultural and European-explorer threads too. The sourcing philosophy is simple: Florida produce and seafood when available, U.S. family farms otherwise, and organic where they can. In that organic line, there are no hormones or antibiotics.

The star of the kitchen is a 10-foot-diameter barbacoa grill. Dishes come off it, and it's the heart of the place.

The building itself is the reason I'd come even if the food were average. It's the old Tampa Heights Water Works building, sitting beside Ulele Spring and next to Water Works Park. You feel the history as you walk in.

It's a big restaurant, too. There's nearly 7,000 square feet, with about 240 seats inside, about 95 in the beer garden and about 50 on the rooftop terrace with river views. The lawn can handle private events of about 400 people.

The riverside seats are the draw, and they're also the ones that bake in the afternoon sun before the river breeze kicks in. In summer, I'd save those tables for later in the day.

## What to Order

I'm not going to invent an entree list for you, because the menu changes. Ask for the current one when you sit down. What I can tell you is what I'd build the meal around.

![Barbacoa grill at Ulele restaurant with food cooking over the flames](/images/wm/articles/5779781.webp)
*Photo by [RDNE Stock project](https://www.pexels.com/@rdne) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/a-person-cooking-on-the-grill-5779781/)*

**Anything off the barbacoa grill.** The 10-foot grill is the whole point of the kitchen, so I'd choose from the dishes that come off it. After a heavy plate, I was very glad Water Works Park was next door for a walk.

**The house-brewed beer.** The on-site brewery is Ulele Spring Brewery, and the regular tank-to-tap lineup includes:

- Rusty Red
- Water Works Pale
- Hydration Station Lager
- Ulele Light
- Magbee's Honey Lager
- Wedding Beer

There are seasonal beers too. You won't find these anywhere else, since the craft beer is only available at Ulele and made right there.

**Wine, if you prefer it.** The list leans on domestic family-winery wines, plus some Spanish private-label bottles as a nod to the early Spanish explorers.

**A to-go drink for the Riverwalk.** Beer and cocktails can be ordered to go in a special cup that lets you drink legally along the 2.4-mile Tampa Riverwalk. That's a very Tampa quirk. Stay within the Riverwalk rules, and don't wander into traffic with a drink.

## Hours and Reservations

![Host stand and waiting guests at the entrance of Ulele in Tampa Heights](/images/wm/articles/8312018.webp)
*Photo by [Denys Gromov](https://www.pexels.com/@jdgromov) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/ukulele-and-picture-frames-on-a-blue-wall-8312018/)*

Ulele serves lunch and dinner daily:

| Days | Hours |
| --- | --- |
| Sunday–Thursday | 11 a.m.–10 p.m. |
| Friday and Saturday | 11 a.m.–11 p.m. |

The restaurant is closed on Thanksgiving and Christmas. Hours can change, so check them the morning you go.

The kitchen opens at 11 a.m. and the restaurant serves lunch and dinner, so don't show up at 9:30 a.m. hoping for eggs.

Reservations are the first struggle. Call **813-999-4952** to book. If you hit a recording, leave the details you want. You can also book through OpenTable, but online booking didn't go through for me, and the phone was what worked. Parties of 7 or more should call instead of relying on a quick online booking. Groups of 20 or more should contact **813-310-3701** or **groups@Ulele.com**. For general questions, the email is **info@ulele.com**.

Don't treat reservations as optional on a nice evening. On a clear Saturday, I watched walk-ups lingering by the host stand while reserved parties flowed past them to the river side. If you have tickets at the Straz, build in walking time. A 5:30 curtain doesn't mean you can count on a same-day riverside table for four without calling first.

## Parking and Getting There

**Address:** 1810 North Highland Avenue, Tampa, FL 33602
**Phone:** 813-999-4952

![Front drive and entrance of Ulele on North Highland Avenue in Tampa Heights](/images/wm/articles/36756673.webp)
*Photo by [Matt Fitz Gibaud](https://www.pexels.com/@mfitzart) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/charming-street-view-with-boutique-and-palm-tree-36756673/)*

Parking is where people get tense before they ever taste the food. Here's how I'd plan it.

### Driving and Valet

The restaurant fronts Highland Avenue. When Ulele opened, complimentary valet at the front drive was part of the plan for Columbia Restaurant Group properties. Ask at the entrance whether it's running when you arrive, and check for any current charge.

Street parking near the building fills around curtain times at the Straz and during weekend brunch hours. I wouldn't bet a reservation on finding a free curb spot at 6:45 p.m. on a Saturday.

### Walking the Riverwalk

The Riverwalk is the approach a lot of downtown hotel guests take, and it's a pretty one. You can also walk in from the Water Works Park or Doyle Carlton side. Leave extra time in summer heat. It's a lovely walk, but you'll arrive warm.

### Bike, Boat, Canoe or Kayak

You can also arrive by bike or on foot. If you're on the water, you can come by boat, canoe or kayak and dock next door at Water Works Park. I didn't arrive this way, but it's the most memorable way to get there.

## Tips Before You Go

**Say the name with confidence.** It's You-lay-lee. Softening the vowels at the host stand is a common mistake, and nobody minds, but it's nice to get it right.

**Wear sleeves if you want the indoor rooms.** The atmosphere is casual elegance. Formal is fine and up to you, but men must wear sleeves. If you're dressed more relaxed than they want for the main dining rooms, you may be seated outdoors instead. I watched a host redirect a sleeveless guest toward the patio. That surprises beach-vacation visitors who walked the Riverwalk in tank tops.

**Know which Ulele you mean.** There's a second Ulele at Tampa International Airport in Airside C, near Southwest. If your layover is the only meal you have, that's the one for you. If you want the brewery, the barbacoa grill, the rooftop and Water Works Park next door, you want the Tampa Heights restaurant on Highland Avenue.

**Don't mix it up with Columbia.** Whether you search Tampa Ulele, ulele restaurant tampa or ulele restaurant tampa florida, you're looking for one riverside dining room on Highland Avenue. It isn't the Columbia Cafe at the History Center or the Columbia in Ybor City. They're the same company, but separate restaurants in different places.

**Ask for the current menu.** The offerings change, so I'm not quoting prices. Ask what's on offer when you sit down, and check the seasonal beers.

**Make a plan for the walk.** Water Works Park is great for families and for anyone who needs to move after dinner. I'd arrive early enough to stroll before or after the meal.

## Ulele Tampa FAQ

### How do you pronounce Ulele?

It's pronounced You-lay-lee. The spelling doesn't give it away, so don't feel bad if you get it wrong at first.

### Where is Ulele in Tampa?

Ulele is at 1810 North Highland Avenue, Tampa, FL 33602, in Tampa Heights on the Riverwalk. It sits next to Water Works Park, about 400 yards from the Straz Center for the Performing Arts.

### Is Ulele Restaurant Tampa Florida the Same as the Airport Location?

No, the airport Ulele is a second location in Airside C at Tampa International Airport. Searching ulele restaurant tampa most likely means the river restaurant at 1810 North Highland Avenue. The Columbia Restaurant Group runs other restaurants in Florida cities, but those aren't Ulele.

### Do I Need a Reservation at Ulele?

I'd say yes, especially for patio and waterfront tables at sunset. Call 813-999-4952 or book through OpenTable. Parties of 7 or more should call, and groups of 20 or more should use 813-310-3701 or groups@Ulele.com.

### What Are Ulele's Hours?

Ulele is open for lunch and dinner daily. Hours are Sunday through Thursday 11 a.m. to 10 p.m. and Friday and Saturday 11 a.m. to 11 p.m. It's closed on Thanksgiving and Christmas, so check before you go.

### What Is the Dress Code at Ulele?

The atmosphere is casual elegance, and formal is fine. Men must wear sleeves. If you're dressed more relaxed than they want for the main dining rooms, you may be seated outdoors instead.

For a downtown Channelside stop when you want an indoor attraction, see my [Florida Aquarium](/things-to-do/florida-aquarium-tampa) guide.

For the Riverwalk art museum on Gasparilla Plaza, see [Tampa Museum of Art](/things-to-do/tampa-museum-of-art).

For the Heights food hall on North Ola (not the motor shop), see [Armature Works Tampa](/food-and-drink/armature-works-tampa).

## Final Thoughts

What won me over at Ulele Tampa was the whole setting: a 1903 water works building, a huge barbacoa grill and beer you can't get anywhere else, all with the Hillsborough River right there. Water Works Park next door makes it feel like an outing, not just a meal.

My big planning tip is simple: call ahead, wear sleeves and plan your parking before you leave. Do those three things and the evening runs smoothly. Then walk the river and enjoy it. 🌅

coverCredit: Photo by Connor Scott McManus on Pexels
body:
# Things to Do on Saturday in Tampa

A Saturday in Tampa is one day, and the city is bigger than one day. The version that works any week is a free morning, one ticketed stop, and an evening you can reach without crossing town again. 🌴

![Tampa skyline seen from the Hillsborough River at midday](/images/wm/articles/11665707.webp)
*Photo by [Connor Scott McManus](https://www.pexels.com/@connorscottmcmanus) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/pier-and-skyscrapers-on-horizon-11665707/)*

## Short on Time?

- **Morning:** Walk the Riverwalk while it is still cool. It is free, and it is open day and night.
- **Midday:** Pick one indoor place, the Florida Aquarium or MOSI, if you want air conditioning.
- **Afternoon:** Give ZooTampa or Busch Gardens the whole afternoon. They sit on the north side, so they do not pair well with a downtown night.
- **Evening:** Stay downtown. Ride the streetcar to Ybor, or eat at the Armature Works food hall.
- **Before you buy:** Check hours the morning you go. Parks and museums change them.

## 1. Start on the Riverwalk

The Riverwalk is the free part of a Saturday I would not skip. It runs along the Hillsborough River toward the Garrison Channel, through downtown parks, and it does not need a ticket. The [Friends of the Riverwalk](https://thetampariverwalk.com/) list the path as open 24 hours. I would still start in the morning. A Florida afternoon on open pavement is a different walk than the same path at 9 a.m.

Curtis Hixon Park, at 600 N. Ashley Drive, sits on the route. It is about 8 acres, with fountains, a playground, and a dog park, so it works if you have kids or just want a bench. Farther north, Julian B. Lane Riverfront Park has courts and a water playground. Armature Works, the old trolley barn with a food hall, is an easy place to start or to stop for lunch.

Two rules are easy to miss. Fishing is not allowed on the path. Drinks are allowed only in an approved specialty cup, and only inside the cup zone. If you want coffee, buy it in a regular cup and finish it before you treat the path like a bar.

Parking depends on which end you use. The Beneficial Drive and Channelside end and the Armature Works end are both real starts. Pick the one closest to where you leave the car.

![Tampa Riverwalk in downtown Tampa with the Hillsborough River and palm trees](/images/wm/articles/6416111.webp)
*Photo by [Quang Nguyen Vinh](https://www.pexels.com/@quang-nguyen-vinh-222549) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/residential-buildings-and-palms-on-riverside-in-modern-city-6416111/)*

## 2. Ride the Streetcar to Ybor

The TECO Line Streetcar is the easiest way I know to get from downtown to [Ybor](/guides/ybor-city-tampa-fl-33605) without a car. It runs seven days a week, it is free, it has 11 stations, and it comes about every 15 minutes. The ride goes from downtown through the Channel District to Ybor. Confirm the day's service before you build the afternoon around it, because a free ride is only useful if the car is actually running.

Get off on Seventh Avenue. The street is brick, with cigar shops, the Columbia Restaurant, and La Segunda, which has been baking in the same place for a long time. The chickens are the part you do not buy. They have wandered these streets for more than a century, and the neighborhood is a bird sanctuary by city ordinance. Do not feed them, do not chase them, and watch where you step.

Saturday night in Ybor is busier than Saturday afternoon. If you want the brick street without the crowd, go before dinner. If you want the crowd, stay.

![TECO Line Streetcar tracks in Ybor City](/images/wm/articles/12181717.webp)
*Photo by [Connor Scott McManus](https://www.pexels.com/@connorscottmcmanus) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/grayscale-photo-of-a-city-street-12181717/)*

## 3. Bayshore, If You Want a Long Flat Walk

Bayshore Boulevard is the other no-ticket walk that is there every Saturday. The path along the water is about 10 feet wide, and it is billed as the largest continuous sidewalk in the country. People walk dogs, run, and push strollers. It is flat, it is sunny, and it is a better morning than a midday. Bring water.

Bayshore and the Riverwalk are the same kind of plan: outside, free, and as long as you want. I would not try to do both at a serious pace and still make a north-side park. Pick one walk.

## 4. One Indoor Stop: The Aquarium or MOSI

The Florida Aquarium is at 701 Channelside Drive, which keeps it in the same part of town as the Riverwalk and the streetcar. That is why it fits a Saturday that started downtown. The habitat they lead with is Heart of the Sea, with a loggerhead sea turtle, a Maori wrasse, and a blue speckled grouper. Penguin greetings, stingray feeding, and sloth feeding are add-ons, not the basic visit.

I would go in the morning and be done in time for lunch on the water. Hours change, and I am not quoting a ticket price. Look at [the aquarium's own page](https://www.flaquarium.org/) the day you go.

MOSI, the Museum of Science and Industry, is the other indoor choice. It is at 4801 E. Fowler Avenue, in Terrace Park, which is not a downtown errand. Treat it as the day's main stop, not a bonus after the Riverwalk. The museum sometimes opens a quieter, sensory-friendly morning. If someone in your group needs that, check the calendar and register. Do not assume you can walk up.

![A sea turtle swimming, the kind of exhibit the Florida Aquarium is known for](/images/wm/articles/24906366.webp)
*Photo by [Wijs (Wise)](https://www.pexels.com/@wijs-wise-136435282) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/hatchling-of-sea-turtle-swimming-in-sea-24906366/)*

## 5. The Zoo or Busch Gardens Takes the Whole Day

[ZooTampa at Lowry Park](/things-to-do/tampa-zoo) is at 1101 W. Sligh Avenue. It is a real Saturday, especially with kids, and it is on its own side of town. Busch Gardens is farther north, on North McKinley Drive, and Adventure Island sits with it. Either park is a full day once you add parking and the walk back to the car.

A north-side park and a downtown evening do not fit in the same Saturday unless you are willing to cut one of them short. I would pick the park or the Riverwalk-and-Ybor day, not both.

The parks also add seasonal events. A fall or holiday overlay sometimes needs its own ticket, and member rules can change on those nights. Check the park's calendar before you promise anyone a specific evening.

## 6. Keep the Night Downtown

Once you are downtown, stay there. Armature Works is the easy food stop on the river. Sparkman Wharf, at 615 Channelside, is the easy one near the aquarium end. Ybor is one streetcar ride away.

If you want a show, look at the [Straz Center](/things-to-do/tbpac-tampa) on the river or [Tampa Theatre](/things-to-do/tampa-theatre) on Franklin Street. Both run through the year. The useful habit is to check that week's calendar, then park for the building you are actually attending. Fortune Street fills up before a curtain.

A game night does the same thing to downtown, any week the team is home. You do not need the schedule in advance to know the advice: if the arena or the stadium is busy, give yourself extra time, or stay on the Riverwalk and out of that traffic.

## Useful Things to Know

Parking is the first thing people get wrong. The aquarium, the zoo, Busch Gardens, and the museums each have their own lot, and most of them charge. Look it up for the one place you picked.

Heat is the second thing. A lot of the year is still hot in the afternoon. Do the exposed walk in the morning. Save the indoor ticket for the hot part of the day, or flip that if a storm is on the radar.

Do not stack three ticketed places. One anchor plus a free walk is a good Saturday. Two anchors is a day in the car.

## FAQ

### What are the best things to do on Saturday in Tampa?

For a free morning, walk the Riverwalk or Bayshore. For an easy afternoon without a car, ride the streetcar to Ybor. For one ticket, choose the Florida Aquarium if you are already downtown, or give ZooTampa or Busch Gardens the whole day. Pick one of those and leave the others for another visit.

### Is the Riverwalk free on Saturday?

Yes. The path is free and listed as open 24 hours. Curtis Hixon Park and Julian B. Lane Riverfront Park are on the way. Fishing is not allowed, and drinks belong in an approved cup inside the cup zone.

### Do I need a car for a Saturday in Tampa?

Not for the Riverwalk, the streetcar, the aquarium, Armature Works, or Ybor. You will want a car for ZooTampa, Busch Gardens, MOSI, or Bayshore if you are starting downtown and do not want a long ride-share.

### Can I do the zoo and Ybor on the same Saturday?

Only if you cut both short. The zoo is on Sligh Avenue, north of downtown. Ybor is a streetcar ride from the river. The drive between them is the part that eats the day. I would choose one.

### Is the TECO Line Streetcar free?

It is free, it runs seven days a week, and the cars come about every 15 minutes across 11 stations. I would still check that service is running before you leave a restaurant to catch one.

### What is a good indoor Saturday if it rains?

The Florida Aquarium on Channelside or MOSI on Fowler Avenue. The aquarium is the one that stays attached to a downtown morning. MOSI is its own trip.

Looking for the seasonal water park next to Busch Gardens? See [Adventure Island Tampa](/things-to-do/adventure-island-tampa).

Hunting a flea market? Big Top is closed—see [Tampa flea market options](/shopping/tampa-flea-market) (Oldsmar and Ybor Saturday Market).

## Final Thoughts

The Saturday that works any week is a small one. Walk the river or Bayshore, ride the streetcar if you want Ybor, and buy one ticket. Leave the second park for the next time you are here. The city is still there next Saturday. The wider list of [things to do in Tampa](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa) is for a longer stay, and a second day is how I use [the rest of the weekend](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa-this-weekend).

body:
# Things to Do in Tampa This Weekend

A weekend in Tampa works when you stop treating it like one long list. Use one day for a ticket and the other day for walks that are free every week of the year. The Riverwalk, the streetcar, and Bayshore do not expire. The parks do not need a special occasion. 🌴

![Tampa Riverwalk at dusk looking toward downtown](/images/wm/articles/39737894.webp)
*Photo by [Trev W. Adams](https://www.pexels.com/@trev-takes-photos) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/stunning-philadelphia-skyline-view-from-river-39737894/)*

## Short on Time?

- **One free day:** Riverwalk in the morning, streetcar to Ybor after lunch.
- **One ticketed day:** Florida Aquarium if you want to stay downtown. ZooTampa or Busch Gardens if you are fine spending the day on the north side.
- **The other morning:** Bayshore Boulevard, early, with water.
- **Food without a reservation hunt:** Armature Works, on the river, or Sparkman Wharf at 615 Channelside.
- **Skip the double ticket.** Two paid attractions in two days is plenty. Three means you mostly see the car.

## 1. Give One Morning to the Riverwalk

The Riverwalk is the default I trust, because it is there every weekend and it does not care what else is on sale. The path follows the Hillsborough River toward the Garrison Channel. It is free, and the [Friends of the Riverwalk](https://thetampariverwalk.com/) list it as open 24 hours. Go early or go near sunset. Midday is the version people regret.

Curtis Hixon Park, at 600 N. Ashley Drive, is the easy stop in the middle. About 8 acres, fountains, a playground, and a dog park. Julian B. Lane Riverfront Park, farther north, has courts and a water playground if the group needs to burn energy before lunch.

People argue about where the path starts. Some descriptions begin at Armature Works. Others begin around Beneficial Drive and Channelside. Both ends work. Use the end nearest your parking.

Fishing is not allowed on the path. A drink is allowed only in an approved specialty cup, and only inside the cup zone. Plan the coffee before you plan the cocktail.

![Riverwalk path along the water with downtown buildings behind it](/images/wm/articles/34761559.webp)
*Photo by [Allen Boguslavsky](https://www.pexels.com/@allen-boguslavsky-1344061) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/winter-scene-at-chicago-river-with-iconic-skyline-34761559/)*

## 2. Ride the Streetcar to Ybor on Either Day

The TECO Line Streetcar is free, runs seven days a week, stops at 11 stations, and comes about every 15 minutes. It connects downtown, the Channel District, and Ybor. I would still glance at the service notice the day you go. A weekend plan that depends on the streetcar should know if the cars are out.

[Ybor](/guides/ybor-city-tampa-fl-33605) is where you get off and walk. Seventh Avenue is brick. The Columbia Restaurant and La Segunda are the old reasons to be hungry there. The chickens are the reason to look down. They have been in the neighborhood for more than a century, the area is a bird sanctuary by city ordinance, and you are a guest. Do not feed them.

Night is louder than afternoon. If this is the free day of the weekend, go to Ybor before dinner and leave the late hours alone. If you want the late hours, make Ybor the night and do not schedule a north-side park the next morning at opening time. You will feel it.

![A street in Ybor City, where the TECO Line Streetcar lets you off](/images/wm/articles/12181717.webp)
*Photo by [Connor Scott McManus](https://www.pexels.com/@connorscottmcmanus) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/grayscale-photo-of-a-city-street-12181717/)*

## 3. Use the Other Morning for Bayshore

Bayshore Boulevard is the long, flat walk on the water. The path is about 10 feet wide, and it is billed as the largest continuous sidewalk in the country. It is a good second morning because it does not repeat the Riverwalk and it does not need a ticket. It is also uncovered. Bring water and go before the pavement heats up.

I would not put Bayshore, the Riverwalk, and a theme park in the same day. Across two days, Bayshore plus one downtown walk is a good pair.

## 4. Spend the Other Day on One Ticket

The Florida Aquarium, at 701 Channelside Drive, is the ticket that stays in downtown. If you are staying downtown for the weekend, [The Tampa EDITION](/guides/the-tampa-edition) is on Channelside with it. You can walk there from the Riverwalk end near Channelside, see Heart of the Sea, and still have the streetcar for later. The room they lead with has a loggerhead sea turtle, a Maori wrasse, and a blue speckled grouper. Feeding experiences are extra. Hours and prices move, so read them on [the aquarium's site](https://www.flaquarium.org/) that morning.

[ZooTampa](/things-to-do/tampa-zoo) is the ticket if the weekend belongs to kids and animals. The address is 1101 W. Sligh Avenue. It is not a quick add to a downtown day. Busch Gardens, on North McKinley Drive, is the ticket if you want a full park, and Adventure Island next to it is the water-park version of that same trip. Pick one of the three. The north side and downtown are far enough apart that a second paid stop turns the day into driving.

Those parks sometimes run seasonal evenings, and a special event can be a separate ticket. I would not plan a weekend around an overlay until the park's own calendar says it is on.

MOSI, at 4801 E. Fowler Avenue, is the indoor backup when the sky looks bad. It is a destination, not a stop between the river and the zoo. If you need a sensory-friendly morning, the museum offers those on its own schedule. Register if you see one. Do not count on walking in.

![A sea turtle in a large tank, the centerpiece of a Florida Aquarium visit](/images/wm/articles/24906366.webp)
*Photo by [Wijs (Wise)](https://www.pexels.com/@wijs-wise-136435282) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/hatchling-of-sea-turtle-swimming-in-sea-24906366/)*

## 5. Eat Near Where You Already Are

Armature Works is the food hall in the old trolley barn on the river. It is the right lunch when the morning was the Riverwalk, because you are already there. Sparkman Wharf, at 615 Channelside, is the right stop when the day was the aquarium. In Ybor, eat on Seventh Avenue instead of riding back downtown just for a table.

None of these require a festival. They are open week after week. If a place takes reservations, book the one meal you care about and leave the other meals loose.

## Useful Things to Know

Split the weekend by geography. Downtown, the Channel District, and Ybor can share a day because of the streetcar and the river path. Sligh Avenue, Fowler Avenue, and North McKinley Drive each want their own day.

Check hours the morning you leave, not the screenshot you saved last month. Museums and parks change them.

A home game downtown changes traffic and parking around the arena and the waterfront. You do not need to be going to the game for it to matter. If you are, go early. If you are not, use the other end of the Riverwalk.

Rain moves the plan indoors. Aquarium, MOSI, or the food hall. The Riverwalk will be there after the storm.

## FAQ

### What are the best free things to do in Tampa on a weekend?

Walk the Riverwalk, ride the TECO Line Streetcar to Ybor, and take a morning on Bayshore Boulevard. Curtis Hixon Park, at 600 N. Ashley Drive, is free and sits on the river path. None of these need a ticket.

### How should I split two days?

Put the free walks on one day and a single paid place on the other. The aquarium pairs with downtown. The zoo, Busch Gardens, or MOSI should be the paid day by itself.

### Is the streetcar a real way to get to Ybor?

Yes. It is free, it runs all week, and the ride from downtown to Ybor is the point. Confirm service the day you go, then get off and walk Seventh Avenue.

### Do I need a car?

Not for a downtown weekend of the Riverwalk, the aquarium, Armature Works, and Ybor. You want a car for the zoo, Busch Gardens, MOSI, or a relaxed trip out to Bayshore.

### Can I see the zoo and Busch Gardens in one weekend?

You can, and you will not see much else. They are both north of downtown, and each one fills a day. I would pick the one your group will actually enjoy and use the other day on the river.

### What if the parks are advertising a seasonal event?

Treat it as optional. The zoo, the aquarium, and Busch Gardens are open as ordinary attractions the rest of the time. A seasonal evening can be a different ticket. Check the park's calendar, then decide if it is worth building the weekend around.

## Final Thoughts

The weekends that go well here are the small ones. One free day on the water and in Ybor. One paid day, chosen because it is the thing you wanted, not because it was on a poster. Leave room to sit down. The Riverwalk is still there if the rest of the plan changes. The full list of [things to do in Tampa](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa) is for a longer trip. If you only have [Saturday](/things-to-do/things-to-do-on-saturday-in-tampa), use the free day and skip the second morning.
