coverCredit: Photo by Colon Freld on Pexels
body:
# 5 Things to Know Before You Play TPC Tampa in Lutz

If you type tpc tampa into a search box, you probably expect a course somewhere near downtown, maybe tucked beside a hotel or a casino. I did too. It turns out the golf course is [TPC Tampa Bay](https://www.tpctampabay.com/), and it is not in downtown Tampa at all. It sits in [Lutz](/guides/zip-code-hillsborough-tampa-fl), north of the city, a short hop off the Veteran's Expressway. Once I got that straight, the rest of the picture made a lot more sense. ⛳

![TPC Tampa Bay clubhouse and entrance in Lutz, Florida](/images/wm/articles/4117878.webp)
*Photo by [Colon Freld](https://www.pexels.com/@gapeppy1) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/landscape-photography-of-the-club-house-of-the-sea-pines-resort-4117878/)*

## Short on Time?

- TPC Tampa Bay is a golf course in Lutz. It is not downtown Tampa, and it is not a casino or a stadium.
- The address is 5300 W Lutz Lake Fern Rd, Lutz, FL 33558. The main phone number is 813-949-0090. The toll-free directions line is 866-PLAY-TPC.
- From the Veteran's Expressway (589 North), take Lutz Lake Fern Road, exit 16, and go east about half a mile. The club is on the right.
- It is an 18-hole course, par 71, designed by Bobby Weed. The club says the PGA TOUR built it in 1991.
- Pricing is dynamic. There is no fixed green fee posted, so book ahead or call the golf shop for the best rate.
- The golf shop opens at 7:00 a.m. and closes at 6:30 p.m.

## 1. Lutz, Not Downtown: Clearing Up What "TPC Tampa" Means

The first mistake most people make is assuming the name puts them in the middle of the city. I made that mistake in my head before I ever pulled up a map. The club's address is in Lutz, and that matters for your whole day.

Lutz is a different drive than [downtown](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa), [Westshore](/guides/westshore-marriott-hotel-tampa), or Ybor. If you are coming from a hotel near the water or from a meeting in the financial district, you are not doing a quick cross-town trip. You are heading north and east to a suburban golf property, and you should build that into your timing. Leaving 20 minutes before your tee time is cutting it close if traffic is bad.

The other reason the location matters: the golf course is the whole point. There is no separate attraction on the property that I know of, and nothing in what I was given suggests you would be stuck on a casino floor or at a concert. If you came for golf, you will spend your time on fairways, in the golf shop, and maybe at the grill. If you came for something else, you are in the wrong place, and that is worth figuring out before you get in the car. [Topgolf](/events/topgolf-tampa) is the bay-and-screen building people mix up with a course, and it is not in Lutz.

![Road sign for Lutz Lake Fern Road exit off the Veteran's Expressway near Tampa](/images/wm/articles/31173602.webp)
*Photo by [Jeff S.](https://www.pexels.com/@jeff-s-2150433163) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/serene-lakeside-with-stop-sign-and-bare-tree-31173602/)*

## 2. TPC Tampa Is Really TPC Tampa Bay, a Golf Course Built in 1991

When you say the name out loud, say TPC Tampa Bay. That is the real name on the club's materials, and it is what you will hear from the staff. Saying "TPC Tampa" alone is fine for a search, but in conversation, use the full name so there is no confusion about which Tampa Bay place you mean.

The club says the PGA TOUR built the course in 1991. Bobby Weed designed the 18-hole resort course. Their championship-golf description also lists Chi Chi Rodriguez as a PGA TOUR player consultant. Weed's own account of the course lines up with that story: wide fairways, large greens, and the same long history of hosting. The club says the layout is 18 holes with a par of 71, and it lists yardage from 4,990 yards on the forward tees to just under 7,000 from the championship tees. I am not going to invent a scorecard total past what they published. If you want the exact number for a specific set of tees, ask the golf shop.

The course also has a reputation for a particular kind of challenge, and this is where it became real for me. Water, cypress heads, lagoons, and bunkers show up on a lot of holes. Hole 6 is a short par 3 played over wetland marsh. Hole 7 is a long par 5 with a lagoon down the left side. Holes 10 and 18 both ask for accuracy with water in play. Hole 17 is a long par 3 to a very large green with water on the right. The green on 17 is about 11,000 square feet, which the club calls out, and the average green on the course is roughly 6,400 square feet. I would not call that a beginner course. I would call it a fair test for someone who can hit a straight ball and wants to think their way around a little trouble.

The club's own marketing makes a few bigger claims: a 4 1/2 star rating from a national golf ranking, a top-five spot in a statewide ranking, Audubon Cooperative Sanctuary status as one of only two Tampa Bay courses, and 21 consecutive years hosting PGA TOUR Champions events. I have not checked those rankings or designations myself, so I am passing them along as the club's claims, not as things I verified. The Champions Tour hosting history is the piece that explains the course's reputation, and it is why the layout is built the way it is.

![Water hazard and cypress trees along a fairway at TPC Tampa Bay in Lutz](/images/wm/articles/32386690.webp)
*Photo by [CK Seng](https://www.pexels.com/@keat007) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/scenic-golf-course-by-water-on-a-sunny-day-32386690/)*

## 3. Getting There From the Airport, Westshore, and Downtown

The club's directions are blunt, which I appreciated. From Tampa International Airport or the Westshore area, follow the signs to 589 North, the Veteran's Expressway. Continue to the Lutz Lake Fern Road exit, which is exit 16. Travel east about half a mile, and the entrance is on the right.

From downtown Tampa, the route runs through Ashley and onto the Veteran's Expressway. You still take exit 16, then turn left and head east about half a mile to the club on the right. Both routes include tolls. The club's directions mention two toll booths and $2.25 in tolls. That is the figure they give, so use it as a starting point, and check your own route and your own car's toll setup before you go.

A few things I would do if I were you. Put the full address into your navigation app, but also look at the exit number so you are not relying on one voice telling you to turn. Plan for the tolls in your budget. And if you are staying downtown or at the Seminole Hard Rock, do not assume a quick cab ride to the first tee. You are driving a real distance, and the time you spend on the expressway counts. If you need a ride, plan it like a trip, not like a hop across the street. 🚗

![Veteran's Expressway toll plaza on the drive north toward Lutz, Florida](/images/wm/articles/16310595.webp)
*Photo by [Araf Khan](https://www.pexels.com/@araf-khan-506660412) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/toll-plaza-on-highway-16310595/)*

## 4. Hours at the Golf Shop, The Grill, and CUATRO

The golf shop is open from 7:00 a.m. to 6:30 p.m. ⏰ That is the window for gifts, shop questions, and anything you need before or after a round. If you are picking up something on the way out, do not wait until 6:15 to walk in.

The food side is where things get a little messy. The club lists The Grill with these hours: Monday 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., Tuesday through Thursday 7 a.m. to 9 p.m., Friday and Saturday 7 a.m. to 10 p.m., and Sunday 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Breakfast at The Grill runs daily from 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. That is useful if you want to eat before your tee time.

The same company that runs the club, Heritage Golf Group, also names CUATRO as a modern restaurant on site. The club's own hours still say The Grill, and CUATRO menus show up in the dining information too. I am not going to pretend I know exactly which spot you will walk into, or whether they are the same room under two names. Call ahead or ask the golf shop when you check in, especially if you have a specific meal in mind after a round.

![Dining room and outdoor patio at a golf clubhouse in Lutz, Florida](/images/wm/articles/30963921.webp)
*Photo by [虎 曼](https://www.pexels.com/@jyjyjyjy) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/cozy-outdoor-patio-with-wicker-furniture-30963921/)*

## 5. Tee Times and Dynamic Pricing: No Fixed Green Fee to Quote

This is the part people will want a number for, and I do not have one to give you. The club says TPC has moved to dynamic pricing. Costs change in real time based on supply and demand, the same way airline seats or hotel rooms do. The club says the best price is usually when you book ahead or through their app. The golf shop can quote the best rate available by phone, and flexibility on low-demand days can help you save.

There is no fixed green-fee board I could point to, so I am not writing a price into this article. Anything I wrote would be a guess, and a guess that goes stale in a week is worse than no number. If budget is what decides whether you play, call the golf shop at 813-949-0090, ext. 1, and ask for the best rate on the date you want. Be specific about the day and time. Weekday mornings and weekend afternoons can price very differently.

Tee times are booked ahead. If the slot you want is gone, you can sign up for a waitlist. Plan on booking early for weekends, and keep a backup time in mind in case your first choice disappears.

The club also talks about memberships and a preferred annual pass. Members get advanced tee times, member-only tournaments and social events, and merchandise discounts. Membership sales go through extension 104. The club also mentions outings for groups from 12 to 120 people. I never saw a filled-in outing contract, so I cannot tell you what a group package costs. If you are planning a company day or a buddy trip, ask for a written quote before you commit to a date.

![Golfers teeing off on a morning round at TPC Tampa Bay in Lutz](/images/wm/articles/9207240.webp)
*Photo by [Mikhail Nilov](https://www.pexels.com/@mikhail-nilov) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/man-wearing-white-polo-shirt-playing-golf-9207240/)*

## Useful Things to Know

**Don't confuse this with the Seminole Hard Rock.** This is the most common mix-up I can see, and it is easy to fall into. The Seminole Hard Rock Hotel and Casino Tampa sits on Orient Road in Tampa. TPC Tampa Bay sits in Lutz off the Veteran's Expressway. Different addresses, different drives, different reasons to be there. If you typed "tpc tampa" hoping for a casino night, the casino is a separate trip. If your navigation sends you toward Orient Road, stop and check the address you typed.

**Sports tickets are not the same thing.** Some people searching this name are also looking for Rays tickets, Bucs games, or a Lightning game. Those are stadium and arena plans, separate from golf. I would not plan a golf round and a stadium night on the same day without checking the timing carefully, because the drive between Lutz and downtown can eat more time than you expect, especially in traffic.

**Hotels are a separate question.** TPC did not give me a lodging partner, so I am not naming a hotel near the course. If you want to stay close to Lutz, search for lodging there on your own terms. If you are staying downtown or near the water, plan the drive and the tolls into your morning.

**Shows and nightlife are not on the scorecard.** If you want a show, a casino floor, or a dinner downtown after golf, that is a second destination. Think of it as a separate outing, and leave enough time in your evening to get back and forth without rushing.

**Parking and arrival.** I would check parking and the arrival process when you book, so you know where to drop your bag and whether you need a specific entrance. Give yourself time to check in at the golf shop before you head to the first tee.

**Champions Tour dates.** The club's materials talk about years of Champions Tour events. I do not have a confirmed 2026 tournament date, so do not plan a trip around one unless the club confirms it. If you are hoping to watch a tournament, ask the club directly before you book.

**Weather.** Florida golf means heat, humidity, and afternoon storms in many seasons. Water hazards on the course make a long day feel even longer if you are not ready for it. Bring water, a hat, and a plan for a fast exit if lightning shows up. 🌧️

## FAQ

### Is TPC Tampa in downtown Tampa?

No. TPC Tampa Bay is in Lutz, north of downtown Tampa. The club's address is 5300 W Lutz Lake Fern Rd, Lutz, FL 33558. If your map puts you on Orient Road or in the middle of the city, you have the wrong place.

### How do I get to TPC Tampa Bay from the airport?

From Tampa International Airport or the Westshore area, follow the signs to 589 North, the Veteran's Expressway. Take the Lutz Lake Fern Road exit, which is exit 16. Head east about half a mile, and the entrance is on the right. Expect tolls on the way.

### How much does it cost to play TPC Tampa Bay?

The club uses dynamic pricing, so there is no fixed green fee I can quote. Prices shift with demand. The best approach is to call the golf shop at 813-949-0090, ext. 1, and ask for the best rate on the date you want, or book through the club's app or tee sheet.

### Is TPC Tampa Bay open to the public?

The club says the course is open to the public as well as to members, and it also offers a preferred annual pass. You can book a public tee time ahead of time, and you can join a waitlist if the slot you want is full.

### Who designed the course?

Bobby Weed designed the 18-hole resort course. The club says the PGA TOUR built it in 1991, and that Chi Chi Rodriguez served as a PGA TOUR player consultant.

### Is TPC Tampa Bay the same as the Seminole Hard Rock casino?

No. The Seminole Hard Rock Hotel and Casino Tampa is on Orient Road in Tampa. TPC Tampa Bay is a golf course in Lutz. They are separate places with separate addresses.

### What time does the golf shop open?

The golf shop opens at 7:00 a.m. and closes at 6:30 p.m. The club lists The Grill hours separately, including daily breakfast from 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m.

### What is the hardest hole at TPC Tampa Bay?

I would not hand out a difficulty ranking, because the club's ratings are its own and I have not tested them against a scorecard. Hole 17 stands out in the description as a long par 3 to a large green with water on the right, and holes 10 and 18 both put water in play. Those are the ones I would plan around.

## Final Thoughts

TPC Tampa is really TPC Tampa Bay, and it is a golf course in Lutz, not a downtown attraction. If you keep that straight, the rest of the trip falls into place. Use the full name, put Lutz in your navigation, take exit 16 off 589, and budget for the tolls.

Book ahead, call the golf shop if you want a real rate, and do not plan around a number I never saw posted. Give yourself time to get there, and check the hours for the shop and The Grill before you go. If the map sends you toward Orient Road or a stadium gate, you have the wrong Tampa Bay. Go find the Lutz address, pick a tee time, and enjoy the water on the back nine.

# Trampoline Park Tampa Hillsborough: 5 Things to Know Before You Jump at Altitude Drew Park

If you ask someone for the trampoline park on Hillsborough, you will usually get a nod and then a pause. That is how most people remember it. They recall the street or the county, not the brand. There is more disagreement than I would like.

![Altitude Tampa trampoline park building on West Hillsborough Avenue in Drew Park, Tampa](/images/wm/articles/5129490.webp)
*Photo by [Brett Sayles](https://www.pexels.com/@brett-sayles) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/facade-of-geometric-stone-building-against-cloudy-sky-5129490/)*

## Short on Time?

- **📍 The place:** Altitude Tampa - Drew Park, 4340 West Hillsborough Ave, Tampa, FL 33614. Some listings add Suite 350. Put the street address in your map app and look for the suite when you get there.
- **The hours:** Sunday 11:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. Monday through Thursday 10:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. Friday 10:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. Saturday 9:30 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. If the sign on the door says something else, trust the door.

- **The prices:** The dollar figures I have contradict each other, and some promotions are old. Call before you promise anyone a jump time or a dollar amount. The number I would use for anything specific is (813) 399-1529.
- **The mix-ups:** Bradenton and Spring Hill have Altitude parks too, but they are not this one. Rays games, Bucs games, Lightning, the Seminole Hard Rock Hotel and Casino, and an AMC are all separate plans in separate places.

## 1. Trampoline Park Tampa Hillsborough Is Altitude Tampa in Drew Park

The first thing to settle is whether "Hillsborough" points to one building or to several. I checked Altitude's Florida locations to find out. Tampa shows up once. The Tampa park is [Altitude Tampa - Drew Park](https://www.altitudetrampolinepark.com/locations/florida/tampa/4340-west-hillsborough-ave/), and Drew Park is the neighborhood in the name. Hillsborough is the street. The county-wide [Hillsborough zip codes](/guides/zip-code-hillsborough-tampa-fl) are a different lookup.

The address is 4340 West Hillsborough Ave, Tampa, Florida 33614. Street, city, and ZIP agree across the places I looked. Some versions add Suite 350 to the line, and some leave it off. I would put the street address in your map and plan to look for the suite number on the building when you arrive. Altitude's birthday material describes the location as being on W. Hillsborough Ave. and N. Lois Ave., near Crunch Fitness. If a friend says "the trampoline place on Hillsborough," that is the pin I would use.

There are two phone numbers on file for this park: (813) 399-1529 and (813) 503-4428. Altitude uses 813-399-1529 when it tells you to call about something specific, so that is the one I would dial first. The second number is listed with no label, and I do not know what it is for. I would not guess which one reaches the front desk.

![Street sign and storefront entrance for Altitude Tampa on West Hillsborough Avenue, Drew Park](/images/wm/articles/38422982.webp)
*Photo by [Quang Vuong](https://www.pexels.com/@quang-vuong-724225078) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/colorful-liquor-store-front-with-mural-in-urban-area-38422982/)*

## 2. Check the Weekly Hours Before You Leave

The hours for this location are more specific than the usual "open daily" you see on many attraction pages. Here they are as I have them:

- Sunday: 11:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m.
- Monday through Thursday: 10:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m.
- Friday: 10:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m.
- Saturday: 9:30 a.m. to 11:00 p.m.

These are the hours I would plan around, but hours change. Holidays, private events, and staffing can all shift the schedule, and I do not have a list of those exceptions. If you are coming on a holiday weekend or a night you have a party booked, call first. ⏰ The phone call is also the best way to find out whether a late jump will still get you the full time you paid for.

The Saturday window is the one I would think about most. Opening at 9:30 gives you a little extra room for a morning session, and closing at 11:00 makes it easier to fit in a late jump after dinner. Friday runs late too. Sunday closes earliest, at 9:00, so plan your session with that in mind.

![Customers lined up at the front desk of Altitude Tampa trampoline park in Drew Park](/images/wm/articles/7682356.webp)
*Photo by [Mikhail Nilov](https://www.pexels.com/@mikhail-nilov) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/call-center-agents-smiling-while-looking-at-camera-7682356/)*

## 3. Know What Is Actually Inside

Altitude lists a set of attractions for this Tampa location. The ones I would look for first are:

- Basketball Trampoline Dunk
- Battle Beam
- Extreme Dodgeball
- Kid's Court
- Main Court
- Performance Trampoline
- Trapeze
- Tumble Track
- ZipLine

Programs named alongside these include birthday parties, Glo in the Park, Jump Happy Hour, and Junior Jumpers. Glo in the Park and Happy Hour are the kind of sessions that change with the calendar, so ask about them on the phone before you plan around one.

Altitude's general marketing mentions dodgeball, battle beams, climbing, digital experiences, and party packages. It also says that programs differ from park to park. That matters here. I am not adding a foam pit, a ninja course, or anything else that sounds like a trampoline park feature unless it is on the Tampa attraction list. If you have a specific activity in mind, like the trapeze or the ZipLine, ask whether it is open during your session. Equipment can be closed for maintenance, and I would rather you hear that on the phone than find out at the door.

For a first visit, I would start with the Main Court and the Battle Beam if you want the classic trampoline park experience. Kids who want the lower-key version tend to head for the Kid's Court. Those are my picks, not a ranking, and your group might disagree.

![Battle Beam and open trampoline court inside Altitude Tampa in Drew Park](/images/wm/articles/6572607.webp)
*Photo by [Tima Miroshnichenko](https://www.pexels.com/@tima-miroshnichenko) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/a-little-girl-training-in-a-gymnastics-gym-6572607/)*

## 4. Sign the Waiver Before You Drive

Altitude's safety rules say to watch a short orientation video and sign the waiver before you jump. I would do both before you leave the house. A trampoline park that sends you back to the car for a missing waiver is a wasted trip, and the rule is printed on their own materials, so there is no excuse to be surprised by it.

Before you go, check that everyone in your group has a plan for the waiver. If you are bringing kids, adults need to sign too, and it helps to know who is responsible for each child. The orientation video is short, but it covers the basics you will need in the building. Give everyone a few minutes to watch it.

If you are booking a party, the waiver process still applies to every jumper, not just the person who made the booking. A birthday group of twelve kids and their parents is a lot of signatures. Sort it out early so you are not standing at the desk holding up the line.

![Waiver and orientation signage at the entrance of Altitude Tampa trampoline park on West Hillsborough Avenue](/images/wm/articles/14995539.webp)
*Photo by [Jan van der Wolf](https://www.pexels.com/@jan-van-der-wolf-11680885) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/no-parking-sign-on-door-14995539/)*

## 5. Confirm Prices and Booking Before You Promise Anyone a Jump

This is the part I would be most careful about. 💳 The prices I have for this location do not agree with each other. Some of the figures I have seen for Tampa include:

- A 90-minute jump at $24.99
- A 120-minute jump at $27.99
- A Happy Hour three-hour jump at $27.99, Monday through Thursday
- Monthly memberships at $44.99, with a note to come in and ask

The party package numbers also shift from one listing to the next. Some old promotions are still floating around, including an Easter 2024 hunt and a flash sale that ran into April 2026. Those are not the walk-up price today. Do not plan around a sale that has already ended.

Jump time, Happy Hour, membership, deposit, and party package are separate purchases. None of them is a sock fee or a parking fee, and I have not seen a list that covers those details. For booked events, the event terms call for a $100 deposit. If you book ahead, someone from Altitude will call to collect it. That means the phone number you give them matters.

There is also a "book the entire park" offer that Altitude says is available at participating locations. It does not clearly say whether 4340 West Hillsborough is one of them. If you are thinking about booking the whole room for a big group, call (813) 399-1529 and ask that question directly before you commit to a date or a deposit.

![Pricing and jump session board at the front desk of Altitude Tampa in Drew Park](/images/wm/articles/14772272.webp)
*Photo by [Tim Mossholder](https://www.pexels.com/@timmossholder) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/man-wakeboarding-on-ocean-waves-14772272/)*

## Useful Things to Know

**Figure out which "Hillsborough" you mean.** Hillsborough Avenue is a long road, and Tampa is not the only place with a park near it. The trampoline park on West Hillsborough in Drew Park is the Altitude Tampa location. The Altitude parks in Bradenton (201 Cortez Road West) and Spring Hill (11162 Spring Hill Drive) are separate places with separate phones and separate hours. If your GPS sends you to one of those, you are in the wrong city.

**Keep the entertainment plans separate.** People often ask about a trampoline park in the same breath as Rays tickets, a Bucs game at Raymond James Stadium, a Lightning game, a night at the Seminole Hard Rock Hotel and Casino, or a movie at an AMC. Those are all real places, and some of them are a fun day out. But none of them is the trampoline park. The Seminole Hard Rock Hotel and Casino Tampa is at 5223 Orient Road, Tampa, Florida 33610. Raymond James Stadium is the Bucs building. [Benchmark International Arena](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa) is downtown on Channelside. [Topgolf](/events/topgolf-tampa) on Palm River Road is a different night out. None of those is the Suite 350 door on West Hillsborough.

If you want to combine a jump with one of those outings, plan them as separate trips. A jump session can run long, and jumping hard before a ballgame or a casino night is a bad combination. Leave a buffer, and plan to eat something before you go.

**Timing and crowds.** I do not have crowd counts or peak-time information to share. What I can say is that the Saturday window is the longest of the week, which tells you where people are likely to spend a lot of their time. Ask the phone line when the quieter sessions are before you commit to a time.

**Parking.** I do not have parking details I can vouch for here, so ask about it when you call. It is a simple question, and the answer will be more useful than whatever I could guess.

**Promos are not prices.** Old promotions are still advertised online, including ones from 2024 and early 2026. Treat any promo as a question to ask, not a price you can count on. If a sale has an end date that has already passed, ask whether the current price is different.

**What people get wrong.** Most of the mistakes I can think of come from relying on a memory of the brand name or a single online page. People show up at the wrong Altitude. They expect a deal that has expired. They forget the waiver. They assume a party package includes everything in the room. A short phone call clears up most of that.

## FAQ

Yes. The trampoline park on West Hillsborough in Tampa is Altitude Tampa - Drew Park, at 4340 West Hillsborough Ave. Drew Park is the neighborhood in the name, and Hillsborough is the street. I did not find a second Altitude on Hillsborough Avenue in Tampa.

Saturday is 9:30 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. Sunday is 11:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. Those are the hours I have for this location. Holidays and private events can change them, so call (813) 399-1529 before a special day.

For booked events, the event terms call for a $100 deposit. Someone from Altitude calls to collect it. Confirm the amount and the process when you call, since prices and terms can change.

### Are there other Altitude parks near Tampa?

There are Altitude locations in Bradenton and Spring Hill, but they are not Tampa, and they are not on Hillsborough Avenue. Altitude Bradenton - Sarasota is at 201 Cortez Road West, Bradenton, Florida 34207, phone (941) 584-4700. Altitude Spring Hill is at 11162 Spring Hill Drive, Spring Hill, Florida 34609, phone (352) 399-9884.

## Final Thoughts

The trampoline park Tampa Hillsborough people are looking for is Altitude Tampa in Drew Park. The address is 4340 West Hillsborough Ave, and the suite is worth looking for when you get there. body:
# The Pearl Tampa Guide: Five Things to Know Before You Go

If you typed "the pearl tampa" into a search bar expecting a club with a velvet rope, you are not alone, and you would be wrong. [The Pearl Tampa](https://thepearlrestaurant.com/locations-menus/tampa/) is a restaurant. It sits on Water Street [downtown](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa), it is a gastropub with an oyster bar, and it has a private dining room that does most of the heavy lifting when a group needs a real table. I went in expecting a nightlife room and came out with a list of things people get wrong. Here is that list, plus the details that actually matter if you are going. 🦪

![The Pearl restaurant exterior on Water Street in downtown Tampa](/images/wm/articles/4120665.webp)
*Photo by [Brett Sayles](https://www.pexels.com/@brett-sayles) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/illuminated-cafe-entrance-in-downtown-at-night-4120665/)*

## Short on Time?

- **It is a restaurant.** The Tampa room is The Pearl Water Street, 823 Water St. Suite C-100, Tampa, FL 33602. It is not a nightclub and not the Pearl in Ohio.
- **Know your meal.** Weekday lunch runs 11:30 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. Weekend brunch runs 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. Dinner runs until 10, 11, or 9 depending on the night.
- **Oyster Hour is Monday through Thursday, 2 to 5 p.m.,** in the Tavern Bar. It is a discount, not a free-for-all.
- **Reservations are recommended, not required.** Call if the app shows nothing for your time. Call if your party is larger than six. Expect a credit card for parties of eight or more.
- **Parking is valet at Water Street and Raybon Court,** or other Water Street options nearby.
- **The private dining room seats up to 32** on weekdays and evenings, and it is a request, not a walk-up.

## 1. The Pearl Tampa Is a Restaurant, Not a Nightclub

The phrase "the pearl tampa" sounds like a room. A lounge, a club, maybe a hotel bar with a line out the door. That is the trap in the name. So I stopped guessing and pinned down what the place actually calls itself. The Tampa location describes itself as a restaurant, tavern, and oyster bar. Its address is 823 Water St. Suite C-100, Tampa, FL 33602, and the same address shows up in its private dining material too. [Yard House](/food-and-drink/yard-house-tampa) is the other Water Street restaurant I keep separate from this room, and [Ulele](/food-and-drink/ulele-tampa) is the Riverwalk room in Tampa Heights. [The Tampa EDITION](/guides/the-tampa-edition) is the hotel in that same neighborhood.

The brand also runs rooms in Dublin, Ohio and Columbus, Ohio. Tampa is one of those rooms, not a Tampa-only club that happens to share the name. Its own language leans on a "well-polished culinary jewel," seasonal seafood, shareable plates, handcrafted cocktails, and décor that is stylish and a little nostalgic. That is a fair description of what I walked into. It is a gastropub, and the Tampa location calls itself casual when you ask whether it is fancy. Nobody is going to check your ID at a velvet rope.

There is one thing about the reputation I want to flag. The restaurant says it is honored to be included in the MICHELIN Guide, and in two places it gives two different year spans: 2024–2026 in one spot and 2024–2025 in another. I am not going to pick a winner for you. A guide mention is not a star rating, and I did not see a star count in anything, so I am not going to suggest one. If the Michelin line matters to your decision, ask the host stand which version they are going by.

![Oyster bar counter with raw oysters on ice at The Pearl Tampa on Water Street](/images/wm/articles/10375817.webp)
*Photo by [RDNE Stock project](https://www.pexels.com/@rdne) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/man-in-gloves-preparing-food-10375817/)*

## 2. Know Which Meal You Are Walking Into

This is where people get tripped up, so I am going to be specific. The Tampa-specific hours I wrote down look like this:

- **Lunch:** Monday through Friday, 11:30 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.
- **Brunch:** Saturday and Sunday, 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.
- **Dinner:** Monday through Thursday, 3:00 to 10:00 p.m. Friday and Saturday, 3:00 to 11:00 p.m. Sunday, 3:00 to 9:00 p.m.
- **Happy hour:** Monday through Friday, 2:00 to 5:00 p.m., in the Tavern Bar.

The brand-level version of the schedule, the one that covers all its locations together, repeats the Tampa dinner hours and the happy hour window and mentions brunch. It does not spell out the weekday lunch block as cleanly. If I had only gone by that version, I would have missed that weekday lunch is its own service. The practical result is simple. If you show up at 11:30 on a Saturday expecting the weekday lunch menu, you will be looking at brunch instead. Pick your meal first, then pick your time. ⏰

Sunday dinner ends at 9:00, which is earlier than the rest of the week. If you are planning a late Sunday meal, that matters.

![Tavern Bar at The Pearl Tampa with bar stools and taps lined up along the counter](/images/wm/articles/5858038.webp)
*Photo by [Pavel Danilyuk](https://www.pexels.com/@pavel-danilyuk) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/photo-of-wooden-stools-in-a-bar-5858038/)*

## 3. Oysters, the Marble Counter, and What to Order

The oyster bar is the reason to walk in without a plan. The restaurant offers raw and cooked seafood, and its advice is the same advice I would give a friend: drop in, take a stool at the marble counter, and watch the oysters get shucked. That counter is the best free show in the building. Nobody needs a ticket for it. You are just sitting there, eating something cold and salty while a person opens shells in front of you.

Dishes the restaurant calls out and that I would start with:

- Creamy Clam Chowder
- Devils on Horseback, which are dates wrapped in bacon with a chimichurri gremolata
- Garlic Shrimp
- Great Lakes Fish N Chips
- Old Fashioned Deviled Eggs
- Tater tots
- Jalapeño Corn Spoon Bread, served in a cast iron skillet with whipped butter and honey
- N'awlins Style Baked Oysters
- Parmesan Baked Clams
- The Pub Burger
- Brown Sugar Pie, which is always on the board, with pies made daily

The restaurant says the oyster selection rotates, so check what is on the board when you get there rather than trusting any list, including this one. The same goes for the cocktails. The names they point to are the Barrel-Aged Old Fashioned, the Manhattan, Bourbon.Bacon.Boozy., and the Water Street Punch, which is a rotating punch with seasonal ingredients. The list changes, so do not show up expecting a specific drink to be on the card. On the beer side, the draft list leans on Cigar City Brewing, Coppertail Brewing, Green Bench Brewing, and Tampa Bay Brewing Co., with a few from outside Tampa Bay. That list also changes.

If you are eating with someone who has dietary limits, the menu marks items as gf or v, and some dishes can be made gluten-free or vegetarian on request. Tell your server about allergies. I did not hear a promise that the whole kitchen is allergen-free, so take the server's word on specific dishes and do not treat the menu as a guarantee.

The patio is covered and lively, which makes it a good call on a warm evening. Check in at the host stand, and you can ask about patio seating when you do.

![Plate of Devils on Horseback and Old Fashioned deviled eggs at The Pearl Tampa](/images/wm/articles/24186308.webp)
*Photo by [Change C.C](https://www.pexels.com/@change-c-c-974768353) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/fish-served-with-lemons-in-a-restaurant-24186308/)*

## 4. Reservations, Large Parties, and the Card You May Need

Reservations are not required, and the restaurant recommends them. Here is the friction I would actually warn someone about. If you try to book and no slot shows up for your time, call. 📞 If your party is larger than six, call and talk through the plan before you assume an online request is enough. For reservations of eight or more, a credit card is required, seven days a week.

The two situations are very different. A walk-in for two at 5 p.m. on a Tuesday is an easy night. Eight people on a Saturday who assumed a quick booking request was enough is the one that goes sideways. If you have eight or more, call first, have a card ready, and confirm the time out loud.

One small operational snag: if you are placing an order ahead and paying with a gift card, call the restaurant. Do not assume the online or phone process will handle it the way a regular card would.

![Booths and tables in the dining room at The Pearl Water Street in Tampa](/images/wm/articles/35285632.webp)
*Photo by [Andy Lee](https://www.pexels.com/@andy-lee-222330306) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/stylish-restaurant-interior-with-colorful-seating-35285632/)*

## 5. Private Dining: The Barrel Room and the Rest

The Pearl Tampa is more useful than its name suggests if you are planning a group event. The private dining room seats up to 32 on weekdays and evenings. You can fill out the request form on the restaurant's site or call 813.709.7776.

The brochure breaks the rooms down more specifically:

- **Barrel Room:** 32 seated, 45 for a reception, 381 square feet, flatscreen TV.
- **Tavern Bar:** no seated figure given, 30 for a reception, 337 square feet, flatscreen TV.
- **Full buyout:** 232 seated, 6,931 square feet, flatscreen TV.

The events the brochure lists as the point of the room include business meetings, sales presentations, holiday parties, anniversary parties, bar and bat mitzvahs, birthday celebrations, family gatherings, graduation dinners, luncheon events, rehearsal dinners, retirement parties, and wedding parties.

Pricing for private events is set per person, excluding tax and gratuity. Menu A is $65, Menu B is $75, and Menu C is $85. The lunch Menu A is $55, and the brunch Menu A is $55. The brochure also lists a few à la carte items at event pricing, such as jalapeño corn spoon bread at $16 per skillet, Old Fashioned Deviled Eggs at $3.25 each, tater tots at $9 per pound, and oysters on the half shell at $4.33 each. Those are event numbers. A regular night at the oyster bar is not automatically priced the same way, so do not use the brochure as a price list for a casual dinner.

If you want the Barrel Room, treat it as a request. It is not something you walk up and claim.

![Barrel Room set for a private party at The Pearl Tampa on Water Street](/images/wm/articles/18247667.webp)
*Photo by [Luca Istrate](https://www.pexels.com/@lukzy) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/men-in-suits-and-shirts-sitting-at-winery-18247667/)*

## Useful Things to Know

**Parking.** 🅿️ Valet is at the corner of Water Street and Raybon Court, between the crosswalk and the northwest corner of the Thousand and One building. The restaurant points people toward additional Water Street parking options and says reserved valet is available. I do not have a valet price, so I am not going to make one up. Ask when you book, or ask when you arrive.

**Confirm the city.** One answer on the Tampa restaurant's materials talks about "The Pearl in the Short North." That is the Columbus room's neighborhood, not Water Street. The wine answer that follows describes a list from France to Argentina, Spain to New Zealand, and Oregon, California, and Washington. If you are trying to confirm you have the Florida restaurant, that sentence will make you doubt yourself. Check the address. The one that kept coming up was 823 Water St. Suite C-100, Tampa, FL 33602.

**Oyster Hour is not happy hour.** The clock overlaps, but they are not the same thing. Happy hour runs Monday through Friday from 2 to 5 p.m. in the Tavern Bar. Oyster Hour is Monday through Thursday from 2 to 5 p.m. in that same bar. Oyster Hour gives $4 off specialty cocktails, $3 off snacks and apps, and $2 off oysters on the half shell. Those are discounts, not full menu prices. So a Friday happy hour is not automatically the oyster discount. Check which one is running before you order.

**Describing the place.** The restaurant calls the Tampa room a newer entry on the Tampa restaurant scene that has become a favorite for locals and out-of-town friends. That is its own description of itself. I can tell you the room has been busy on the nights I have been in, but I am not going to tell you it is packed every night of the week.

**Dress.** It is a casual gastropub, so everyday clothes will fit right in.

## FAQ

### Is The Pearl Tampa a nightclub?

No. The Pearl Tampa is a restaurant, tavern, and oyster bar on Water Street. It calls itself a casual gastropub. The name can sound like a club, but the menu, the oyster bar, and the private dining room are what define it.

### What are the hours at The Pearl Tampa?

Lunch runs Monday through Friday from 11:30 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. Brunch runs Saturday and Sunday from 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. Dinner runs Monday through Thursday from 3:00 to 10:00 p.m., Friday and Saturday from 3:00 to 11:00 p.m., and Sunday from 3:00 to 9:00 p.m. Happy hour runs Monday through Friday from 2:00 to 5:00 p.m. in the Tavern Bar.

### Do I need a reservation at The Pearl Tampa?

Reservations are not required, but the restaurant recommends them. If the time you want does not show up, call. If your party is larger than six, call first. For eight or more, a credit card is required.

### Is The Pearl Tampa the same as The Pearl in Columbus or Dublin, Ohio?

They are part of the same restaurant brand, but they are separate rooms in separate cities. The Tampa location is The Pearl Water Street at 823 Water St. Suite C-100. Some of the brand's materials mention Columbus neighborhoods, so check the address before you assume you are at the right place.

### Where do I park for The Pearl Tampa?

Valet is at the corner of Water Street and Raybon Court, between the crosswalk and the northwest corner of the Thousand and One building. The restaurant also points guests toward other Water Street parking options and says reserved valet is available. Ask about pricing when you book, because I do not have a valet price to share.

### What is Oyster Hour at The Pearl Tampa?

Oyster Hour runs Monday through Thursday from 2 to 5 p.m. in the Tavern Bar. It offers $4 off specialty cocktails, $3 off snacks and apps, and $2 off oysters on the half shell. It is separate from the Monday-through-Friday happy hour, even though the times overlap.

### Can I host a private event at The Pearl Tampa?

Yes. The private dining room seats up to 32 on weekdays and evenings, and there is a full buyout option that seats 232. Submit the request form on the restaurant's site or call 813.709.7776. Event pricing is set per person and excludes tax and gratuity.

### Does The Pearl Tampa have gluten-free and vegetarian options?

Some items on the menu are marked gf or v, and some can be made gluten-free or vegetarian on request. Tell your server about any allergies. The restaurant did not promise an allergen-free kitchen, so confirm specific dishes with your server before you order.

For the Heights food hall on North Ola (not the motor shop), see [Armature Works Tampa](/food-and-drink/armature-works-tampa).

## Final Thoughts

The Pearl Tampa is not the nightlife room the name suggests. It is a casual gastropub with a good oyster bar, a marble counter where you can watch the shucking, and a private dining room that is useful for groups. The details people get wrong are the ones I listed here: which meal you are walking into, what Oyster Hour actually discounts, when you need to call instead of booking online, and the difference between the Tampa restaurant and the Ohio rooms. Get those right and you will have an easy night. Sit at the counter, order the chowder and a dozen oysters, and let the person shucking do the show.

title: 5 Things to Know Before You Go to Topgolf Tampa
dek: Topgolf Tampa is at 10690 Palm River Road, not downtown or St. Petersburg. Here is how bays, hours, age rules and booking work before you go.

body:
# 5 Things to Know Before You Go to Topgolf Tampa

If you have been trying to plan a night out at topgolf tampa, the first thing to know is that you are not signing up for a round of golf on a course. You are renting a hitting bay by the hour, in a big bay-and-screen building east of downtown, and the details of how that works are where people get tripped up. The confusion usually starts with the spelling. ⛳ Below is what I would tell a friend before they booked, including the parts I could not pin down.

![Topgolf Tampa exterior on Palm River Road with the bay building lit up at dusk](/images/wm/articles/8735930.webp)
*Photo by [RDNE Stock project](https://www.pexels.com/@rdne) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/palm-trees-beside-a-building-8735930/)*

## Short on Time?

- Topgolf Tampa is at 10690 Palm River Road, Tampa, FL 33619. Phone (813) 298-1811. It is not the Topgolf in St. Petersburg.
- The company writes the name as one word, Topgolf. Spell it that way when you search or book.
- You pay per hour, per bay, not per person. A bay holds up to six players. Sales tax is extra.
- Walk-ins pay as they play, with a 30-minute minimum, and may have to wait on a list the day of. You can also reserve a bay up to two weeks ahead.
- Tampa hours: Monday through Thursday 10 a.m. to 11 p.m., Friday and Saturday 10 a.m. to 1 a.m., Sunday 10 a.m. to midnight.
- Under 16 needs a guest 21 or older supervising at all times. Under 18 needs the same after 9 p.m. You must be 18 or older to book.
- Check current bay rates with the venue before you go. I am not giving a number here because it changes.

## 1. Spell It One Word, and It Is Still the Same Building

The company spells the brand Topgolf, one word, capital T. That is how it shows up on the building, on the booking screens, and in the app. The Tampa venue is Topgolf Tampa. When you go to book, you will see [Book Topgolf Tampa](https://topgolf.com/us/tampa/), and you will be told to sign into your bay or order food and drinks with the Topgolf App.

People write it as two words, top golf, usually when they are thinking about the game rather than the company. Both spellings are trying to reach the same place. The one-word form is the one the company uses, so start there.

The spelling does not change the building. One word or two, if the address you are heading to is 10690 Palm River Road in 33619, you are going to the Tampa venue. Nothing about the name creates a second location.

![Topgolf Tampa sign and entrance showing the one-word Topgolf logo](/images/wm/articles/2763246.webp)
*Photo by [Prateek Katyal](https://www.pexels.com/@prateekkatyal) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/photo-of-open-signage-2763246/)*

## 2. Topgolf Tampa Is Not the St. Petersburg Venue: Check the Address

This is the mistake I would worry about most. The same logo and nearly the same amenities show up across the bay at Topgolf St. Petersburg, at 220 Carillon Pkwy N, St. Petersburg, FL 33716, phone (727) 870-4030. It is a sister venue, not the Tampa one. It has its own clock, its own street, and its own phone number.

I looked at the St. Petersburg listing specifically because the one-word brand name blurs the bay. It is the same kind of building, with three floors, more than 100 all-weather bays, Toptracer games, more than 200 HDTVs, a rooftop terrace, and a bar and restaurant. The hours are different, though. If you say "meet at Topgolf" and someone shows up on Carillon Parkway, you are going to have a bad night.

Tampa is not downtown and it is not a [Riverwalk](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa) bar. It sits out on Palm River Road in east Tampa. When you tell your group where to meet, use the full name and address: Topgolf Tampa, 10690 Palm River Road, Tampa, FL 33619. Say "Tampa" out loud so nobody ends up across the bay.

![Map-style view of the Palm River Road area in east Tampa where Topgolf Tampa sits](/images/wm/articles/34263960.webp)
*Photo by [Chris  The Island](https://www.pexels.com/@chris-the-island-3570397) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/aerial-view-of-florida-s-coastal-greenery-and-waterways-34263960/)*

## 3. Book a Bay, Not a Tee Time

Nothing at the Tampa venue is an eighteen-hole green fee. Topgolf prices per hour, per hitting bay, and the price is for the group, not per person. Each bay fits up to six players. Bays for seven or more may be limited, so if your group is bigger than six, plan on two bays and check ahead.

There are two ways in. The first is a walk-in. You walk in, book a tee time on the spot, and pay as you play. The minimum is 30 minutes. On a busy night you may have to join a waitlist, so don't assume you can wander in at 9 and start hitting right away. Walk-in rates can be higher than the prices quoted for booking ahead.

The second is a reserved bay. You book ahead, choose how long you want to play, and can book up to two weeks in advance. There is also an option to choose your location at booking. If the night matters, reserve. A reserved bay is the only way I would plan a birthday or a group dinner around a specific time.

Neither path includes food or drinks. Order those separately through the app or at the bar and restaurant. Sales tax is extra on top of the bay price, so the number on the screen is not always the number you pay. Keep your tickets or confirmation handy on your phone in case the front desk asks for them.

![Golfers in a Topgolf Tampa hitting bay with the screen and target area ahead](/images/wm/articles/8763237.webp)
*Photo by [Kevin  Malik](https://www.pexels.com/@kevin-malik) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/dart-on-bullseye-8763237/)*

## 4. Know the Tampa Hours and the Age Rules

I am giving you the Tampa hours, not the St. Petersburg ones. 🕒 Monday through Thursday, the venue runs 10 a.m. to 11 p.m. Friday and Saturday it runs 10 a.m. to 1 a.m. Sunday it runs 10 a.m. to midnight. These are the hours I have for Tampa, and businesses change hours without much notice, so confirm the day you go.

The age rules are the part that catches families. You must be 18 or older to book. Anyone under 16 must be supervised by a guest who is 21 or older at all times. Anyone under 18 must be supervised by a guest who is 21 or older after 9 p.m. Those rules are separate, and they are not the same as "whoever made the reservation." The person who books is not automatically the person who is allowed to stand with a 17-year-old after 9.

If you are bringing teenagers, decide before you arrive who the 21-plus supervisor is, and make sure that person is actually there for the whole visit. I would rather tell you this now than watch someone get turned around at the front desk.

![Friends laughing at a Topgolf Tampa bay with the lit screens behind them in the evening](/images/wm/articles/7915233.webp)
*Photo by [RDNE Stock project](https://www.pexels.com/@rdne) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/men-playing-computer-games-7915233/)*

## 5. Plan the Group: Fees, the Membership, and the Money Side

A night at Topgolf Tampa has a few parts that are easy to forget. There is sales tax on the bays, and there is a $6 one-time Topgolf Account activation fee for new players. If someone in your group has never activated an account, plan for that $6 on top of the bay price.

There is also a membership, Topgolf PlayMore, which I was told includes a free hour of play each month, a free appetizer every visit, and the option to bring up to five guests, for $20 per month. That was the offer when I asked, and I would recheck it before anyone signs up, the same way you would recheck bay rates. A membership price is not the same thing as what you will pay for a bay on a Saturday night, so do not mix the two when you budget.

I am not going to give you an hourly bay rate. The company explains how the pricing works, but the actual numbers change. Any hourly figure you see in a group text or a forum post is probably out of date. Pull up the booking screen for Topgolf Tampa the week you plan to go, and look at the price for the exact time and group size you have. 🎯

![Close-up of a Topgolf Tampa booking screen on a phone showing bay choices and pricing](/images/wm/articles/17610707.webp)
*Photo by [Görkem Cetinkaya](https://www.pexels.com/@gorkemraw) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/man-using-a-smartphone-to-record-a-film-17610707/)*

## Useful Things to Know

**Parking is a gap I cannot fill in.** I never got a lot price or a garage name for the Tampa venue, and I am not going to invent a validation deal. Plan to park on arrival and give yourself a few extra minutes. Since the building is not downtown, do not assume you will find street parking.

**Walk-ins are not guaranteed.** If the group is coming for a set time, reserve. Walk-in means pay as you play, a 30-minute minimum, and a possible waitlist.

**Bay size matters.** Six per bay is the limit. If you have seven or more people, you will likely need two bays. Book them together so the group does not get split up.

**Food and drinks are their own purchase.** Bay pricing does not include them. Use the app to order from your bay or at the bar.

**Sign in on the day.** The instructions are to sign into your bay or order food and drinks with the app. Download it before you leave the house so you are not hunting for signal in the parking lot.

**Staying nearby.** If you are coming from out of town, you may be looking at a hotel. I do not have a specific hotel recommendation for this area, so pick one based on your driving time to Palm River Road, not on the drive to downtown.

**Toptracer and scoring.** The bays use Toptracer to track each shot, and the balls score themselves on the outfield targets. Expect the scoring to be the main game, not a traditional round.

**Golf lessons exist.** The Tampa venue offers golf lessons. I do not have details on price or schedule, so ask the venue directly if you want one.

**Not a stadium, not a course.** People sometimes picture [a golf course](/events/tpc-tampa) or a sports stadium when they hear the name. [Altitude](/events/trampoline-park-tampa-hillsborough), the trampoline park on West Hillsborough, is a different booking. It is a building with bays, screens, and a bar, and the game is closer to a bowling alley than a round of golf.

## FAQ

### Is Topgolf Tampa the same place as Top Golf Tampa?

Yes, as far as I can tell. The company writes the brand as one word, Topgolf, and the Tampa venue is Topgolf Tampa at 10690 Palm River Road, Tampa, FL 33619. The two-word spelling is how a lot of people write it, but it does not point to a different building in Tampa.

### Is Topgolf in St. Petersburg the same as Topgolf Tampa?

No. Topgolf St. Petersburg is a separate venue at 220 Carillon Pkwy N, St. Petersburg, FL 33716, with its own phone number and its own hours. It has a similar building and similar features, so check the address before you go.

### What is the phone number for Topgolf Tampa?

The Tampa venue's phone number is (813) 298-1811. Call if you have a question about your reservation, the group size, or the age rules before you show up.

### What hours does Topgolf Tampa keep?

For Tampa, the hours are Monday through Thursday 10 a.m. to 11 p.m., Friday and Saturday 10 a.m. to 1 a.m., and Sunday 10 a.m. to midnight. Hours change, so confirm the day you visit.

### Do I need to be 21 to go to Topgolf Tampa?

No. You must be 18 or older to book. Anyone under 16 has to be supervised by a guest 21 or older at all times, and anyone under 18 has to be supervised by a guest 21 or older after 9 p.m.

### How much does it cost to play at Topgolf Tampa?

Pricing is per hour, per bay, and the bay fits up to six players. Sales tax is extra, and a $6 one-time activation fee applies to new players. I am not giving an hourly rate because the numbers change, so check the booking screen for the time and group size you plan to use.

### Can I walk in at Topgolf Tampa, or do I need a reservation?

You can walk in. You book a tee time on the spot and pay as you play, with a 30-minute minimum. On busy nights you may have to join a waitlist. A reserved bay lets you book up to two weeks ahead and choose how long you play, so reserve if the time matters.

### Does the Tampa venue offer a membership?

It offers Topgolf PlayMore, which I was told includes a free hour of play each month, a free appetizer every visit, and the option to bring up to five guests, for $20 per month. That was the offer when I asked, so recheck it before you subscribe.

## Final Thoughts

If you remember one thing, make it the address. Topgolf Tampa is at 10690 Palm River Road, and the one-word spelling does not change that. Say Tampa when you tell your group where to meet, because the same brand and nearly the same building exist across the bay in St. Petersburg.

Book a reserved bay if the night matters. Walk in only if you are flexible and do not mind a possible wait. Count six players per bay, plan for tax, and remember the $6 fee if someone is new. Get the 21-plus supervisor sorted before you arrive if you are bringing anyone under 18.

Check the hours and the price the week you go. That is the part I cannot promise will stay the same, and it is the part that matters most when you are standing at the counter. Have a good time out there. 🏌️

body:
# TBPAC Tampa: What the Straz Center Is and How to Visit

If you search for TBPAC Tampa, you are looking for the performing arts building on the river in [downtown Tampa](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa). I still say TBPAC myself, and so do a lot of people who have lived here a while. 🎭 The letters stand for Tampa Bay Performing Arts Center. Today the same campus is best known as the [Straz Center](https://www.strazcenter.org/). Same organization, same doors, and a few different names on the signs, paperwork, and ticket confirmations. This guide covers what those names mean, how to buy tickets without getting burned, and how to park so you are not circling Fortune Street right before curtain.

![Straz Center for the Performing Arts on the Tampa riverfront in downtown Tampa](/images/wm/articles/9422516.webp)
*Photo by [Chris Kim  Creatives](https://www.pexels.com/@chris-kim-creatives-88108966) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/saint-pete-pier-in-tampa-bay-9422516/)*

## Short on Time?

- **TBPAC is the Straz Center.** The legal corporation is still Tampa Bay Performing Arts Center, Inc. It has done business as the David A. Straz, Jr. Center for the Performing Arts since November 11, 2009.
- **Buy tickets from the Straz ticket office, not a reseller.** The center says it will not honor tickets bought from unauthorized sellers, and resale at a premium is prohibited.
- **Ticket office hours are Tuesday through Sunday, noon to 7 p.m.,** and it is also staffed 90 minutes before performances. The phone number is 813-229-STAR.
- **Do not type the building's street address into your map app.** Use a garage on Fortune Street or Ashley Drive instead. The Arrival Plaza on Tyler Street is limited and is not the general event lot.
- **Everyone needs a ticket, including small children.** Broadway shows are not toddler friendly, and the rules change show to show, so ask before you go.
- **Gift cards are narrower than they look.** They do not work at the bars, Canopy Bistro, concessions, or SteamHeat Cafe.

## 1. Why TBPAC Tampa and Straz Mean the Same Place

The first time I looked into this, the building seemed to have two names, and it was not obvious which one was current. The short answer is that both are current, depending on what you are looking at.

The legal entity is Tampa Bay Performing Arts Center, Inc. Its audited financial statements say it was formed on September 15, 1980, to manage and operate the performing arts facility under a lease with the City of Tampa. The stated purpose is to enhance the quality of life in the Tampa Bay region by educating and developing audiences through the performing arts, with an emphasis on diversity and quality. That is a mission statement, but it also tells you this is a nonprofit running a city-owned building, not a private theater company.

The lease is part of why the place can feel civic and private at the same time. The organization leases the operating facility from the City of Tampa for 100 dollars a year, for 99 years unless it ends sooner, and the lease renews. The audited statements put the city's insured value of the operating and education facility at about 150 million dollars, not counting contents, and they say the below-market lease is not something they could readily price. I am not going to turn that into an argument about public money. What it means for you as a visitor is simpler: ticket fees and operating money stay with the center to run and restore the building, rather than going to an outside commercial box office.

The name change came in November 2009. A large endowment went to the Tampa Bay Performing Arts Center Foundation, Inc., which the center established on April 28, 1997. In recognition of that donor, the building began doing business as the David A. Straz, Jr. Center for the Performing Arts effective November 11, 2009. The endowment went to the foundation, not to a second theater, and the initials did not move anywhere. So when the awning says Straz, the ticket confirmation says Straz Center, and an older friend still says TBPAC, they all point at the same doors on the river.

The timeline helps too. The doors first opened to the public in 1987. The center credits Mayor Bob Martinez with the project, and it notes that Mayor Nick Nuccio had floated a downtown music hall back in 1965 that never broke ground. The first touring Broadway show on the main stage was *Cats*. The main hall that was under construction in the early photos was called Festival Hall, and it is now Carol Morsani Hall. If you read old articles or tax letters, expect to see all of these names in the same paragraph.

![Straz Center main entrance and signage on the Tampa riverfront](/images/wm/articles/14536803.webp)
*Photo by [Connor Scott McManus](https://www.pexels.com/@connorscottmcmanus) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/a-signage-of-a-theatre-14536803/)*

## 2. Buy Tickets From the Straz Ticket Office

This is the part where the initials stop being useful. If you want 🎟️ tickets, go to the Straz Center ticket office, or buy through the center's official channels.

The ticket office is open Tuesday through Sunday, noon to 7 p.m. It is also staffed 90 minutes before performances. The phone number is 813-229-STAR, which is the same line as 813-229-7827 if you prefer digits. By mail, the address is Straz Center Ticket Office, 1010 N. WC MacInnes Place, Tampa, Florida [33602](/guides/tampa-zip-code). Fax orders go to 813-222-1080. Visa, MasterCard, and Discover are accepted, and cash and checks are accepted too. Checks need a driver's license number and the issuing state written on them. A check that bounces picks up a 25 dollar fee from the center, so do not write one unless the money is there.

Will Call wants a photo ID from the purchaser, so bring the ID of the person who bought the tickets. Parking is free at the Arrival Plaza while you are buying tickets, which helps if you are doing it in person.

The thing to avoid is the resale market. The center says it is not responsible for tickets from unauthorized sellers, and those tickets will not be honored. Resale at a premium is prohibited. If a link looks official but you did not get it from the center, do not buy from it. Call the office and confirm.

![Straz Center ticket office and Arrival Plaza on Tyler Street in downtown Tampa](/images/wm/articles/32639915.webp)
*Photo by [Kendra Hill](https://www.pexels.com/@kendra-hill-762373489) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/neon-broadway-tickets-sign-in-nyc-at-night-32639915/)*

## 3. Know the Ticket Rules Before You Show Up

The rules are the part people most often trip over, and the center is blunt about them. Read them before you put the date on the calendar.

Every guest needs a ticket, at any age. That includes babies and toddlers. The center strongly recommends that children under 5 skip anything that is not Kid Time, Wee Folk, or marked toddler friendly. Broadway shows are not toddler friendly, and the center says so directly. Some toddler shows offer lap tickets for a child under 18 months, but the policy changes by show, so ask before you assume your toddler can sit on your lap for a long musical.

Dates, performers, and prices can change. Late seating is at management's discretion, which means if you arrive during the second act, the staff may hold you in the back until a break. Sales are final. There are no refunds or exchanges, and lost tickets are not replaced. Those rules apply whether you are buying for a Tuesday matinee or a big weekend show.

Fees are the other surprise. A standard handling fee of 17.5 percent stays with the center, and the center says that percentage can move. Phone and web orders also carry a per-order fee. I did not check a face-value price for any particular show, so I am not going to quote one here. Look at the total on the checkout screen before you commit.

If your plans fall through, there is an option. Operation Tickets takes donations if you give notice at least five business days before the show, and the center says you get a receipt for the value. It goes through the same ticket office, so call them rather than hoping someone at the door will take your seats.

![Patrons arriving for a show in the lobby of the Straz Center, Tampa](/images/wm/articles/39342503.webp)
*Photo by [Rian Setiawan](https://www.pexels.com/@riansetiawan) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/silhouetted-figures-in-a-modern-airport-terminal-39342503/)*

## 4. Gift Cards Work Differently Than You Expect

Gift cards are a smaller trap. Electronic gift cards are delivered electronically. Physical ones are not mailed. You pick them up at Will Call, either at the ticket office or by calling 813-229-7827 to arrange it.

Gift cards can be used for tickets, merchandise, conservatory classes, and at Maestro's restaurant. They are not valid at the bars, at Canopy Bistro, at concessions, or at SteamHeat Cafe. Do not hand someone a gift card and tell them it works at intermission, because it does not, at least not for drinks or snacks. If you are buying one for a theater person, say exactly where it works so they are not surprised at the bar.

![Maestro's restaurant and dining area at the Straz Center, Tampa](/images/wm/articles/15063328.webp)
*Photo by [Connor Scott McManus](https://www.pexels.com/@connorscottmcmanus) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/restaurant-in-shopping-mall-15063328/)*

## 5. Parking Is the Practical Half of a TBPAC Visit

The address 1010 N. WC MacInnes Place is a poor single map pin. If you drive straight to it, you will end up in the wrong part of the campus. The center's advice is to put a garage address into your navigation rather than the center's address, unless you are using valet.

Drop-off depends on which hall you are visiting. For the Patel Conservatory, use Fortune Street. For Morsani Hall, use Fortune Street or the Arrival Plaza. For Ferguson Hall, use the Arrival Plaza. For the Jaeb Theater or the Shimberg Playhouse, use the corner of MacInnes Place and Tyler Street. The Arrival Plaza is on Tyler Street, and it is limited. It is for buying tickets, meetings, valet when it is available, pickups, and disabled parking. It is not the general event lot, so do not plan to park there for a show.

Valet runs through Metropolis. It costs 40 dollars a vehicle including ADA, plus a 5 percent service fee, and it takes credit cards only. When full valet is not running, event self-parking at the Arrival Plaza is 30 dollars including ADA. These are the center's figures, and they can change, so check before you go.

For the garages to save before a show, these are the ones the center has counted:

- **Anchor Garage, 109 W. Fortune Street.** The center has secured 319 spaces there, on weeknights after 6 p.m. and all weekend.
- **Ashley Plaza Garage, 110 W. Fortune Street.** The center still calls this the former Tampa Bay Times garage. It has 200 spaces on the same pattern.
- **Royal Regional, 1200 N. Tampa Street.** It is about a six-minute walk. The center wants weekday arrivals after 6 p.m.
- **Poe Garage, 800 N. Ashley Drive.** You pay by license plate before the show.
- **Fort Brooke, on Franklin.** It is about a 15-minute walk.
- **The Barrymore, 111 W. Fortune Street.** The lot opens for many big nights if you call ahead.

Rates move with whatever else is happening downtown, so treat them as a starting point. If you are being dropped off by rideshare, the pickup belongs on the north side along Fortune Street. Pirate Water Taxi stop 14 is in front of the building, 🌊 which is a good option if you are coming in from the water. A disabled permit can use a meter for up to four hours without paying.

![Anchor Garage on West Fortune Street near the Straz Center, Tampa](/images/wm/articles/20073072.webp)
*Photo by [Stephen Leonardi](https://www.pexels.com/@stephen-leonardi-587681991) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/buildings-in-sacramento-city-in-usa-20073072/)*

## Useful Things to Know

**Give yourself time at Will Call.** The ticket office is open until 7 p.m. on its open days, and it is staffed 90 minutes before a performance. Bring the buyer's photo ID.

**Save the garage address, not the building.** This is the most useful single tip. A plan for parking makes the rest of the night easier, especially on a busy downtown evening. [Tampa Theatre](/things-to-do/tampa-theatre), on Franklin Street, is a different room and a different ticket.

**Ask about children before you buy.** The under-5 guidance is clear, but the lap ticket policy depends on the show. Call the ticket office and ask about the specific production.

**Stick to official channels.** Use the Straz ticket office, the phone line, or the center's official site. The no-refund policy means a bad purchase is hard to undo.

**Compare totals, not ticket prices.** The handling fee and per-order fee add up. The total on the checkout screen is what matters.

**Check the season before you plan around it.** When I looked, the current season listed *The Sound of Music*, *Buena Vista Social Club*, *Black Violin*, *Misery*, *After Dark*, and *Hamilton*. There was also a 26/27 Bank of America Broadway season you build yourself by calling 813-229-7827, Patel Conservatory classes, and Opera Tampa's 2027 season of three Italian works. Seasons change, so check the current listings before you commit.

**Premium options are separate products.** A premium lounge add-on exists for select shows in Morsani Hall. Luxury boxes are six-seat mezzanine boxes in Carol Morsani Hall, offered in an 8- or 12-show package, and they go through the development office by email. They are not the same as a regular ticket, and they do not combine into one price.

## FAQ

### Is TBPAC Tampa the same as the Straz Center?

Yes. TBPAC is the old name for Tampa Bay Performing Arts Center, which is still the legal corporation. The building has done business as the David A. Straz, Jr. Center for the Performing Arts since November 11, 2009. The ticket office, the signs, and most current materials use Straz Center.

### When is the Straz Center ticket office open?

The ticket office is open Tuesday through Sunday, noon to 7 p.m. It is also staffed 90 minutes before performances. Hours can change, so check before you go.

### What is the phone number for Straz Center tickets?

The number is 813-229-STAR, which is the same as 813-229-7827. Use it for ticket questions, gift card pickup, and the 26/27 Broadway season.

### Can I buy tickets from a reseller for a Straz Center show?

You should not. The center says it is not responsible for tickets from unauthorized sellers, and those tickets will not be honored. Resale at a premium is prohibited. Buy from the ticket office or the center's official channels.

### Do toddlers need a ticket to attend a show at the Straz Center?

Yes. Every guest needs a ticket at any age. The center strongly recommends that children under 5 skip anything that is not Kid Time, Wee Folk, or marked toddler friendly. Some toddler shows offer lap tickets for children under 18 months, but the policy varies by show, so ask first.

### Where should I park for a show at the Straz Center?

Put a garage address into your map app, not 1010 N. WC MacInnes Place. Anchor Garage at 109 W. Fortune Street and Ashley Plaza Garage at 110 W. Fortune Street are the largest options the center has counted, on weeknights after 6 and on weekends. The Arrival Plaza on Tyler Street is limited and is not the general event lot.

### Can I use a Straz Center gift card at the bars or concessions?

No. Gift cards can be used for tickets, merchandise, conservatory classes, and Maestro's restaurant. They are not valid at the bars, Canopy Bistro, concessions, or SteamHeat Cafe.

### What happens if I cannot attend a show?

Sales are final, and there are no refunds or exchanges. If you want to donate your tickets, Operation Tickets takes donations when you contact the ticket office at least five business days before the show. The center says you receive a receipt for the value.

## Final Thoughts

I still say TBPAC, and I probably always will. The initials are older than the Straz name, and they are how a lot of people in this city learned the building. But when it comes time to buy tickets or drive down to the river, the initials do not help much. Use the Straz ticket office, buy from the center and not a reseller, read the rules before you bring a toddler, and put a garage on Fortune or Ashley into your map instead of the MacInnes Place address. If something goes sideways, the number is still 813-229-STAR.

title: What Time Zone Is Tampa Florida? 5 Things to Know About Eastern Time
dek: Tampa is on Eastern Time, EDT or EST depending on the season. Here's what the letters mean, the 2026 change dates, and why LA is three hours behind.
