body:
# What Time Zone Is Tampa Florida? 5 Things to Know About Eastern Time

People ask me what time zone is Tampa Florida in more than you would expect. Visitors ask it when they are setting up a call with the office back home. Friends ask when they are trying to figure out if the game starts before or after dinner. The short answer is [Eastern Time](https://www.time.gov/). The longer answer is that the letters attached to Eastern Time change twice a year, and most people, including me for a while, get one of them wrong.

![Downtown Tampa skyline across Hillsborough Bay at dusk](/images/wm/articles/17518170.webp)
*Photo by [John Ray Ebora](https://www.pexels.com/@juansinag) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/cityscape-of-manila-at-dusk-17518170/)*

## Short on Time?

🕐 The Tampa time zone is Eastern. Tampa is on the same zone as New York, Miami, and Atlanta. From the spring change to the fall change it is EDT, which is UTC minus 4. The rest of the year it is EST, UTC minus 5. Clocks are on EDT from the second Sunday in March until the first Sunday in November, then EST. If you only remember one thing, remember that the zone is Eastern, and that the "D" or "S" in the middle depends on the month.

## 1. What Time Zone Is Tampa Florida On? Eastern, Across the USA

Tampa is not on a special zone of its own. It sits on the Eastern row, the same one that covers most of Florida's east coast, the eastern seaboard, and a large part of the eastern USA. When you look at a US time zone map, the Eastern band runs down the right-hand side of the Appalachians and then drops into Florida. Tampa is in that band, along with the rest of the state, with a few exceptions I will get to later.

The name people use in everyday life is "Eastern time," and that is the right name. In the shorthand of the US, the abbreviation is ET. That tells you the zone. It does not tell you whether the clock is on standard time or daylight time, and that second part is where most of the confusion starts.

I think about it this way. Eastern is the family name. EST and EDT are the two children, one for winter and one for summer. You will hear both used for the same city in the same year, and both are correct at different times. The city does not change zones when the season changes. It changes its offset from UTC, which is the part the letters describe.

![Hillsborough River near downtown Tampa in late afternoon light](/images/wm/articles/28456051.webp)
*Photo by [Nothing Ahead](https://www.pexels.com/@ian-panelo) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/golden-sunlight-reflecting-on-rippling-water-28456051/)*

## 2. EDT or EST: Which Letters Apply to Tampa Florida Time Zone

Here is the part I got wrong for years. I would say "EST" for Tampa in any month, because it felt like the proper name of the zone. It is not. EST is the standard-time version, and it only applies for part of the year. The tampa florida time zone label changes with the calendar, even though the place does not.

- **EDT, Eastern Daylight Time**, is UTC minus 4. Tampa uses it from the spring change to the fall change.
- **EST, Eastern Standard Time**, is UTC minus 5. Tampa uses it from the fall change until the next spring change.
- **ET** is the year-round shorthand that just means "Eastern local time, whichever one is in force."

If you say EST in a month when Tampa is on EDT, you are off by an hour and sounding sure of yourself. I did this for years, and it caused more than one muddled conversation about whether a meeting was early or late. The label was wrong, not the clock.

For a sign, a schedule, or a meeting invite that has to stay accurate for months, ET is the safest choice. If you need precision for a specific date, use the actual letter for that date. Your phone will usually show the right one on its own.

![Close-up of a clock face on a wall inside a Tampa office building](/images/wm/articles/8102182.webp)
*Photo by [Nothing Ahead](https://www.pexels.com/@ian-panelo) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/close-up-photo-of-clock-in-black-and-white-8102182/)*

## 3. The Clock Changes Every Year, and the Dates Move

Tampa follows the daylight saving rules the rest of the country uses. Clocks spring forward one hour in March and fall back one hour in November. The rule is that the change happens on a Sunday, at 2:00 a.m. local time. The spring change is the second Sunday in March. The fall change is the first Sunday in November.

Here is where I would have made mistakes if I had memorized one Sunday and assumed it repeated. The dates shift from year to year because the rule is about which Sunday, not a fixed day of the month. Here are the ones I have written down for Tampa:

- **2025:** March 9 (spring forward) and November 2 (fall back)
- **2026:** March 8 (spring forward) and November 1 (fall back)
- **2027:** March 14 (spring forward) and November 7 (fall back)
- **2028:** March 12 (spring forward) and November 5 (fall back)
- **2029:** March 11 (spring forward) and November 4 (fall back)

All of those times are Tampa local time. The 2:00 a.m. is the stable part. The date is not. In 2026, the fall change is November 1, which is why the current month is still on daylight time.

Many phones and computers make the switch by themselves once you have the right location set. That is convenient, but it also means nobody thinks about it until something is off by an hour. If you have a device that does not update on its own, like an older car display or a wall clock, check it around these dates.

![Tampa street sign with a Sunday calendar page in the background](/images/wm/articles/29509482.webp)
*Photo by [Matheus Bertelli](https://www.pexels.com/@bertellifotografia) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/minimalist-february-calendar-close-up-29509482/)*

## 4. Why the Los Angeles Gap Is Three Hours

People often ask how far Tampa is from Los Angeles on the clock. The answer is three hours. Tampa is three hours ahead of Los Angeles. I checked this on a Saturday evening in early October, and the gap was the same as I expected: Tampa on EDT, Los Angeles on Pacific Time, three hours between them.

I wanted to know whether that gap was a quirk of the summer months. It is not. Eastern daylight is UTC minus 4, and Pacific daylight is UTC minus 7. Eastern standard is UTC minus 5, and Pacific standard is UTC minus 8. Both pairs differ by three hours. The two zones switch on the same weekends, so the gap stays put through the whole year.

That means a call to Los Angeles is three hours behind Tampa in any season, as long as both cities are on the usual US schedule. It is a practical rule to use when you are scheduling. Write the time in Tampa's zone first, then convert, and double-check the date if your call falls near a change weekend.

![Palm trees and a sunset over the Gulf of Mexico at Ben Davis Park in Tampa](/images/wm/articles/10490828.webp)
*Photo by [John Hank](https://www.pexels.com/@john-hank-148551387) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/sunset-on-sea-10490828/)*

## 5. Central Time and Other Mix-Ups

The first mix-up is central time. The Gulf of Mexico sounds like it should put a city in the central zone, because a lot of the Gulf coast further west is on central time. Tampa is not. It is on the Eastern row, daylight or standard depending on the date. If your trip includes a stop in another part of the Gulf region, check that place separately. A drive to [Naples](/guides/tampa-to-naples) is one of those trips. I would not assume it shares Tampa's clock.

The second mix-up is the [zip code](/guides/tampa-zip-code). Tampa has many zip codes, and people sometimes assume a zip code tells you the time zone. In practice, time zone lines in the US tend to follow [county lines](/guides/zip-code-hillsborough-tampa-fl), so a zip code can be used as an approximation in a lookup tool. That does not make a zip code a time zone. It is not the name of the zone, and it is not a reliable way to answer the question on its own. For Tampa, the zone name is Eastern.

The third mix-up is assuming other countries use the same dates. They do not. Each country sets its own daylight rules, and some do not use daylight time at all. In the Southern Hemisphere, where daylight time is used, the change often falls at the opposite time of year. If you are coordinating with someone overseas, do not rely on your own calendar for their clock. Use the dates for their location.

🌊 One more thing about this area: the Gulf is a big part of why people visiting Tampa think about the clock differently from the way they think about the beach. The water doesn't change zones, but the sunset time shifts with the season, so plan your evening around the local clock, not the map.

![Tampa International Airport arrivals sign showing local departure times](/images/wm/articles/36406012.webp)
*Photo by [Holiday Extras](https://www.pexels.com/@holiday-extras-2159945971) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/woman-speaking-on-phone-at-gatwick-airport-36406012/)*

## Useful Things to Know

**The current zone.** As I write this, Tampa is on EDT, UTC minus 4. That will hold until Sunday, November 1, 2026, at 2:00 a.m. local time.

**The name to use.** If you are writing a schedule, use ET or the explicit EDT or EST for the date in question. Avoid writing EST in summer, and avoid writing EDT in winter.

⏰ **The one-hour trap.** Most time errors in this city happen on the weekends around the two changes, especially for anything set up weeks ago. If a meeting was booked before the November change and you are confirming now, check the date on the invite against the change dates above.

**Devices and clocks.** Phones usually update automatically. Some older appliances, car clocks, and wall clocks do not. Check them the weekend of each change.

**Shorthand people use.** If you search for the time zone in Tampa FL, you will see the same answer: Eastern. Some people say "Florida time" as a shorthand. That is fine in casual talk, but it does not carry the season-specific letter that matters for scheduling.

**Phone numbers.** A phone number does not reliably tell you where someone is. People move, and cell numbers travel. If you are calling someone in Tampa, ask them rather than trusting the number to tell you the clock.

## FAQ

### What time zone is Tampa Florida in?

Tampa is in the Eastern time zone. It uses EDT, UTC minus 4, from the spring change to the fall change, and EST, UTC minus 5, the rest of the year. The abbreviation ET covers both.

### Is Tampa on EST or EDT right now?

It depends on the date. As of early October 2026, Tampa is on EDT. It will switch to EST at 2:00 a.m. on Sunday, November 1, 2026.

### Does Tampa observe daylight saving time?

Yes. Tampa springs forward one hour in March and falls back one hour in November, on the same schedule as most of the US.

### Is Tampa in the same time zone as Miami?

Yes. Tampa and Miami are both on Eastern time, and both switch between EDT and EST on the same dates.

### What is the time difference between Tampa and Los Angeles?

Tampa is three hours ahead of Los Angeles. That gap holds in both summer and winter, because both cities switch between daylight and standard time on the same schedule.

### Is the time zone in Tampa central?

No. The time zone in Tampa is Eastern. Some places along the Gulf coast further west are on central time, but Tampa is not one of them.

### Does a zip code tell you the time zone?

Not on its own. Time zone lines in the US usually follow county lines, so a zip code can help an approximate lookup. For Tampa, the zone is Eastern, and that is the answer to give.

### How do I know which letter to use for Tampa?

Check the date. Use EDT between the spring and fall changes, and EST the rest of the year. If you are unsure, ET is the safest abbreviation because it covers both.

## Final Thoughts

Tampa is on Eastern Time, and that is the answer to what time zone Tampa Florida is in. The letters on the end depend on the month. Right now it is EDT, and it will be EST after November 1, 2026. If you are scheduling something important, check the date, not just the zone name. The one-hour mistakes I see most often come from memorizing a single letter and forgetting that the calendar moves.

If you are visiting, enjoy the water and the sunsets, and do not let the clock trip you up. The [things to do in Tampa](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa) do not change the clock, but show times and kitchen hours depend on it. Set your phone to the local setting, double-check anything booked near the change weekends, and when in doubt, ask a local.

title: Zip Code Hillsborough Tampa FL: 5 Things I Learned Before Filling Out a Form

metaTitle: Zip Code Hillsborough Tampa FL: Why There's No Single Answer
metaDescription: I wanted one zip code for Hillsborough and Tampa. There isn't one. Here are the 27 Tampa-default codes, what 33602 really is, and how to fill out a form.

body:
# Zip Code Hillsborough Tampa FL: 5 Things I Learned Before Filling Out a Form

📮 I wanted one number, so I asked for the [zip code](https://tools.usps.com/zip-code-lookup.htm) hillsborough tampa fl and expected one answer to come back. Hillsborough County and Tampa are the two names I type into every form, and I figured there had to be one code that covered both. I did it on purpose, because I wanted to see what I would get if I asked the question the lazy way. There is not one zip code for Hillsborough, and there is not one for Tampa. There are a lot of them. Below is what I found, the codes I actually pulled, and what I would write on a form now.

![Hillsborough County ZIP code map showing many colored delivery areas across Tampa and the county](/images/wm/articles/33998346.webp)
*Photo by [Tahir Xəlfəquliyev](https://www.pexels.com/@tahir) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/yellow-markers-on-map-indicating-location-tracking-33998346/)*

## Short on Time?

- Hillsborough County does not have one zip code. Neither does Tampa. Both are covered by many codes, and a lot of those codes cross into the names of other places.
- ZIP codes are mail delivery areas built around post offices and carrier routes. They do not follow city lines, so the city name on an envelope is not a jurisdiction.
- On the county's ZIP map I pulled, 27 codes list Tampa as the default city. All of them start with 336.
- 33602 is the number people grab, but it is City Hall's address. Tampa beaches and parks sit under other 336 codes.
- Some codes carry acceptable alternate names like Ybor City, Temple Terrace, or Carrollwood. Some codes also carry default cities like Plant City, Brandon, and Riverview.
- For a form, you need three things: the county (Hillsborough), the city your address actually uses, and the five-digit ZIP for that exact delivery area. Look up your own address rather than trusting a single number.

## 1. Zip code Hillsborough Tampa FL is three different questions

I had been treating "county," "city," and "ZIP" as if they meant the same thing. They do not, and that is the whole reason this search feels like it should have one answer.

Hillsborough is the county. Tampa is a city inside it. The ZIP is a third thing. It is a delivery area in the USA mail system, and the Postal Service uses it to sort mail. Think of it as a delivery zone, not a city limit. The first three digits point to a large sectional center or city area, the next two narrow it to a post office or delivery area, and the last digits (after the hyphen, if you have the plus four) break it down into smaller blocks and sides of a street. That is a sorting system. It was never meant to draw city limits.

The Postal Service says plainly that ZIP Codes do not necessarily follow city or municipal boundaries. They follow the post offices, delivery units, and carrier routes that actually move the mail. The city name on an address is usually the city where the delivery unit sits, not necessarily where the house sits. When those two differ, there can be an acceptable alternate city name for that delivery area. And when a street, a city, and a ZIP disagree, the mail gets dispatched on the ZIP first.

The Census Bureau makes the same distinction from the other side. It uses the Postal Service to deliver a lot of census mail, but it does not decide which jurisdiction a house is in by looking at the mailing city or the ZIP. It uses where the house physically sits. Census people know the post office city for a ZIP can differ from the legal municipality, and that the name the Postal Service prefers may not be the name residents actually use.

So a form that asks for "city" and a form that asks for "jurisdiction" are not asking the same question. If you live in unincorporated Hillsborough and your mail says Tampa, your mailing city and your legal location are two different things. Neither one is wrong. They answer different questions.

![Tampa city limits and surrounding unincorporated Hillsborough County neighborhoods on a map](/images/wm/articles/37845138.webp)
*Photo by [umar muazu](https://www.pexels.com/@umar-muazu-2147562146) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/expansive-urban-skyline-with-residential-areas-37845138/)*

## 2. The 27 codes on the county map that list Tampa as the default city

I went through the county's ZIP code map entry by entry without drawing any shapes. It held 73 entries and 72 different codes. The repeated one was 33598, and both copies list Wimauma as the default city, so I am not counting it twice and I am not giving it a second meaning.

The part that mattered was the default city. Twenty-seven codes on that map list Tampa as the default, and every one of them is in the 336 range. Here is the full set I pulled, not one I remembered:

33602, 33603, 33604, 33605, 33606, 33607, 33609, 33610, 33611, 33612, 33613, 33614, 33615, 33616, 33617, 33618, 33619, 33620, 33621, 33624, 33625, 33626, 33629, 33634, 33635, 33637, 33647.

If someone gives you a single "Tampa zip" that is not in that list, I would not trust it. If someone gives you one number from that list and calls it *the* Tampa zip, I would not trust that either. Twenty-seven is not one. It is the number of delivery areas on that map that use Tampa as their default mailing name, and that set can change as the Postal Service adjusts its boundaries. 33614 is one of those city codes, not a county code. West Hillsborough Avenue runs through it, which is why the [trampoline park](/events/trampoline-park-tampa-hillsborough) in Drew Park is not a Hillsborough County address.

The codes also show that Tampa is not one clean block. Some codes that say Tampa cover parts of Tampa, and some have Tampa as a mailing label on shapes that reach past the city line. A map that looks tidy from a distance gets messy as soon as you zoom in to a specific street.

![Close-up of a Tampa street map with several ZIP code boundaries overlapping neighborhoods](/images/wm/articles/13637878.webp)
*Photo by [Arturo A](https://www.pexels.com/@arturoaez225) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/map-on-a-book-13637878/)*

## 3. Why 33602 is not the answer, even though it is the one everyone grabs

I know why 33602 is the number people reach for. It shows up on City of Tampa contact information. [City Hall](https://www.tampa.gov/)'s address is 306 East Jackson Street, Tampa, Florida 33602. It is a real address and a real building, and if you need to mail something to Tampa's city government, that is the right code.

🏛️ But it is a building, not a whole city and not a whole county. I tried to treat it as the Tampa code for a whole trip, and it fell apart as soon as I looked at the addresses the city gives for its own beaches and parks. Ben T. Davis Beach and Cypress Point Park are both 33607. The Davis Islands seaplane basin is 33606. Picnic Island Park is 33616. That is one city and four different codes, and none of them is the county code.

I am not going to turn those into a theory about neighborhoods beyond what the addresses say. The point is simpler. The city itself already refuses the single-number story. If the places the city runs are spread across several codes, a house in Tampa can easily be on a different one.

So if you are mailing something to City Hall, use 33602. If you are filling out a form for your own house, use the code for your house. The shorter list of [Tampa zip codes](/guides/tampa-zip-code) is the city-only version of this question. [Hillsborough County](https://hcfl.gov/) is the government behind the county name on the form.

![Tampa City Hall building in downtown Tampa on East Jackson Street](/images/wm/articles/17073729.webp)
*Photo by [Brandon Ricketts](https://www.pexels.com/@brandon-ricketts-450464466) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/residential-skyscraper-behind-buildings-wall-17073729/)*

## 4. The names attached to codes: acceptable alternates and default cities

This is the part I wish someone had explained to me years ago. Each ZIP entry on the county map carries a default city, and sometimes it also carries other names. Some of those names are marked acceptable. Some are marked not acceptable. Those labels are the Postal Service's way of saying what it will recognize as a valid city on an address. On 33605, the acceptable name is [Ybor City](/guides/ybor-city-tampa-fl-33605).

Here are a few I pulled. I am not going to explain each one, because the labels are the useful part:

- 33605 lists Ybor City as an acceptable name, with Tampa as the default.
- 33606 lists Davis Island as acceptable, and University of Tampa marked not acceptable.
- 33615 lists Town N Country as acceptable.
- 33617 and 33637 list Temple Terrace as acceptable, with Tampa still the default.
- 33618 and 33625 list Carrollwood as acceptable.
- 33620 lists University of South Florida as acceptable, and a shortened "Univ of So Florida" as not acceptable.
- 33624 lists Northdale as acceptable. 33626 lists Northdale/Westchase.
- 33629 lists Palma Ceia as acceptable. 33647 lists Tampa Palms as acceptable.

On the not-acceptable side I also found Seminole Heights on 33603, Sulphur Springs and Twin Lake on 33604, Palma Ceia on 33609 (acceptable on 33629, not on 33609), East Lake on 33610, Forest Hills on 33612, Palm River and Progress Village on 33619, and MacDill AFB on 33621.

The lesson is that a neighborhood name and a mailing name can disagree. Some names are fine as alternates. Some names people like to write on forms are not acceptable for that code. If you write a neighborhood name that the Postal Service does not accept on your delivery area, the mail may still arrive, but the address can get messy.

![Ybor City street sign with historic brick buildings in Tampa](/images/wm/articles/14536799.webp)
*Photo by [Connor Scott McManus](https://www.pexels.com/@connorscottmcmanus) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/coca-cola-wall-painting-on-brick-wall-14536799/)*

## 5. The county map is full of codes whose default city is not Tampa

🧭 Here is where the single-number idea really breaks down. The same county ZIP map has many codes whose default city is somewhere other than Tampa.

Plant City is the default on 33563, 33565, 33566, and 33567. Brandon is the default on 33510 and 33511. Riverview is the default on 33569, 33578, and 33579. [Lutz](/events/tpc-tampa) is the default on 33548, 33549, 33558, and 33559. I also found default cities of Dover, Gibsonton, Lithia, Odessa, Ruskin, Apollo Beach, Sun City Center, Seffner, Thonotosassa, Valrico, Wimauma, and Zephyrhills, among others.

Those are mailing labels on delivery areas the county keeps on its map. I am not declaring each of those places a city. I am saying the county ZIP map is not a list of Tampa codes with some extras. It is a map of delivery areas, and the mail names on those areas go well beyond the city of Tampa.

The map also includes shapes whose default city is outside the county altogether, such as Saint Petersburg, Clearwater, Lakeland, Wesley Chapel, Palm Harbor, Oldsmar, Tarpon Springs, New Port Richey, Land O Lakes, Palmetto, and Parrish. I am not moving those cities into Hillsborough. I am saying that a county ZIP map contains pieces of delivery areas whose preferred city name is somewhere else. That is what a delivery route that crosses a county line looks like on paper.

If I had treated every code on the county map as a "Hillsborough zip" in the sense of a place inside the county seat, I would have pulled the neighbors in by accident.

![Plant City downtown with the historic train depot and a street sign](/images/wm/articles/2706750.webp)
*Photo by [Thomas Ward](https://www.pexels.com/@thomasleeward) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/union-station-building-2706750/)*

## Useful Things to Know

📬 **The codes change, and your address might not match what you read today.** The Postal Service adds new ZIP codes or moves boundaries when population or local mail operations change. Hillsborough has grown a lot, and the map I pulled is a snapshot. Before you rely on any code, check the current lookup for your exact street address.

**The national lookup can lag the local update.** A ZIP that changed in the local post office may not show the change in a national lookup right away. A brand new street may not come back from a lookup at all until the local post office fixes it. If your address looks off, call or visit your local post office rather than assuming the first result is final.

**Plus four matters only if you have it.** The four extra digits after the hyphen narrow the delivery area down to blocks and street sides. I did not look up a house, and I am not going to invent a plus four. Use the full nine-digit code only when you have confirmed it from the Postal Service.

**Mailing city and legal location are not always the same.** If you live in an unincorporated part of the county but your mail says Tampa or Temple Terrace, that does not mean you are inside those city limits. It means the delivery area uses that name. If a form asks about jurisdiction, such as which city's services you use or which city you vote in, check with the right office, not your mailing label.

**Do not trust a single "Tampa zip" from a random source.** If someone hands you one code without asking your street, they are guessing. Tampa has 27 default codes on the county map I pulled, and that is before you count the acceptable alternate names.

**Watch for time-based offers and hours.** If you are dropping off mail at City Hall or a post office, check the current hours before you go. Those change, and I am not going to put numbers in here that you could end up relying on.

## FAQ

### Is there one zip code hillsborough tampa fl for the whole county?

No. There is not one zip code for Hillsborough County, and there is not one for Tampa. Hillsborough is covered by many delivery areas, and Tampa is spread across a set of them, not a single code. The right code depends on your exact address. Look up your street, then use the five-digit code the Postal Service gives for that location.

### Is 33602 the main zip code for Tampa?

33602 is the code for City Hall's address, 306 East Jackson Street. It is a correct code for that building. It is not a code that covers all of Tampa. Other Tampa addresses, including several city-run beaches and parks, use different 336 codes.

### How many zip codes does Tampa have?

On the county's ZIP code map I went through, 27 codes list Tampa as the default city, and all of them start with 336. That number comes from one map and one pass through it, so treat it as a snapshot, not a permanent count. The Postal Service can adjust boundaries over time.

### Why does my mail say Tampa if I do not live inside the city?

ZIP codes are built around post office and carrier routes, not city limits. A delivery area can use Tampa as its mailing city even when some of the houses on it sit outside the city. The mailing city tells the Postal Service how to route mail. It does not decide which city you legally live in or which services you get.

### Can I use a neighborhood name like Carrollwood or Ybor City on a form?

It depends on the code for your address. Some neighborhood names are listed as acceptable alternate names for certain delivery areas, and others are marked not acceptable for that code. If a form asks for city, the safest choice is the city name the Postal Service accepts for your ZIP. If you are unsure, check the lookup for your exact address.

### What should I write on a form that asks for county, city, and ZIP?

Write Hillsborough for county. For city, use the name your address actually uses, which might be Tampa, or might be Plant City, Brandon, Temple Terrace, or another acceptable name for that delivery area. For ZIP, use the five digits for your specific location. If you only know the county, you do not know the code yet, so look up your address first.

### Does Hillsborough County have a ZIP code map I can check?

Yes. The county publishes a ZIP code map that shows the delivery areas in Hillsborough County with their codes. It is useful for seeing the big picture, but for a specific address, confirm the code through the Postal Service lookup, since boundaries can shift.

### Why should I care about the difference between county, city, and ZIP?

Because forms, government offices, and mail carriers each use those terms differently. Mixing them up can send your mail to the wrong place, make a form reject your address, or put you in the wrong jurisdiction on paper. Keeping the three separate avoids most of the trouble.

## Final Thoughts

I started out wanting one number, and I ended up with a set of 27 codes, a county map full of mailing names that go well beyond Tampa, and a clear picture of why the single-number answer does not exist. The short version is that Hillsborough is the county, Tampa is a city inside it, and a ZIP code is a delivery area that does not care about city lines.

If you are filling out a form right now, do not hunt for one magic code. Write the county, write the city your address actually uses, and look up the ZIP for your exact street. That is more work than one number, but it is the answer that will get your mail to the right door.

body:
# Tampa Zip Code: 5 Real Addresses and Why It Isn't One Number

📬 People search for a tampa zip code and expect one answer. I understand why. A zip code feels like it should be a single box on a map with the city written inside it. In Tampa it doesn't work that way. If you pick the wrong code, your letter or package can end up somewhere you never meant it to go. Below I give you the codes I can tie to real addresses, what the City of Tampa says about its own limits, and how I would choose the right one for the job.

![Downtown Tampa skyline seen from the Hillsborough River at dusk](/images/wm/articles/7453905.webp)
*Photo by [M-DESIGNZ LLC](https://www.pexels.com/@m-designz-llc-463260) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/city-skyline-across-body-of-water-during-night-time-7453905/)*

**Short on Time?**

📍 There is no single Tampa zip code. Tampa uses several, and the city itself warns that many addresses with "Tampa" in them are not inside the City of Tampa at all. Here is the short version:

- If you are writing to City Hall, use **33602**. That is the code the city gives with its own address at 306 East Jackson Street.
- For ZooTampa on West Sligh Avenue, the code is **33604**.
- For the city parks department office on West Columbus Drive, it is **33607**.
- For Busch Gardens and Adventure Island, both on North McKinley Drive, the code is **33612**.
- For the Costco warehouse on West Linebaugh, it is **33625**.
- The Museum of Science & Industry (MOSI) on East Fowler Avenue has an address I can give you, but I don't have a zip code for it, so I won't guess one.
- To know whether an address is inside the city limits, use the city's address lookup. Don't assume from the word "Tampa."
- City Hall's main line is (813) 274-8211.

If you only remember one thing, remember this: the code depends on the street address, not on the word Tampa.

## 1. 33602 Is City Hall's Tampa Zip Code, and It Shows Up Downtown a Lot

If you ask someone for the tampa zip code, 33602 is the one you will hear most often. It is also the one I would be most careful with. The City of Tampa lists 33602 with its own contact address, 306 East Jackson Street, Tampa, Florida 33602, and the main phone is (813) 274-8211. That is City Hall's code. The city does not present it as the code for the whole city, and it shouldn't be treated that way.

Downtown addresses that carry 33602 include the Barrymore Hotel at 111 West Fortune Street, the Florida Aquarium at 701 Channelside Drive, and the Glazer Children's Museum at 110 W Gasparilla Plaza. If you are mailing something to one of those places, 33602 is the right code. If you are mailing to the zoo, 33602 will not help you there.

The city's own warning is the reason I keep coming back to this. It says a lot of [Hillsborough addresses](/guides/zip-code-hillsborough-tampa-fl) include the word Tampa and still sit outside the City of Tampa. Temple Terrace and unincorporated parts of the county are the examples it gives. A mailing address that says Tampa doesn't tell you much about whether you are inside the city. For that, use the city's address lookup, not a guess.

![City Hall building on East Jackson Street in downtown Tampa](/images/wm/articles/31474037.webp)
*Photo by [Dominik Gryzbon](https://www.pexels.com/@gryziu) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/historic-government-building-in-jackson-ms-31474037/)*

## 2. 33604 Is the Code for ZooTampa on West Sligh Avenue

[ZooTampa](/things-to-do/tampa-zoo)'s address is 1101 W. Sligh Avenue, and that address uses 33604. Use it for anything you're mailing to the zoo. It is a good example of why you should not reach for the downtown code. Tampa has a lot of north and west side addresses, and many of them carry codes that people don't expect if they only know the middle of town.

Sligh Avenue is a long road, and distances on a map can fool you. If you are driving there for the first time, leave a little extra room in your plans, especially [on a weekend](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa-this-weekend). I don't have a current traffic report to give you, so check your own app before you go.

![Entrance to ZooTampa at Lowry Park on a sunny morning](/images/wm/articles/31098244.webp)
*Photo by [DΛVΞ GΛRCIΛ](https://www.pexels.com/@davegarcia) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/scenic-university-campus-pathway-in-coral-gables-31098244/)*

## 3. 33607 Is the Parks Department on West Columbus Drive

The City of Tampa lists two offices that matter here, and that is where the confusion starts. The parks director's office is at 3402 W. Columbus Drive, Tampa, Florida 33607, with the phone 813-274-8615. That is 33607. The same city material then repeats the downtown Jackson Street address, which carries 33602.

So if you are writing to the parks director, use 33607. If you are writing to the city in general, City Hall's code is 33602. Two city offices, two different codes, and both are called Tampa. If someone asked me for the tampa zip code while I only had City Hall's address in front of me, I would say 33602 and be wrong about the parks building. That kind of mistake can leave a letter sitting in the wrong sorting center for a week.

![Tampa parks department office building on West Columbus Drive](/images/wm/articles/35784380.webp)
*Photo by [Aditya Oberai](https://www.pexels.com/@oberai) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/monochrome-modern-office-buildings-bengaluru-35784380/)*

## 4. 33612 Covers Busch Gardens and Adventure Island on North McKinley Drive

Busch Gardens and Adventure Island both sit on North McKinley Drive, and both use 33612. If you are mailing something to either park, that is the code. Because the two places share a road, it is easy to assume every address on that road shares the same code, or that the Fowler Avenue address for MOSI does too. It doesn't follow. Same road does not mean same zip, and I don't have a code for MOSI at all.

Both parks draw large crowds, so plan the trip in general terms. Arrive early if you can, and check the parks' own published hours before you leave home, because I can't speak to the current schedule. I'm not going to give a parking price here, because I don't have one I can stand behind.

![Busch Gardens Tampa Bay entrance on North McKinley Drive](/images/wm/articles/34074671.webp)
*Photo by [Katie Brittle](https://www.pexels.com/@katiebrittle) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/harambe-sign-at-theme-park-entrance-florida-34074671/)*

## 5. 33625 Is the Costco on West Linebaugh

The Costco warehouse on the west side of Tampa sits on West Linebaugh, and the code for that store is 33625. If you're ordering a delivery or sending a return to that store, use 33625. I'd still type the full street address, since many people shop at the closest Costco and assume every nearby store has the same code.

This is a good example of how the codes are spread out. Within a few miles of one another you can find different codes, and if you rely on the one you used last time, you can end up with a letter in a different part of the county.

![Costco warehouse entrance on West Linebaugh in west Tampa](/images/wm/articles/20021122.webp)
*Photo by [Thomas  balabaud](https://www.pexels.com/@thomas-balabaud-735585) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/exterior-of-an-industrial-building-in-sunlight-20021122/)*

## Useful Things to Know

The main thing people get wrong is treating a zip code as a city boundary. A zip code is a mail-delivery area. Zip codes are used across the USA for sorting mail, but they were never meant to draw city lines. The City of Tampa's own warning is that the word Tampa in an address does not mean the address is inside the city limits. The county's ZIP code maps show the areas across Hillsborough County, and most of those areas are not labeled as Tampa.

People who search for the zip code of Florida Tampa are usually trying to answer a simple question, and the honest answer is that it depends on the street. When I looked at the county's map, it showed 73 zip areas in total. Narrowing that to the areas that name Tampa as the default city gave me 27: 33602, 33603, 33604, [33605](/guides/ybor-city-tampa-fl-33605), 33606, 33607, 33609, 33610, 33611, 33612, 33613, 33614, 33615, 33616, 33617, 33618, 33619, 33620, 33621, 33624, 33625, 33626, 33629, 33634, 33635, 33637, and 33647. The list has gaps. 33601, 33608, 33622, and 33623 did not come up in that Tampa set, and I am not claiming those numbers don't exist anywhere. They just didn't appear in that slice of the map.

That gives you the zip code for Tampa Florida in the sense the county map uses it, but it is still a snapshot of one map, not a postal bulletin, and I can't tell you when it was last updated. A PO box or a single-building code might never appear as a mapped area, and I didn't check for those. If your mail goes to a PO box, ask the post office that serves that box.

I also want to be clear about what I don't have. I don't have a population figure to attach to any of these codes. I don't have a [time zone](/guides/what-time-zone-is-tampa-florida) statement from the city or the county. The phone numbers I can confirm start with 813, which is a phone prefix I saw on city material, not a full area-code map. If you need any of those, check [the official source](https://tools.usps.com/zip-code-lookup.htm) directly. The phone number for [City Hall](https://www.tampa.gov/), (813) 274-8211, is the one I'd trust for general questions.

For boundary questions, use the city's address lookup before any important mailing. It is one more step than most people expect, but it is much faster than finding out a week later that a permit or payment went to the wrong office.

Finally, check the code on the envelope or the form itself. If a form asks for one zip code and you're not sure which is right, don't guess. Look up the street address.

## FAQ

### What is the Tampa zip code for City Hall?

City Hall's address is 306 East Jackson Street, Tampa, Florida 33602, and the main phone is (813) 274-8211. The city gives 33602 with that address. It is City Hall's code, not a code for the entire city.

### Is there one Tampa zip code for the whole city?

No. Tampa uses several zip codes, and the code depends on the street address. The city itself warns that many addresses with "Tampa" in them sit outside the City of Tampa, so the word Tampa alone does not settle it.

### What zip code should I use for the zoo?

ZooTampa's address is 1101 W. Sligh Avenue, and that address uses 33604. Use the street address when you're mailing something, not the downtown code.

### Do Busch Gardens and Adventure Island share a zip code?

Yes. Both sit on North McKinley Drive and use 33612. Shared road names don't always mean shared codes, though, so check the exact address for any other business on that road.

### Is MOSI in the same zip code as Busch Gardens?

I don't have a zip code for MOSI. I have its address, 4801 E. Fowler Avenue, but not the code. I wouldn't borrow 33612 from Busch Gardens just because both are on roads that show up in the same directions. Check the address or ask MOSI directly.

### How do I tell if an address is inside the City of Tampa?

Use the city's address lookup. The city warns that the word Tampa in an address does not mean the address is inside the city limits, and it names Temple Terrace and unincorporated parts of the county as common mix-ups. Don't rely on the mailing address alone.

### Which map should I use to find the Tampa Florida zip code?

For Hillsborough County, the county's ZIP code map is a useful way to see which areas name Tampa as the default city. It is not a city boundary map, and it is a snapshot. For a specific address, the city's address lookup is the better tool.

### What should I write on a form that asks for a Tampa FL zip code?

Write the code for the street address on the form, not the one you remember from City Hall or from the last time you mailed something. If the form only has room for one code and the address is a business or a park, look up that exact address first. If you can't confirm it, ask the office that is receiving the form.

## Final Thoughts

🗺️ I wish I could hand you one number and be done with it. I can't, and I'd rather say that than pretend. What I can give you is a list of codes tied to real addresses, a warning from the city about what "Tampa" does and doesn't mean, and a plain rule: use the street address, not the word Tampa.

If you're writing to City Hall, use 33602. For the zoo, use 33604. For the parks office, use 33607. For Busch Gardens and Adventure Island, use 33612. For the Costco on West Linebaugh, use 33625. For everything else, look up the address and don't guess. A few extra minutes on the lookup will save you from a letter going to the wrong side of the county 📮.

body:
# Westshore Marriott Hotel Tampa: 6 Things to Know Before You Book

If you search for westshore marriott hotel tampa, you will see the words flipped half the time, as marriott westshore hotel tampa. I have done both. Either way you are looking at the same large hotel on [North Westshore Boulevard](https://www.marriott.com/en-us/hotels/tpawe-marriott-tampa-westshore/overview/), a few minutes from the malls and a long drive from [downtown](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa). I live here, and I spent a while going through the hotel's own details alongside a local visitor listing. Some things are clean. Some things do not match. This is what I would want to know before paying for a room.

![Westshore Marriott Hotel Tampa exterior on North Westshore Boulevard](/images/wm/articles/30542439.webp)
*Photo by [Abhishek  Navlakha](https://www.pexels.com/@navlakha) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/modern-architecture-in-hong-kong-urban-area-30542439/)*

## Short on Time?

- **It is on North Westshore Boulevard, not downtown.** Plan on a car for most trips. The listing puts the convention center about 5 miles away.
- **The free airport shuttle and free self-parking are the main reasons to pick it.** 🚐 Confirm both at the front desk before you arrive.
- **It is a big hotel with very few suites.** A local visitor listing counts 310 sleeping rooms and only 2 suites.
- **The Grand Ballroom is the room to trust on the hotel's chart.** Use the 500-person theater figure, and ignore the "up to 120 guests" wedding line until the hotel explains it.
- **The pool closure notice covered January 5 through February 10, 2026.** That window has passed. Ask the desk for the current status.
- **I do not have a nightly rate, and I will not guess one.** Call (813) 287-2555 and ask for today's price on your dates.

## 1. Where It Actually Sits

The address is 1001 N Westshore Boulevard, Tampa, Florida 33607. The 813 number is the one I would call: (813) 287-2555. The toll-free line is 1-800-346-7079.

This is Westshore, and it is its own part of the city. The malls are close. Westshore Mall, also called Westshore Plaza, is less than a mile away, and that is the main thing you can walk to. Raymond James Stadium is on North Dale Mabry Highway, home of the city's professional football team. The listing I looked at does not give a distance for it, so check the drive yourself. Busch Gardens is listed at about 13.7 miles.

The mistake I see most often is treating this hotel as downtown. It is not. The local listing gives about 5 miles to the convention center, and anyone who has driven that stretch of Tampa in afternoon traffic knows that "5 miles" can be a long 5 miles. Downtown has its own feel, its own hotels, the [Westin Tampa Waterside](/guides/the-westin-tampa-waterside) and [The Tampa EDITION](/guides/the-tampa-edition), and its own walkable blocks. This is a different kind of Tampa: office parks, big parking lots, and a lot of car traffic. [Texas de Brazil](/food-and-drink/texas-de-brazil-tampa), the churrascaria on Boy Scout Boulevard, is the Westshore dinner I would not confuse with the hotel restaurant.

People also fold the rest of the city into this address. The "south" part of Tampa is not this boulevard. [Ybor](/guides/ybor-city-tampa-fl-33605) is a historic neighborhood several miles from here, and I would not navigate there from any nearby-attractions list. I looked at one list of nearby places that had a wrong [zip code](/guides/tampa-zip-code) on a museum and two addresses that were one digit apart for different attractions. Use a map app, not a printed rundown, for anything past the malls.

The aquarium is on Channelside, and so is Amalie Arena. Older listings still call the arena by its previous name, the St. Pete Times Forum. Do not type the old name into a rideshare app. Channelside is a drive from here, not a stroll.

If what you really wanted was a big airport-area hotel from a different chain, a Hilton is a separate brand with its own properties, and it is worth comparing the two on their own terms. Do not assume they sit in the same spot or offer the same things.

Tampa is a big city, and this part of it feels like a suburb with a highway running through it. That is the point for some people. For others it is the wrong city entirely.

![Westshore area road view near the Westshore Marriott Hotel Tampa with traffic and office buildings](/images/wm/articles/5224607.webp)
*Photo by [Ivan  Aguilar](https://www.pexels.com/@ivantomate) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/steel-trusses-of-a-building-roof-5224607/)*

## 2. Rooms at the Westshore Marriott Hotel Tampa

Here is the room count as the local visitor listing gives it: 310 sleeping rooms including suites, spread across 13 floors and served by 3 elevators. The breakdown is 127 doubles, 181 kings, 2 suites, and 16 accessible rooms. Those add up to 310.

Two suites out of 310 means this is not a suite hotel. If you need a separate living room, a big apartment-style layout, or a suite-heavy family setup, look elsewhere. The word "apartments" does not fit these rooms either. The hotel says it accepts long stays, but a long stay here is still a hotel room on a long booking, not a furnished apartment.

The hotel's own materials describe renovated rooms, new bedding, mobile check-in, high-speed Wi-Fi, a flat-screen TV, an ergonomic desk, and a plug-in panel. They never give the room count, which is why the visitor listing number matters.

I tried to book an accessible room through the hotel's site, and it showed none available for my dates. The listing counts 16 accessible rooms. I read that as "none left for those dates," not as a building with zero accessible rooms. Still, call before you assume. If you need one, ask for an accessible room by type on the date you want, and ask whether they can hold one.

The hotel's materials mention an Executive Lounge that is complimentary for top-tier loyalty members and one guest, plus a separate concierge-access option for continental breakfast and evening hors d'oeuvres. Those are two different offers, and they do not require the same status. Ask which one applies to you.

There is also a floor problem. The dining information places a Concierge Lounge on the 14th floor, with breakfast Monday through Friday from 6:30 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. The visitor listing says the building has 13 floors. I cannot make 14 and 13 agree. It could be a numbering quirk, an old floor plan, or a lounge somewhere else in the building. Ask the front desk which floor it is on before you plan around it.

The listing gives check-in at 4:00 p.m. and check-out at noon, with a 48-hour cancellation window. I never found those times in the hotel's own materials, so treat them as the listing's version and confirm at booking.

Full service is the right phrase for this place. "Inn" undersells it. You get a lobby, a bar, a restaurant, meeting space, and a fitness room. It is a large property, and that is the first thing to know about it.

![Guest room at the Westshore Marriott Hotel Tampa with king bed and desk](/images/wm/articles/3755585.webp)
*Photo by [Castorly Stock](https://www.pexels.com/@castorlystock) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/white-pillows-on-bed-3755585/)*

## 3. Getting Here: The Free Shuttle and Parking

The biggest reason I would pick this hotel over something closer to the middle of town is the transportation. The listing describes a free airport shuttle and a courtesy area shuttle. It gives the hotel about 2 miles from Tampa International Airport. ✈️ That is a short trip, but schedules change, so ask the desk for current pickup times before you plan a flight around it.

Parking is listed as free self-parking with 387 spaces. The hotel's own materials did not restate the spaces or the free parking to me, so confirm both when you check in, especially if you are driving a larger vehicle. If the desk tells you something different from the listing, believe the desk.

The listing also mentions motorcoach parking. That is for buses and tour groups, not for a room booking, so I am leaving the number out.

If you are coming from the airport and staying for a short trip, the shuttle plus free parking is a real advantage. If you plan to spend your days downtown, the drive is the cost. Five miles sounds small until you are sitting on a highway on a weekday.

![Westshore Marriott Hotel Tampa entrance and parking area with the courtesy shuttle lane](/images/wm/articles/31891120.webp)
*Photo by [Joshua Manglian](https://www.pexels.com/@joshua-manglian-716707173) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/sunlit-urban-parking-garage-entrance-31891120/)*

## 4. Pool, Fitness, and the Other Amenities

🏊 The fitness room is complimentary and includes cardio machines, ellipticals, bikes, free weights, treadmills, and weight machines. For a hotel gym that is a decent setup, and it does not cost extra.

The pool is where the details get messy. The hotel describes an indoor/outdoor heated pool that is connected, and then a separate answer that talks about multiple pools while naming that same connected pool once as indoor and once as outdoor. I would count it as one connected pool unless the desk tells you otherwise.

The visitor listing adds a whirlpool, a locker room with a shower, and a gift shop. The hotel's own materials did not mention a whirlpool, so ask if that matters to you.

There is also a closure notice for the pool covering January 5 through February 10, 2026. I am writing this after that window. I will not promise you the pool is open, and I will not promise it is closed. Call the desk and ask whether it is running and whether any work is scheduled for your dates.

![Indoor and outdoor heated pool area at the Westshore Marriott Hotel Tampa](/images/wm/articles/36301138.webp)
*Photo by [Latitude Suites](https://www.pexels.com/@latitude-suites-2159797712) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/elegant-indoor-pool-at-tinton-falls-hotel-36301138/)*

## 5. Dining on Property

There are two places to eat on site. Blue Bistro and Blue Bar is the full restaurant and bar. The hotel's hours are Monday through Friday from 6:30 a.m. to 11:00 p.m., and Saturday and Sunday from 7:00 a.m. to midnight. Room service is available, and breakfast is served there for a fee I do not have. The hotel's event material also refers to it as Blue Bistro/Blue Bar, so the name is consistent in more than one place.

Rooted Grounds Lobby Cafe is the coffee and grab-and-go spot. The hotel lists it every day from 6:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. It also offers breakfast for a fee, and I would confirm the price rather than assume it is cheap.

Here is where the details disagree. The visitor listing gives the restaurant as Tampa Blue Bistro, an American restaurant with 106 seats, and gives hours of Sunday through Monday from 6:30 a.m. to midnight. It also names a Starbucks in the lobby instead of Rooted Grounds. I am not averaging those hours or picking one name over the other. When you call, ask which coffee shop is in the lobby and what the restaurant's hours are on your days.

🍽️ Blue is the place to watch a game. The hotel's description says you can order a three-course meal or a drink while a game is on. That is a reasonable thing to do on a Tampa evening, and it is one of the few details here that feels like the hotel is describing an actual room rather than a brochure.

![Blue Bistro and Blue Bar dining room at the Westshore Marriott Hotel Tampa](/images/wm/articles/29394553.webp)
*Photo by [Sydney Sang](https://www.pexels.com/@urfriendlyphotog) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/modern-bar-interior-with-unique-wooden-design-29394553/)*

## 6. Meetings and Ballrooms at the Westshore Marriott Hotel Tampa

The meeting space is the part I trust most, mainly because I could check it against more than one source.

The hotel has 22 event rooms totaling 19,680 square feet, with a largest capacity of 500. Those totals match between the hotel's chart and the visitor listing.

The Grand Ballroom is 4,840 square feet on the hotel's chart. It seats 500 in theater style, 300 in schoolroom style, 500 for a reception, and 360 for a banquet. The listing swaps the dimensions around, giving a width and length that do not match the hotel's version. Use the square footage and capacities from the hotel's chart. The listing gives a reception figure of 600, which does not match the hotel's 500, so I would plan on 500.

The hotel's wedding pitch says the Grand Ballroom can hold up to 120 guests. That number does not match the chart, and I would not plan a wedding around it until the hotel explains it. Ask for the room layout in writing.

Other rooms on the chart include the Junior Ballroom at 1,848 square feet, with theater seating for 175 and banquet seating for 150. The Westshore room is 1,500 square feet, with theater seating for 150 and banquet seating for 110. The Kennedy room is 756 square feet, with theater seating for 75. The listing gives Kennedy as 750 square feet with theater seating for 35, so check that one directly. There are two boardrooms at 288 square feet with 16 conference seats, and Cypress and Spruce are at 338 square feet with 14 conference seats. The listing gives Cypress and Spruce as 340 square feet.

There was a Bonvoy signing bonus advertised with deadlines in 2020 and 2023. Those offers are over, so do not plan around them. The line I would use with a planner is a block of 10 or more rooms for a special group rate. Ask for the rate in writing, because I do not have one to give you.

![Grand Ballroom setup at the Westshore Marriott Hotel Tampa with theater-style seating](/images/wm/articles/19569865.webp)
*Photo by [Clément Proust](https://www.pexels.com/@clement-proust-363898785) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/luxury-restaurant-hall-19569865/)*

## Useful Things to Know

**Call before you book.** The 813 number is the one I would use: (813) 287-2555. Ask the questions the listing cannot answer. Is the pool open? Which floor is the concierge lounge on? Is it Starbucks or Rooted Grounds in the lobby? Is an accessible room available for your dates?

**Ask about the shuttle schedule.** The listing says the airport shuttle is free, but it does not give you a schedule. Ask for pickup times and where you meet the van.

**Confirm parking.** Free self-parking is the listing's claim. Ask the desk to confirm it, and ask whether there is a fee for a second car.

**Do not plan around downtown.** If you need a short walk to restaurants, museums, or the waterfront, this is the wrong base. Plan on a car or a rideshare for most trips.

**Watch for old names.** Some listings still call the arena by its previous name. Use the current name, and check the address in a map app before you go.

**Check the dates on offers.** Loyalty and signing offers have deadlines. Some of them have already passed, so ask for current terms rather than repeating what you read elsewhere.

**Know what the room count means.** With 310 rooms and only 2 suites, this is a standard large hotel. If you need a suite, ask for one by name and confirm it is available on your dates.

**Expect the rate to change.** I do not have a nightly rate, and I will not make one up. Check the price for your dates on the hotel's site or by phone.

## FAQ

### Is the Westshore Marriott Hotel Tampa downtown?

No. It is on North Westshore Boulevard, in the Westshore part of the city. The visitor listing gives about 5 miles to the convention center, which is a real drive from downtown. Plan on a car or rideshare for most trips.

### How many rooms does the Westshore Marriott Hotel Tampa have?

A local visitor listing counts 310 sleeping rooms, including suites. The breakdown is 127 doubles, 181 kings, 2 suites, and 16 accessible rooms. The hotel's own materials do not give the count, so confirm the number and room types when you book.

### Does the hotel offer a free airport shuttle?

The listing describes a free airport shuttle and a courtesy area shuttle, with the airport about 2 miles away. Ask the front desk for current pickup times and where to meet the shuttle before you arrive.

### Is parking free?

The listing describes free self-parking with 387 spaces. Confirm that with the desk when you check in, since the hotel's own materials did not restate it to me.

### Is there an accessible room?

The listing counts 16 accessible rooms. When I tried to book one through the hotel's site, none showed as available for my dates. Call the front desk and ask about accessible rooms for your specific dates.

### What are check-in and check-out times?

The listing gives check-in at 4:00 p.m. and check-out at noon, with a 48-hour cancellation window. I did not find those times in the hotel's own materials, so confirm them when you book.

### Is the pool open?

The hotel had a closure notice for January 5 through February 10, 2026, and that window has passed. I cannot promise the pool is open or closed right now. Call the desk and ask about the current status and any work scheduled for your dates.

### How big is the Grand Ballroom?

The hotel's chart gives the Grand Ballroom as 4,840 square feet, with theater seating for 500, schoolroom for 300, reception for 500, and banquet for 360. Use those numbers for planning, and ask the hotel to explain the "up to 120 guests" wedding line before you rely on it.

For the Westshore mall people mean by “Tampa Mall,” use my [International Plaza](/shopping/international-plaza-tampa) notes.

Flying in first? Start with my [Tampa International Airport](/getting-around/tampa-international-airport) arrival guide.

Comparing downtown Riverwalk stays? I also covered the [Barrymore Hotel Tampa](/guides/barrymore-hotel-tampa).

## Final Thoughts

The Westshore Marriott Hotel Tampa is a large, full-service hotel on the Westshore side of the city. It is not a suite hotel, it is not downtown, and it is not an apartment. Its best features are the free airport shuttle, the listed free self-parking, and a meeting space whose chart I trust more than the wedding pitch.

If you are flying in, staying a few nights, and planning to drive to what you want to see, it can make sense. If you want to walk out the door into a downtown neighborhood, it is the wrong base.

Before you book, call (813) 287-2555. Ask about the pool, the lounge on the 14th floor, the lobby coffee, the parking, the shuttle, and your accessible-room needs. Those five questions will tell you more about this hotel than any listing can.
