body:
# 6 Things to Know About Ybor City Tampa FL 33605: A Local's Guide to 7th Avenue, Parking, and the Cigar District

Ybor City Tampa FL [33605](/guides/tampa-zip-code) is the address I end up typing into my phone whenever I head to the cigar district, and it is the one most visitors need too. Ybor is a historic neighborhood northeast of [downtown Tampa](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa), with brick storefronts, wrought-iron balconies, a bar street that keeps going well past dinner, and a parking setup that trips up almost everyone. I live here and go to Ybor often. This is my honest rundown of the history worth the walk, the garages that actually work, and the permit streets that do not.

![Brick storefronts and wrought-iron balconies along 7th Avenue in Ybor City, Tampa](/images/wm/articles/37444400.webp)
*Photo by [Jose Luis  Vanasco](https://www.pexels.com/@jose-luis-vanasco-2155044313) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/ornate-balconies-on-historic-barcelona-building-37444400/)*

## Short on Time?

Ybor City is a historic neighborhood northeast of downtown Tampa, inside ZIP code 33605. The heart of it is 7th Avenue, a brick commercial strip with restaurants, bars, and clubs. Come in daylight to see the architecture, the old cigar history, and the Columbia Restaurant. Come after dark if you want nightlife, and expect it to be loud and adult-oriented.

Park in one of the named city garages or lots, not on a residential block south of 6th Avenue. Those side streets are permit zones, and the signs are not decorative. Take the TECO streetcar if you are coming from downtown or Channelside and want to skip the parking search entirely. Call ahead to confirm hours at the visitor center on 8th Avenue, and check any tour schedule before you show up at a factory.

## 1. Ybor City Tampa FL 33605: The District Under One ZIP

People ask me constantly whether Ybor is its own town or just a nickname for a part of Tampa. It is a historic district, and it is very much part of the city. It sits northeast of downtown, and the ZIP code 33605 covers the addresses you will actually use: the visitor center, the garages, the factories, and the side streets that fan out from 7th Avenue.

The Ybor City Visitor Information Center is inside the Centro Ybor complex at 1600 East 8th Avenue, Suite B104, Tampa, Florida 33605. The phone number is 813-241-8838. The posted hours are Monday through Saturday from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., and Sunday from noon to 4 p.m. Hours change, especially around holidays and during the slow season, so call before you rely on them. The staff is helpful, and it is a good place to grab a map if you have never been here.

If you are coming from the rest of the city, the district is close to downtown but feels separate once you are on the brick. You can walk between the two if you are fit and the weather is cool. In the heat of a Tampa summer, I would not. Plan on a short drive or the streetcar.

![Ybor City Visitor Information Center entrance inside the Centro Ybor complex](/images/wm/articles/27972901.webp)
*Photo by [Quang Vuong](https://www.pexels.com/@quang-vuong-724225078) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/the-inside-of-a-building-with-a-large-skylight-27972901/)*

## 2. Seventh Avenue, the Street Everyone Means

When someone asks me which street Ybor is, I say 7th Avenue. It is the commercial core, and it is the reason most people come. The welcome is the archway just east of 7th at Nick Nuccio Parkway. From there the strip runs about eleven blocks toward 26th Street, lined with blond and red brick buildings, wrought-iron balconies, and restaurants with patios that spill onto the sidewalk.

Several places on 7th are worth knowing by name. The Marti-Maceo Club and L'Unione Italiana are there, along with El Centro Espanol. The Columbia Restaurant has been on historic 7th Avenue since 1905 and is still run by the original family. It takes up a full city block, and it has long called itself the largest Spanish restaurant in the world. I cannot tell you if that title holds up, but the dining rooms are big and the flamenco shows at dinner are a real draw. The Ritz, historically the Rivoli, served the Afro-Cuban community in the neighborhood and is a reminder that the district had a lot more going on than cigars.

The TECO Line streetcar connects Ybor with downtown and Channelside, and it is the easiest way for many visitors to get here. Hop off on 7th, walk the strip, and hop back on when you are tired. It is slow, but that is part of the fun. If you are coming from Channelside, the streetcar is often faster than trying to park, and you will not need to hunt for a spot on a [crowded weekend](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa-this-weekend).

🚋 The streetcar is the stress-free option, and I recommend it whenever you can use it.

![TECO Line streetcar on 7th Avenue in Ybor City at midday](/images/wm/articles/30765369.webp)
*Photo by [Arlind D](https://www.pexels.com/@arlindphotography) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/dynamic-urban-tram-motion-in-cityscape-30765369/)*

## 3. Getting In: The Palm Avenue Approach and the Garages

This is the part of the trip where people get lost, and it is the part I think about most. The driving directions I have all funnel through the same sequence. Coming from I-4, take Exit 1, go onto 21st Street, turn right on Palm, then left on 15th Street. If you are using valet, the turn is a left on 9th Avenue. If you are parking yourself, the garage sits farther down 15th Street, past 7th Avenue, with the entrance on the left just past the railroad tracks. From there you walk out the 16th Street side and head north to Centro Ybor.

The problem is that the brick on 7th Avenue looks like the destination, so people turn early and end up in the nightlife lane with no plan. Stay on 15th, get into the garage, and walk the rest of the way. You will save yourself a headache.

🅿️ The [City of Tampa parking office](https://www.tampa.gov/parking) number is 813-242-5483. These are the garages and lots I know are in the district:

- **Fernando Noriega Jr. Garage**, 2010 North 13th Street. It is bounded by Nick Nuccio Parkway, East 8th Avenue, North 13th Street, and East 9th Avenue.
- **Centro Ybor Garage**, 1500 East 5th Avenue, north of 5th, between 15th and 16th Streets.
- **Ybor Lot 3**, 1701 North 19th Street, north of East 6th Avenue, between 19th and 20th Streets.
- **Ybor Lot 5**, 1812 North 19th Street, south of East 8th Avenue, between Angel Oliva Senior Street and 19th Street.
- **Ybor Lot 6**, 1813 North 19th Street, south of 8th Avenue, between 19th and 20th Streets.

I do not have garage prices I trust, so check the rates when you arrive. Rates can change, and the signs at each lot are the final word.

Tour buses drop off at 9th Avenue and 16th Street. Bus parking is on 12th Avenue between 15th and 17th Streets. As far as I know it is free, but confirm on the signs before you leave a bus parked there.

![Centro Ybor garage entrance on 15th Street, Ybor City, Tampa](/images/wm/articles/12636559.webp)
*Photo by [Joshua Brown](https://www.pexels.com/@lolimjoshingyou) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/a-man-pushing-a-garbage-cart-12636559/)*

## 4. Factories, Museums, and the Little Park

Ybor's history is the reason the architecture is here, and it is worth understanding before you walk. The area was built as a cigar town. Vicente Martinez-Ybor, born in Valencia, partnered with Ignacio Haya in 1885 to build a cigar community near Tampa after trade trouble and political upheaval in Cuba pushed manufacturers north. The first worker houses went up in 1886. The city annexed Ybor in 1887, but the neighborhood kept its own identity. By 1890 the population was around 6,000, a mix of Cuban, Spanish, Italian, German, Romanian Jewish, and Chinese residents. Mutual-aid clubs like Centro Asturiano, Circulo Cubano, El Centro Espanol, and La Union Marti-Maceo gave the community its social backbone. José Martí came through before the 1895 war for Cuban independence.

The district is a National Historic Landmark, and the number of historic buildings from the factory years is large, well over 950. The peak was the 1920s. Then came the Depression and machines that changed how cigars were made. A 1965 urban renewal plan tore out a lot of the old neighborhood, and the preservation fight that followed is the reason you can walk the streets today.

🏭 If you want to see cigar making, the tradition is still alive but limited. J.C. Newman Cigar Company at El Reloj offers tours and rolling and tasting classes, and it is the one I would point most visitors toward. E. Regensberg and Sons, also known as S. Fernandez and Co., is on 16th Street and is described as the only large factory still producing cigars in the district. These are two different places, and I would confirm which one currently runs public tours before you go. Don't assume every factory on the map is open to visitors.

The [Ybor City Museum State Park](https://www.floridastateparks.org/parks-and-trails/ybor-city-museum-state-park) occupies the old Ferlita Bakery, and the exhibits give you the context the buildings can't. Chickens wander the streets, which surprises first-timers. A short walk from the museum, Parque Amigos de José Martí sits on a small piece of land that was donated to Cuba in the 1950s. It is a quiet place to sit for a few minutes if the bar street is getting loud. Centennial Park is also in the district and gives you a bit of green space near the center of things.

![Ybor City Museum State Park building, the former Ferlita Bakery, in Tampa](/images/wm/articles/18326893.webp)
*Photo by [Arian Fernandez](https://www.pexels.com/@troopper84) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/key-west-museum-of-art-and-history-key-west-florida-usa-18326893/)*

## 5. South Ybor Is Not 7th Avenue

This is the piece that matters most for parking, and the one people least expect. The side streets south of 6th Avenue look quiet and close to the action, and that is exactly why they are a trap. The City of Tampa has a residential permit program covering the area it calls South Ybor. The boundaries I have are 6th Avenue on the north, Nick Nuccio Parkway and North 13th Street on the west, Adamo Drive on the south, and North 21st Street on the east. The city's map uses North Republica de Cuba as the western edge in its fine print, so check the signs on the ground rather than trusting my summary of the line.

Residents in that zone need permits. The permit office is on the ground floor of the Centro Ybor garage, on the 16th Street side, at 1500 East 5th Avenue. It is open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. To get a permit you need two proofs that you live inside the boundary. You can get one residential permit per address, and a second only if there is no off-street space. Guest permits are also available. Enforcement questions go to 813-274-8524.

Here is what I would do as a visitor: don't park on a residential block south of 6th Avenue on a Friday or [Saturday night](/things-to-do/things-to-do-on-saturday-in-tampa), and don't assume the empty street means free parking. I am not going to guess at a fine amount, because I don't know it. I would just pay for a garage space and walk the extra block.

![Residential side street south of 6th Avenue in South Ybor with permit parking signs](/images/wm/articles/40068776.webp)
*Photo by [Malcoln Oliveira](https://www.pexels.com/@malcolnphoto) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/aerial-view-of-belo-horizonte-cityscape-40068776/)*

## 6. Night on 7th, and What I Won't Pretend to Know

🌙 Ybor after dark is a different place. The bars, clubs, and live music are the reason many people come, and 7th Avenue is the hub. Names you will see along the strip include Bad Monkey Ybor, The Ritz Ybor, Madame Fortune, and Sterling Cigar Lounge, and Funny Bone is in the entertainment complex. The late-night crowd skews adult. If you are visiting with kids, come in the afternoon, do the museum and the park, eat a long dinner, and head home before the strip gets rowdy.

I want to be direct about one thing. I don't have crime figures I would stand behind, so I am not going to write a safety ranking, a list of blocks to avoid after 11, or a number that sounds official but isn't. Use common sense. Stay in populated areas, keep your phone and wallet out of sight, and don't leave valuables in your car.

The city did announce a roadway plan in March 2026 tied to a deadly crash on November 8, 2025. That plan is seven months old as I write this, so treat it as an announcement rather than a finished project. The first step described was repaving part of 7th Avenue from Nebraska Avenue to Nick Nuccio Parkway, adding 36 on-street spaces and two bus bays, and narrowing the road to slow drivers at the gateway. The plan also called for more paving elsewhere, about 3.75 lane-miles and nearly 45 new spaces in total, lower speed limits on the corridor, and crash-rated bollards at busy crosswalks. The city also said that over the prior decade there had not been a deadly crash on 7th other than the November incident. That is a statement about traffic deaths on one avenue. It is not a crime report. Check the current street layout when you go, because some of this work may already be done and some may still be in progress.

![Crosswalk on 7th Avenue in Ybor City with pedestrians and nightlife storefronts](/images/wm/articles/5288961.webp)
*Photo by [Udayaditya Barua](https://www.pexels.com/@ubarua1) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/the-busy-downtown-new-york-5288961/)*

## Useful Things to Know

**Timing matters.** Daytime is for the architecture, the museum, the factories that run tours, and a long lunch. Night is for music and bars. If you want the neighborhood without the crowds, go on a weekday morning.

**Parking is the main trap.** Go to a named garage or lot first. Don't cruise for a spot on 7th Avenue on a busy evening. The garages on 15th Street and the lots on North 19th are the right answer for most visits.

**The visitor center has set hours.** It is on 8th Avenue, phone 813-241-8838. Call before you plan your day around it.

**The streetcar is worth using.** It connects the district with downtown and Channelside and saves you the parking question altogether.

**Some of the district is residential.** Respect the permit zones south of 6th Avenue, and don't treat quiet side streets as free parking.

**Confirm tours before you go.** Factory tours and classes change. Call or check the schedule ahead of time, especially if you have a specific time in mind.

**The Saturday market is nearby.** There is a Saturday market at 1901 North 19th Street, also in ZIP 33605. Check its schedule before you plan a trip around it.

**Bring water and shade.** Walking the brick in Tampa heat wears people out faster than they expect.

## FAQ

### What ZIP code is Ybor City Tampa FL 33605 in?

Ybor City is in ZIP code 33605. That is the code on the visitor center, the garages, the factories, and most of the addresses you will use when you visit. If you are entering an address into a map app, 33605 will get you into the district.

### Is Ybor City part of downtown Tampa?

Ybor is a historic district northeast of downtown Tampa, and it is part of the city. It feels separate once you are on 7th Avenue, with its own history, architecture, and nightlife. Walking between downtown and Ybor is possible but takes a while, so most people drive or take the streetcar.

### Where should I park in Ybor City?

Use one of the city garages or lots, such as the Centro Ybor Garage at 1500 East 5th Avenue, the Fernando Noriega Jr. Garage at 2010 North 13th Street, or the Ybor lots on North 19th Street. Avoid residential blocks south of 6th Avenue unless you know the signs allow visitor parking. The City of Tampa parking office is at 813-242-5483.

### Do I need a permit to park on the side streets in South Ybor?

Residents do, and the city runs a permit program covering the South Ybor zone. If you are a visitor, don't assume the side streets are open to you. Check the signs, and when in doubt, use a garage. Enforcement questions go to 813-274-8524.

### Can I take a tour of a cigar factory?

J.C. Newman Cigar Company at El Reloj offers tours and rolling and tasting classes. E. Regensberg and Sons, on 16th Street, is a large factory still producing cigars. Confirm current tour availability before you go, because the schedule can change.

### Is the streetcar a good way to get to Ybor City?

Yes. The TECO Line streetcar connects Ybor with downtown and Channelside. It is slower than driving, but it saves you the parking search and lets you hop on and off along 7th Avenue.

### Is Ybor City safe at night?

I don't have crime figures I would trust enough to publish, so I won't give you a safety ranking. Common sense goes a long way. Stay in populated areas, keep valuables out of sight, and don't leave things in your car. Night in Ybor is lively and crowded, and a lot of people have a good time there without incident.

### What is the best time of day to visit Ybor City?

For the history, architecture, museum, and factory tours, go in the daytime, ideally on a weekday morning. For music and bars, come after dark on a weekend. If you are bringing kids or want a calmer visit, the afternoon is the way to go.

For the skatepark east of Ybor off I-4 exit 3, read [Skatepark of Tampa](/things-to-do/skatepark-of-tampa).

Hunting a flea market? Big Top is closed—see [Tampa flea market options](/shopping/tampa-flea-market) (Oldsmar and Ybor Saturday Market).

## Final Thoughts

Ybor City is one of the most distinctive places in Tampa, and it earns the trip. The brick, the balconies, the cigar history, and the Columbia Restaurant are worth an afternoon. The night scene is a separate experience, and it is a lot louder than the daytime version. Most of the frustration people have here is not about the neighborhood itself. It is about parking, and about not realizing that 7th Avenue is one thing and the residential streets south of 6th Avenue are another.

Park in a garage, walk the strip, and take the streetcar when you can. Call ahead for the visitor center and any factory tour you want. And remember that a road project in the news is not the same as a crime statistic, and that the best guidance is what you can see with your own eyes when you get there.

title: 6 Things to Know About the Westin Tampa Waterside Before You Book

body:
# 6 Things to Know About the Westin Tampa Waterside Before You Book

If you have asked around Tampa about the Westin Tampa Waterside, you have probably heard it called three or four different things. People say westin waterside tampa, tampa westin waterside, or the westin tampa waterside tampa, and they nearly always mean the same hotel on the same stretch of Harbour Island. I have walked past it, eaten near it, and talked to enough people who booked it to know where the confusion comes from. Some details are solid. Some are not. This is the version I would give a friend who asked me what to expect before they booked. 🌊

![The Westin Tampa Waterside on Harbour Island seen from the edge of the channel](/images/wm/articles/10869786.webp)
*Photo by [Marek Kupiec](https://www.pexels.com/@marek-kupiec-1696944) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/a-row-of-sailboats-in-the-ocean-10869786/)*

## Short on Time?

- The address is 725 South Harbour Island Boulevard, Tampa, FL 33602. Marriott's current name for it is Westin Tampa Downtown Waterside.
- This is a downtown waterfront hotel, not a beach hotel. Clearwater Beach is about 25 miles away.
- If you are comparing hotels on Harbour Island, match on the street address rather than the name, because the name has changed over time.
- Breakfast is not included. Room service exists, but I did not get its hours.
- The bar and restaurant can list midnight, but the kitchen stops taking food at 10 p.m.
- The room counts I have seen do not agree with each other. Ask which number is current before you repeat one.
- If an accessible room, the shuttle, a pet policy, or a rate matters to you, ask the hotel directly. Do not assume.

## 1. Which Name to Use for the Westin Tampa Waterside

This is the part people get wrong first, so I will go slow.

Marriott calls the hotel [Westin Tampa Downtown Waterside](https://www.marriott.com/en-us/hotels/tpawh-westin-tampa-downtown-waterside/overview/). The restaurant on the ground floor, Blue Harbour, still carries the older name, The Westin Tampa Waterside, in its own description. Some local listings call the property The Westin Tampa Harbour Island. These are all the same building on the same street. The street does not move, so I treat them as one hotel.

The address you want is 725 South Harbour Island Boulevard, Tampa, Florida 33602. The main phone line is 813-229-5000. Marriott's toll-free number is 800-937-8461. If you are typing the name into a map or an email, watch the spelling. The island is spelled Harbour, with a u. People who write Harbor with the American spelling can end up searching for a slightly different place or getting autocorrect to fight them.

Harbour Island is a downtown island off the channel. It is not a barrier island on the Gulf. That distinction matters more than it sounds like it should, and I will come back to it. When people say "waterside," they usually mean the channel and the downtown waterfront, which is exactly what you get here. You do not get sand.

![Entrance and street sign for South Harbour Island Boulevard outside the Westin Tampa Waterside](/images/wm/articles/31087072.webp)
*Photo by [Mingyang LIU](https://www.pexels.com/@mingyang-liu-301813241) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/entrance-to-underbelly-boulevard-soho-on-peter-street-31087072/)*

## 2. How Close It Really Is to What People Expect

Here is the honest geography.

The beach is far. Clearwater Beach is about 25 miles from the hotel. St. Petersburg Beach is about 29 miles. If you book here because you want to walk out the lobby doors and put your feet in the sand, you will be disappointed, and it is better to find that out now. Plan a beach day as its own trip. [Naples](/guides/tampa-to-naples) is a longer drive than Clearwater, and it is its own day.

What is close is the downtown core. The Convention Center is one block away, and a stop on the [electric streetcar](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa) is also one block away. The cruise port is a few blocks off, which is useful if you are catching a ship and do not want to haul luggage far. Bayshore Linear Park is within reach if you like to walk along the water and do not mind a bit of distance.

On the island itself, the next marina is The Pointe Marina. Paramount Water Sports operates from there. That is a real neighbor, and if you want to get on the water, it is the closest option I would name. ⛵

Some of the places a hotel lists as nearby are not the same kind of walk. Office towers for big accounting and banking firms, the Henry B. Plant Museum, and Westshore Plaza are all in the general area. They are not all a stroll. Westshore Plaza in particular is a drive for most people, so check your route before you count it as a walk. The [Westshore Marriott](/guides/westshore-marriott-hotel-tampa) is the hotel on that side of town, and it is a drive from Harbour Island too. [The Tampa EDITION](/guides/the-tampa-edition) is the Water Street hotel if you wanted Channelside instead of Harbour Island.

The airport is roughly seven to eight miles away, depending on how you measure it and which road you take. Plan for a car ride, not a short hop.

On the shuttle: the hotel lists a complimentary shuttle that runs on demand within about three miles, based on availability. That is not a timetable. If you need a ride to the airport or a specific event, ask before you rely on it.

Most rooms have water views, and that is one of the real selling points. I would still ask for a view by name when you book if it matters to you.

![Harbour Island marina with boats tied up near the Westin Tampa Waterside](/images/wm/articles/16968907.webp)
*Photo by [Thomas Dudek](https://www.pexels.com/@thomas-dudek-576898596) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/ships-moored-in-harbor-16968907/)*

## 3. The Rooms, and the Numbers That Don't Agree

The hotel describes newly renovated suites and rooms, waterfront rooms, and a residence-inspired waterside suite. The suites come with bottled water, robes, and mini-fridges. Rooms have high-speed Wi-Fi and pillowtop mattresses, and room service is available. Room sizes are listed as approximate, so do not plan a furniture arrangement around a square-footage number.

The harder part is the room count. I have seen the total given as 299 guest rooms with 19 suites, and I have also seen 309 sleeping rooms including suites, with 23 suites. The breakdown I have seen is 122 doubles and 160 kings, spread over 12 floors served by 3 elevators. I cannot tell you which total is current, and I would not repeat any single one as if I had counted the keys myself. If the exact room count matters to your group or your event planning, ask the hotel which inventory it is currently using.

The accessible room question deserves its own paragraph. When I tried to book an accessible room through Marriott's site, I got a message that there might be a limited number of accessible rooms, and then a flat line: "No Accessible Rooms Available at this Hotel." That looked like sold-out inventory for those dates, not a policy that the hotel has no accessible rooms at all. The count of accessible rooms I have seen listed elsewhere does not match that screen either. If you need an accessible room, call the hotel directly and ask about your exact dates before you assume it is available or unavailable.

Refrigerators are another place where the marketing blurs. The hotel's descriptions put mini-fridges in the suites. Other descriptions say refrigerators are in every room. I do not know that to be true, so I would ask. The same goes for coffee makers, hair dryers, and in-room hot tubs, which are not something I can confirm for any room type.

I never got a nightly rate, from the hotel or anywhere else. I am not going to make one up. If a booking site shows a price, that is the number that matters, and it will change by date and season.

![Waterside suite living area with a view across the Tampa channel](/images/wm/articles/37258376.webp)
*Photo by [Murat Ak](https://www.pexels.com/@muratak) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/expansive-ocean-and-sky-with-distant-horizon-37258376/)*

## 4. Dining, and the Hours That Don't Match the Sign

🍽️ This is where I would slow down before you plan a late night.

There are three places to eat on the property. The Marketplace is grab-and-go and casual, and it runs 24 hours a day, which is the most useful thing on the list if you land late or leave early. Blue Harbour Lounge serves American food every day from 11 a.m. to midnight. The hotel says food service stops at 10 p.m., though. That means the room can say midnight while the kitchen has already closed. If you want a real dinner, get there well before 10. Then there is 725 South Breakfast, which is weekdays 6:30 a.m. to 11 a.m., and weekends 7 a.m. to 12 p.m. The name is the street number. It is not a second address.

Complimentary breakfast is not currently served. Plan for it to cost money, and budget accordingly. Room service is available, but I did not get its hours, so do not promise yourself a 2 a.m. meal until you have asked.

Some places nearby are not in the building, and I want to be clear about that. A Starbucks is about 0.1 miles away, and American Social and Jackson's are at about the same distance. Malio's Prime is about 1.8 miles off, and it is not one of the hotel's restaurants. I made that mistake once when reading the list, and I would not want you to make it when you are hungry.

![Blue Harbour restaurant interior at the Westin Tampa Waterside during dinner service](/images/wm/articles/1484529.webp)
*Photo by [Valeria Boltneva](https://www.pexels.com/@valeriya) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/classic-interior-of-dining-hall-with-served-glasses-in-restaurant-1484529/)*

## 5. Pool, Gym, and Meeting Space

The fitness center is complimentary for guests. It has cardio equipment, ellipticals, bikes, treadmills, free weights, and weight machines. I have seen it described as recently expanded, which fits with the renovation talk, but I would not plan a workout around a specific piece of equipment until you have confirmed it.

There is one outdoor pool for hotel guests, with a bar nearby. 🏊 I have seen it described as heated, and I have seen descriptions that do not mention heat at all. If you are coming from out of town in cooler months and the pool temperature matters to you, ask.

Now the meeting space, which is where the numbers really get messy. The property has 15 event rooms in one place I looked and 13 in another. Total event space is listed as 23,331 square feet in one source and 18,000 in another. The largest room is the Oasis Ballroom, which is 85 feet by 56 feet with a 15-foot ceiling, or about 4,760 square feet. The capacity chart for Oasis lists reception for 800, banquet for 432, theater for 600, classroom for 288, conference for 70, and U-shape for 100. Other material gives seated capacity as 750 and theater as 700. I would plan the room from the chart and then confirm every figure with the events team before anything gets printed or ordered. The largest-capacity figure of 800 is the one I see repeated most often, and it is a reception number, not a seated one.

![Oasis Ballroom set up for a meeting at the Westin Tampa Waterside](/images/wm/articles/27758878.webp)
*Photo by [Jonathan Cooper](https://www.pexels.com/@theshuttervision) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/a-large-empty-room-with-a-wooden-floor-27758878/)*

## 6. Check-In, Parking, Pets, and Money

Standard check-in is listed at 3 p.m., and checkout at 12 p.m. The listed cancellation policy is 24 hours before arrival. The hotel also carries a Three Diamond AAA rating. Confirm these when you book, because policies change and I am not sure they are current.

Parking is offered as self-park and valet, and both carry a charge. I have seen a parking count of 188 spaces, and I have seen motorcoach spaces mentioned, but I did not get a dollar amount for either self-park or valet. Ask for the current rate when you book, and ask whether a motorcoach can get in if you are planning a group arrival.

Pets are listed as allowed. I did not get a pet fee or a weight limit, so ask before you show up with a dog.

![Valet drive and front entrance of the Westin Tampa Waterside on a weekday afternoon](/images/wm/articles/35831390.webp)
*Photo by [DΛVΞ GΛRCIΛ](https://www.pexels.com/@davegarcia) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/transportation-van-with-wheelchair-access-and-driver-35831390/)*

## Useful Things to Know

A few practical things that will save you a bad surprise:

**Call before you count on anything specific.** Accessible rooms, the shuttle, room service hours, pool heat, the in-room fridge, and parking rates are all things where the answer I got from a screen or a listing did not settle it. A phone call to the front desk will settle more than a booking page.

**Book for the name on the confirmation.** Search for the Westin Tampa Waterside, Westin Tampa Downtown Waterside, or the street address, and make sure the listing you choose is this hotel at 725 South Harbour Island Boulevard. The spelling of Harbour is worth a second look.

**Plan dinner before 10.** The lounge may list hours to midnight, but the kitchen stops at 10 p.m. Eat early or plan for the Marketplace.

**Do not book a beach trip from here.** If sand is the point of the trip, you will spend a lot of your time in the car. Clearwater Beach is about 25 miles off.

**Expect to pay for breakfast.** Complimentary breakfast is not currently served, so budget for it, or plan to eat somewhere else.

**If you are hosting an event, plan from the chart.** Capacity numbers in the materials I have seen disagree with each other. Get the final numbers in writing from the events team before you finalize seating or catering.

## FAQ

### Is the Westin Tampa Waterside on the beach?

No. It is on Harbour Island, a downtown island off the channel, not on a Gulf beach. Clearwater Beach is about 25 miles away, and St. Petersburg Beach is about 29 miles. You will get water views and waterfront access, but not sand outside the door.

### What is the address of the Westin Tampa Waterside?

The address is 725 South Harbour Island Boulevard, Tampa, FL 33602. The main phone line is 813-229-5000. Note that the island is spelled Harbour, with a u.

### Is breakfast included at the Westin Tampa Waterside?

Not as far as I can tell. Complimentary breakfast is not currently served. The on-site breakfast spot, 725 South Breakfast, is open on weekdays from 6:30 a.m. to 11 a.m. and on weekends from 7 a.m. to 12 p.m., and it is a paid option.

### Does the Westin Tampa Waterside have accessible rooms?

I cannot promise it does for your dates. When I tried to book one through Marriott's site, I got a "No Accessible Rooms Available at this Hotel" message, which looked like sold-out inventory rather than a permanent policy. Call the hotel directly with your exact dates.

### How far is the Westin Tampa Waterside from the airport?

Roughly seven to eight miles from Tampa International, depending on your route. You will need a car, a rideshare, or a taxi. The hotel lists an on-demand shuttle within about three miles, but availability is not guaranteed, so ask before you count on it.

### Is there a pool and gym at the Westin Tampa Waterside?

Yes. There is one outdoor pool for hotel guests and a complimentary fitness center with cardio equipment, free weights, and weight machines. I have seen the pool described as heated and seen no mention of heat at all, so ask if that matters to you.

### How many rooms does the hotel have?

I have seen two totals, 299 and 309, and I have seen suite counts of 19 and 23 that do not match each other. I would not repeat one number as fact. Ask the hotel which room count is current before you rely on it.

Comparing downtown Riverwalk stays? I also covered the [Barrymore Hotel Tampa](/guides/barrymore-hotel-tampa).

## Final Thoughts

The Westin Tampa Waterside is a solid downtown hotel on Harbour Island. You get water views, the Convention Center and streetcar a block away, and easy access to the rest of downtown. What you do not get is a beach. Plan your trip around that fact.

The things I trust least are the things that have the most numbers attached to them: room counts, event capacity, accessible inventory, and the shuttle. Those are the ones to confirm with the hotel directly. The things I trust most are the address, the location, the restaurant hours as listed, and the fact that breakfast is not included.

If you are coming, call ahead, ask the specific questions, and eat dinner before the kitchen closes. You will have a better stay for it.

body:
# The Tampa EDITION: 5 Things to Know Before You Book

If you search for the tampa edition, the edition tampa, or just "EDITION Tampa," you are almost certainly looking for the same place: [The Tampa EDITION](https://www.editionhotels.com/tampa/) at 500 Channelside Drive, [downtown](/things-to-do/things-to-do-in-tampa), inside the Water Street Tampa neighborhood. It is a luxury hotel with a lot of restaurants and bars under one roof, and it sits close to two other large Marriott-family hotels that people mix up with it all the time. I have spent a fair amount of time going through how the hotel describes itself, and I want to lay out what it is, what it is not, and where people trip up before they show up with a bag and a reservation that does not match the building.

![The Tampa EDITION hotel exterior on Channelside Drive in downtown Tampa](/images/wm/articles/17073730.webp)
*Photo by [Brandon Ricketts](https://www.pexels.com/@brandon-ricketts-450464466) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/sunlight-over-modern-building-wall-17073730/)*

## Short on Time?

- **Address:** 500 Channelside Drive, Tampa, FL 33602. This is not the Tampa Marriott Water Street on Water Street, and it is not the JW Marriott. Check the street before you confirm.
- **Rooms:** 172 guest rooms and 30 suites, with a penthouse listed at 2,059 square feet.
- **Dining:** Several venues. Lilac is the dinner splurge and it is closed on Sunday and Monday. Call ahead for anything rooftop, and ask whether Azure and the Pool Bar are open.
- **Parking:** 🚗 Valet only as far as I could find. Overnight is $58 plus taxes, daytime or daily is $40 plus taxes, and event parking is $60 plus taxes.
- **Beach:** 🌊 It is a downtown bay-side hotel, not a beach hotel. The Gulf is a drive west.

## 1. The Tampa EDITION: Where It Is, and Which One You Actually Mean

The first thing to get straight is the name. The hotel is The Tampa EDITION, and the brand is written in capital letters, but people say it every way you can imagine. The address stays the same no matter how you type it. The hotel's booking details use the code TPAEB, and the phone number is +1 (813) 221-4600.

Why does this matter? Because EDITION is part of the Marriott world, and downtown Tampa has several luxury doors within a short walk of each other. The Tampa Marriott Water Street is at 505 Water Street. The JW Marriott is at 510 Water Street. Those are real hotels in the same district, and people land at the wrong one all the time because the map shows a cluster of glass towers and they assume it is one building. Harbour Island is [the Westin Tampa Waterside](/guides/the-westin-tampa-waterside). The airport side of town is the [Westshore Marriott](/guides/westshore-marriott-hotel-tampa).

My rule of thumb: Channelside Drive versus Water Street is the first filter. If your confirmation email says 500 Channelside Drive, you are at The Tampa EDITION. If it says anything on Water Street, you are at one of the Marriott or JW properties, which is fine if that is what you wanted, but it is not the same front desk, not the same restaurants, and not the same room inventory.

The EDITION brand also carries design credits that the hotel leads with. Architecture is by Morris Adjmi with Nichols Brosch Wurst Wolfe & Associates. Interiors are by Roman & Williams. The creative vision is credited to Ian Schrager and Ian Schrager Company. I mention those because they explain the look of the lobby and the bar, which is moody, green, and a little theatrical. They are branding context, not a reason to pay more.

The neighborhood matters too. Water Street Tampa is a newer, large development that the hotel describes as a 56-acre neighborhood. From the hotel, the [Florida Aquarium](https://www.flaquarium.org/) and the Channelside area are the obvious walk. [Yard House](/food-and-drink/yard-house-tampa) is the casual room across from the arena, a short walk on Channelside. [The Pearl](/food-and-drink/the-pearl-tampa) is the other Water Street restaurant. The Tampa Convention Center is about a mile away, close enough to walk on a nice day and far enough that you may want a ride when you have boxes of conference materials.

![Water Street Tampa waterfront with the bay and downtown skyline at dusk](/images/wm/articles/35588389.webp)
*Photo by [Robert So](https://www.pexels.com/@robertkso) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/illuminated-city-skyline-at-dusk-35588389/)*

## 2. Rooms, Suites, and the Penthouse

The room count is one of the few numbers I saw repeated the same way across the hotel's own description and the Marriott listing. EDITION lists 172 guest rooms and 30 spacious suites. The Marriott count matches, with 30 suites including one penthouse. Other descriptions of the property give 172 sleeping rooms including suites, nine floors, and 30 suites. Those do not read identically, and the difference may just be how the total is labeled. If it matters for a group block, ask at check-in how many standard rooms there actually are.

The hotel leads with the rooms themselves: floor-to-ceiling windows, marble bathrooms, and rainforest-style shower heads. Free wireless internet is included, and the coffee bar downstairs serves La Colombe. The hotel also calls out pet-friendly accommodations for downtown Tampa, so if you are traveling with a dog, ask about the rooms that allow pets before you book, since I did not see enough detail to tell you which room types qualify.

The penthouse is the room people ask about, and it is the one I can describe with any confidence. The hotel and its event material both repeat 2,059 square feet. The penthouse has a private bedroom, a separate living room, a half-bath, a dining room with an oak table, and a full kitchenette with a service entrance. The big draw is the 180-degree view: Tampa Bay on one side, Channelside on another, and the skyline on the third. It is the kind of room you book for a special night, not a standard weekend.

The Bay Suite is the other suite I can describe. It has a corner-view bedroom, a living and dining area, a powder room, and a full bath. I did not find square footage for every suite type, so I am not going to invent it. If square footage matters to you, ask for the exact figure for the specific room you are booking.

Amenities listed for the hotel include complimentary 24-hour fitness facilities, a gym with two Peloton bikes, personal training on request, a spa with steam rooms and a deep relaxation lounge, room service, and a concierge desk. Those are reasonable things to expect at this price point, but check whether the spa and gym are open at the hours you plan to use them.

![Penthouse suite at The Tampa EDITION with floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking Tampa Bay](/images/wm/articles/6890242.webp)
*Photo by [Spencer Cook](https://www.pexels.com/@spencer-cook-15614259) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/a-woman-standing-near-the-glass-window-6890242/)*

## 3. Restaurants and Bars: It Is a Stack, Not One Dining Room

This is where most first-time guests get tangled. The Tampa EDITION is less a single restaurant than a set of spaces, each with its own hours, its own dress code, and its own rules. 🍽️ Here is what I saw listed, and I would confirm all of it before you plan a night around it.

**Lilac** is the Michelin-starred Mediterranean restaurant, led by Chef John Fraser. The hours I found put it open for dinner Tuesday through Saturday, with Monday and Sunday closed. On Tuesday through Thursday, dinner runs from 5:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m., and Friday and Saturday run from 5:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. The dress code is formal, and the restaurant phone is +1 813-771-8022. Reservations matter here. If you walk in hungry on a Monday, you will be disappointed, and a weekend without a reservation is a gamble.

**Market at EDITION** is the more casual option, serving Italian and Mediterranean food with Neapolitan-style pizzas. It is listed as open every day from 7:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. This is the place I would point someone to if they wanted to eat without planning ahead.

**The Market coffee bar** is open every day from 6:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., with La Colombe coffee and pastries. Breakfast on property is served through Market and the coffee bar, and it costs extra. Plan for that if your rate does not include a meal.

**The Lobby Bar** is the billiards-and-cocktails room with the greenery. Hours I found run Monday through Thursday and Sunday from 4:00 p.m. to midnight, and Friday and Saturday from noon to 1:00 a.m. It is the most relaxed bar in the building, and it is where I would start an evening if I were meeting someone for a drink and did not want a dinner reservation.

**The Punch Room** is the cocktail spot with a smart casual dress code. The listed hours have it closed Monday, Tuesday, and Sunday. It is open Wednesday and Thursday from 5:00 p.m. to midnight, and Friday and Saturday from 5:00 p.m. to 1:00 a.m.

**The Arts Club** is closed Monday through Wednesday and on Sunday. Thursday hours run from 6:00 p.m. to midnight, and Friday and Saturday from 6:00 p.m. to 1:00 a.m. Like the Punch Room, it is a night spot, not a daytime stop.

**Azure at EDITION and the rooftop** is where the information got messy. Ask the hotel whether Azure and the Pool Bar are open before you book a rooftop dinner. I would call +1 813-771-8022, and I would not trust an old set of hours.

![Lilac restaurant dining room at The Tampa EDITION with white tablecloths and bay-view windows](/images/wm/articles/27138849.webp)
*Photo by [Alfie Binne](https://www.pexels.com/@alfie-binne-646217215) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/close-up-of-a-table-with-roses-in-vases-27138849/)*

## 4. Getting Here and Parking

If you are flying in, the hotel gives directions from Tampa International via I-275, and also via George J. Bean Parkway and State Road 60. One of those routes includes tolls, so check the route before you commit to it. The hotel is about seven miles from the airport, which is a reasonable drive on a weekday and a longer one at rush hour.

Parking is valet, and the prices are the ones I would plan around. Overnight valet is $58 plus taxes. Daytime or daily valet is $40 plus taxes. Event parking valet is $60 plus taxes. I did not find a self-park garage rate, so I would not assume you can park yourself cheaply. There is also an electric car charging station, which is worth knowing if you are driving an EV. 🚗

There is a partial break on parking. Patrons who spend $60 or more in the food and beverage venues get 50 percent off the parking validation. That does not apply on event nights, so check whether your stay overlaps with a booking in the ballroom or on the rooftop before you count on it.

If you are coming by rideshare, the drop-off at Channelside Drive is the main address to give the driver. Give the street, not just "The EDITION," because the driver may pull up at the wrong Water Street building.

![Valet drop-off at The Tampa EDITION on Channelside Drive at night](/images/wm/articles/36333607.webp)
*Photo by [分 参](https://www.pexels.com/@fungraphy) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/rainy-night-cityscape-from-car-window-36333607/)*

## 5. Events, Meeting Space, and Weddings

If you are booking the hotel for a meeting or event, the space is the main reason to look closely. The event details list more than 28,000 square feet of meeting space across 21 event rooms. The largest spaces are the Ballroom and the Rooftop Pool Bar & Deck, each with a capacity of 250. The Ballroom is about 3,257 square feet with 18-foot ceilings and white oak floors. It connects to a pre-function area and an outdoor terrace.

For smaller groups, there is a Boardroom that seats roughly 8 to 12, and a Garden Terrace on the third floor. The Penthouse Suite can be used for intimate dinners, which fits the hotel's overall approach. Weddings are offered.

The Rooftop Pool Bar & Deck has the same June 15 to October 3 closure note I mentioned above, so do not lock in a rooftop event without confirming the space is open and running on the date you want. If you are planning a large event, ask about the rooftop status and the ballroom's availability at the same time.

I would also read the rate and cancellation rules closely. Standard rooms need to be cancelled five days before arrival to avoid a penalty, and suites need seven days. That is stricter than a lot of downtown hotels, and it is the kind of detail that is easy to skip past when you are excited about the building. Do not assume you can cancel 24 hours out.

![Ballroom at The Tampa EDITION set up for an event with white oak floors and high ceilings](/images/wm/articles/34278805.webp)
*Photo by [Justin Agyarko](https://www.pexels.com/@justinagyarko) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/elegant-50th-birthday-celebration-decor-setup-34278805/)*

## Useful Things to Know

**Check-in and check-out.** The hotel lists check-in at 4:00 p.m. and check-out at 11:00 a.m. Guests must be at least 18 to check in. If you are arriving early, ask about options before you plan a morning meeting in the building.

**Accessibility.** The hotel offers mobility-accessible rooms for certain room types. When I tried booking through Marriott, the site showed the same inventory warning other Marriott hotels show when you select accessible rooms during booking. That message appeared as a momentary "no accessible rooms available" line, and I am not treating it as a permanent fact about the building. If you need an accessible room, call the hotel directly before you assume there is none.

**The bay side versus the beach.** People get this wrong. The Tampa EDITION is a downtown waterfront hotel on the bay side of the city. It is not a beach hotel. If you want Gulf sand and the feeling of a beach day, you will need to drive west, and that is a real drive, not a short walk. Plan your day accordingly.

**Reservations.** Lilac requires a reservation, especially on weekends. Treat it like a required step, not an optional one, and call +1 813-771-8022 as soon as you know your dates.

**Confirmation wording.** Capital-letter EDITION is the brand, and "the Tampa EDITION hotel" or "EDITION Tampa" will still get you there. But when you get the confirmation, make sure it says 500 Channelside Drive. That address is the one that separates this hotel from the Marriott and JW properties on Water Street.

**Rates.** I am not going to give you a nightly rate, because I did not find a number I am willing to stand behind. Room prices shift with dates, events, and availability. The dollar figures I can give you with confidence are the valet prices and the food-and-beverage validation threshold, both mentioned above.

**The rooftop window.** The June 15 to October 3 closure note has passed as of today, but I cannot say whether the rooftop bar and Azure are running a normal schedule now. Call before you plan anything up there.

## FAQ

### Is The Tampa EDITION the same as the Tampa Marriott Water Street?

No. The Tampa EDITION is at 500 Channelside Drive. The Tampa Marriott Water Street is at 505 Water Street, and the JW Marriott is at 510 Water Street. They are all in the same downtown district and part of the same Marriott-family group of brands, but they are separate hotels with separate front desks and restaurants. Check the address on your confirmation before you arrive.

### What is the phone number for The Tampa EDITION?

The main hotel number I found is +1 (813) 221-4600. For Lilac and for the rooftop and Azure hours, I would call +1 813-771-8022. Confirm the number on your booking, and call ahead for anything that depends on hours.

### How much is parking at The Tampa EDITION?

Parking is valet only, as far as I could find. Overnight valet is $58 plus taxes, daytime or daily valet is $40 plus taxes, and event parking valet is $60 plus taxes. Guests who spend $60 or more in the food and beverage venues get 50 percent off the validation, but that does not apply on event nights.

### Is Lilac open on Sundays and Mondays?

From what I found, Lilac is closed on Sunday and Monday. Dinner runs Tuesday through Saturday, with a formal dress code. Reservations are strongly recommended, and the phone number is +1 813-771-8022.

### Is Azure or the rooftop bar open right now?

I cannot tell you that for sure. The hotel said Azure and the Pool Bar were temporarily closed from June 15 through October 3, 2026, but other listings still showed hours for both. That window has passed as of October 8, 2026, but I did not confirm a reopening date. Call the hotel before you plan a rooftop visit.

### Does The Tampa EDITION have a pool or beach?

It has a rooftop pool bar and deck, and that space is the one to confirm before you go. It is not a beach hotel. The hotel is on the bay side of downtown Tampa, and the Gulf beaches are a drive west.

### Are there rooms for guests with mobility needs?

Yes, the hotel offers mobility-accessible rooms for certain room types. I saw an inventory warning on the booking page when selecting accessible rooms, which is common across Marriott properties and not a permanent statement about the hotel. Call the hotel directly to confirm what is available for your dates.

### How far is The Tampa EDITION from the airport and the Convention Center?

The hotel is about seven miles from Tampa International and about one mile from the Tampa Convention Center. Traffic can change the drive time a lot, so give yourself extra room on a weekday.

Comparing downtown Riverwalk stays? I also covered the [Barrymore Hotel Tampa](/guides/barrymore-hotel-tampa).

## Final Thoughts

The Tampa EDITION is a good hotel for a specific kind of stay: a downtown night with a view, a serious dinner, a few drinks in a moody room, and a spa or gym if that matters to you. It is not a beach resort, and it is not a budget stop. The best way to enjoy it is to know exactly which building you are booking, call ahead for the restaurants and the rooftop, and read the cancellation rules before you commit.

The confusion around the name is real, but the fix is simple. Confirm 500 Channelside Drive, book Lilac early, plan your parking as a valet expense, and check the rooftop status before you tell anyone you will be up there. Do those four things and the hotel is easy to enjoy. Comparing the Marriott collection next door? See [Marriott Water Street Tampa](/guides/marriott-water-street-tampa) at 505 Water Street.

title: Yummy House Tampa: Which Room, Hours and Menu to Know
dek: Two Yummy House restaurants sit in Tampa, with different addresses and closing times. Here's which one is which, when dim sum runs, and what to order.
metaTitle: Yummy House Tampa: Which Room, Hours and Menu to Know
metaDescription: Two Yummy House restaurants sit in Tampa, with different addresses and closing times. Here's which one is which, when dim sum runs, and what to order.
coverAlt: Yummy House restaurant exterior on East Hillsborough Avenue in Tampa
coverCredit: Photo by Tien Nguyen on Pexels
body:
# Yummy House Tampa: Which Room, Hours and Menu to Know

If you search for yummy house tampa, you will find more than one restaurant. Two Yummy House rooms in Tampa use nearly the same name, sit in different parts of town, have different phone numbers, and close at slightly different times on Sunday. I have sent friends to the wrong one, and I have been the friend who showed up at the wrong one, so I am writing this down in one place. The short version: know which address you mean before you get in the car, and do not plan around the afternoon gap.

![Yummy House restaurant exterior on East Hillsborough Avenue in Tampa](/images/wm/articles/17873841.webp)
*Photo by [Tien Nguyen](https://www.pexels.com/@tiennguyen) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/sunlit-food-bar-by-street-17873841/)*

## Short on Time? 🥡

- **There are two Yummy House restaurants in Tampa.** The one the brand calls Tampa is at 2620 E Hillsborough Ave, Tampa, FL 33610, phone (813) 237-3838. The other is a South Tampa restaurant at 302 N Dale Mabry Hwy, Tampa, FL 33609, phone 813-513-4788.
- **Both rooms close between lunch and dinner.** The Hillsborough location gives lunch from 11 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. and dinner from 5 to 9:30 p.m. Monday through Saturday, and Sundays are 11 to 2:30 and 5 to 9. Plan around that break.
- **Dim sum is a lunch thing.** At Hillsborough it runs only during lunch service, not dinner.
- **Michelin's mention is not a star.** The Hillsborough restaurant is in the guide. It does not have a star, and the room is casual.
- **Call before you drive.** Confirm which address you are going to, because the phone numbers do not cross over.

## 1. Yummy House Tampa on East Hillsborough: The Room the Brand Calls Tampa

When people say "the original," or just the name with no other detail, they almost always mean the restaurant on East Hillsborough Avenue. That is the location the chain itself points to as its Tampa restaurant. The address is [2620 E Hillsborough Ave](https://yummyhouseflorida.com/tampa/), Tampa, FL 33610, and the phone is (813) 237-3838. Those are the two details to write down.

The restaurant lists its locations, and when it names all of them, it repeats this same Tampa address and then lists sister restaurants in Sarasota, Gainesville, and Ocala. So "tampa fl" in the search is not a hint that you should drive to Sarasota. Sarasota is a different city by the chain's own count. If someone is proud of Tamiami Trail, that is not the Tampa dining room.

It is a lot of restaurant for the money. The room is big and plain. Nobody is going to give you a tasting menu or a candle on the table. You sit down, a server hands you a menu, and you start figuring out whether you want the lunch dim sum or the long dinner list. The energy is loud on a busy weekend, and that is part of what people come for.

I would not call this place a quiet date-night spot. I would call it the place you take a group that wants a lot of food, a lot of variety, and a fast, cheerful pace. If you want a dark room and a slow, careful dinner, you will be disappointed. If you want a table full of plates and nobody complaining about the bill, you will probably like it.

![Dining room at Yummy House on East Hillsborough Avenue in Tampa with tables set for lunch](/images/wm/articles/6646235.webp)
*Photo by [RDNE Stock project](https://www.pexels.com/@rdne) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/two-people-eating-asian-food-6646235/)*

## 2. The Other Yummy House in Tampa: The South Tampa Bistro on Dale Mabry

This is where most of the confusion starts. There is a second Yummy House restaurant in Tampa, and it is a separate place with its own address and its own phone number. The address is 302 N Dale Mabry Hwy, Tampa, FL 33609, and the phone is 813-513-4788. It presents itself as YHS China Bistro. It is the South Tampa room that fits the "more upscale one" description you will sometimes hear in car conversations about this brand.

The Dale Mabry room gives dim sum and lunch from 11 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. and dinner Monday through Saturday from 5 to 9:30 p.m. It is open seven days. Sunday dinner closes at 8:45, not 9. That quarter hour is the kind of detail that trips people up. I am not rounding it. If you pull up at 8:50 on a Sunday night expecting a seat, you will be standing outside.

I have not treated older information about this place as current. Older writeups mention ratings, prices, and history that may have changed, so I am only using the address, phone, and hours. If you want to know what the room feels like now, call or go, and trust what you see over what someone wrote a few years ago.

The main thing to remember is that a phone call to one room will not seat you in the other. The Hillsborough number will not get you a table on Dale Mabry, and the Dale Mabry number will not get you a table on Hillsborough. Pick one before anyone gets in the car. [Wright's Gourmet House](/food-and-drink/wrights-gourmet-house-tampa), farther south on Dale Mabry, is a lunch deli, not either of these rooms.

![Exterior of YHS China Bistro on North Dale Mabry Highway in South Tampa at dusk](/images/wm/articles/30199534.webp)
*Photo by [Adam Sage](https://www.pexels.com/@adamlowly) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/taste-of-china-restaurant-at-night-in-fog-30199534/)*

## 3. Why the Hours Trip People Up at Yummy House Tampa

The schedule is the part I care about most, because it is where people lose a whole afternoon. Both Tampa rooms close their lunch service at 2:30 p.m. and do not reopen for dinner until 5. That means if you leave a [downtown hotel](/guides/the-tampa-edition) at 3 p.m. because you are hungry and you have "open daily" in your head, you are early for dinner and late for dim sum. [Yard House](/food-and-drink/yard-house-tampa) is the Water Street meal if you would rather stay downtown.

At the Hillsborough restaurant, dim sum is lunch only. It does not carry into the dinner hours. The restaurant's own dim sum menu says dim sum is available only during lunch service, so do not plan a 6 p.m. dumpling order. If dim sum is the reason you are coming, go at lunch.

There is also a weekday-only lunch special. The lunch specials are available on weekdays, and they do not run on weekends or holidays. They include jasmine rice, soda, or tea, and several of them land in the $11.99 to $13.99 range. Saturday dim sum can still be a great move, but it is not the same deal as a Tuesday lunch special. Read the card before you order and do not assume the special applies because it is lunch.

![Dim sum carts and steamer baskets on a lunch table at Yummy House Tampa](/images/wm/articles/6378654.webp)
*Photo by [FOX ^.ᆽ.^= ∫](https://www.pexels.com/@fox-58267) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/dumplings-in-a-bamboo-steamer-6378654/)*

## 4. What to Order From the Yummy House Tampa Menu 🥟

The Tampa menu is really two menus. The lunch dim sum menu is a separate card, and the full dinner menu is a long list of a la carte dishes. I went through both rather than assuming the word "Chinese" meant one thing.

The dim sum card sorts dishes by size and price. When I went through it, small plates were $5.50, medium $6.25, large $6.75, chef's special $7.25, and a kitchen-special tier was $13.99. Those were the prices I saw at the time I looked, not a promise for the next visit, so check the card when you sit down. The names are the familiar Hong Kong lunch set: honey glazed barbecue pork buns, sesame balls, shu mai, ha gow, rice rolls, chicken feet in black bean sauce, egg tarts, pineapple buns, turnip cake, Shanghai dumplings, and sticky rice. If you have never ordered dim sum before, start with a few dumplings and a pork bun, then add a sweet item at the end. Pineapple buns and egg tarts are the easy wins for a first-timer.

The dinner menu is long and it leans toward American-Chinese plates alongside more traditional dishes. It includes orange chicken and salt-and-pepper calamari or tofu, clay-pot fish, and a salt-and-pepper section the restaurant describes as a signature mix of green onion, cilantro, roasted garlic, and chili. Hong Kong roast duck is served by the half and the whole, Peking duck is on the list, and there are XO beef, chow fun, and fried rice. I am not building a ranking out of that. The honest advice is to order a mix. One roast or clay-pot dish, a salt-and-pepper plate, and a vegetable go a long way for a table of four.

Do not order dim sum at dinner and expect it to show up. Do not show up at 2:45 expecting the full dinner menu either. Neither works in that gap.

![Salt and pepper calamari and clay-pot dishes on the dinner menu at Yummy House Tampa](/images/wm/articles/11160095.webp)
*Photo by [Shameel mukkath](https://www.pexels.com/@shameel-mukkath-3421394) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/close-up-shot-of-fried-calamari-in-a-bowl-11160095/)*

## 5. The Michelin Mention and the Star Nobody Should Expect

Michelin includes the Hillsborough restaurant in its Tampa coverage. It describes the cuisine as Chinese with dim sum, gives a $$ price level, and describes a spacious, no-frills room. It does not give the restaurant a star. Being in the guide and holding a star are different things, and this is where people get the wrong expectation.

The restaurant itself makes the picture fuzzier. It says it is brought to you by the team behind restaurants featured on the Michelin Guide. That is true as a sentence, but it is not a star at this address, and it is worded in a way that makes it easy to hear more than is there. I would not repeat it as if it were a rating.

The better expectation is the one Michelin's description gives: no frills, crowds, orange chicken and clay pot on the same menu. Go in expecting a busy, fun, affordable room with a lot of choices, and you will be happy. Go in expecting a tasting menu and you will be irritated.

Michelin's hours are also a trap. For the Hillsborough address, the guide gives a lunch window of 11:00 to 14:30, seven days. That leaves out the dinner service the restaurant lists after its break. If you use Michelin's hours and skip the restaurant's own hours, you will think they do not serve dinner. They do. Use the Michelin mention to decide whether you want to go. Use the restaurant's hours to decide when.

![Yummy House Tampa storefront on East Hillsborough Avenue with the sign lit at night](/images/wm/articles/19183610.webp)
*Photo by [Jimmy Liao](https://www.pexels.com/@jimmy-liao-3615017) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/traffic-on-a-narrow-street-among-buildings-with-lots-of-signboards-19183610/)*

## 6. Mistakes That Send People to the Wrong Yummy House

Most of the mistakes I have seen come from one of four things. The first is the two Tampas. One name, two addresses, two phones, and two different Sunday closing times. I got this wrong in my own head until I put the two restaurants side by side.

The second is the afternoon closure. Both rooms close lunch at 2:30 and open dinner at 5. People show up at 3 p.m. and get turned around. If you are coming in the afternoon, plan a snack, or plan to be early for dinner and wait it out.

The third is "tampa fl" leaking to the rest of the state. Sarasota, Gainesville, and Ocala are their own locations by the chain's count. If the address says Tamiami Trail, you are not in Tampa. I have heard people say they were going to "the Tampa one" and then drive an hour south. Check the street name before you leave the house.

The fourth is treating the Michelin mention as a star. It is a mention, the room is casual, and the menu is wide. Set your expectations to the room, not to the guide.

![Map view of Tampa showing East Hillsborough Avenue and North Dale Mabry Highway as two separate Yummy House locations](/images/wm/articles/6564830.webp)
*Photo by [Nothing Ahead](https://www.pexels.com/@ian-panelo) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/old-paper-map-with-continents-and-oceans-6564830/)*

## Useful Things to Know 📍

**Parking and reservations.** I do not have reservation policy or parking details for either Tampa room, so I am not going to make up a waitlist rule or a free lot. Call ahead. The phone numbers are the most useful practical detail I can give you. For the Hillsborough room, that is (813) 237-3838. For the Dale Mabry room, it is 813-513-4788.

**Timing.** Lunch runs 11 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. and dinner runs 5 p.m. until closing. The Hillsborough room closes at 9:30 Monday through Saturday and at 9 on Sunday. The Dale Mabry room closes at 9:30 Monday through Saturday and at 8:45 on Sunday. Those are the restaurant's own hours, and they are the ones to use.

**Dim sum.** It is a lunch thing at the Hillsborough room. Get there before 2:30 if you want it. Saturday dim sum is still a good option, but the weekday lunch special does not run on weekends or holidays.

**Prices.** The dim sum prices I saw were in the $5.50 to $13.99 range, depending on the tier. Prices change, so treat them as a guide and check the card when you sit down.

**Where to start.** For the Yummy House that the brand calls Tampa, start at 2620 E Hillsborough Ave and call (813) 237-3838. Go at lunch if dim sum is the point. Only head to 302 N Dale Mabry if someone specifically wants the South Tampa bistro, and call 813-513-4788 first.

## FAQ

### Is yummy house tampa one restaurant or two?

There are two Yummy House restaurants in Tampa. The one the brand calls Tampa is on East Hillsborough Avenue at 2620 E Hillsborough Ave. The other is a separate South Tampa restaurant at 302 N Dale Mabry Hwy, with its own phone number. They are not interchangeable.

### What are the hours for the Yummy House on Hillsborough Avenue?

The Hillsborough restaurant lists lunch from 11 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. and dinner from 5 to 9:30 p.m. Monday through Saturday. On Sunday it is lunch from 11 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. and dinner from 5 to 9 p.m. It closes between lunch and dinner every day, so plan around the gap.

### Is dim sum available all day?

No. At the Hillsborough restaurant, dim sum is available only during lunch service, which ends at 2:30 p.m. Do not plan on dim sum at dinner. The South Tampa restaurant also lists dim sum with lunch hours.

### Does yummy house tampa fl mean the Sarasota location?

No. The word "Florida" in the search does not point to a particular city. The Tampa restaurant is at 2620 E Hillsborough Ave, Tampa, FL 33610. Sarasota is a separate location at 1737 S Tamiami Trail, and it is not the Tampa dining room.

### Does the Yummy House in Tampa have a Michelin star?

Michelin includes the Hillsborough restaurant in its Tampa coverage, but it does not give the restaurant a star. Michelin describes it as a no-frills, busy room with Chinese food and dim sum. Expect a casual room, not a tasting menu.

### What should I order at Yummy House Tampa?

If you come at lunch, order dim sum and mix a few savory dumplings with a pork bun and a sweet item like an egg tart or pineapple bun. At dinner, the menu is a la carte and wide. A roast or clay-pot dish, a salt-and-pepper plate, and a vegetable make a good spread for a group.

### Why does the Michelin listing show different hours?

Michelin's listing for the Hillsborough address gives a lunch window of 11:00 to 14:30 seven days a week. It does not show the dinner service that the restaurant lists after its afternoon break. Use the restaurant's own hours for planning. The Michelin mention is useful for deciding whether to go, not for timing your visit.

## Final Thoughts 🥢

Yummy House in Tampa is easy to enjoy once you know which room you are walking into. The Hillsborough restaurant is the one the brand calls Tampa, it is big and loud, and the menu is long enough that you can fill a table without trying very hard. The South Tampa bistro on Dale Mabry is a different room with a different phone and a Sunday close that is fifteen minutes earlier. Both have the same afternoon gap, so the simplest rule is to decide on the address, call the number, and check the clock before you leave.

Go at lunch if you want dim sum, go at dinner if you want the full menu, and do not expect a star just because the name shows up next to Michelin. Bring a group, order a mix, and have a good time with it.

For the Dale Mabry churrascaria (not Boy Scout), see [Terra Gaucha Tampa](/food-and-drink/terra-gaucha-tampa).
